title: Bug Report: Incorrect RTL (Right-to-Left) Text Rendering and Alignment
author: baobabprince
body:
### Description
When typing or rendering Right-to-Left (RTL) text (specifically Hebrew), the character order is reversed (rendered Left-to-Right character by character), and default paragraph alignment does not correctly adapt to RTL context.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Open a document/editor instance.
2. Type a sentence or paragraph in Hebrew (e.g., `הוראות שימוש...`).
3. Observe the rendered text and cursor/paragraph orientation.

- Text should read correctly from right to left (e.g., `הוראות`).
- Paragraph alignment and BiDi algorithm should correctly handle Hebrew context and display end-of-paragraph formatting characters (`¶`) on the far left or relative to the RTL flow.

### Actual Behavior
- The text string is printed backwards (e.g., `הוראות` appears as `תאורה`).
- Text alignment defaults to LTR layout, causing improper text placement and symbol wrapping.

### Environment
- **App/Component:** WordCraft Editor / Document Viewer
- **OS:** Windows
- **Font:** Aptos Display (28pt)

Since you are the user and not the developer, you cannot fix this on your Mac yourself—the application developers must fix the way the app registers itself with macOS file handlers. title: Symbol-font bullets (U+F0B7) render as a wrong glyph instead of •
author: rclinux
body:
**Version:** wordcraft 0.3.0, Linux x86_64 release tarball (Arch-based distro, Wayland)

### What happens
In a bulleted list from a .docx that uses Word's standard bullet, the bullet renders as a wrong glyph that looks like a small logo or arrow, not a round dot. Second-level bullets ("o" in Courier New) render correctly.

### Cause (as far as I can tell)
The bullet level is defined the way Word writes it by default:

```xml
<w:numFmt w:val="bullet"/>
<w:lvlText w:val=""/>
<w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Symbol" w:hAnsi="Symbol" .../></w:rPr>
```

U+F0B7 is a Private Use Area code point that only means "bullet" in the Symbol font. When Symbol isn't installed (common on Linux), the fallback font draws whatever it has at U+F0B7. Word and LibreOffice map Symbol-font PUA characters (U+F020–U+F0FF) back to their standard Unicode equivalents (U+F0B7 → U+2022 •) when Symbol isn't available.

### Steps to reproduce
```sh
printf -- '- one\n- two\n  - nested\n' > list.md
pandoc list.md -o list.docx        # pandoc 3.10.2; its reference docx uses Word's default Symbol bullet
wordcraft-cli render list.docx list.png
```
The same glyph shows up in the app and in `wordcraft-cli convert list.docx out.pdf`.

### Expected
A round bullet (•), as in Word and LibreOffice.

### Suggested fix
Map Symbol (and maybe Wingdings) PUA characters to their Unicode equivalents when that font isn't available, at least U+F0B7 → U+2022 and U+F0A7 → U+25AA (Wingdings §-square, also common in Word lists).

title: Control server (--control) accepts unauthenticated commands, including file.saveAs to any path
author: Seronsecurity
body:
## Summary

When WordCraft is started with `--control <port>` (or `WORDCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT`), `apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs` listens on `127.0.0.1:<port>` and runs every JSON line it receives as an engine command. There is no token or other authentication, so any local process can drive the app. The command set includes `file.saveAs`, `file.exportPdf` and `file.exportPng` with arbitrary paths, which means any local process can write files anywhere the user can.

The server is opt-in and loopback-only, so this is low severity. I'm reporting it as defense in depth, because the feature exists so agents can use it and people may leave it running.

## Browser reachability

`serve()` replies `bad JSON` to a line it can't parse and then keeps reading the connection. An HTTP request therefore isn't rejected: its request line and headers fail to parse, and a body such as

```
\n{"method":"file.saveAs","params":{"path":"..."}}\n
```

is still executed. A web page could send that with `fetch("http://127.0.0.1:<port>/", {method: "POST", mode: "no-cors", body})`. Recent Chromium Local Network Access checks block many of these requests, but not every browser or version does, and the port is often predictable.

## Suggested fixes

1. Require a per-launch random token, printed to stderr or written to a 0600 file, sent as the first line or in each request, and have `wordcraft mcp --connect` pass it along.
2. Close the connection on the first line that isn't valid JSON, or reject anything that looks like HTTP (`GET `, `POST `, `Host:`). This kills the cross-protocol vector.
3. Optionally, by default, gate file-system commands (`file.open`, `file.save*`, `file.export*`, `insert.picture` with `path`, mail-merge recipients from a path) behind a flag.

## Related, minor

Ctrl/Cmd+click on a hyperlink (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, around line 511) passes any URL to `ctx.open_url` without checking the scheme. Allowing only `http`, `https` and `mailto`, or confirming before anythi…

title: Track formatting changes as revisions (w:rPrChange / w:pPrChange)
author: gunnertown
body:
With Track Changes on, inserted and deleted text is tracked, but formatting changes (bold, italic, font, paragraph style) are not recorded as revisions. Word writes these as `w:rPrChange` and `w:pPrChange` and shows them as "Formatted:" balloons.

I see "formatting revisions" is item 2 on the roadmap; this is to register interest from a legal user. In contract redlining a formatting change (for example, a clause heading restyled, or a defined term un-bolded) has to appear as a revision so the other side can see and accept or reject it.

Round-trip matters too: formatting revisions already present in a .docx from Word should survive opening and saving in WordCraft.

title: Full Arabic and RTL Support
author: Wyetgf
body:
### Overview

If this project aims to become a complete, open-source replacement for Microsoft Word, **comprehensive Arabic language support and native right-to-left (RTL) functionality must be treated as core requirements, not optional features or secondary improvements.**

As an Arabic user, I find that Microsoft Word, despite its extensive feature set, still suffers from numerous problems when working with Arabic text, mixed Arabic-English content, RTL document layouts, and right-to-left user interface elements. These problems can make everyday writing, editing, formatting, and document management unnecessarily frustrating.

I would like to see this project address these shortcomings by providing a genuinely complete Arabic writing experience, matching Word's capabilities where necessary and improving upon them wherever possible.

The goal is not simply to make Arabic text appear correctly on the page. It is to ensure that **every part of the application, from text rendering and cursor movement to paragraph formatting, tables, lists, keyboard shortcuts, and document navigation, behaves naturally and consistently in RTL workflows.**

### 1. Native RTL interface

The application should support a fully right-to-left interface when an RTL language is selected, particularly Arabic.

This should go beyond translating menus and labels. The entire interface should adapt appropriately to the selected writing direction.

Expected behavior includes:

- **Complete interface mirroring:** Sidebars, navigation panels, document outlines, formatting panels, dialogs, contextual menus, and other directional interface elements should be positioned and aligned appropriately for an RTL interface.
- **Toolbar layout:** Toolbars, ribbon-like interfaces, formatting controls, and navigation elements should follow a logical RTL layout without reversing the meaning or behavior of controls that should remain unchanged.
- **Text alignment:** Arabic interface labels, menus, dialogs, input fiel…

title: Linux (GNOME Wayland): window title bar doesn't match the desktop theme
author: fqazzazee
body:
## Environment

- Fedora 44, GNOME Shell 50.5, Wayland session, 167% display scaling
- Built from source at `d7d9702`

## Title bar doesn't follow the GNOME theme (Wayland)

On GNOME Wayland, the app draws its own title bar. This app shows winit's plain fallback bar, which
ignores the GNOME theme, dark mode and button layout.

The workspace sets `eframe = { version = "0.36", default-features = false }` (`Cargo.toml:53`),
which also drops winit's default `wayland-csd-adwaita` feature, so `sctk-adwaita` isn't in
`Cargo.lock`.

Possible fixes:

- Enable `winit/wayland-csd-adwaita`, so the title bar follows GNOME's look and light/dark mode, or
- Draw an in-app title bar, as PhotoCraft does on Linux.

Workaround: start the app through Xwayland (`env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY wordcraft`), so GNOME draws a real
title bar.

Same issue in GridCraft, with more detail: https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/issues/54

title: Export: a numbered list right after a bulleted list becomes bullets in ODT/RTF and is numbered "3., 4." in Markdown
author: wzsxb233
body:
**Summary**

When a numbered list immediately follows a bulleted list, with no ordinary paragraph between them, the ODT and RTF exporters merge both into one bulleted list. The Markdown exporter keeps counting across the two lists, so the numbered list starts at 3. WordCraft's own rendering, PDF export and HTML export are correct (`•`, `•`, `1.`, `2.`). Imported .docx files are affected the same way: a python-docx document with one "List Bullet" paragraph followed by one "List Number" paragraph exports its numbered item as a bullet in ODT/RTF and as `2.` in Markdown.

**Environment**
- WordCraft `main` @ d7d9702 (v0.3.0), `wordcraft-cli` release build
- Linux x86_64 (Debian 13), Rust 1.99; LibreOffice 25.2.3 used to view the exported ODT/RTF

**Steps to reproduce**
```sh
wordcraft-cli run --template blank \
  --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"bullet A"}' --cmd 'para.bullets' --cmd 'text.newParagraph' \
  --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"bullet B"}' --cmd 'text.newParagraph' --cmd 'para.bullets' --cmd 'para.numbering' \
  --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"num one"}' --cmd 'text.newParagraph' --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"num two"}' --save adj.docx
wordcraft-cli inspect adj.docx      # bullets have numbering num=1, the numbered items num=2 (model is right)
wordcraft-cli convert adj.docx adj.pdf    # • bullet A • bullet B 1. num one 2. num two   (correct)
wordcraft-cli convert adj.docx adj.odt
wordcraft-cli convert adj.docx adj.rtf
wordcraft-cli convert adj.docx adj.md
```

**Expected**
In ODT: two `<text:list>` elements, the second using a `list-level-style-number` style. RTF should have its own numbered `\ls`. Markdown should have `1. num one` / `2. num two`.

**Actual**
- ODT: a single `<text:list text:style-name="L1">` (bullet style) holding all four items. LibreOffice shows four bullets.
- RTF: LibreOffice shows four bullets.
- Markdown:
  ```
  - bullet A
  - bullet B
  3. num one
  4. num two
  ```
With an ordinary paragraph between the two lists, all formats export correctly. So …

title: Page breaks are dropped in ODT export and glue words together in TXT/Markdown/HTML ("num twoPage two")
author: wzsxb233
body:
**Summary**

A page break inserted with `text.pageBreak` (Ctrl+Enter) exports correctly to PDF (2 pages) and RTF (`\page`). In ODT export it disappears: the text before and after it ends up in one `<text:p>` with nothing between, so LibreOffice shows a single page. The TXT, Markdown and HTML exports drop it without adding any whitespace, which joins the last word before the break to the first word after it.

**Environment**
- WordCraft `main` @ d7d9702 (v0.3.0), `wordcraft-cli` release build; Linux x86_64; LibreOffice 25.2.3 used to check the ODT

**Steps to reproduce**
```sh
wordcraft-cli run --template blank --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"num two"}' --cmd 'text.pageBreak' \
  --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"Page two"}' --save pb.docx
wordcraft-cli convert pb.docx pb.pdf   # 2 pages (correct)
wordcraft-cli convert pb.docx pb.odt   # content.xml: <text:p>num twoPage two</text:p>
wordcraft-cli convert pb.docx pb.txt   # "num twoPage two"
wordcraft-cli convert pb.docx pb.md    # "num twoPage two"
```
The `test.docx` from python-docx (`doc.add_page_break()`) behaves the same way: ODT opens in LibreOffice as 1 page and not 2.

**Expected**
- ODT: start the following text in a new paragraph whose automatic style has `fo:break-before="page"`, or emit `<text:soft-page-break/>` plus a paragraph split.
- TXT/MD: at least a newline. A form feed in TXT is fine too.
- HTML: a paragraph split with `style="break-before: page"`.

**Actual**
The break is dropped and the surrounding words run together.

title: Track Changes: `edit.replaceAll` makes untracked edits when Track Changes is on
author: thaynej
body:
With Track Changes on, Replace All changes the text directly instead of recording tracked insertions/deletions. Replacing one match at a time (`edit.find` + `edit.replace`) *is* tracked, so the two paths behave differently.

**Steps**
```
wordcraft-cli run --file a-replaceall.docx \
  --cmd 'edit.replaceAll={"text":"towards","with":"toward"}' \
  --save a-replaceall-after.docx --print
```
Input paragraph: `We walked towards the light, then towards home.` (settings.xml has `<w:trackRevisions/>`)

**Expected:** two tracked replacements (`<w:del>towards</w:del><w:ins>toward</w:ins>` ×2). Rejecting all changes restores the original sentence.

**Actual:** `edit.replaceAll: {"replaced":2}`, and the saved document.xml has plain runs `We walked toward the light, then toward home.` with no `w:ins`/`w:del`. The edit can't be reviewed or rejected.

This is the most dangerous path for scripted/MCP mass edits, since it's the obvious command to reach for.

Environment: WordCraft 0.3.0, macOS universal, headless `wordcraft-cli run`.
**Repro documents** (minimal synthetic files; `word/settings.xml` contains `<w:trackRevisions/>`; `word/document.xml` body shown):

`a-replaceall.docx`
```xml
<w:p><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">We walked towards the light, then towards home.</w:t></w:r></w:p>
```

`a-replaceall-after.docx`
```xml
<w:p><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">We walked toward the light, then toward home.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:sectPr><w:type w:val="nextPage"/><w:pgSz w:w="12240" w:h="15840"/><w:pgMar w:top="1440" w:right="1440" w:bottom="1440" w:left="1440" w:header="720" w:footer="720" w:gutter="0"/><w:cols w:space="720" w:num="1"/></w:sectPr>
```

title: Track Changes: Find/Replace matches text inside tracked deletions; replacing it brings deleted text back (and repeated Replace gives "towardtoward")
author: thaynej
body:
`edit.find` / `edit.replace` treat text inside a tracked deletion (`w:del`) as live text. Replacing a match there inserts new text into the final document where the author had deleted it. Since a tracked replacement leaves the old word behind as a `w:del`, the *next* `edit.replace` finds that same deleted word again and stacks a second insertion.

**Steps (a): match inside someone else's deletion**
Input: `The cat sat ` + `<w:del w:author="Alice">towards the door </w:del>` + `quietly.`
Final view: `The cat sat quietly.`
```
wordcraft-cli run --file b-in-deletion.docx \
  --cmd 'edit.find={"text":"towards"}' \
  --cmd 'edit.replace={"text":"towards","with":"toward"}' \
  --save b-in-deletion-after.docx --print
```
**Expected:** no match (the word is deleted), or at least nothing new appearing in the final text.
**Actual:** `edit.find` reports 1 match. After the replace, the final view reads **`The cat sat towardquietly.`**: a live insertion lands where Alice's text had been removed. Alice's deletion is also split, and the `towards` part is re-attributed to `WordCraft User`:
`<w:ins author="WordCraft User">toward</w:ins><w:del author="WordCraft User">towards</w:del><w:del author="Alice"> the door </w:del>`

**Steps (b): two replaces on clean text**
Input: `We walked towards the light, then towards home.`
```
wordcraft-cli run --file a2-replace.docx \
  --cmd 'edit.find={"text":"towards"}' \
  --cmd 'edit.replace={"text":"towards","with":"toward"}' \
  --cmd 'edit.replace={"text":"towards","with":"toward"}' \
  --save a2-replace-after.docx --print
```
**Expected:** `We walked toward the light, then toward home.` (two tracked replacements)
**Actual:** both replaces report `{"remaining":2}`, and the final text is **`We walked towardtoward the light, then towards home.`** The second replace re-matched the first replacement's own tracked deletion.

With `wholeWord: true` the second case happens to come out right, because the deleted word sits next to the inserted one. The …

title: Headless/MCP: set the revision author name; list review.trackChanges {value} in the command params
author: thaynej
body:
> **Edit:** I originally reported that `review.trackChanges` can only toggle. That was wrong. It already accepts `{"value": true|false}` in 0.3.0. It just isn't listed in `wordcraft-cli commands`, which shows its params as `{}`. I've rewritten this issue accordingly. Sorry for the noise.

Two small gaps for scripted/agent review edits in headless mode:

1. **The revision author name can't be set headlessly.** Every revision is authored `WordCraft User`. `file.setAuthor` takes no params (it's the dialog). For agent/script edits it matters to label who made them, e.g. `"Claude (copyedit)"`, so a reviewer can tell them apart from human edits.
   **Request:** `file.setAuthor={"name": "…"}`, or an `--author` flag on `wordcraft-cli run` / `mcp`.

2. **Document the explicit form of `review.trackChanges`.** `review.trackChanges={"value": true}` works, but `wordcraft-cli commands` lists the params as `{}`. A script that only reads the command list will call it as a toggle. Documents that already have `<w:trackRevisions/>` load with tracking on, so a toggle turns tracking **off**, and the following edits are silently untracked. Listing `{"value"?: bool}` in the command's params would steer scripts to the safe form.

Environment: WordCraft 0.3.0, macOS universal, headless `wordcraft-cli run`.

title: Default font ignored when Normal style has no w:ascii: text renders as Times New Roman instead of docDefaults font
author: s3pp3ku
body:
**Version:** WordCraft 0.3.0 (Linux, Arch / Hyprland)

## Problem

When the `Normal` style has an `rFonts` element with no `w:ascii`, WordCraft renders text in Times New Roman instead of falling back to the font set in `w:docDefaults`. Word and LibreOffice both use the `docDefaults` font.

With AutoSave on, the wrong font is then written back into the file on open. A Word-made document went from 68,674 to 50,946 bytes, with its styles rewritten and its table layout changed.

## Repro

`styles.xml`:

```xml
<w:docDefaults><w:rPrDefault><w:rPr>
  <w:rFonts w:ascii="Calibri" w:eastAsia="Calibri" w:hAnsi="Calibri" w:cs="Calibri"/>
</w:rPr></w:rPrDefault><w:pPrDefault/></w:docDefaults>
<w:style w:type="paragraph" w:default="1" w:styleId="Normal"><w:name w:val="Normal"/><w:qFormat/>
  <w:rPr><w:rFonts w:eastAsia="Times New Roman" w:cs="Times New Roman"/></w:rPr>
</w:style>
```

`document.xml` body: one plain paragraph with no run font, and one centred bold 24 pt run with colour FFC000. Neither sets a font.

Open it with `wordcraft-cli render file.docx out.png`.

- **Expected:** Calibri, as LibreOffice produces (`pdffonts` lists Calibri embedded).
- **Actual:** Times New Roman, for both paragraphs.

Runs that set `rFonts` explicitly come out correctly, so only the inherited case is affected.

## Suspected cause

When the style's `rFonts` has no `ascii`, the font probably isn't resolved through `docDefaults`.

(The font dropdown hang is #5 / PR #9 and is separate.)

3. **Deadlock / Unresponsive Event Loop:** Because the main UI thread is synchronously blocked on , WordCraft stops pumping window manager events, rendering the entire window completely frozen while the dialog waits for user interaction that cannot be seen or focused.

Inspecting the frozen process with GDB shows Thread 1 blocked in 's portal backend:

wordcraft-cli text br-outside-run.docx

title: [Feature Request] Support Hunspell / system dictionaries and configurable proofing language (multilingual spell check)
author: rzajanckauskas
body:
### Summary
Currently, WordCraft's proofing engine (`crates/proof`) is hardcoded to US English (`dict::Dictionary::en_us()` with embedded Moby word list). When drafting documents in other languages (such as Lithuanian, French, German, Polish, etc.), every non-English word containing Latin/ASCII characters is flagged as a spelling mistake with red underlines, and no language selection is available.

It would be fantastic to support multilingual proofing, either via system dictionaries (Hunspell / Enchant) or by allowing users to load custom Hunspell `.aff` / `.dic` dictionaries.

---

### Current Behavior & Limitations
1. **Embedded US English Dictionary Only:**
   `crates/proof/src/lib.rs` and `dict.rs` compile the Moby word list (`assets/hyphenation/en-us.dic`) into the binary. There is currently no way to load or switch to other language dictionaries.
2. **False Positives on Non-English Latin Characters:**
   In `crates/proof/src/lib.rs`:
   ```rust
   if !w.is_ascii() && !w.chars().any(|c| c.is_ascii_alphabetic()) {
       return true; // other scripts: no dictionary
   }
   ```
   For European languages with extended Latin scripts (e.g. Lithuanian `ąžuolas`, French `élève`, German `über`), `w.chars().any(char::is_ascii_alphabetic)` evaluates to `true`, so these words bypass this check and are evaluated against the English word list, causing virtually every word in the document to be marked misspelled.
3. **English Grammar Rules:**
   `check_grammar()` applies English-specific rules (such as `a` vs `an`), which flag valid text in other languages.
4. **No UI Language Selector or Toggle:**
   The Status Bar and Review ribbon do not currently provide an option to select the active document language, nor a toggle to turn off inline spellcheck.
5. **In-Memory User Dictionary:**
   Words added via "Add to Dictionary" (`user_words()`) are held in memory only and not persisted across sessions (related to #40).

title: Add a System theme option that follows the macOS light/dark appearance
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Add a System choice to WordCraft's interface theme setting that follows the macOS light/dark appearance live, so the app changes with the rest of the desktop when macOS switches appearance automatically.

## Problem to solve

macOS can switch between Light and Dark appearance automatically (System Settings → Appearance → Auto changes it at sunset and sunrise), and many Mac apps offer a "System" theme choice that tracks it.

WordCraft offers only a manual dark-mode switch. `UiState.dark` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` is a boolean defaulting to light and persisted in `ui.json`. Users change it with File → Options → General → "Dark mode" or the View ribbon's Dark Mode → "Switch Modes" button, which toggles a separate session flag. The palette depends only on those two flags; no code path reads the OS appearance.

Because WordCraft only has manual choices, a user whose macOS appearance switches automatically has to change the app theme by hand at least twice a day, or leave it mismatched with every other app.

## Proposed behavior

Add System to the existing theme choice. With System selected, the app applies a light theme while macOS is in Light mode and a dark theme while it is in Dark mode, both at launch and immediately when the OS appearance changes while the app is open. The saved choice stays System; only the displayed theme changes. The existing manual choices keep working as they do today.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The theme control offers a System choice (for example "System" or "Use system setting") alongside the existing manual choices, and every place that exposes the theme (File → Options → General and the View ribbon's Dark Mode group) shows it.
2. With System selected, the app starts in its light theme when macOS is set to Light and in its dark theme when macOS is set to Dark.

title: Desktop app redraws every frame while idle (window title sent each frame)
author: castlelele
body:
The desktop app never goes idle: it redraws at the monitor's refresh rate even when nothing on screen changes.

## Observed (v0.3.0, Linux/Wayland, Intel UHD 620)

- An empty document left alone: ~180 `wl_surface.commit` per second (`WAYLAND_DEBUG=1`, 90 Hz monitor), about 14% CPU and 10% GPU.
- GridCraft and DeckCraft 0.3.0 on the same machine: 0 commits per second, 0% CPU when idle.

## Cause

`WordApp::ui` sends the window title at the end of every frame (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`, still on `main`):

```rust
let title = format!("{}{} - WordCraft", self.title_stem(), if self.session.dirty { " •" } else { "" });
ctx.send_viewport_cmd(egui::ViewportCommand::Title(title));
```

`Context::send_viewport_cmd_to` calls `request_repaint_of` for every command (egui 0.36.2, `context.rs`), so each frame schedules the next one. With egui's `repaint_causes()` logged per frame, every cause while idle is that `send_viewport_cmd` call.

## Suggested fix

Send the title only when it changes, as GridCraft does (`grid.last_title`):

```rust
let title = format!("{}{} - WordCraft", self.title_stem(), if self.session.dirty { " •" } else { "" });
if self.last_title.as_deref() != Some(title.as_str()) {
    ctx.send_viewport_cmd(egui::ViewportCommand::Title(title.clone()));
    self.last_title = Some(title);
}
```

(with `last_title: Option<String>` on `WordApp`).

## Reproduce

1. Start `wordcraft` with an empty document and leave it alone.
2. `WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 wordcraft 2>&1 | grep -c 'wl_surface#[0-9]*.commit()'` over a few seconds, or watch its CPU use: it keeps rendering frames instead of going idle.

title: Touchpad scrolling lacks smooth/inertial behavior on Wayland
author: AlexandrLatin
body:
## Description
Scrolling documents using the touchpad in Wordcraft feels noticeably worse than in other applications on the same system.
The main problem is that scrolling with the touchpad is more like discrete scrolling with a mouse wheel than like regular scrolling with a touchpad.
In particular:
- after a light swipe of the finger across the touchpad, there is no sense of inertial/impulse scrolling;
- short gestures using the touchpad stop almost immediately.
- scrolling feels less smooth and less precise than in other Wayland applications;
- the difference is especially noticeable when switching between Wordcraft and other applications, for example, browsers or native desktop applications.
- scroll sensitivity is also low
## Expected behavior
Scrolling with the touchpad should be smooth and continuous, and should also maintain the usual inertial scrolling provided by the Wayland/libinput stack.
## Actual behavior
The scrolling feels discrete and stops immediately after the fingers lift off the touchpad.
## Environment
- Wordcraft: `0.3.0-1`
- OS: Arch Linux
- Kernel: `7.2.8-arch1-2`
- Display server: Wayland
- Compositor: Hyprland `0.56.2`
- DMS: `1.6.2`
## Additional notes
Normal scrolling using the touchpad works correctly in other applications on the same system, so the problem is apparently related to the implementation of input or scrolling in Wordcraft.
If the scrolling implementation is used in Wordcraft, Gridcraft, and Deckcraft, then the problem may also occur in these applications.

title: Feature: Add touchpad pinch-to-zoom support
author: AlexandrLatin
body:
## Description
When reducing the document zoom level, Wordcraft continues to display pages in a single vertical column.
It would be useful if the layout could automatically place multiple pages side-by-side when enough horizontal space is available.
For example:
- high zoom → one page per row;
- lower zoom → two pages per row;
- very low zoom / large monitor → potentially three or more pages per row.
## Expected behavior
The page layout should make better use of available screen space instead of keeping all pages in a single narrow vertical column.
This could either be:
- automatic depending on zoom level and viewport width; or
- exposed as a layout option such as `Single page / Multiple pages`.
## Why this would be useful
Multi-page layout makes it much easier to:
- inspect the overall structure of a document;
- compare neighboring pages;
- navigate long documents;
- use large or ultrawide displays efficiently.
This would also pair naturally with touchpad pinch-to-zoom support.

title: Table grids are not visible

body:
## Problem

Table grids must be visible. In the attached file `table-grids-invisible.docx`, the table grids are not visible in Wordcraft 0.3.0.

## Steps to reproduce

The table grids are visible. In ONLYOFFICE, the borders are visible in this file.

The table grids are not visible in Wordcraft.

- The table uses table style `715`. In `word/styles.xml`, this style defines single black borders (`sz="2"`) on all sides, inside and outside.

- An empty element has no border child, so it must not override the style. The style borders must still apply.
- Wordcraft possibly reads an empty `<w:tblBorders>` or `<w:tcBorders>` as "no borders". Or it possibly does not apply the borders from the table style. This is not confirmed.

title: DOCX: absolute VML text box in header becomes inline and pushes body to page bottom (0.4.0)
author: kidtic
body:
## Summary
WordCraft 0.4.0 on Windows imports an absolutely positioned VML text box in a DOCX header as an inline object. Its full height contributes to the header flow height, pushing body text near the page bottom and inflating pagination.

Initially observed in a private real-world document: Microsoft Word displayed 4 pages, WordCraft displayed 12 with a large blank area above the body. No original document or private screenshot is included.

## Verified synthetic reproduction
Two generated DOCX fixtures contain identical 30 English body paragraphs (210 words) and a short header.
- Control, header label only: **2 pages**.
- Repro, header plus an absolutely positioned, non-wrapping 405 pt × 491.4 pt VML text box: **6 pages**.

The installed `wordcraft-cli --version` reports `0.4.0`. The first-page PNG exports confirm body text moves from the normal top margin to near the page bottom. This does not require Chinese text or fonts.

### Steps
Run the synthetic fixture generator below (Python 3 standard library), then:
```text
wordcraft-cli info header-control.docx
wordcraft-cli info header-floating-textbox.docx
wordcraft-cli render header-control.docx control.png
wordcraft-cli render header-floating-textbox.docx repro.png
```
Compare page counts and the first body paragraph position.

### Expected
An absolutely positioned, non-wrapping header text box must not add its full height to normal header flow. Both fixtures should have the same body pagination.

### Actual
Adding the box changes pagination from 2 to 6 pages and pushes the body toward the page bottom.

- `crates/docx/src/read/story.rs`, `read_vml`: reads width/height, ignores absolute position, offsets, relative anchors and wrapping; constructs the text-box shape with `Float::default()`.
- `crates/doc/src/para.rs`: `Wrap` defaults to `Inline`.
- `crates/layout/src/para.rs`: inline object height contributes to paragraph flow.

title: Crash on startup on Windows with Intel UHD Graphics (Access Violation 0xc0000005 in igvk64.dll)
author: quantavil
body:
### Description:
    On Windows with Intel UHD Graphics, WordCraft crashes immediately on launch without opening a window. The crash
  occurs when `wgpu` enumerates Vulkan physical devices, triggering an access violation inside Intel's Vulkan driver
  (`igvk64.dll`).

    ### Environment:
    - **WordCraft Version:** 0.4.0 (and 0.3.0)
    - **OS:** Windows 10/11 x64
    - **GPU:** Intel(R) UHD Graphics 630 (Driver: 31.0.101.1999)
    - **Faulting Module:** igvk64.dll (Exception: 0xc0000005, offset: 0x0000000000636952)

    ### Workaround:
    Setting `$env:WGPU_BACKEND="dx12"` bypasses Vulkan and runs WordCraft without crashes.

title: Footnote and endnote numbers are missing from the note text in Word documents
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Footnotes and endnotes from Word documents show no number in the note text: they read " First footnote text." instead of "¹ First footnote text.". The numbers in the body text are fine.

**Repro:** any `.docx` with a footnote made in Word. Its `footnotes.xml` looks like:
```xml
<w:footnote w:id="1"><w:p><w:r><w:rPr><w:rStyle w:val="FootnoteReference"/></w:rPr><w:footnoteRef/></w:r>
<w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve"> First footnote text.</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:footnote>
```

**Expected:** the note starts with its number (¹, or a, i… with a custom number format), as in Word.

**Actual:** no number in the note, on screen or in PDF export. Endnotes are the same.

**Cause:** `w:footnoteRef` / `w:endnoteRef` are never read (`read_notes` in `crates/docx/src/read/mod.rs`). Layout and the writer already expect a note to start with a reference to itself (#53), but notes read from Word files never contain one.

**Environment:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, wordcraft `main` @ d7d9702 (0.3.0).

Fix in #103.

title: Table style paragraph/run formatting is ignored: Word tables render ~60% taller
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Text in table cells ignores the table style's own paragraph and run formatting. Word's default "Table Grid" style sets `<w:spacing w:after="0" w:line="240" w:lineRule="auto"/>`, but cell text uses the document defaults instead (8 pt after, 1.08 lines). So almost every Word table renders about 60% taller than in Word and paginates differently.

**Repro:**
- A `.docx` with an 80-row "Table Grid" table, and docDefaults of `after=160 line=259` (Word's normal template).
- A custom table style `basedOn` TableGrid that adds red bold text (`rPr`).

**Expected:**
- Compact rows of about 14 pt; the 80-row table fits on 2 pages, as in Word.
- The derived style shows red bold text with borders.

**Actual:**
- Rows of about 22 pt; the table takes 3 pages.
- The derived style shows no red, no bold and no borders.

**Cause:**
- `resolve_para` / `resolve_char` (`crates/doc/src/resolve.rs`) have no table-style level, so table-style pPr/rPr are parsed but never used.
- `style_parts` (`crates/layout/src/table.rs`) takes the first style in the basedOn chain without merging in its bases.
- The reader also drops `wholeTable` and the table style's `tblPr` shading and cell margins.

**Environment:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, wordcraft `main` @ d7d9702 (0.3.0).

Fix in #104.

title: Zotero integration: cite while you write, with a Zotero tab in the ribbon
author: gledguri
body:
I've implemented Zotero integration in a local copy of WordCraft and would like to contribute it.

**What it does**
- A **Zotero** tab in the ribbon: Add/Edit Citation, Add Note, Add/Edit Bibliography, Refresh, Document Preferences, Unlink Citations.
- Talks to the running Zotero app through Zotero's published word-processor protocol (port 23116), the same one the Word and LibreOffice plugins use.
- Citations and bibliographies are stored as Word's Zotero plugin stores them (`ADDIN ZOTERO_` fields, prefs in custom document properties). Documents round-trip between WordCraft and Word with the Zotero plugin.
- Switching between an in-text style and a note style moves citations into and out of footnotes/endnotes.
- Each Zotero operation is one undo step.
- Also available headless: `wordcraft-cli zotero <command> <file>`.

**Groundwork it needed:** citation-manager `ADDIN` fields (Zotero, Mendeley, EndNote) are kept as real range fields with formatted results, including multi-paragraph bibliographies. Before, they were flattened to plain text.

**Testing:** a fake Zotero server over a real socket, hostile arguments for every protocol call, random frames (proptest), DOCX round trips, and manual checks against Zotero 10.0.6 on macOS. Docs in `docs/zotero.md`.

It's a series of focused commits; I'm happy to send it as a PR, or split it further, if you'd like it.

title: Read Aloud: player with speed control, sentence skipping, and skipping citations
author: gledguri
body:
I've improved Read Aloud in a local copy and would like to contribute it.

**What it does**
- Reads sentence by sentence using the system speech program (`say` on macOS, espeak on Linux, SAPI on Windows) on a worker thread, so it can pause, skip and change speed.
- A small floating player: previous sentence / play-pause / next sentence / stop, and a 0.5×–3× speed slider.
- The sentence being read is highlighted and the caret follows it.
- **Skip citations & bibliography** (on by default): Zotero, Mendeley, EndNote and Word citation fields aren't read out, which makes academic papers much easier to listen to.
- New commands: `readAloud.playPause/next/previous/stop/speed/skipCitations/status`. Speed and the skip setting are remembered between runs.

Happy to send a PR if you're interested.

title: AutoSave: off per document by default, with an "AutoSave all documents" option
author: gledguri
body:
**Problem:** AutoSave is always on for any document that has a file, so every edit is written straight to the original file. That's risky when you open a document just to look at it or try something out.

**What I implemented (in a local copy):**
- New and opened documents start with AutoSave **off**. The title-bar switch turns it on for that one document.
- **File › Options › AutoSave all documents** turns it on for every document you open or create, and is remembered between runs. Single documents can still opt out with the title-bar switch.
- New command `file.autosaveAll`; `file.autosave` now documents its `value` param.

This changes the default behaviour, so I wanted to check that it matches your plans before sending a PR. (Possibly related: #176.)

title: Dark mode: show the page dark with inverted colours (View › Switch Modes)
author: gledguri
body:
**Problem:** Dark mode darkens the interface but the page stays bright white, which is harsh at night.

**What I implemented (in a local copy):**
- **View › Switch Modes**, and a **File › Options › Dark page** checkbox, show the page as dark grey (80% black, `#333333`) with white text.
- Every document colour has its lightness inverted while keeping its hue, so dark-blue headings become light blue and highlights stay recognisable. Pictures are left untouched, and the caret turns white.
- Screen only: saving, printing and PDF export are unchanged.
- The setting is remembered between runs.

Happy to send a PR. (Possibly related: #115.)

title: [Bug] File › Close discards unsaved changes without a prompt
author: lpgn
body:
**Environment**
- Linux (Ubuntu 26.04), native build of main `a1caf22` with PRs #124, #125 and #178 on top. None of them change the code below.

**Steps to reproduce** (through the control port, `wordcraft --control <port>`)
1. `file.open` a `.docx` file.
2. `text.insert` some text.
3. At once (before AutoSave runs), `file.close`. This is the command of File › Close and Ctrl+W.

**Expected**
The app asks "Save changes to <name>?" with Save, Don't Save and Cancel, as Word does.

**Actual**
The app closed at once. The file on disk did not change. The inserted text was lost.

**Cause (from the code)**
- `file.close` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs`) asks the UI to close and does not look at `dirty`.
- `apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs`: `on_exit` saves only the preferences. There is no handler for the close request (egui `close_requested` with `ViewportCommand::CancelClose`).
- `file.recover` (Recover Unsaved Documents) lists only versions held in memory, so it cannot help after the app closes.

title: [Bug] AutoSave does not save .md files
author: lpgn
body:
**Environment**
- Linux (Ubuntu 26.04), native build of main `a1caf22` with PRs #124, #125 and #178 on top. None of them change the code below.

**Steps to reproduce** (through the control port, `wordcraft --control <port>`)
1. `file.open` a `.md` file. AutoSave is at its default (on).
2. `text.insert` some text.
3. Wait 8 seconds. Look at the file on disk.

**Expected**
AutoSave saves the file. Or, if this is by design (`.md` loses formatting), the AutoSave toggle is off or disabled for this file and says why.

**Actual**
After 8 s the `.md` file did not change. The same test with a `.docx` file: the file was written. `file.save` on the same `.md` file worked.

**Cause (from the code)**
- `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`: the AutoSave block calls `file.save` only when the extension is `docx`, `json`, `odt` or `rtf`. For other extensions it does nothing.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/chrome.rs`: the toggle state is `has_path && autosave`. It does not look at the extension.

Related: #176 (AutoSave in the browser build). This report is about the desktop build.

title: [Bug] Hebrew and Arabic render left-to-right; Right-to-Left Text Direction has no effect
author: lipera1337
body:
**Environment**

- macOS 15.6 (24G84), Apple silicon (arm64)
- WordCraft 0.4.0, official macOS build (`/Applications/WordCraft.app`)
- Code references checked against `main` at `a70042a`

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open a new blank document.
2. Type or paste Hebrew (`שלום עולם`) or Arabic (`مرحبا بالعالم`).
3. With the caret in that paragraph, run the `para.rtl` command — "Right-to-Left Text Direction", listed under Home › Paragraph in the feature catalog.
4. Add a line that mixes directions: `שלום WordCraft 2026`.

**Expected** (what Word does)

- The paragraph's base direction becomes RTL: text starts at the right margin, alignment and indents mirror, the paragraph mark sits at the left end.
- Inside a line the Unicode bidirectional algorithm (UAX #9) resolves runs: Hebrew/Arabic read right to left, embedded Latin and digits stay left to right, neutrals resolve from the surrounding levels.
- Caret movement, selection, Home/End and hit-testing follow the visual order.

**Actual**

- Hebrew and Arabic glyphs are placed in logical order starting at the left margin, so the words read backwards on screen (same visible symptom as #19, #63 and #211).
- `para.rtl` has no visible effect: the paragraph stays LTR and left-aligned, and the flag only survives a save/load round trip.
- Mixed Hebrew/Latin lines get no bidi resolution at all.

**Scope**

Hebrew and Arabic documents open fine in general — .docx files load, the characters and fonts come through, and `w:bidi`/`w:rtl` survive a round trip. The problem is confined to how lines are laid out and to the direction flag having no consumer.

**Cause (from the code)**

- `crates/fonts/src/lib.rs` shapes RTL correctly: `direction_runs()` splits on strong direction, `shape_dir()` sets `Direction::RightToLeft` for rustybuzz, and each run's clusters are then put back in logical order. The doc comment on `shape()` ends "line layout reorders them visually".
- That reorder never happens. `crates/layout` contains no bidi or RTL code…

title: [Bug] Windows 简体中文界面菜单显示为豆腐块（tofu），发布包未内嵌中文面 Noto Sans CJK SC
author: Bawts
body:
## 问题描述

在 Windows 上把界面语言切成简体中文后，**功能区、菜单、按钮的中文显示为方框（豆腐块）**，而**文档正文里的中文完全正常**。

同一条标签内会出现「部分字正常、部分字是方框」：例如「删除」只显示「□除」，「接受 / 拒绝」里「接受」正常、「拒绝」是方框。

## 复现步骤

1. Windows 11，运行官方发布包 WordCraft 0.4.0
2. `文件 ▸ 选项 ▸ 界面语言` 选 **简体中文**
3. 功能区 / 菜单 / 按钮的中文变成 □□□
4. 在正文输入同样的中文 → 正常显示（这条区分了问题范围）

版本标识：

```
wordcraft: WordCraft 0.4.0 (a1caf22a)
```

## 根本原因

`crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` 把 craft-fonts 的面按语言挂到界面字体族，中文界面时 `ui_cjk_fonts(true)` 返回**中文面在前**：

```rust
for f in wordcraft_fonts::ui_cjk_fonts(prefer_hans) { ... }   // 中文面优先
```

也就是说中文面只要真在二进制里，简体界面就不会出方框。问题是**发布包没有内嵌中文面的字体数据**，于是回退到日文面 `BIZ UDPGothic`，而日文面缺少简体专用汉字。

三点验证：

**1. 字体数据是否存在**（内嵌字体的 `name` 表字符串会原样出现在二进制中）：

| craft-fonts 中的面 | `Noto Sans CJK SC` name 表字符串（UTF-16BE）出现次数 |
| --- | --- |
| `BIZ UDPGothic` / `BIZ UDMincho` / `Shippori Mincho`（Jpan） | 5 / 3 / 3 ✅ 已内嵌 |
| `Noto Sans CJK SC`（Hans） | **0** ❌ 未内嵌 |

exe 里只有 1 处 `Noto Sans CJK SC` 的 ASCII 字符串，那是 `theme.rs` 里 `format!("{} {}", f.family, f.style)` 编译进去的名字字面量。而 `craft-fonts` 的 `NotoSansCJKsc-Regular.otf` 文件本身带 UTF-16BE 的这个字符串 —— 它没进二进制。

**2. 字体格式**：该 `.otf` 是 CFF 轮廓（`OTTO`），三个日文面是 TrueType（`glyf`）。扫描 exe 的 sfnt 表目录，日文面都在（`BIZ UDPGothic` @ `0x292E9A1` 等），而 **CFF/`OTTO` 表目录为 0 个**。

**3. 缺字数量对得上现象**。用 `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/zh-hans.tsv`（603 个不同汉字）统计覆盖：

| 面 | 覆盖 | 缺失 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Noto Sans CJK SC`（应有） | 600 | 3（`⌥ ➕ 📂`，非汉字） |
| `BIZ UDPGothic`（实际生效） | 446 | **157** |

缺的正是简体专用字：`页 ×64`、`选 ×28`、`标 ×26`、`样 ×24`、`线 ×24`、`图 ×24`、`编 ×20`、`删 ×19`、`单 ×18`、`题 ×18`、`显 ×17`…… 日文面认识的字用日文字形画出、不认识的变方框，与截图一致。

另外，`craft-fonts/fonts/manifest.txt` 里 `Noto Sans CJK SC | Regular | … | Hans,Latn` 那条 **2026-10-06** 就存在，v0.4.0 是 **2026-10-10** 发布，且 `release.yml` 各打包任务都设了 `CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED: "1"`（本该构建失败）。所以是**日文面进了、中文面没进**，建议查一下打包时 checkout 的 craft-fonts 版本和该 16.4 MB `.otf` 是否被丢弃。

## 修复方案

治本：让发布包正确内嵌 `Noto Sans CJK SC`。

兜底：给界面字体链补系统 CJK 字体回退，避免内嵌面缺失时直接出方框。在 `theme.rs::font_definitions()` 追加：

```rust
// 内嵌 craft-fonts 覆盖不了时，用系统 CJK 字体兜底
if let Some(name) = ins…

title: Formatting marks: ¶ drawn on top of a letter in mixed-direction paragraphs
author: vangel76
body:
With Show/Hide ¶ on, the paragraph mark lands on a letter when the paragraph's direction differs from the direction of its last characters:
- LTR paragraph containing Hebrew: ¶ is drawn over the leftmost letter instead of at the right end.
- RTL paragraph ending in Latin "abc": ¶ is drawn inside "abc" instead of at the far left.

Cause: `crates/layout/src/display.rs` (formatting marks) places the mark from `line.end_x()` — the caret position after the logically last character — and then offsets by the paragraph direction. It should go at the line's visual end for the paragraph direction (right edge of the glyphs for LTR, left edge for RTL).

Found while checking the RTL issues on current main. I'm working on this — PR follows.

title: fix(theme): System pins the native macOS window appearance
author: coygeek
body:

WordCraft resolves the first System frame correctly but then fixes the native macOS window appearance. The normal native reporting path cannot deliver later manual or scheduled OS appearance changes to the resolver. The saved automatic mode need not be corrupted for this failure to occur.

title: Program really laggy in Windows 11 (with Intel graphics card without DirectX 12 support)
body:
The 0.4.0 release is really laggy with everything in Windows 11 and Intel 4th gen graphics card. 

With this workaround and powershell (found in README.md): 
$env:WGPU_BACKEND = "GL"
it works all smooth.

Apparently the newest graphic drivers for 4th gen Intel don't support DirectX 12, which seems to be on by default in the newest release. Also Vulkan is not supported. More info in https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/support/articles/000057520/graphics.html

title: Keyboard shortcuts: add the missing common Word shortcuts
author: vangel76
body:
Gap #24 in docs/gaps.md: WordCraft has ~100 of Word's ~250 keyboard shortcuts.

Plan: go through Word's documented default shortcuts (feature names and key combinations only) and bind the missing ones to existing commands — e.g. heading styles (Ctrl+Alt+1/2/3), Normal style (Ctrl+Shift+N), Apply Styles (Ctrl+Shift+S), line spacing (Ctrl+1/2/5), paragraph spacing (Ctrl+0), indent/hanging indent (Ctrl+M/Ctrl+T and shifted), superscript/subscript, small caps, all caps, hidden, font size steps (Ctrl+[ / ], Ctrl+Shift+< / >), insert page/column/line breaks, em/en dash, ©/®/™, field shortcuts (F9, Ctrl+F9, Shift+F9, Alt+F9, Ctrl+Shift+F9), Insert Comment (Ctrl+Alt+M), Track Changes (Ctrl+Shift+E), word count (Ctrl+Shift+G), Go To (F5), Repeat (F4), extend selection (F8), and their macOS equivalents — without stealing shortcuts already in use. Shortcuts show in tooltips and command search.

title: Objects: free rotation with a rotation handle (pictures, shapes, text boxes)
author: vangel76
body:
Gap #10 in docs/gaps.md: pictures, shapes and text boxes can't be rotated freely — `arrange.rotate` only turns picture pixels by 90°, there's no rotation handle, and a DrawingML `a:xfrm rot` from Word files is ignored.

Plan: a rotation angle on drawings (read/write `a:xfrm rot` / `flipH`/`flipV`), drawn rotated on screen and in PDF, text wrapping around the rotated bounds, a rotation handle above the selection frame (Shift snaps to 15°), Rotate Right/Left 90° and Flip Vertical/Horizontal working on the angle instead of the pixels, and Size › Rotation in the Format pane/Layout dialog. Undoable.

title: Mail merge: use an Excel workbook (.xlsx) or OpenDocument spreadsheet (.ods) as the recipient list
author: vangel76
body:
Gap #21 in docs/gaps.md: Mailings › Select Recipients › Use an Existing List only accepts CSV/TSV/TXT and typed lists; Word users mostly keep recipient lists in Excel.

Plan: read .xlsx (SpreadsheetML, ECMA-376 Part 1 §18: shared strings, inline strings, numbers, booleans, dates via number formats) and .ods (ODF 1.3) sheets with the zip/XML crates already used for .docx/.odt — first row as field names, a sheet picker when there are several sheets, bounded for hostile files. Desktop picker and the web inbox accept the new extensions.

title: UI localization: translation mechanism (and Polish as a first community language?)
author: mariuszurbaniak
body:
Hi, and thanks for WordCraft!

I couldn't find any UI localization support in WordCraft (nothing in the README, `AGENTS.md` or `ROADMAP.md`). The roadmap lists "localisation" as part of item 7 of the estimate to 100%, so I understand it is planned for later.

The sibling project [CADCraft](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft) already has live language switching (English and Ukrainian) with a remembered Auto/system-language choice, and its README links `docs/localization.md`. Could WordCraft get the same mechanism, ideally reusing the CADCraft approach?

**Why it looks feasible here**
- Every action is a `CommandSpec` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/*.rs` with a label, so command labels are centralized (389 commands).
- Command ids stay English, so the CLI, MCP and control channel are unaffected by the UI language.

**Open questions**
- Where should translations live: engine (command labels) vs `ui-egui` (dialogs, menus, status text)?
- How should missing keys fall back (English)?
- Is a Polish translation (`pl`) welcome as a first community contribution once the mechanism exists? I'm happy to help with it.

**Related but separate:** spelling, grammar and hyphenation currently come from an English word list (Moby Hyphenator II per the README), so proofing in other languages would need its own work. Polish needs a Latin Extended-A capable font in the UI as well (ąćęłńóśźż).

Thanks!

title: Fields: show field codes, unlink, lock and jump between fields
author: vangel76
body:
Word's field toolbox is missing: Toggle Field Codes (Shift+F9 for the selected field, Alt+F9 for all), editing a field's code in place and updating it (F9), Unlink Fields (Ctrl+Shift+F9: replace with the result), Lock/Unlock (Ctrl+F11 / Ctrl+Shift+F11), Next/Previous Field (F11 / Shift+F11), and Ctrl+F9 inserting an empty field to type a code into. Also the right-click menu on a field (Update Field, Edit Field…, Toggle Field Codes).

Plan: a per-field and global "show code" view in layout (`{ DATE \@ "M/d/yyyy" }` drawn in place of the result, shaded like Word), editable code text that becomes the field's instruction on update, and the commands + shortcuts above, all undoable; .docx unchanged (codes already round-trip).

I'm working on this — PR follows.

title: Editing: move paragraphs, promote/demote headings, Go Back and Alt+X
author: vangel76
body:
Missing Word editing commands (found while adding shortcuts in #338):
- Move Paragraph Up/Down (Alt+Shift+Up/Down; ⌃⇧↑/↓ on Mac) — moves the selected paragraphs (or table rows) past the neighbouring paragraph, undoable.
- Promote/Demote (Alt+Shift+Left/Right) — heading level up/down (Heading n ↔ n±1, Body ↔ Heading 9), as in Outline view; also works in Print Layout.
- Go Back (Shift+F5) — returns the caret to the last few edit locations (Word keeps the last 4, including after reopening via a document variable — the in-session part is enough here).
- Alt+X — converts the hex code before the caret to its character and back (U+ toggle).

Plan: engine commands + shortcuts, tests in the typing/engine suites.

I'm working on this — PR follows.

title: Parity: Insert › Illustrations › Drawing Canvas (insert.canvas)
author: vangel76
body:
Missing parity feature from `docs/parity-checklist.md`: Insert › Illustrations › New Drawing Canvas (`insert.canvas`, also on the Draw tab).

Plan: a drawing canvas is a frame (inline or floating) that holds shapes, pictures, text boxes and ink; objects drawn or pasted while it's selected go inside it and move with it; the canvas can have fill/outline and be resized (Fit/Expand/Scale drawing). Build it on the group object model that landed in #323; save as `wpc:wpc` (word processing canvas) in .docx and read Word's canvases.

title: Layout: balance newspaper columns before a continuous section break
author: vangel76
body:
Gap #4 in docs/gaps.md (pagination differs from Word): text in multiple columns that ends at a continuous section break (or at the end of the document in Word's balancing cases) isn't balanced — the first column fills completely and the next ones stay short or empty, while Word evens the columns out.

Plan: when a multi-column section ends with a continuous section break, lay out its last page's columns balanced (minimum common column height so all content fits, respecting keep-with-next/widow-orphan and unbreakable lines), as Word does; leave next-page/even/odd breaks and explicit column breaks unbalanced, as Word does. Tests with bundled fonts.

I'm working on this — PR follows.

title: Layout: long footnotes continue onto the next page
author: vangel76
body:
Gap #4 in docs/gaps.md (pagination differs from Word): a footnote too long for the space left on its page isn't continued onto the next page as Word does (Word splits the note, continues it at the top of the next page's footnote area, and draws the continuation separator `w:continuationSeparator` above it).

Plan: allow footnote text to split across pages at line boundaries (keeping at least the reference line's page holding the note's first line, as Word does), carry the rest to the next page's footnote area before that page's own notes, draw the continuation separator (longer line) there, honour `w:continuationSeparator`/`w:continuationNotice` from the document if present. Tests with bundled fonts.

I'm working on this — PR follows.

title: Objects: Tight and Through text wrapping follow the object's outline
author: vangel76
body:
Gap #10 in docs/gaps.md (contour wrap): Tight and Through wrapping are treated like Square — text keeps clear of the bounding box instead of following the object's outline (shape geometry, or the picture's wrap polygon `wp:wrapPolygon`).

Plan: per line band, compute the free horizontal intervals from the object's wrap polygon (from `wp:wrapPolygon` when the file has one, else derived from the shape outline / the picture's non-transparent area, with the wrap distances), so text flows into concave areas; Through also lets text into interior holes between polygon edges. Round-trip `wp:wrapPolygon` (edited = false) in .docx. Works with rotated objects (#340).

I'm working on this — PR follows.

title: feat(agents): guide desktop users through CLI and MCP setup
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Help a person connect an agent to WordCraft from the desktop app, with a checked CLI invocation and usable MCP configuration.

## Problem to solve

A desktop installation does not tell the user whether an agent can find the CLI, initialize MCP, or reach the open document. macOS distributes the CLI separately. Windows and Linux package it in different locations, sometimes inside a portable or container package. Copying a bare executable name leaves those differences unresolved.

## Proposed behavior

Extend the existing File > Options Agents guidance. The [current text](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/a7c809e63bdd939b4d8349808a6012a76cd20962/crates/ui-egui/src/backstage.rs#L408-L409) already describes MCP and the control channel.

Locate CLI candidates, show the selected command and version, and allow another installation. If none works, offer a matching official platform and release download or installation route. Check the resulting command before using it. Support today's separate CLI downloads independently of improvements to desktop packaging.

Explain headless MCP as a separate session and connected MCP as access to the running app. Produce client-ready configuration or a registration command with the actual executable path or wrapper arguments. Identify the connected target and explain launch or authorization prerequisites.

Offer a local check that starts the selected command, initializes MCP, and discovers tools without editing the document. Show client registration separately through instructions or an explicit action. A successful local check cannot establish registration in an external client.

## Acceptance criteria

- For live-app setup, a bounded non-mutating request must reach the intended running app and identify the relevant document, project, session or library. Report an unavailable or wrong target, and any headless fallback, separately from local stdio readiness; initialization and tool discovery alone do not verify live-a…

title: feat(distribution): provide reliable CLI access with desktop packages
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Give desktop installations of WordCraft a documented CLI invocation that people, scripts, and agents can use on Windows, Linux, and macOS.

## Problem to solve

Including a CLI executable in a package does not always make a shell command available. Windows installs the CLI beside the app; Linux native packages install it in `/usr/bin`, while AppImage and Flatpak keep it inside their package. macOS publishes a separate CLI download. Users need a supported invocation that matches their desktop installation without guessing its location or modifying global settings.

## Proposed behavior

Provide a callable CLI with each desktop distribution or an integrated installation route where needed, and document the exact invocation outside the agent setup UI. Preserve the existing CLI commands and MCP subcommand.

For Windows MSI, document full-path invocation of the installed CLI and make any shell exposure an explicit choice. Portable ZIP users can run its included executable without a global installation. For Linux DEB/RPM, preserve the existing `/usr/bin` CLI. Provide supported AppImage and Flatpak invocation through a wrapper or command override with the required arguments. For macOS, supply a compatible CLI with the desktop distribution or through its integrated installation route so users need not manually coordinate another download.

Define update, relocation, and removal behavior for each advertised invocation. Managed launchers must not become stale or overwrite a separately installed CLI. Keep the standalone CLI download supported for users who do not want the GUI.

## Acceptance criteria

- Linux tarball users can invoke the extracted CLI using the advertised path or optional installation procedure without building from source.
- A fresh Windows MSI installation has a documented full-path command that reports its matching CLI version. A fresh portable ZIP works from its extracted directory, including paths with spaces.
- Fresh Linux DEB/RPM installatio…

title: Parity: Tools › Templates and Add-ins (tools.templates)
author: vangel76
body:
Word's Templates and Add-ins dialog is missing: see and change the document's attached template (`w:attachedTemplate` in settings.xml), "Automatically update document styles" (`w:linkStyles`) which re-applies the template's styles on open, and the Organizer to copy/delete/rename styles between the document and a template or another document.

title: Parity: Tools › Customize Ribbon (tools.customizeRibbon) and Quick Access Toolbar customization
author: vangel76
body:
Word lets users customize the ribbon and the Quick Access Toolbar; WordCraft has neither:
- **Customize Ribbon**: show/hide built-in tabs, add custom tabs and custom groups (on built-in or custom tabs) holding any commands, rename and reorder them, Reset.
- **Quick Access Toolbar**: add/remove/reorder commands (from the dialog and via right-click on any ribbon command: "Add to Quick Access Toolbar"), Reset.

Plan: a user ribbon/QAT layout in the persisted UI preferences (command ids only; unknown ids ignored), applied when building the ribbon; `tools.customizeRibbon` opens a two-list dialog (commands ↔ ribbon tree / QAT list) next to the Customize Keyboard entry from #368/#378. Engine/agent side: the commands stay as they are; the layout is UI state.

I'm working on this (vangel76); PR follows (builds on #378).

title: Parity: Developer › Controls — content controls (w:sdt): keep, show and edit
author: vangel76
body:
Content controls (`w:sdt`, ECMA-376 §17.5.2) are unwrapped on open today (gap #5 in docs/gaps.md), so forms and templates lose their fields on a round trip.

Plan:
- Model: inline/block content controls with their properties (tag, title/alias, id, lock, placeholder, showing placeholder) and type: Rich Text, Plain Text, Check Box (`w14:checkbox`), Combo Box, Drop-Down List, Date Picker, Picture, Building Block Gallery, Repeating Section (keep).
- DOCX read/write round trip (unknown types kept as rich text with their properties).
- Layout: the control's content laid out inline; bounding box / title tab shown when the caret is inside (Design Mode shows tags).
- Editing: typing replaces placeholder text; check box toggles on click; drop-down/combo/date open a picker; locked controls refuse edits/deletion.
- Commands + Developer tab › Controls group (insert each type, Design Mode, Properties dialog); headless params for agents.
- Tests: round trip, placeholder replacement, check box toggle, lock behaviour.

Formatting revisions (#41) are not part of this.

I'm working on this (vangel76); PR follows.

title: Parity: References › Citations & Bibliography — more citation styles
author: vangel76
body:
WordCraft formats citations and bibliographies in 4 of Word's 12 built-in styles (APA, MLA, Chicago, IEEE). Missing: Harvard – Anglia, ISO 690 (author-date and numerical reference), Turabian, GB/T 7714, GOST (name and title sort), SIST02, Association for Computing Machinery-like numbered (as "ACM" only if it fits), plus APA 7th edition details where ours differ.

Plan: table-driven style definitions in `crates/engine/src/cmd/citations.rs` (citation form, bibliography entry per source type, sort order, numbering), the style picker lists them all, `w:bibliography`/`CITATION` field switches keep working; one test per style family (author-date vs numbered, sort order). Formats come from the published style guides, written in our own code.

Doesn't overlap #169 (bibliography sources round-trip) beyond touching the same file.

I'm working on this (vangel76); PR follows.

title: Parity: References › Footnotes — Footnote and Endnote dialog, options per section
author: vangel76
body:
Footnote/endnote options are only partly kept (document-wide number format). Word's Footnote and Endnote dialog sets per section: location (bottom of page / below text; end of section / end of document), number format, custom mark, start at, numbering (continuous / restart each section / restart each page), apply to whole document or this section, and Convert (footnotes ↔ endnotes).

Plan: `w:footnotePr`/`w:endnotePr` in `sectPr` and settings (pos, numFmt, numStart, numRestart) in the model and DOCX round trip (ECMA-376 §17.11); layout/numbering honours restart per section/page and position below text / end of section; commands (`references.noteOptions`, `references.convertNotes`) + the dialog (References › Footnotes launcher). Tests: round trip, restart-per-page numbering, end-of-section endnotes, convert.

Builds on #361 (note separators). I'm working on this (vangel76); PR follows.

title: Parity: Review › Accessibility — Alt Text pane for all objects, decorative flag, checker depth
author: vangel76
body:
Accessibility is at ~35% (docs/target-app-parity.md). Alt text exists for pictures only (`picture.altText`), and the checker knows a few rules.

Plan:
- Alt Text pane (Review › Check Accessibility › Alt Text, right-click › View Alt Text) for pictures, shapes, text boxes, groups/canvas, charts/OLE and tables; "Mark as decorative" (`adec:decorative` ext in `wp:docPr`, ECMA-376 + [MS-ODRAWXML]); table alt text (`w:tblCaption`/`w:tblDescription`).
- DOCX round trip for all of these.
- Accessibility checker: more rules (missing alt text on shapes/tables, heading levels skipped, table without header row, blank table rows/cells used for layout, low text contrast, floating objects (reading order), repeated blank paragraphs for spacing, merged cells) with a "Fix" action where one exists; pane lists errors/warnings/tips with jump-to.
- Screen-reader (AccessKit) node tree for the document canvas: at least paragraphs as text nodes with role/heading level and the caret/selection exposed — and tests that read the tree (#18), if feasible in egui's AccessKit integration.

I'm working on this (vangel76); PR follows.

title: Parity: Layout › Page Setup › Document Grid (w:docGrid) and East Asian line-break options
author: vangel76
body:
East Asian typography is at ~15% (docs/target-app-parity.md). Missing: the document grid that fixes lines per page and characters per line, which Chinese/Japanese/Korean documents rely on for their page look.

Plan:
- Model + DOCX round trip of `w:docGrid` in `sectPr` (`type` default/lines/linesAndChars/snapToChars, `linePitch`, `charSpace`; ECMA-376 §17.6.5) and the paragraph `w:snapToGrid` / run `w:snapToGrid` flags.
- Layout: with a lines grid, each line's height snaps to a multiple of the line pitch (paragraphs with snapToGrid on); with linesAndChars/snapToChars, East Asian characters are placed on the character pitch.
- Page Setup › Document Grid tab: no grid / lines only / lines and characters / text snaps to characters, characters per line and lines per page (pitches computed from the page size), View gridlines option draws the grid.
- Asian Typography paragraph options (kinsoku, word wrap, hanging punctuation, auto-space East Asian/Latin and digits) already round-trip; make the layout honour kinsoku line-start/line-end rules if not already, and expose the options in the Paragraph dialog.
- Tests: round trip, lines-per-page count, character pitch placement (font-independent assertions).

I'm working on this (vangel76); PR follows.

title: Parity: Draw — Lasso Select, Add Pen, Ink to Shape, Ink Replay (draw.lasso, draw.addPen, draw.inkToShape, draw.replay)
author: vangel76
body:
Follow-up to the Draw tab (#307/#315, now merged). Missing from Draw:
- **Lasso Select**: draw a free loop to select the ink strokes (and objects) inside it; move/delete/recolour the selection.
- **Add Pen**: add a custom pen (pen/pencil/highlighter type, colour, thickness) to the pen gallery; remembered between runs; remove/reorder pens.
- **Ink to Shape**: convert recognisable strokes to shapes (line, arrow, rectangle/square, ellipse/circle, triangle, polygon) — a geometric fit in our own code, toggle mode converts strokes as they are drawn.
- **Ink Replay**: replay the strokes in the order they were drawn (play/pause/rewind/forward), from per-stroke timestamps (kept in the InkML trace when present).

Ink to Math needs handwriting recognition and stays out of scope.

I'm working on this (vangel76); PR follows.

title: Parity: Review › Track Changes — move tracking (w:moveFrom / w:moveTo)
author: vangel76
body:
Moved text is read as a plain insertion/deletion today (`w:moveTo` → insert, `w:moveFrom` → delete) and saved that way, so Word's move markup (double strikethrough/underline in green, "Moved (insertion)" / "Moved from" balloons) and the link between source and destination are lost (rest of gap #5 in docs/gaps.md).

Plan:
- Model: move revisions with a shared move name linking source and destination; `w:moveFromRangeStart/End` / `w:moveToRangeStart/End` round-trip (ECMA-376 §17.13.5.22–27).
- Recording: with Track Changes on, cut + paste / drag-and-drop of whole paragraphs or a sentence within the document records a move (as Word does when the moved text is a sentence or more), otherwise insert/delete as now.
- Markup per Track Changes Options (moves colour/marks), Reviewing Pane "Moved" entries; Accept/Reject on either end accepts/rejects both.
- Tests: round trip, recording a paragraph move, accept/reject both ends.

Builds on #399 (formatting revisions). I'm working on this (vangel76); PR follows.

title: Dialog depth: References dialogs — Caption, Index, Table of Contents, Create Source
author: vangel76
body:
Gap #7 (dialog depth): the References tab runs its commands with defaults, but Word's dialogs behind them are missing:
- **Caption**: label (Figure/Table/Equation + New Label/Delete Label), position (above/below), exclude label, Numbering… (format, include chapter number with heading level and separator), AutoCaption is out of scope.
- **Index**: type (indented/run-in), columns, language, right-align page numbers, tab leader, formats, Mark Entry… (main/sub entry, cross-reference, current page/page range bookmark, bold/italic page numbers), Mark All.
- **Table of Contents** (Custom Table of Contents…): show page numbers, right-align, tab leader, use hyperlinks, formats, show levels, Options… (build from styles with levels, outline levels, TC fields), Modify… styles.
- **Create Source / Edit Source** for citations: source type with its fields, "show all bibliography fields".

Plan: each dialog drives the existing engine commands (extending their params where needed), so agents keep the same headless commands; field switches written as Word does (`TOC \o \h \z \u`, `INDEX \c \e`, `SEQ \* ARABIC \s`…). Tests per dialog flow + field-code output.

I'm working on this (vangel76); PR follows.

title: Feature Request: Extensible Plugin System for WordCraft
author: ckstc
body:
**Summary**
I would like to propose adding an extensible plugin system to WordCraft, allowing third-party developers to build custom features without modifying the core codebase.
A well-designed plugin API would make it easier for developers to extend its functionality for specialized workflows, while keeping the core application maintainable.
**Proposed Capabilities**
1. Custom Commands and Actions
Allow plugins to register custom commands that can be invoked through the application, keyboard shortcuts, menus, or toolbars.
For example:
Register a command to format selected text.
Add a command to compare two documents.
Provide custom document-processing actions.
2. UI Extensions
Provide APIs for plugins to add UI elements, such as:
Custom toolbar or ribbon buttons.
Menu items and context-menu actions.
Panels or sidebars.
Settings pages.
Plugins should be able to integrate with the existing UI without directly modifying the core UI implementation.
3. Document API
Expose a stable, documented API for interacting with documents, including:
Reading and modifying document content.
Accessing the current selection and cursor position.
Applying formatting and styles.
Inserting, deleting, or replacing text.
Integrating with the undo/redo system where appropriate.
Ideally, plugin-driven document changes should use the same editing commands and document model as native operations, rather than manipulating internal data structures directly.
4. Plugin Lifecycle and Permissions
Provide a clear plugin lifecycle, including discovery, loading, activation, deactivation, and error handling.
For security and reliability, the system should also consider plugin permissions, API boundaries, and isolation between third-party code and the core application.
5. Developer Experience and API Stability
Provide:
A documented plugin API and example plugins.
A manifest format describing plugin metadata, version requirements, and permissions.
A mechanism for checking compatibility between plugins and…

title: Dialog depth: Layout and Review dialogs — Line Numbers, Hyphenation, Language, Envelopes, Labels
author: vangel76
body:
Gap #7 (dialog depth): these commands exist but run with defaults or a menu only; Word's dialogs behind them are missing:
- **Line Numbers** (Line Numbering Options…): start at, from text, count by, restart each page/section/continuous (`w:lnNumType`).
- **Hyphenation** (Hyphenation Options…): automatic, hyphenate words in CAPS, hyphenation zone, limit consecutive hyphens, Manual… (step through suggested breaks).
- **Language** (Set Proofing Language…): language list for the selection, do not check spelling/grammar, detect language automatically, Set As Default.
- **Envelopes** and **Labels** (Mailings › Create): delivery/return address, envelope size and options, label product/size, full page of the same label / single label → create document.

title: fix(paste): regular Paste leaves tracked paragraph breaks after Reject All
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Regular Paste introduces a paragraph break that Reject All does not remove when Track Changes is enabled. In a paragraph containing `AB`, pasting `X` and `Y` as separate paragraphs between the letters and then rejecting all changes leaves two paragraphs, `A` and `B`. The rejected structural edit also remains in the saved DOCX.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the native CLI described under Runtime or environment. The following executed sequence starts with a fresh blank document and uses only synthetic text. Inspect the paragraph entries printed by each `document.inspect` command.

```sh
wordcraft-cli run --print \
  --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"AB","raw":true}' \
  --cmd 'caret.set={"pos":{"block":0,"off":1}}' \
  --cmd 'review.trackChanges={"value":true}' \
  --cmd 'edit.paste={"text":"X\nY"}' \

title: fix(paragraph): Center changes the paragraph beyond the selection endpoint
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Center applies to an extra paragraph when a nonempty selection ends at that paragraph's start. Select Paragraph produces this range for a paragraph followed by another paragraph, so centering the selected paragraph also changes its unselected neighbor. The failure was observed with two plain body paragraphs and with explicit ranges in either direction.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the CLI build described under Runtime or environment. Each invocation below starts a fresh blank document and uses synthetic text. These commands were executed.

```sh
wordcraft-cli run --print \
  --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"Alpha\rBeta","raw":true}' \
  --cmd 'caret.set={"pos":{"block":0,"off":2}}' \
  --cmd 'select.paragraph={}' \
  --cmd 'edit.copy={}' \
  --cmd 'para.alignCenter={}' \
  --cmd 'document.inspect={}'
```

Compare with the executed text-only selection control:

```sh

title: fix(replace): Replace All keeps paragraph separators inside one paragraph
author: coygeek
body:

title: fix(equations): removing equation numbers deletes later rows
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Turning off equation numbering on a supported two-row equation leaves only the first row's content. The command succeeds without warning, and saving and reopening a DOCX preserves the missing second row. The failure also occurs when only the second row has a number.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the CLI build identified under Runtime or environment. In an empty working directory, run this sequence to inspect the equation, remove its numbers, observe Undo, and save the destructive result again:

```sh
wordcraft-cli run --template blank --print \
  --cmd 'insert.equation={"linear":"█(a#(1)@b#(2))"}' \
  --cmd equation.get \
  --cmd 'equation.number={"value":false}' \
  --cmd equation.get \
  --cmd edit.undo \
  --cmd equation.get \
  --cmd 'equation.number={"value":false}' \
  --save removed.docx
wordcraft-cli run --file removed.docx --print \
  --cmd caret.docEnd \
  --cmd equation.get
```

Repeat the number-removal sequence with the input `█(a@b#(2))` to check a number confined to the later row. For controls, use `a#(1)` and `█(a@b)`. To check the available replacement workaround, insert the original numbered array, run `equation.set={"linear":"█(a@b)"}`, save it, and reopen it with the same inspection commands. These inputs and operations were executed independently.

## Expected behavior

Removing equation numbers should retain both equations in their original order and two-row structure. The resulting unnumbered array should contain `a` and `b`, with neither number marker. title: fix(layout): long endnotes lose readable content beyond the final PDF page
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

A single endnote created with ordinary editing commands can retain all its text in DOCX while producing an incomplete PDF. With 80 short paragraphs on Letter paper, WordCraft places the entire note on the second page instead of adding continuation pages. The later paragraphs fall outside that physical page. This affects sharing a document as PDF; the saved source still contains the complete note.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the baseline under Runtime or environment with `wordcraft-cli` and Poppler's `pdftotext` on PATH. Run the following Python script in an empty disposable directory. It creates one long endnote, a short endnote control and a body-text control through public commands, saves each as DOCX, reopens it for JSON inspection and exports it as PDF. Every child process has a 60-second timeout.

```sh
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
import pathlib
import re
import subprocess

cli, directory = "wordcraft-cli", "endnote-repro"
root = pathlib.Path(directory)
root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

def run(args):
    result = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    if result.returncode:
        raise RuntimeError(result.stderr)
    return result.stdout

for name, count, note in [('long-endnote', 80, True),
                          ('short-endnote', 3, True),
                          ('body-control', 80, False)]:
    commands = ['layout.size=' + json.dumps({'name': 'Letter'}),
                'layout.margins=' + json.dumps({'top': 72, 'bottom': 72, 'left': 72, 'right': 72})]
    if note:
        commands += ['text.insert=' + json.dumps({'text': 'Body reference '}),
                     'references.endnote=' + json.dumps({'text': 'Endnote line 1'})]
