title: Question: should AutoCorrect be off by default in headless runs?
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
AutoCorrect runs in `wordcraft-cli run`. A script that types a lowercase word at the start of a paragraph gets it capitalised once the paragraph ends:

```sh
wordcraft-cli run --template blank --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"x"}' --cmd text.newParagraph --save a.docx
wordcraft-cli text a.docx    # X
```

Without the `text.newParagraph`, it stays `x`.

The text a script passes is usually the text it wants saved. We now start every run with `tools.autocorrect={"enabled":false}`, but it took a format audit of the output to notice.

Would you take one of these?

1. AutoCorrect off by default in `run` and headless MCP, with `tools.autocorrect={"enabled":true}` to turn it on.
2. A `--no-autocorrect` flag on `run`.
3. Keep the current behaviour and document it in `docs/mcp.md`.

We can send a PR for whichever you prefer.

title: Tables: AutoFit in a nested table, whole-cell shading for selections through a table, Shift+Right at a cell's end
author: rabis7575

Three small follow-ups to the table mouse and selection work (#637, #722):

1. **AutoFit by double-clicking a column border in a nested table** — `table_mouse::fit_column` lets the table widen up to the page's right margin. A table nested in a cell should stay inside the outer cell's text area instead.

title: No CI on most pull requests: `cargo xtask ci` isn't enforced, and releases ship without running tests
author: Higgs32584
body:
## Summary

Most pull requests to WordCraft run no automated checks. The project's quality gate, `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, assets, layers, wasm), is documented in `AGENTS.md` as something to run before every commit, but nothing runs it on GitHub. The release pipeline also builds, signs and publishes without running the test suite first.

## Current state

The existing workflows are all either path-filtered, scheduled, or tied to the `release` branch:

| Workflow | Runs on PRs? | What it checks |
|---|---|---|
| `printing.yml` | Only if `Cargo*`, `apps/wordcraft/**`, `apps/wordcraft-web/**` or `crates/ui-egui/**` change | fmt, plus clippy and tests for `wordcraft` and `wordcraft-ui-egui` only; wasm check of `wordcraft-web` |
| `packaging-lint.yml` | Only if `.github/workflows/**`, `packaging/**` or `assets/app-icon/**` change | Workflow syntax, packaging scripts, Linux metadata |
| `freebsd.yml` | Only if `crates/fonts/**`, its own file or `packaging/env.sh` change; otherwise nightly and on `release` | Full build and tests on FreeBSD |
| `windows-arm64.yml` | Only if its own file or `packaging/windows/**` change; otherwise nightly and on `release` | ARM64 MSI packaging and install |
| `release.yml` | No (push to `release`) | Builds, signs and publishes all platforms |

As a result, a PR that only touches crates such as `doc`, `docx`, `docbin`, `layout`, `engine`, `render`, `pdf`, `formats`, `mcp`, `apps/wordcraft-cli` or `xtask` matches no trigger and shows **no checks at all**. title: Ruler: tab stops can't be set, moved or cleared with the pointer; Tabs dialog loses un-Set alignment changes
author: iot-root
body:
Editing tab stops is harder than it should be, in both places they live:

**On the ruler** (Word parity gaps — `docs/ui-parity.md` Rulers row):
- There is no tab-type selector in the rulers' corner, so there's no way to choose what a click would set.
- Clicking the ruler doesn't set a stop, dragging a marker doesn't move it, and dragging it off doesn't clear it — the only interaction is double-click, which opens the Tabs dialog (#320).
- Every marker draws with the same left-tab shape, whatever its alignment.

**In the Tabs dialog** (#320):
- Selecting a stop in the list, changing Alignment or Leader and pressing OK silently discards the change unless Set is pressed first — reproducing Word's least-loved dialog behaviour, and inconsistent with the dialog's own rule of setting a typed-but-not-Set position on OK.
- Adding a stop at a position effectively requires leaving the dialog for the ruler, since the dialog preselects the first stop and the typed-position-on-OK rule only applied with nothing selected.

Repro for the dialog data loss: a paragraph with a stop → double-click its ruler marker → select it in the list → pick Center → OK → the stop is still Left.

title: CLI: render silently accepts invalid or duplicate page and scale options
author: NavidZamanKhan
body:
### Summary
In `wordcraft-cli`, passing malformed, missing, duplicate, or out-of-range values for `--page` or `--scale` does not return an error or exit non-zero:
- **Malformed or missing values** (e.g. `--page banana`, `--scale banana`, `--page` without a value, `--page -1`): parsing via `.ok().unwrap_or(...)` fails silently and the command falls back to default values (Page 1 and Scale 2.0), returning exit code 0 and writing a full-sized 1224x1584 PNG.
- **Non-positive scales** (e.g. `--scale 0` or `--scale -2`): the CLI parses the float and passes it to the engine command `file.exportPng`, which clamps the scale to `0.1`, silently outputting an 80x62 pixel thumbnail PNG with exit code 0 rather than reporting an invalid scale.
- **Duplicate options** (e.g. `--page 1 --page 2` or `--scale 1 --scale 2`): the CLI silently accepts the first occurrence and ignores subsequent ones without error.

Both `wordcraft-cli render` and `wordcraft-cli run --save output.png` exhibit these behaviors.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. `wordcraft-cli render document.docx out.png --page banana`
   - Exit code: `0`
   - Stderr: *(empty)*
   - Output: `out.png` created (Page 1 at 2.0x, 1224x1584)
2. `wordcraft-cli render document.docx out.png --page`
   - Exit code: `0`
   - Stderr: *(empty)*
   - Output: `out.png` created (Page 1 at 2.0x, 1224x1584)
3. `wordcraft-cli render document.docx out.png --scale 0`
   - Exit code: `0`
   - Stderr: *(empty)*
   - Output: `out.png` created (Page 1 clamped to 0.1x scale, 80x62)
4. `wordcraft-cli render document.docx out.png --page 1 --page 2`
   - Exit code: `0`
   - Stderr: *(empty)*
   - Output: `out.png` created (silently uses Page 1)
5. `wordcraft-cli run --template sample --save out.png --scale banana`
   - Exit code: `0`
   - Stderr: `wrote out.png`
   - Output: `out.png` created (default 2.0x PNG)

title: Flaky test: native print PDFs differ by their creation time
author: dkhlapov
body:
`native_ranges_and_parity_do_not_duplicate_spooler_copies` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/native_print.rs` can fail when a clock second ticks over during the test. It failed on **Print (macos-latest)** for #882 (run 38273500467), while Ubuntu and Windows passed. The same job passes on other PRs.

**Cause:** the test builds the expected PDF with `session.print_pdf(...)`, then submits the job, which builds the PDF again. With no creation date in the document properties, `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs` stamps each PDF with the current time (`now_unix()`). The two PDFs in the failed run are the same length (8092 bytes) and differ only in `CreationDate`/`ModDate` (`D:20261012160849Z` vs `D:20261012160850Z`) and the values derived from them.

**Fix:** give the test document a fixed creation date before printing, so both PDFs carry the same timestamp, for example setting the core properties' `created` to `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`. Alternatively, compare the PDFs with the date fields masked.

title: Saving replaces Office 2016 charts (cx:chart) with their fallback pictures and drops the chart data
author: Mart95Dev
body:
## Summary

Opening and re-saving a .docx that contains Office 2016 charts (`cx:chart`: box & whisker, sunburst…) **replaces each chart with its fallback picture**. The `mc:Choice` branch (the chart) is dropped, together with its `chartN.xml` part and its embedded workbook, and only the `mc:Fallback` picture is written. After one save in WordCraft, the document has static images where Word had editable charts, and the chart data is gone from the package.

WordCraft draws these charts correctly on screen and in PDF export (the box & whisker and the sunburst both render). The loss only happens on save.

## Reproduction

File: Apache POI test data `test-data/document/chartex.docx` (https://github.com/apache/poi/blob/trunk/test-data/document/chartex.docx). It has 6 charts: bar, line, radar, box & whisker (cx), stock and sunburst (cx).

```
wordcraft-cli run --file chartex.docx --save roundtrip.docx
```

Package parts, before → after:

| Part                                         | Original | After save |
|----------------------------------------------|----------|------------|
| `word/charts/chart4.xml` (box & whisker, cx) | ✓        | ✗          |
| `word/charts/chart6.xml` (sunburst, cx)      | ✓        | ✗          |
| `word/embeddings/Microsoft_Excel_Worksheet3.xlsx` | ✓   | ✗          |
| `word/embeddings/Microsoft_Excel_Worksheet5.xlsx` | ✓   | ✗          |
| `word/media/image1.png`, `image2.png` (fallbacks) | ✓   | ✓          |

In `document.xml`, `wp:docPr name="Chart 4"` and `"Chart 6"` become `"Picture 4"` and `"Picture 6"`. The `mc:AlternateContent` wrapper is gone and only the `pic:pic` from `mc:Fallback` remains. The classic charts (`c:chart`: bar, line, radar, stock) survive.

## Expected

Charts that WordCraft can't edit are written back unchanged (the whole `mc:AlternateContent`, the chart parts, their relationships and embeddings), the way the original `c:chart` charts already are. This fits the "charts from Word stay read-only" note in `docs/gaps.md`.…

title: Radar and stock charts render as blank space, with no placeholder or warning
author: Mart95Dev
body:
## Summary

Radar (`c:radarChart`) and stock (`c:stockChart`) charts from Word are drawn as **empty space**: no frame, no title, no placeholder, and no warning from `convert`, `info` or the UI. Converting a report to PDF silently drops these charts. LibreOffice renders both from the same file.

`unsupported_chart_types_draw_nothing` in `crates/docx/src/read/chart.rs` makes this explicit, and `docs/gaps.md` lists radar and stock charts as missing. So the missing chart types themselves are known. This issue is about the silent result.

## Reproduction

File: Apache POI test data `test-data/document/chartex.docx` (https://github.com/apache/poi/blob/trunk/test-data/document/chartex.docx). Chart 3 is a radar chart ("This is a radar chart") and chart 5 is a stock chart ("This is a stock chart").

```
wordcraft-cli convert chartex.docx out.pdf     # exit 0, no warning
```

Page 2 of `out.pdf` has a blank area where the radar chart is. Page 3 has a blank area where the stock chart is. In LibreOffice's PDF of the same file, both charts are there with their titles, axes and legends. The text in the PDF reflects this: about 58 words for WordCraft against 113 for LibreOffice.

## Suggestion

Until these types are drawn:

1. Draw a placeholder in the chart's frame: a light border, the chart title if there is one, and "Radar chart (not supported yet)".
2. Add an import note, the way PdfCraft and VectorCraft report what didn't come in: "2 charts of a type WordCraft can't draw yet (radar, stock)", shown in the status bar or notices and printed by `convert`/`info`.
3. Optionally, a rough renderer for the classic types, since `c:radarChart` and `c:stockChart` are plain `c:ser` data with categories, like the line charts that already work.

## Environment

WordCraft `159b84f` (main), built from source with `cargo build --release` (Rust 1.95.0), macOS on Apple Silicon. Reference rendering: LibreOffice headless `--convert-to pdf`.

title: Page background picture/texture fill is not drawn, and is removed on save
author: Mart95Dev
body:
## Summary

A page background that uses a **picture or texture fill** (Design › Page Color › Fill Effects › Texture/Picture) is ignored when drawing: only the fallback `w:color` is painted. The texture image is also **removed from the package on save**, so a document round-tripped through WordCraft permanently loses its page texture.

## Reproduction

The document starts with:

```xml
<w:background w:color="FFFFCC">
  <v:background id="_x0000_s1025" o:bwmode="white" fillcolor="#ffc">
    <v:fill r:id="rId2" o:title="Пергамент" type="tile"/>
  </v:background>
</w:background>
```

`rId2` → `word/media/image1.jpeg`, Word's "Parchment" texture tiled across the page. The file is a real-world Russian library calendar from Apache POI's test data: `test-data/document/bib-chernigovka.netdo.ru_download_docs_17459.docx` (https://github.com/apache/poi/blob/trunk/test-data/document/bib-chernigovka.netdo.ru_download_docs_17459.docx).

1. `wordcraft-cli convert file.docx out.pdf`: the page is flat `#FFFFCC`. LibreOffice draws the tiled parchment texture.
2. `wordcraft-cli run --file file.docx --save roundtrip.docx`: `word/media/image1.jpeg` and the `v:background`/`v:fill` are no longer in the saved package.

`crates/docx/src/read/mod.rs` (around line 228) only reads `w:background/@w:color`.

## Expected

- Drawing: tile the `v:fill` picture when `type="tile"`, and stretch it for `type="frame"`, in Print Layout and PDF export, consistent with how the page color is handled today.
- Saving: write the `v:background` and its image relationship back even while the fill isn't drawn, so the texture survives a round trip.

(Unrelated detail from the same file: its title uses `w14` text effects, an orange gradient fill with an outline and a shadow, and WordCraft renders them where LibreOffice doesn't. Nice!)

## Environment

WordCraft `159b84f` (main), built from source with `cargo build --release` (Rust 1.95.0), macOS on Apple Silicon. Reference rendering: LibreOffice headless.

title: Require a test, or a stated reason for none, in every pull request
author: Higgs32584
body:
## Summary

Every pull request should either add or change a test, or say in one line why it
doesn't need one. Today that is required only for some kinds of change.

## Current state

The suite has 1,927 test functions across 19 crates. `CLAUDE.md` requires tests in
three cases:

- crash fixes (a regression test)
- typing behaviour changes (a test in `crates/engine/src/tests_typing.rs`)
- new commands (a `CommandSpec` plus tests)

Nothing covers other bug fixes, file format changes or layout changes. There is no
pull request template and no `CONTRIBUTING.md`, so a reviewer has no prompt to ask
where the test is.

## Proposed rule

A pull request that changes behaviour comes with a test that pins the change.

| Change | Test required |
|---|---|
| Bug fix | A test that fails before the fix and passes after |
| New command or feature | Tests for the command (already the rule) |
| File format read/write | A round-trip or fixture test |
| Layout | A test for the specific case being changed |

These are exempt, and say so in the description:

- pure refactors, where the existing tests passing unchanged is the proof
- docs, CI config, dependency bumps, renames, formatting
- visual-only UI changes, where a screenshot comparison is the evidence

An exempt pull request carries one line, for example:
`Tests: none — refactor, covered by existing layout tests.`

## Why not "every pull request adds tests"

A blanket rule gets met with filler: tests that restate what the code obviously
does, or that lock in implementation details. Those slow the suite and make
refactors harder without catching bugs. The aim is that each risky behaviour is
pinned, not that the count goes up.

## Work

- [ ] Add the rule to the Quality gates section of `CLAUDE.md` and to `AGENTS.md`
- [ ] Add `.github/pull_request_template.md` with a `Tests:` line to fill in
- [ ] Decide whether CI should fail a pull request that touches `crates/*/src`
      with no test change and no `Tests:` line (optional; the t…

title: [ui] Equation elements have mismatched and errant background colors

title: DOCX: a hyperlink with an empty target (LibreOffice export) is read as a link, so every run shows "Ctrl+Click to follow link"
author: python2121
body:
## Summary

A `w:hyperlink` whose relationship has an **empty `Target`** is read as a link with an empty URL instead of no link. Every run inside it then shows the "Ctrl+Click to follow link" tooltip when hovered, with a blank line where the address would be. LibreOffice writes such hyperlinks when a document's runs carry the Hyperlink character style without an address, so a .docx that has been through LibreOffice can arrive with **every word in it wrapped in an empty hyperlink**, and the tooltip follows the pointer across the whole page.

The text looks normal (the runs carry direct colour/underline overrides), nothing is underlined or blue, and the document has one real link, so from the user's side it reads as "WordCraft shows a link tooltip on all text".

The writer already drops empty links on save (`crates/docx/src/write/story.rs:299` filters `!l.is_empty()`), so the reader and writer currently disagree about what an empty target means.

## Reproduction

A real-world case was a two-page résumé saved by LibreOffice 26.8.1.1 (`docProps/app.xml`): 78 `<w:hyperlink r:id="…">` elements over 92 runs, with 77 of the relationships `Target=""` and one `mailto:`.

Minimal package: one paragraph, two hyperlinks, one empty target.

<Relationship Id="rId3" Type="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/hyperlink" Target="mailto:someone@example.com" TargetMode="External"/>
```

title: Down arrow from the start of the line above a table skips the table
author: rabis7575
body:
**Bug:** Down (and Shift+Down) from the start of the line directly above a table skips the whole table: the caret lands in the paragraph after it. From the middle of the same line it goes into the first cell, as it should. Up from the start of the paragraph after a table skips it the same way.

Reproduce with the CLI:

```
wordcraft-cli run --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"Intro line"}' --cmd 'text.newParagraph' --cmd 'insert.table={"rows":3,"cols":3}' --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"a"}' --cmd 'caret.docStart' --cmd 'caret.down' --print
```

The focus ends at `[2]` (after the table) instead of `[1,0,0,0]`.

**Cause:** `DocLayout::vertical` takes the nearest line below whose horizontal extent covers the caret's x. At the left margin no cell line does: a cell's text starts a cell margin in from the table's edge. So the next line that covers it, the paragraph after the table, wins. The same happens when the caret's x falls in the gap between two cells' text, or left of an indented table.

**Fix:** lines between the caret's paragraph and that line in document order (a table row) come first. The caret goes to the cell under its x, or the nearest one. Another cell of the caret's own row doesn't count, so Down inside a table still goes to the cell below. A test goes in `tests_typing.rs` and `docs/typing-parity.md`.

I'm working on this; a PR will follow.

title: Markdown table round-trip moves or drops content in code-span cells
author: NavidZamanKhan
body:
### Summary

When exporting Markdown tables containing inline code spans with literal pipe characters (`|`) or literal backticks, WordCraft emits output without the required GFM backslash escaping (`\|`).

During import, WordCraft's `split_row` parser naively toggles an `in_code: bool` flag on every single backtick character (`'`), desynchronizing on multi-backtick delimiters or inline code containing backticks.

Consequently, an export/import round trip or importing GFM tables containing code spans with pipes or backticks causes cell boundaries to be miscalculated:
1. **Misplaced / shifted cell content**: Text in subsequent columns shifts into earlier cells.
2. **Discarded cell content**: Columns past the expected header count are truncated and discarded, or cells are overwritten with empty content.

---

### Observed Behavior & Reproduction

#### Case 1: Cell Content Shifts and Disappears in Round Trip

Consider a table with two cells in a row:
- **Cell A**: Code-formatted text containing a literal backtick and pipe: ``a`b|c``
- **Cell B**: Distinctive text `CRITICAL_DISTINCTIVE_INFO`

**Exported Markdown (`export` / `table_md`):**
WordCraft exports the row without escaping the pipe:
```markdown
| Col A | Col B |
| --- | --- |
| ``a`b|c`` | CRITICAL_DISTINCTIVE_INFO |
```

**Import Behavior (`import` / `split_row`):**
During `split_row`, the five backticks in ``a`b|c`` toggle `in_code` as follows:
- Backticks 1 & 2: `in_code: true -> false`
- Backtick 3 (inside `a`b`): `in_code: true`
- Backticks 4 & 5: `in_code: false -> true`
- When reaching the delimiter `|`, `in_code` is `true`, so `split_row` fails to recognize the delimiter and merges the rest of the line into Cell A.
- Because the header has 2 columns, Cell B is filled with an empty string and `CRITICAL_DISTINCTIVE_INFO` is completely removed from its cell.

**Document Model After Round Trip:**
- Original:
  - Cell A: `Inline::Text("a`b|c", code: true)`
  - Cell B: `Inline::Text("CRITICAL_DISTINCTIVE_INFO",…

title: Accessibility: expose ribbon tabs and Alt/F10 KeyTips to screen readers
author: keyang556
body:
WordCraft v0.6.1 provides keyboard-based ribbon navigation through Alt/F10 KeyTips. However, keyboard operability and screen-reader accessibility are separate requirements.
The current source implementation draws ribbon labels and KeyTip indicators manually, without clearly exposing equivalent semantic information to assistive technologies.
As a result, users relying on screen reader softwares may be unable to identify ribbon tabs, available commands, or their current navigation context, even when keyboard shortcuts function correctly.
Steps to reproduce
1. Start WordCraft v0.6.1 on Windows with screen reader software running.
2. Focus the document editor.
3. Press Alt or F10 to activate ribbon navigation.
4. Check whether NVDA announces the active tab and available commands.
5. Press H to enter the Home tab.
6. Navigate through ribbon commands and check their names, roles, states, and focus announcements.
Expected behavior
Ribbon tabs expose appropriate accessible names, roles, and selected states.
Ribbon controls expose their names, roles, and enabled/disabled states.
Screen-reader users can identify the active ribbon tab and focused command.
Alt/F10 navigation provides accessible feedback rather than relying exclusively on visually rendered KeyTips.
Escape exits ribbon navigation and restores an appropriate focus position.

title: Double-click doesn't open header/footer editing until one exists, and the footer is unreachable from the body
author: iot-root
body:
Word enters header/footer editing from a double-click in the page's margin bands. WordCraft has the handler, but two defects keep it from working:

1. **No entry until a part exists.** The double-click gate uses `layout.header_footer_at`, which only reports the band when the page already has that header/footer story. On a fresh document the double-click falls through to text selection, and the only way in is Insert › Header / `insert.editHeader` — which creates the part on demand, so only the gate is wrong.

2. **The footer is unreachable from the body even when it exists.** The first click of the double-click places the caret at the nearest body hit — the body text far above — and the scroll-to-caret slides the page out from under the pointer, so the second click lands mid-body and selects a word. The header appears to work only because its nearest body text is adjacent (no scroll), which makes the bug look footer-specific: "double-click works for the header but not the footer".

Repro: new document, type a line, double-click the bottom margin → a word gets selected (or nothing); the footer never opens. With Insert › Footer used once first, double-click from the body still fails whenever the body text is far from the band.

Related: while editing a header, double-clicking the footer band doesn't switch to it either; and in a multi-section document `insert.editHeader` resolves the section from the caret rather than the page the user acted on.

title: Saving a .docx silently drops settings and parts the model doesn't represent (compat settings lost in 18/18 real-world Word files)
author: przemek-arch
body:
## Summary

Opening and re-saving a Word `.docx` in WordCraft silently drops everything the document model doesn't represent. **Visible content survives very well**: on 18 real-world Word documents nothing visible was lost. The losses are in settings, metadata and a few package parts, and some of them change how Word behaves with the saved file. The cause is architectural: the DOCX writer serializes from the model, and only a few part kinds have a passthrough. So every OOXML element or part the model doesn't know is removed on save, with no warning.

This issue collects what I measured and proposes a staged fix. I'd like to know which direction you prefer before sending code.

## How it was measured

- Build: `main` @ `159b84f`, macOS arm64, plus #1020 and #1024. Neither touches the DOCX writer; #1020 matters for the Accept/Reject check below.
- Round trip: `wordcraft-cli convert in.docx out.docx`.
- Documents: 18 real-world business documents from 1 to 34 pages (16 last saved by Word, 2 by another OOXML producer), with tracked changes from other parties, comments, tables, images, fields (TOC, PAGE, hyperlinks), content controls, text boxes and landscape sections. I can't share them; everything below is counts and element names only.
- Comparison scripts (stdlib Python) diff part lists and per-part element/attribute histograms. They resolve effective character formatting (docDefaults → paragraph style chain → character style chain → direct, theme fonts included) and effective paragraph formatting (alignment, indents, spacing, keep options, borders, shading, tabs) for every character/paragraph. A part is counted as "lost" only when no used relationship reaches it in the source (orphans aren't counted).

**What survives (0 differences in 18/18 files):**
- text: body, deleted text, headers, footers, footnotes;
- tables, rows and cells;
- used images (by content hash);
- fields, by type;
- content controls, text boxes / shapes (`mc:Choice` side), footnotes and endnotes,…

title: Track Changes: a tracked deletion inside a field result (e.g. a =SUM(ABOVE) subtotal) is read as ordinary text; Accept All gives "$$140.00"
author: ryanjshields
body:
WordCraft doesn't recognize a tracked deletion (`<w:del>`) when it sits inside a field's result (between `fldCharType="separate"` and `fldCharType="end"`). The deleted text is treated as ordinary text, so:

- **Accept All in WordCraft** keeps the "deleted" characters: a subtotal tracked from `$150.00` to `$140.00` becomes **`$$140.00`**, and a formula field whose result `5` was tracked-deleted and replaced with `five` becomes **`5five`**.
- **Saving** writes the field result back as ordinary text without the `<w:del>`, so other apps see the damage too (checked with pandoc).

I ran into this on a real manuscript: a tracked edit to a `=SUM(ABOVE)` subtotal in a table. In that file the field result held only `$`, the rest of the old value followed the field end, and each piece had its own `<w:del>`. The minimal file below reproduces it with made-up content.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build the three-file `.docx` below: `zip -X -r tracked-delete-in-field-result.docx '[Content_Types].xml' _rels word`.
2. `wordcraft-cli run --file tracked-delete-in-field-result.docx --cmd 'review.acceptAll={}' --save accepted.docx`, then `wordcraft-cli text accepted.docx`.
3. Or round-trip it with `wordcraft-cli convert tracked-delete-in-field-result.docx resaved.docx` and compare with `pandoc --track-changes=accept -t plain`.

### Result

| | Original | WordCraft Accept All | After a WordCraft save (pandoc, accept) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Subtotal cell | `$150.00` deleted, `$140.00` inserted | `$$140.00` | `$$140.00` |
| `=2+3` field | `5` deleted, `five` inserted | `5five` | `5five` |

pandoc reads the original correctly (`[$150.00]{.deletion}[$140.00]{.insertion}`; accepting gives `$140.00` and `five`). After the WordCraft save, pandoc shows `$[150.00]{.deletion}`: the `$` that was inside the field result is no longer deleted.

### Expected

Tracked deletions and insertions inside a field result are kept as revisions, so Accept All gives `$140.00` / `five`, Reject All gives `$150.00` / …

title: Eraser: borders beside vertically merged cells merge or hide, as in Word
author: rabis7575
body:
**Bug:** Table Layout › Eraser refuses every vertical border that runs beside a vertically merged cell. The status bar says "erasing a border beside a vertically merged cell isn't supported". It also refuses a horizontal border between cells that don't line up. In a table whose right-hand cells are merged down two rows, no vertical line can be erased at all.

**What Word does** (observed black-box, Word 16 on Windows, on the same synthetic table):
- Erasing the border between two cells that are both merged down the same rows **merges them**. The result is one cell, still merged down those rows.
- Erasing a border whose two sides can't become one rectangle doesn't merge. Examples: a one-row cell beside a two-row merged cell, or a full-width cell above a two-cell row. Word **hides the border** instead: it sets both sides' cell borders to `nil` along the whole shared edge (the merged cell's full height).

**Fix** (`cmd/table_draw.rs::eraser`):
- Merge when the cells beside the border make a rectangle, including cells merged down the same rows.
- Otherwise set both sides of the border to no border instead of failing.
- Tests in `table_draw`.

I'm working on this; a PR will follow.

title: Comments: an option to show a comment only for the selected text (default stays as in Word)
author: lasse-tech
body:
Feature request, split off from the second comment on #1013 (https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/issues/1013#issuecomment-6129393334).

## Request
An option to show comments only when asked: the comment of the text under the caret or clicked is shown, the others are hidden (a small marker at most), as OnlyOffice and Google Docs do. It also frees the markup column beside the pages (216 pt) in narrow windows.

## What exists
Comments are shown in balloons in the margin, in the Comments pane, or hidden with Show Markup › Comments. With "hidden" they can't be read at all, so there is no middle setting.

## Default
**The default stays as in Word** (balloons in the margin); the new mode is opt-in.

- WordCraft targets parity with Word, and in Word comments are shown in the margin by default. Anyone coming from Word expects that, and the parity docs measure against it.
- For review a hidden default is risky: someone who only reads the text overlooks comments.
- A new default is the owner's decision (product direction), not a side effect of an option.

## Sketch
- A choice next to the existing balloon settings (Review › Track Changes Options and Show Markup): "Show comments: in the margin | only for the selected text".
- Saved per user, like the other markup options (`review.trackingOptions`).
- A command param for agents, as everything is a command.
- Selecting a comment already works (`select_balloon`), so the mode mostly changes which balloons are laid out.

## Not in scope
The bug from #1013 (a click inside a selected balloon left it) is fixed in #1051.

title: Saving ignores "remove personal information" / "remove date and time" (authors, dates and document properties are still written)
author: przemek-arch
body:
## Summary

Word documents can carry two privacy settings in `word/settings.xml`:
- `w:removePersonalInformation` — ECMA-376 Part 1, document settings: remove personal information from comments, revisions and document properties when saving;
- `w:removeDateAndTime` — same section: remove date and time information from annotations when saving.

Users turn them on in Word's privacy options for documents that go to other parties.

WordCraft doesn't honour them:
1. On `main`, saving **drops both settings**, so after one WordCraft save, Word stops stripping the information too. #1059 fixes the dropping.
2. With the settings kept (#1059), WordCraft still **writes the personal information on save**:
   - comment and revision authors;
   - comment and revision dates;
   - `dc:creator` / `cp:lastModifiedBy` in `docProps/core.xml`;
   - Manager / Company in `docProps/app.xml` are dropped by #1060 when the flag is set; nothing else is.

For anyone who relies on the option (law firms sending drafts to the other side, for example), the file looks safe in Word's options but isn't.

## Reproduction

A synthetic test document (no real data):
- `settings.xml` with `<w:removePersonalInformation/><w:removeDateAndTime/>`;
- 5 comments by 2 named authors, each with `w:date`;
- `core.xml` with a creator and a last-modified-by.

| step | settings kept | comment authors in the file | `w:date` attributes | `core.xml` creator / lastModifiedBy |

| input | yes | 2 named | 5 | names |

title: No setting for a Hunspell dictionaries folder (WORDCRAFT_DICTIONARIES doesn't reach apps started from Finder)
author: przemek-arch
body:
## Summary

There's no user-facing way to point WordCraft at a folder of Hunspell dictionaries. `crates/proof/src/hunspell.rs` searches:
1. a folder set by `set_dictionary_dir`;
2. `WORDCRAFT_DICTIONARIES`;
3. system locations.

Nothing in the app calls `set_dictionary_dir`, and Options › Proofing has no such field. #983 keeps the function, still without a caller.

On macOS this matters because an app started from Finder or Dock doesn't inherit shell variables, so `WORDCRAFT_DICTIONARIES` only works when the app is launched from a terminal. The only alternative is putting files into `~/Library/Spelling`, which also makes macOS offer the dictionary in other apps' spelling menus.

Observed with a Polish `pl_PL` dictionary in a custom folder:
- started from a terminal with the variable: errors are underlined;
- started from Finder: no checking at all, and no message telling the user why.

## Proposal

- An Options › Proofing field "Dictionaries folder" (stored in the preferences, applied via `set_dictionary_dir` at start and on change).
- Optionally, a hint in that pane when a document language has no dictionary installed. The log already says "no Hunspell pl_PL dictionary installed", but the user never sees it.

title: Mouse pointer disappears over table selection areas while dragging/scrolling
body:
## What happens

While scrolling or drag-selecting, when the pointer is over one of a table's selection areas (the strip above a column, left of a row, or along a cell's left edge), the mouse pointer vanishes entirely: no system cursor and no drawn selection arrow.

Two ways to hit it:

1. **Dragging**: press on a selection area (e.g. above a column) and drag to extend the selection, including the drag-select edge auto-scroll (#688). During the whole drag there is no pointer at all.
2. **Dark mode**: with a dark page, scroll (wheel) so a column/cell selection area passes under a stationary pointer. The filled selection arrow is black on dark-grey paper (`DARK_PAPER = 0x33`), so only its 1px white outline shows and the pointer looks gone. The hollow row arrow (white) stays visible, which is why it only happens on "some part" of the table.

## Expected

As in Word, a visible selection arrow follows the pointer in both cases.

## Cause (`crates/ui-egui/src/table_mouse.rs`)

- `cursor()` hides the system pointer with `CursorIcon::None` from the drag's *stored* spot, but `paint()` draws the replacement arrow at `hover_pos`, which is `None` while a button is down (it's the tooltip position). Hidden cursor + undrawn arrow = no pointer during the drag.
- `arrow()` hard-codes `BLACK` fill / `WHITE` edge, which has almost no contrast on dark paper.

## Fix (tested locally on 0.6.1, Linux/XWayland)

- In the `table_drag` branch of `paint()`, fall back to `latest_pos` (`hover.or(latest)`), matching what `cursor()` hides.
- Pass `dark_mode` into `arrow()` and use `WHITE` fill on dark paper (`wordcraft_render::DARK_PAPER`), keeping `BLACK/WHITE` on light paper so the light appearance is pixel-identical.

```diff
@@ paint(): drag branch
-                if let Some(p) = hover {
-                    arrow(painter, p, spot);
+                if let Some(p) = hover.or(latest) {
+                    arrow(painter, p, spot, dark);
                 }
@@ arrow()
-fn arrow(painter: &egui:…

title: Add clear hover hints (tooltips) to UI controls
author: StrajnarFilip
body:
## Problem

Hovering over UI elements currently shows little to no feedback. Toolbar buttons, ribbon commands, icons, and other controls don't explain what they do, so users have to click and guess. This makes the app harder to learn, especially for people coming from Microsoft Word who expect tooltips everywhere.

## Expected behavior

Hovering over any interactive element should show a clear, helpful hint after a short delay (roughly 300-500 ms).

A good tooltip should include:
- **The command name** (e.g. "Bold")
- **The keyboard shortcut**, if one exists (e.g. `Ctrl+B`)
- **A short description** of what it does, where the name alone isn't enough
- **The disabled reason** for greyed-out controls (e.g. "Select text to enable")

## Suggested scope

- [ ] Toolbar / ribbon buttons
- [ ] Icon-only controls (these need hints the most)
- [ ] Dropdowns and pickers (font, size, color, style)
- [ ] Menu items
- [ ] Status bar items (zoom, page count, word count, etc.)
- [ ] Disabled controls

## Implementation notes

- Use one shared tooltip component or helper so all hints look and behave consistently, instead of adding them ad hoc per widget.
- Keep tooltip text in a central place so it can be translated (see #8 on localization).
- Tooltips should not obscure the control being hovered and should stay inside the window bounds.
- Hints should also appear on keyboard focus, for accessibility.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every interactive control has a tooltip, or an explicit reason it doesn't.
- Tooltips appear after a short delay and dismiss when the pointer leaves.
- Shortcuts shown in tooltips match the actual keybindings.

title: Perf: every edit and zoom step re-renders whole pages on the CPU
author: przemek-arch
body:
Every edit and every zoom step re-rasterises whole pages on the CPU, which is now the largest part of the time between a keystroke and the screen.

**Measured** (macOS arm64, release build, a 106-page contract, headless with the `perf_probe` example from #1108 and in a real window over the control channel):

| action | layout | page re-render | frame |
|---|---|---|---|
| one keystroke in a long paragraph | ~7 ms | 9–15 ms | ~17 ms (p95 ~26) |
| one keystroke in a table cell | ~7 ms | ~15 ms | ~23 ms (max 28) |
| one zoom step (50 → 75 → 100 → 150 → 200 %) | — | 20–29 ms headless, 25–95 ms in the window | — |

Scrolling, ribbon tabs and resizes are fine (no frame over 33 ms; tabs ~1 ms).

**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` keeps one texture per page, keyed by the page's content fingerprint (#811); any change to a page's content re-renders the whole page with `vello_cpu`.

**Ideas** (not tried):
- re-render only the band of the page whose lines changed (the layout knows which lines moved) and patch the texture;
- while zooming, keep drawing the previous textures scaled and swap in the new ones when they're ready (a frame or two later), instead of blocking the frame;
- render the visible page first, neighbours after.

With the one-frame key fix (#1107) the estimated key-to-screen latency is about 33 ms; the re-render is most of what remains above a 30 ms target.

title: Narrow window: ribbon tabs run under the Comments / Editing / Share buttons
author: przemek-arch
body:
In a narrow window the ribbon tab strip runs under the buttons on its right (Comments, Editing, Share) instead of making room for them.

**Repro:** open any document, make the window 1024 pt wide (or narrower), Home tab active. The last visible tabs ("Review", "View") are drawn underneath "Comments" and the Editing-mode button; the tab text and button overlap and clicks hit whichever was drawn last.

**Cause:** `crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs` lays the tabs out left to right at full width, then puts the right-hand buttons in a right-to-left layout in whatever space is left — nothing reserves their width.

**Suggested behaviour** (close to Word's): reserve the right-hand group's width first; when tabs don't fit, show those buttons as icons only; if that still isn't enough, move the tabs that don't fit (never the active one) into a "»" overflow menu.

I'm working on a fix locally and can send it as a PR if this direction is welcome.

title: macOS: pinch zoom isn't anchored at the pointer; ribbon groups don't collapse in narrow windows
author: przemek-arch
body:
Two macOS polish items found while comparing with Word for Mac:

1. **Pinch zoom isn't anchored at the pointer.** A trackpad pinch (or Ctrl/⌘ + wheel) over the page changes the zoom through `view.zoom` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, around the `zoom_delta` handling), but the scroll position isn't adjusted, so the point under the pointer drifts away while zooming. Expected: the document point under the pointer stays under it (keep the pointer's document position before the zoom and scroll so it maps to the same screen point after).

2. **Ribbon groups don't collapse when the window narrows.** When the ribbon is wider than the window, groups are simply cut off on the right (the ribbon scrolls horizontally, with the scroll bar hidden). Word collapses groups step by step: large buttons become small ones, labels disappear, and finally a group becomes a single drop-down button with the group's name. Related to #1110 (tab strip overlap in narrow windows).

title: Layout: a paragraph ending above footnotes needs its space after clear of the separator (pagination drifts from Word)
author: przemek-arch
body:
**Pagination with footnotes drifts from Word: a paragraph that ends on a page with footnotes doesn't keep its space after clear of the separator.**

Measured on a 107-page test contract (Calibri 11 pt, list paragraphs with 6 pt space after, ~80 pages with footnotes), comparing WordCraft's PDF with a PDF exported from Word on the same machine (black-box; reference not committed):

- On every Word page whose body **ends with a paragraph's last line**, the gap between that line and the footnote separator is **at least the paragraph's space after** (smallest: 6.21 pt for 6 pt after).
- On pages that **end mid-paragraph**, the last line runs right up to the separator (gaps down to 1.41 pt).

WordCraft checks only the line itself. In the test document, page 6 ends with a 5-line list item whose last line carries footnote 4: in WordCraft all 5 lines fit with 1.6 pt to spare above the separator, but the paragraph's 6 pt space after doesn't. Word moves the last line — and, by widow control, one more — to page 7 together with the footnote. From there every page start differs (11 of 107 page starts match), and WordCraft ends up with 106 pages instead of 107.

**Repro in words:** a page of 11 pt lines; near the bottom, a paragraph with 6 pt space after whose last line has a footnote reference, placed so that its last line plus the separator and the note fit, but not with the 6 pt after. Word: the last two lines move to the next page with the note. WordCraft: they stay.

**Where:** the line-fit loop in `crates/layout/src/lib.rs` (around the `line_notes` / `limit` computation in `place_para_in_flow`): when the page has footnotes and the line is the paragraph's last, the paragraph's space after has to fit above the notes too.

I have a local fix with a regression test (a paragraph swept down the page a point at a time must keep its space after above the separator); with it the test document has 107 pages like Word's.

title: The interface-translation audit is red on main: 2 Mailings labels bypass translation, and the Russian catalog is missing 24 strings
author: RicSchonfelder
body:
`cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui untranslated_interface_text -- --ignored --nocapture` is red on current `main`. The test is `#[ignore]`d (its own doc note says it once failed under load), so CI never runs it and it has drifted. Two separate things fail, and both look fixable — but one needs a call from the maintainers.

## 1. Two Mailings labels never go through translation

The first assertion reports (state: `Mailings › click`):

```
"#10   4.13 × 9.5 in"                              (Envelopes dialog)
", 3 × 10, 2.625\" × 1\" (Letter)"                 (Labels dialog)
```

Both are built with `format!` in `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs_layout.rs` and the result is drawn as-is, so no catalog can ever translate it (the unit `in` and the decimal separator are exactly what a locale wants to change):

- `envelope_label()` — lines 542 and 545 (`"{short}   {} × {} in"` / `… mm`)
- `product_label()` — line 597 (`"{kind}, {} × {}, {} ({})"`)

Wrapping the composed label in `i18n::t(...)` — what the assertion asks for, "wrap them in tl!" — clears this part. (`pseudo::unmarked` already handles nested marks, so wrapping the whole label is safe even though `kind` is already `tl!`-translated.)

With #1 patched, the second assertion (`russian_has_every_string_the_interface_looked_up`) fails, and that is not caused by the patch — the extra entries are pre-existing. Full list:

title: Startup: a blank document is created behind the File (Backstage) Home page; Back shows it instead of an empty window
author: netoverlord
body:
## Summary

When WordCraft launches, it shows the File (Backstage) Home page, but a blank document has already been created behind it. Clicking the **Back** button at the top of the side menu reveals that blank document, even though the user never chose "Blank document". In Microsoft Word, no document exists until the user creates or opens one.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Launch WordCraft (without opening a file or passing a file path).
2. The File (Backstage) view appears, with templates and recent files.
3. Without choosing a template or "Blank document", click the **Back** button at the top of the side menu.

## Current behavior

- A blank, editable document is shown, so one was created automatically at startup.
- The ribbon is fully enabled and the user can type into the document.

## Expected behavior (as in Microsoft Word)

- No document is created at launch.
- Clicking **Back** with no document open shows an empty document area:
  - no page is shown
  - all ribbon commands are disabled (grayed out), except **Help**
- A document is only created when the user picks **Blank document** or a template, or opens a file.
- Launching with a file (double-click, "Open with") still opens that file directly.

## Why this matters

- An unused "Document" is created on every launch, which the user never asked for.
- The empty state in Word (nothing open, ribbon disabled) is a familiar cue that no document is open.

title: Dark theme: ruler margin and text areas have inverted shading (text area is darker than the margins)
author: netoverlord
body:
## Summary

In the dark theme, the shading of both rulers is inverted compared to the light theme and to Microsoft Word. The **text area** (the part of the ruler between the margins) should be lighter than the **margin areas**. In WordCraft's dark theme it is darker instead. This affects both the horizontal and the vertical ruler.

## Terms used

- **Text area:** the section of the ruler between the left and right margins (or top and bottom margins for the vertical ruler), where the text goes.
- **Margin areas:** the sections at the ends of the ruler, over the page margins.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open WordCraft and a document.
2. Turn on the ruler (**View › Ruler**).
3. In the light theme, look at the horizontal ruler (and the vertical ruler).
4. Switch to the dark theme and look at both rulers again.

## Current behavior

- **Light theme (correct):** the text area is lighter than the margin areas.
- **Dark theme (wrong):** the text area is darker than the margin areas, the opposite of the light theme.
- This happens on both the **horizontal** and the **vertical** ruler.

## Expected behavior

In the dark theme, the text area should be **lighter** than the margin areas, as in the light theme. I checked Microsoft Word in dark mode, and its rulers show the text area lighter than the margins. The exact shades differ from the light theme, but the lighter/darker relationship stays the same.

## Why this matters

The contrast between the text area and the margins is how the ruler shows where the margins are. When it's inverted, it's confusing, and it looks like a color bug in the dark theme.

title: Layout: text in an earlier column doesn't wrap around a shape anchored in a later column
author: dkhlapov
body:
On a multi-column page, text laid out before a floating shape's anchor paragraph never wraps around the shape. For example, a square-wrapped shape anchored to a paragraph in column 2 but positioned over column 1 leaves the column-1 lines at full width, running through the shape. Word wraps every column's text around the shape wherever its anchor is.

**Repro:** the file attached to #884 (`Multicolumn_Shapes_Wrap_Issue.docx`) as it opens, before any drag. Its shape is anchored in column 2 at x≈266 pt, over column 1.

**Where:** `crates/layout`. A shape's wrap area is added only when its anchor paragraph is laid out, so anything already placed earlier on that page/column isn't re-flowed. Matching Word needs a re-pass: when an anchor adds an exclusion zone that overlaps already-placed lines on the same page, lay that page out again with the zone known from the start.

Found while fixing #884 (#1139), which fixes the drag case by anchoring a dropped shape in the column it lands in.

title: [Feature Request] Surface a visible hint when a proofing dictionary isn't installed
author: regalf
body:
When a proofing language has no dictionary on the system (Polish without `pl_PL`, Portuguese without VERO, Italian without `it_IT`), WordCraft silently shows no spelling marks — exactly like Word without the language's tools. The only trace is a `log::info!` line in `logs/wordcraft.log`, which normal users never open (see the confusion behind #951, where red English underlines were at least *visible* feedback that something was off).

**Request:** make the missing-dictionary state discoverable in the UI, without being noisy. Ideas (pick one):

1. **Status bar**: when the caret is in a proofing language with no dictionary, show the language dimmed/with an info glyph; tooltip names the missing dictionary (`it_IT` from `hunspell-it`, …) and where it is looked up.

title: Picture Adjustments compound instead of re-applying from the original (transparency 80% → 0% stays faded)
author: DevCoderMax
body:
**Summary**

`picture.transparency` (and, by the same mechanism, `picture.corrections` and `picture.color`) applies on top of the already-edited bitmap instead of the original pixels. Setting Transparency to 80% and back to 0% leaves the picture faded: 0% means "don't touch", not "opaque". Only Reset Picture restores the original. Word treats these sliders as absolute/live values recomputed from the original.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Insert a picture.
2. Picture Format › Adjust › Transparency › 80%.
3. Transparency › 0%.

**Expected result**

Step 3 restores the fully opaque original (like Word, and like Reset Picture does).

**Actual result**

The picture stays at 20% opacity: the second pass multiplies the already-faded alpha by `(1 - 0.0) = 1.0`, a no-op.

**Root cause**

`adjust()` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/objects.rs` always decodes the picture's *current* media. The `s.originals` chain (media → pre-edit original) exists precisely to remember the source, but only `picture.reset` consults it. So every `adjust()`-based command compounds:

| Command | How it compounds |
|---|---|
| `picture.transparency` | alpha multiplied again each pass |
| `picture.corrections` | brightness +20 then −20 doesn't restore (second pass edits brightened pixels) |
| `picture.color` | grayscale then vivid can't recover colors |
| `picture.iconColor` | re-tints already-tinted pixels |
| `picture.effects` | blur/sharpen/posterize/pixelate degrade on every pass |
| `picture.removeBackground` | each pass eats further into edges |
| `picture.compress` | re-compresses the already-reduced PNG |
| `picture.style` / `picture.border` | frames/shadows drawn on top of previous ones |

This also blocks a transparency slider with live preview: every drag tick would multiply again.

**Suggested scope**

- Make the *parameter-like* adjustments absolute from the original: `transparency`, `corrections`, `color` (there is now a helper for exactly this, `adjust_media`, next to `adjust`).
- Keep the *d…

title: Proposal: LawCraft, legal drafting tools for WordCraft
author: pattalkslaw-del
body:
I'm a practicing attorney in Missouri, and I filed #96 through #99 last week. Thanks for turning those around in a day.

I want to build legal drafting tools into WordCraft and contribute them here. I'm calling the set LawCraft. Lawyers pay for Word mostly to format court filings, and WordCraft already has most of the hard parts: styles, line numbering, table of authorities, track changes, the command layer and the MCP server. What's missing is the court-specific layer.

**What I'd build**

1. **Court profiles.** A profile is a data file, not code: one per court, with three parts per document type (petition, motion, brief and so on):
   - *Sections:* the document skeleton, including a caption with fields (parties, case number, attorney, bar number).
   - *Styles:* page size, margins, font, spacing, page numbering, named paragraph styles, and optional pleading-paper line numbers.
   - *Checks:* rules that aren't styles, like word limits, no active hyperlinks, or no party addresses after the original petition.

   Pick a court and a document type, and WordCraft builds the skeleton and applies the styles. Profiles are managed through commands, so a settings page, the CLI and an agent over MCP can all list, create, validate and update them. Agent-made profiles stay marked unverified until a person approves them. I'd ship two profiles, Missouri and federal; users add their own courts.
2. **Legal proofing.** A legal word list for the existing offline spell checker, and confusion checks for pairs like statute/statue and principal/principle.
3. **Legal symbols.** A palette and shortcuts for § and ¶, with non-breaking spacing.
4. **Citation form check.** Format suggestions for citations: state-specific forms (starting with Missouri) and Bluebook forms for federal sources. It checks form only, and the formats are encoded as rules; no text is copied from any citation manual.

**How I'd work**

Small PRs, one feature each, following AGENTS.md: clean room, no panics, every actio…

title: Proofing: help users get a Hunspell dictionary (a link and the dictionaries folder now, an opt-in download later?)
author: witkowski01
body:
## Problem

Since #346, spelling for Polish (and Portuguese since #797) reads a Hunspell dictionary installed on the system, and none is bundled, which keeps third-party data and its licences out of the repo. Most users on Windows and macOS have no such dictionary installed, though, so these languages have no spelling marks out of the box, and the web build has none at all.

With #1084, File › Options › Proofing now says which dictionary each language found, or "no dictionary found". storytold/craft-libs#31 adds a per-app folder on every desktop system (`~/Library/Application Support/WordCraft/dictionaries` on macOS). What's still missing is an easy way to get a dictionary into that folder. Word does this by offering to install a language's proofing tools.

I mentioned this as a possible follow-up on #346. I'd like to check the direction with the maintainers before writing any code, because step B adds network access, which WordCraft doesn't have today.

## Proposal: two steps

**A. No network code.** Next to "Polish: no dictionary found" in Options › Proofing, add:
- **Get dictionary…**: opens the browser at the language's folder in LibreOffice's dictionaries repository (e.g. `LibreOffice/dictionaries/pl_PL`, which holds `pl_PL.aff` and `pl_PL.dic`);
- **Open dictionaries folder**: creates the per-app folder if needed and shows it in Finder or Explorer.

The user downloads two files, drops them in, and the line turns into "Polish: …/pl_PL.dic". Nothing is fetched by WordCraft itself.

**B. Opt-in download, if you want it.** A **Download** button that fetches the dictionary for the user:
- only on that click, never in the background or at start-up;
- from a fixed source at a pinned version (LibreOffice's dictionaries repository), checked against a SHA-256 kept in the code, so a changed or tampered file is refused;
- the dictionary's licence is shown before downloading (Polish SJP.PL is multi-licensed GPL/LGPL/MPL/Apache/CC BY; Portuguese VERO is LGPL/MPL);

title: Web: Save does nothing in a cross-origin iframe on Chromium (showSaveFilePicker rejects asynchronously, no fallback to download)
author: natocool2
body:
## What happens

WordCraft 0.6.1 web, running inside a **cross-origin iframe** in Chromium (Chrome/Edge 13x). The app is served from its own origin and embedded by another site, for example a web desktop or an LMS. Ctrl+S / File > Save does nothing. The document stays marked unsaved, and no file is written or downloaded.

## Why

`apps/wordcraft-web/src/web.rs` `download()` uses `showSaveFilePicker` whenever `window.showSaveFilePicker` exists, and falls back to the `<a download>` path only if the **synchronous** call fails:

```rust
match trigger_save_file_picker(saves, ctx, &window, &picker_fn, &name, bytes) {
    Ok(()) => return Ok(()),
    Err(e) => { /* falls back to trigger_anchor_download */ }
}
```

In a cross-origin sub-frame, Chromium still exposes `showSaveFilePicker`, but always **rejects the returned promise** with a `SecurityError` ("Cross origin sub frames aren't allowed to show a file picker."). The call itself returns a promise without throwing, so `trigger_save_file_picker` returns `Ok(())`. The rejection then arrives in the `spawn_local` block. It is not an `AbortError`, so it is recorded as an unsaved error (`showSaveFilePicker error: SecurityError…`), and nothing falls back to `trigger_anchor_download`. The user's work can only leave the tab through Save As to another format, which takes the same path, so in practice it cannot leave at all.

Firefox and Safari are not affected, because they have no `showSaveFilePicker` and take the anchor path. Top-level pages and same-origin iframes are not affected either.

## Repro

1. Serve the 0.6.1 web zip on origin A.
2. On origin B, add `<iframe src="https://A/wordcraft/" sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-downloads allow-popups"></iframe>`.
3. Type something and press Ctrl+S. The console shows `showSaveFilePicker error: SecurityError…` and no download starts.

We embed WordCraft this way, and we currently work around it by hiding `showSaveFilePicker`/`showOpenFilePicker` from the app when it…

EndNote is still the standard tool for reference management in many academic fields, institutions and publishers. An EndNote-compatible feature would make Wordcraft a real option for a very large group of users: researchers, PhD students and academic writers.

Motivation

Many researchers stay with Microsoft Word plus EndNote because their whole workflow, their reference libraries and their collaborators are built around EndNote. These licenses are very expensive, and research groups, universities and especially early-career researchers often have very small budgets.

To get these users to switch, Wordcraft would need more than generic citation support. It would need to feel familiar to EndNote users and work with their existing EndNote data. Then switching would be easy and wouldn’t mean starting over.

title: Persistent default formatting for new documents (Normal template), and RTF losing the default font and size
author: Appshines
body:
## Summary

There is no way to set the default formatting for new documents, the equivalent of Word's Normal template. Every File › New document starts with the built-in style sheet: Aptos 12 pt, 8 pt space after paragraphs, 1.15 line spacing (`crates/doc/src/styles.rs:179–181`).

We write and edit RTF documents that must be in Courier New with no space after paragraphs. RTF has a default font (`\deff`) but no Normal style WordCraft could keep, so the formatting has to come from WordCraft's defaults. Today that means reformatting every new document by hand.

While looking into it, we found three RTF problems that make it worse: even a correctly formatted document doesn't come back the same after saving it as RTF.

## Current behaviour (checked on 159b84f)

1. **No persistent default for new documents.** `Session::blank_document()` (`crates/engine/src/session.rs:952`) always uses the built-in defaults. Modify Style on Normal only changes the open document.
2. **Design › Set as Default stores nothing.** `design.setDefault` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/design.rs:80`) only shows "These settings will be used for new documents." The next File › New is unchanged, so the message is misleading.
3. **RTF import drops a monospaced default font.** `crates/formats/src/rtf.rs:1728` filters `\deff` through `!model::is_mono(..)`. A file whose default font is Courier New opens in Aptos for all text that doesn't select a font itself.
4. **RTF export loses the default font size.** The default font is written as `\deff0` (`rtf.rs:401`), but no size is written. `\plain` resets to 12 pt, so a document with a 10 pt default comes back as 12 pt.
5. **RTF export loses the Normal style's font.** `model::effective()` (`crates/formats/src/model.rs:656`) leaves the paragraph style out. A document whose Normal style is Courier New is written with only `\deff0 Aptos` and no `\f` on its text, so the file opens in Aptos, in other RTF readers as well.

2. Connect: `wordcraft-cli mcp --connect 127.0.0.1:7981`
3. Call `type_text {"text": "unsaved edit "}`; `ui_inspect` now reports `"dirty": true`
4. Call `execute {"command": "file.close"}`

**Expected:** The usual save prompt (Save / Don't Save / Cancel), or an error to the client that the document has unsaved changes, with an explicit option to discard.

**Actual:** The process exits. The file on disk is unchanged and `~/Library/Application Support/WordCraft` has no recovery data, so the edit is gone.

**Notes:** An agent that closes a document a person is also working on can lose that person's work with no warning.

Same symptom as #195 (closed on 11 Oct 2026). It still reproduces on 0.6.1 for macOS through the control channel.

title: Icons: lettered fallback and Highlight colour bar (review of #500)
author: dkhlapov
body:
These are review findings on #500 (redrawing the icon set). They are filed separately so they can be fixed on top of it.

- **Commands without their own icon now look identical (important).** The fallback icon used to be a tile with the command's first letter. It is now an empty frame, the same for every command. A Quick Access Toolbar or custom ribbon group holding several such commands (Save As, Select All, Repeat, Export PDF…) shows identical blank buttons.
- **Highlight shows the wrong colour (important).** The mini toolbar's Highlight button passes no swatch, so the new split button draws an accent-blue bar instead of the highlight colour. Draw › Highlighter and Shape Fill show an accent bar unrelated to any colour too.
- An icon is drawn as disabled when its colour equals the theme's icon colour, so a font colour of exactly #424242 (light) or #DDDDDD (dark) looks disabled.
- A disabled split button's arrow still opens its menu.
- The PR description says only `icons.rs` changes, but `ribbon.rs` and `widgets.rs` change too.

title: LanguageTool: server fields send text to half-typed addresses (review of #672)
author: dkhlapov
body:
These are review findings on #672 (opt-in LanguageTool checking). They are filed separately so they can be fixed on top of it.

**Privacy: text goes to half-typed servers (important).** While checking is on, the Server, Username and API key fields in Options apply on every keystroke (`crates/ui-egui/src/options.rs`). Each keystroke resets the link and clears the results. The document hasn't changed, so the paragraph is checked again straight away and sent to whatever prefix is in the field so far. Typing `https://lt.company.com` sends text, and the API key if one is set, to `https://lt.co`, which is a different, real domain. Squiggles also flicker, and a half-typed key gets a 401 that stops checking.
Expected: the fields take effect only when committed (Enter or leaving the field), and nothing is sent before then.

Smaller points:
- In "document" language mode, two paragraphs with the same text in different languages keep evicting each other's result, so requests repeat forever. The store is keyed by text only.
- The retry with `auto` after an HTTP 400 skips the pacing gap, so the public server's 20 requests a minute can be exceeded.
- The username and API key are sent over plain `http://` to any host. Refuse or warn when the host isn't loopback.
- Tracked deletions and objects are sent as runs of `\u{1}`, which glues words together. Text marked "Do not check spelling or grammar", and hidden text, are sent too.
- HTTP 4xx answers other than 401/403, and answers that aren't valid UTF-8, retry the same paragraph every 30 s forever.
- Error messages in Options are untranslated English.
- Tests: no test proves that nothing is sent while checking is off, and none covers the same-text-two-languages case.

title: Incremental pagination differs from a full layout after a page break (review of #675)
author: dkhlapov
body:
These are review findings on #675 (incremental pagination for large documents). They are filed separately so they can be fixed on top of it.

- **The incremental layout can differ from a full layout (critical).** The page builder's "after a page-break mark" flag isn't saved in the per-page checkpoints. When a paragraph ends with a page break, the next page's heading should get no space before. After an edit on that page, the relayout resumes from a checkpoint with the flag cleared, so the heading gains its space before and the page shifts.
- **Stale header, footnote or text-box pages (important).** The pass key stores raw block addresses for headers, footers, footnotes and text boxes, but the pass doesn't keep those blocks alive. A freed block's address can be reused by the edited copy, the key compares equal, and pages with the old text are reused.
- After an incremental pass the paragraph cache is never evicted, so a long session grows without bound.
- Edits that change the number of blocks (Enter, or Backspace that joins paragraphs) lay out every following block again. That is correct but not incremental; note it in layout-parity.
- Tests: no cases cover typing in a footnote, header or text box, editing a table cell, renumbering a list, or a document with section breaks.

title: Collapsed ribbon group drop-down closes on any click inside (review of #708)
author: dkhlapov
body:
These are review findings on #708 (ribbon groups shrink to fit the window). They are filed separately so they can be fixed on top of it.

- **A collapsed group's drop-down closes on any click inside it (critical).** The drop-down uses egui's default close-on-click behaviour. With Font collapsed, clicking the font name or size box closes it, so you can't type in it. The combo box, Change Case and colour menus close along with it.
- **Home's Styles gallery folds too early (important).** Labels are given back to groups greedily from the left, so Clipboard and Font get theirs back before Styles is reconsidered. At 1440 pt the whole Styles gallery collapses into a button, though it was visible before this change. Word keeps the gallery and trims it first.
- The status line in `docs/ui-parity.md` names #700 twice instead of #662 (a rebase accident).
- Groups are planned by title, so two custom groups called "New Group" on one tab overwrite each other's widths.
- A collapsed group draws its title twice: on the button and in the label row below.
- Commands inside a collapsed group lose their KeyTips, and the collapsed button has none of its own.
- Recording the measured widths clones the whole width map once per group per frame.
- Measured widths don't refresh after the interface language or zoom changes.
- Tests: nothing checks that a collapsed group's drop-down actually runs its commands.

title: STYLEREF headers re-laid out on every keystroke (review of #882)
author: dkhlapov
body:
These are review findings on #882 (STYLEREF results per page in headers and footers). They are filed separately so they can be fixed on top of it.

- **Every keystroke re-lays out every STYLEREF header (important).** The header paragraph's cache key hashes the text of every body paragraph. Any edit therefore misses the cache on every page and rebuilds the style index. In a 500-page book with running chapter headers, that is a full header pass per keystroke. The key should use each page's computed STYLEREF results instead.
- **Clean room.** Some switch labels in the Field dialog for STYLEREF look like Word's own wording. Reword them in our own words, from ECMA-376 §17.16.5.59.
- `STYLEREF 1` never matches a style named `heading 1` whose id is localized (for example `berschrift1`), so documents from localized Word show the error text.
- `ROADMAP.md` has a stray `|---|---|` row inside the progress-log table.

title: Mail merge: failed Edit Recipients loses the filter; .xls memory blow-up (review of #885)
author: dkhlapov
body:
These are review findings on #885 (mail merge: .xls recipients, encodings, Filter and Sort). They are filed separately so they can be fixed on top of it.

- **A failed Edit Recipients loses the filter (important).** `mailings.editRecipients` takes the filter and sort out of the merge state and then loads the recipients. If loading fails, the filter and sort are gone while the rows stay filtered. The command is pure, so nothing restores them.
- **A hostile .xls file can exhaust memory (important).** Each LABELSST cell clones its shared string, which can be up to 32,767 characters, so a file of about 30 MB can ask for tens of GB. Rows also aren't capped at MAX_ROWS while the cells are collected. The .xlsx path has the same shared-string amplification.
- When OK is pressed in the dialog, a filter rule on a field the user renamed or removed fails with a params error. The engine path drops such rules instead.
- The dialog re-filters and re-sorts every record on every frame, so a list of 100k rows makes it stutter.
- An Excel 2003 XML spreadsheet saved as `.xls` gets the "web page (HTML)" error message.
- A FORMULA's pending string result is never cleared, so a STRING record that arrives late lands in the wrong cell.

title: Table styles: No Border on inherited parts, cell Top alignment (review of #887)
author: dkhlapov
body:
These are review findings on #887 (table style editor for every table style part). They are filed separately so they can be fixed on top of it.

- **"No Border" does nothing on a part that inherits its lines (important).** The dialog's change check treats an unset edge and an explicit "none" edge as equal, so nothing is sent. Example: in a style based on Table Grid, Header Row › No Border keeps every header gridline. The model and layout already support explicit "none" edges.
- **A cell's own Top alignment loses to the style (important).** A cell's vertical alignment defaults to Top, so an explicit Top can't be told apart from "not set". If a style part centres vertically, Align Top Left on a cell, or `w:vAlign w:val="top"` in a .docx, still renders centred. In Word, direct cell formatting wins.
- `tableStyle.edit` silently ignores part fields given without a `"part"` key; it should reject them.
- Clearing the font box can't reset a part's font back to inherited.
- The new optional `"part"` parameter of `ui.dialog` isn't documented in `docs/control-protocol.md`.

title: Layout: space after a paragraph that ends in a page break pushes down the next page's first paragraph
author: dkhlapov
body:
Found while fixing #1284. When a paragraph ends with a page break, `place_para` (`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`, around the `pb.y += space_after` after the break) still adds the paragraph's space after on the new page. So the next paragraph no longer counts as "at the top of the page", and it keeps its space before.

We need to check in Word what happens: does a paragraph that ends in a page break carry its space after onto the next page, and does the next paragraph's space before apply? Then match it.

title: Web: Save-before-New/Open discards the document before the asynchronous save completes
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0 (rechecked against upstream before filing). Audit reference: **H1**.

**Severity:** High (data loss). **Confidence:** High; control flow confirmed.
This is a source-flow finding, not a runtime reproduction. No exploit inputs, destructive tests, or application changes were made.

## Root cause and evidence
[apps/wordcraft-web/src/web.rs:323–363](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/apps/wordcraft-web/src/web.rs#L323-L363) starts the picker/write task with spawn_local and returns Ok immediately. [crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:689–702](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L689-L702) clears dirty on that return; [crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:779–833](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L779-L833) treats downloaded as safely saved and runs the pending replacement. The later failure notification contains filename/error, not the original document identity.

Edit A, request New/Open, choose Save, then cancel the save picker or encounter a write/close failure. The pending replacement can already have discarded A and its undo history. Marking the currently open document dirty afterward cannot restore A. This is distinct from the normal prompt being absent and from iframe-specific picker rejection.

Represent pending/success/failure save outcomes explicitly. Retain the original document identity/revision and the continuation; execute replacement only after write-and-close succeeds. Failure must leave the original available.

## Suggested regression tests
Drive Save-before-New/Open with delayed success, picker cancellation, write failure, and close failure. Assert A remains recoverable until successful completion and unrel…

title: Save safety: RTF/ODT are classified as preserving everything although conversion drops document state
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0 (rechecked against upstream before filing). Audit reference: **H2**.

**Severity:** High (data loss). **Confidence:** High; source confirmed.
This is a source-flow finding, not a runtime reproduction. No exploit inputs, destructive tests, or application changes were made.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:202–209](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L202-L209) adopts RTF/ODT paths and clears dirty. [crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:1690–1692](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L1690-L1692) classifies them as keeps_everything. In contrast, [crates/formats/src/model.rs:747–825](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/formats/src/model.rs#L747-L825) drops hidden/deleted runs and flattens unsupported objects. title: Convert Text to Table silently drops fields above column 63 and intervening selected blocks
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0 (rechecked against upstream before filing). Audit reference: **H4**.

**Severity:** High (data loss). **Confidence:** High; source confirmed.
This is a source-flow finding, not a runtime reproduction. No exploit inputs, destructive tests, or application changes were made.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs:911–935](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs#L911-L935) extracts complete paragraph plain_text values, clamps columns to 63, ignores cells beyond the allocated grid, and then removes every sibling block in the selected range. Selection offsets and non-paragraph blocks are not preserved.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A 64-field row loses its last field. Selecting paragraphs around a table removes that intervening table. Partial boundary-paragraph selections are converted as whole paragraphs. Inline objects/formatting also flatten.

## Recommended remediation
Validate the full selection and dimensions before mutation. Reject unsupported cases instead of dropping content; honor selection offsets or explicitly require whole-paragraph selections.

## Suggested regression tests
64-field row; paragraph–table–paragraph selection; partial boundary paragraphs; embedded objects. Require lossless output or error with exactly unchanged document and undo history.

title: Legacy DOC: overlapping note ranges bypass aggregate decoded-output limits

## Scope and verification

**Severity:** High (availability). **Confidence:** High for missing aggregate bound; OOM not reproduced.
This is a source-flow finding, not a runtime reproduction. No exploit inputs, destructive tests, or application changes were made.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/docbin/src/notes.rs:10–25](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/docbin/src/notes.rs#L10-L25) accepts individually increasing ranges without checking monotonicity/non-overlap across the note PLC. [crates/docbin/src/lib.rs:199–214](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/docbin/src/lib.rs#L199-L214) walks and materializes each accepted range independently. Source-character and part-count caps do not bound aggregate decoded story content.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Malformed note tables can repeatedly reference overlapping large footnote/endnote ranges. A bounded source story becomes many owned output stories, multiplying CPU/memory consumption. This is a static resource-budget finding, not a demonstrated crash or exploit.

## Recommended remediation
Validate PLC order and non-overlap and enforce one shared decoded-character/object/work budget across all stories before materialization.

## Suggested regression tests
Public DOC import with small injected budgets and overlapping/nonmonotonic note ranges; assert deterministic limit/error results and bounded aggregate work. Include a valid nonoverlapping control.
