title: DOCX: continuous section after a page break gets its headers one page late (first-page header lands on the wrong page)
author: PM-CS
body:
## Summary

When a section ends with a paragraph that holds only a manual page break, followed by an **empty** paragraph that carries the section's `w:sectPr`, and the next section is **continuous** with **Different First Page** on, WordCraft assigns the new section's headers one page too late:

| Page | Word 365 (Windows) | WordCraft 0.7.0 (`fd0bb2f`, 2026-10-15) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | section 1 default header | section 1 default header |
| 2 | **section 2 first-page header** | section 1 default header |
| 3 | section 2 default header | **section 2 first-page header** |
| 4 | section 2 default header | section 2 default header |

Word keeps the empty section-mark paragraph with the page break on page 1, so section 2 starts at the top of page 2 and page 2 is its first page. WordCraft puts that empty paragraph at the top of page 2, so page 2 still counts as section 1 and the first-page header shows up on page 3.

This looks like the continuous-section sibling of #2013 ("keep empty section marks with preceding page breaks"), which states it does not change continuous-section handling.

## Repro

`continuous-section-first-page-header.docx` (attached, hand-written OOXML, three headers that just say which header they are):

```xml
<w:p>…Section 1 text…</w:p>
<w:p><w:r><w:br w:type="page"/></w:r></w:p>          <!-- page break only -->
<w:p><w:pPr><w:sectPr>                                <!-- empty paragraph, section 1 properties -->
  <w:headerReference w:type="default" r:id="rIdH1"/>  <!-- HEADER A -->
  …pgSz/pgMar…
</w:sectPr></w:pPr></w:p>
<w:p>…Section 2 text, 40 filler paragraphs…</w:p>
<w:sectPr>                                            <!-- section 2 -->

title: Windows (native): one-finger drag on a touch screen selects text instead of scrolling the document
author: setzor
body:
## Summary

On a touch-screen Windows device, a one-finger drag over the document always
starts a text selection and never scrolls. On touch input, a drag should
pan/scroll the document, as MS Word does. Selection with a finger should require
a long-press first (Word's model) — or a pen/mouse.

## Steps

1. Start WordCraft on a Windows laptop/monitor with a touch screen.
2. Open a multi-page document.
3. Swipe up/down with one finger over the page.

## Expected

The document scrolls 1:1 with the finger and coasts on release (like MS Word,
mobile browsers). A tap places the caret; long-press + drag starts a text
selection; two-finger pinch zooms.

## Actual

The drag selects text. Always. The document never scrolls from a one-finger
swipe.

## How MS Word distinguishes the two (for reference)

- Word checks the input device type (touch vs. pen vs. mouse) via Windows
  pointer input (`WM_POINTER*` / `GetPointerPointerIdType`), not just
  "is a button down".
- A finger that starts moving without a long-press is a **pan gesture**
  (DirectManipulation / `WM_GESTURE`); the finger delta drives smooth scrolling
  with inertia.
- A **stationary press** held briefly (long-press) escalates into selection
  mode, showing selection handles; dragging then extends the selection. Tapping
  places the caret; double-tap selects a word.
- So the disambiguation is: touch drag = scroll by default, selection only
  after press-and-hold; mouse/pen drag = select immediately.

## Related

#1503 reports the same behavior in the web build (`eframe` maps `touchstart`
to a primary pointer press, and `crates/ui-egui/src/scroll.rs` only handles
`Event::MouseWheel`). A fix should probably handle both, but this issue tracks
the native Windows path.

title: feature -  Linux: add a setting to choose the display server (Wayland / X11)
author: Yasas-Sri
body:
Problem
 On Linux, the only way to choose between native Wayland and XWayland is the WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND=1 environment variable (apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs:398). Most users don't launch from a terminal, and the ArtCraft launcher, desktop entries and Flatpak make environment variables awkward to set.

 Each mode has bugs that only happen in that mode, so users need an easy way to switch:
 - Only under XWayland (fixed by WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND=1): #1382 (wrong scaling), #1240 (save dialog too tall), #1956 (save dialog doesn't open), #1169 / #2066 (typing stops when an input method is connected).▎ - Only under native Wayland: no file drag-and-drop from the file manager (winit 0.30; the reason for #220), and the plain title bar on GNOME (#78).▎
 PR #1978 proposes switching the default to native Wayland. Whichever default wins, people who need the other mode still need a way to choose it.

 Proposal
 Add a "Linux display server" option, like PhotoCraft's Preferences › Performance › Linux display server: Automatic (the default), Wayland, or X11 (XWayland).
 - Store it in ui.json. It's read before the window opens (as saved_window() already does), so a change takes effect on the next launch. Say so next to the option.
 - Keep WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND working and let it override the setting, so existing setups don't break.
 - If the chosen mode isn't available (e.g. X11 picked but DISPLAY isn't set), fall back to the other one instead of failing to start.
 - Linux and BSD only. Hide the option on Windows, macOS and the web.

 Related: #1978 (default switch), #220 (why XWayland is the default), #1382, #78, #282, #2058

title: Ruler indent markers use the page body instead of the active text column
author: talmidhon
body:
## Problem

In a multi-column document, the horizontal ruler's paragraph indent markers are positioned relative to the full page body instead of the active text column.

The screenshots use a plain English, left-to-right document. The caret is in the second column, but the ruler's left-indent handle stays near the first column's left edge.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a blank document. Type `Line 1` through `Line 12`, with Enter between lines.
2. Select all, choose Home > Align Left, then Layout > Columns > Two.
3. Press Ctrl+Home, then Down to reach the start of `Line 2`.
4. Press Ctrl+Shift+Enter to insert a column break. `Line 1` remains in the first column; `Line 2` and the following paragraphs move to the second column.
5. With the caret at the start of `Line 2`, compare its position with the ruler's left-indent handle.
6. Drag that handle 0.25 inches (18pt) to the right.

## Actual behavior

Before the drag, the left-indent handle is above the first column's left edge, although the caret is at the start of the second column.

After the drag, `Line 2` moves 0.25 inches to the right within the second column. The ruler handle also moves 0.25 inches, but stays near the first column, far from the edited paragraph.

For Letter paper, 1-inch margins and a 0.5-inch column gap:

| State | Paragraph start (page x) | Left-indent handle (page x) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Before dragging | 324pt | 72pt |
| After an 18pt left indent | 342pt | 90pt |

The handle is displaced by 252pt, one column plus the gap.

## Expected behavior

The ruler's paragraph indent markers should follow the column containing the caret. Dragging a marker should keep its position consistent with the paragraph being edited. The existing table-cell behavior should be preserved.

## Likely cause

`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs::rulers` uses `table_ruler::text_area(...).unwrap_or((page.body.x, page.body.w))`. Outside table cells, the fallback uses the full page body even when the paragraph is in a narrowe…

title: Very high CPU use without a GPU (Hyper-V VM over RDP): egui redraws the whole window in software on every input
author: Appshines
body:
## Summary

In a Windows VM on Hyper-V used over Remote Desktop (no GPU passthrough), WordCraft uses a lot of CPU, while Microsoft Word runs acceptably fast on the same VM. Without a GPU, wgpu ends up on WARP, the DirectX 12 software rasteriser ("Microsoft Basic Render Driver"), so every frame is drawn by the processor. Combined with egui's immediate-mode model, which redraws the whole window for every input event, this wastes a lot of CPU. Remote desktops, terminal servers and VDI are common in offices, so this affects a large group of potential users.

## Why it happens

- **Full redraw on every input.** egui re-runs the UI and egui-wgpu redraws the entire window for every event, including each mouse move over an empty area. egui has no damage tracking, so it doesn't know which regions changed.
- **Software rasterisation.** On WARP every one of those full-window frames is rasterised on the CPU. `apps/wordcraft/src/graphics.rs` already knows this path (#316): when DirectX 12 only offers WARP, it stays enabled as the last resort, and a VM usually has no usable OpenGL driver either.
- **Texture sampling is especially slow on WARP.** Sampling through a sampler costs many times more than a direct texel read. WordCraft's canvas consists mostly of large page textures, so it is likely hit harder than a typical small egui app.
- **Periodic repaints.** The caret blink (`canvas.rs`, `request_repaint_after` every 530 ms) triggers a full-window frame each time, and so do hover effects in the ribbon and the caret glide animation.

## Evidence from a comparable app

We ran into the same problem in another eframe 0.36.2 / egui-wgpu 0.36.2 desktop app of ours and spent some time on it. The measurements below are with WARP forced on a development machine, release build, as CPU time in percent of one core, with the mouse moving over an empty area:

| Version | Idle | Mouse moving | Limited to 4 cores: idle / moving |
|---|---|---|---|
| unchanged | 311 % | 1,288 % | 68 % / 288 % |
|…

title: Feature Request: Import Yomitan Dictionaries
author: flobauke
body:
Yomitan is a free and open-source browser extension created by Darius Jahandarie that provides instant dictionary lookups for language learners.

https://yomitan.wiki/

A valuable addition to WordArt would be the ability to import dictionaries in the Yomitan format. A large number of Yomitan dictionaries are available for many languages, making the format a de facto standard within language-learning communities.

Because many dictionaries are distributed under Creative Commons or similar licenses, direct inclusion in WordArt may not be legally possible. An import function would solve this issue by allowing users to obtain and manage dictionary files themselves.

Imported dictionaries could be used for:

- Spell checking
- Phonetic guides and furigana generation
- Word lookups and definitions
- Dictionary-based writing tools

Supporting Yomitan imports would immediately give users access to a large ecosystem of existing dictionary resources without requiring WordArt to bundle or maintain dictionary content.

title: Web host bridge: lock/unlock editing from the host (readonly)
author: jyviko
body:
**What**
A small follow-up to the `?host=parent` bridge (#1655 / #405): a host message that locks and unlocks editing in the embedded editor.

- `wordcraft:readonly` `{ readonly: bool }` from the parent → the document becomes read-only (typing, paste, ribbon edits and edit commands are disabled; selection, scrolling, find and copy still work) or editable again.
- Optional `?readonly=1` URL flag for the initial state, so the editor doesn't flash editable before the first message.
- Reply / notify with `wordcraft:readonly` `{ readonly }` so the host can confirm the state.
- Same rules as the bridge: host mode only, same-origin parent only.

**Why**
Hosts that show "someone else is editing" (a follow mode where one person or agent holds the pen and others watch) need to stop local edits without reloading the document. No current PR covers it, and #1589's live `execute` builds on the same need.

**Scope**
Only after a bridge PR merges. Ideally it maps onto an existing engine-level read-only/protection state rather than a web-only flag, so the desktop and control channel behave the same.

I'll take this one.

title: Moving a picture by dragging shows no insertion cursor where it will land
author: MatRanc
body:
When you drag a picture to move it to a different spot in the document, WordCraft shows a see-through copy of the picture following the mouse, but no insertion cursor. You can't tell exactly where in the text the picture will go until you let go.

In Word, a dashed insertion cursor moves through the text with the mouse while you drag, showing exactly where the picture will be placed.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Insert a picture into a document with a few paragraphs of text. Leave its layout as In Line with Text (the default).
2. Click and drag the picture to a different spot in the text, without letting go.

**Expected:** an insertion cursor in the text shows where the picture will be placed, like Word.
**Actual:** only the see-through copy of the picture is shown, with no insertion cursor.

title: Dragging an In Line with Text picture turns it into a floating picture with Square wrapping
author: MatRanc
body:
When you drag a picture whose layout is In Line with Text, WordCraft drops it as a floating picture with Square wrapping, so the text wraps around it. In Word, dragging an inline picture moves it to a new spot in the text, and it stays In Line with Text.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Insert a picture into a document with a few paragraphs of text. Leave its layout as In Line with Text (the default).
2. Drag it to a different spot in the text and let go.

**Expected:** the picture moves to where it was dropped in the text and is still In Line with Text, like Word.
**Actual:** the picture's layout changes to Square, and the text wraps around it.

**Notes**
This looks deliberate: `arrange.bounds` says "moving an inline object floats it" (`crates/engine/src/cmd/objects.rs:330`), and a test checks for it (`objects.rs:1503`). Moving inline pictures to a new spot in the text instead would also give a natural place for the insertion cursor in #2233.

**Environment:** macOS, WordCraft v0.7.0

title: Embedded fonts in a .docx are ignored; text renders in a substitute face
author: esmin
body: WordCraft ignores fonts embedded in a .docx (word/fontTable.xml + obfuscated word/fonts/*.odttf) and instead draws text in whatever substitute the machine has. This happens at document-open time in open_bytes_with, so the GUI canvas, print and PDF are all affected, and the rendering varies by platform rather than matching the font the author embedded. A fix means reading the font table, XOR-deobfuscating each part, and registering the faces before layout so they win over installed fonts of the same name.

title: MCP: insert a table with data in one call (insert_table, or values on insert.table)
author: Mortalfast
body:
## Context
I'm driving WordCraft 0.7.0 headless (`wordcraft-cli mcp`) from a local model (Devstral 24B via Open WebUI + mcpo), together with GridCraft's MCP server. Task: read a small range from GridCraft (`read_range`), then write a short report in WordCraft with a title, a table holding that data and a one-paragraph comment.

## What happened
The model did everything except the table: in its place it typed the sentence "Table with the data of the first quarter." An *empty* table works fine (`execute insert.table {rows, cols}`), but filling it means discovering caret and cell navigation commands and typing cell by cell, and a mid-size model gives up.

GridCraft solves the same problem with `write_range` (a 2-D `values` array, one call). WordCraft has no equivalent: `table.fromText` is close, but it needs a multi-paragraph selection first, which is hard for an agent to set up.

## Proposal
1. **Engine:** an optional `values` param on `insert.table`:
   `{"values": [["Month","Cases"],["January",12],["February",15]], "header"?: true, "style"?: string}`
   - rows/cols derived from `values` (cols = longest row); cells filled with the values as text; `header: true` makes the first row a repeating header row.
   - The cell-filling code already exists in `table::from_text` (`Table::new` + `para_block(Paragraph::with_text(..))`).
2. **MCP:** a thin `insert_table` tool wrapping it, mirroring GridCraft's `write_range`, and a mention in the `execute` tool description.

Being a command, it reaches the CLI, the control channel and MCP at once.

## Acceptance
- One `insert_table` call with a 2-D array produces a filled table at the caret; `inspect_document` shows the cell text.
- The table survives a .docx round trip and PDF export.
- Hostile params (non-array, ragged rows, more than 63 columns, huge arrays) return errors and never panic; `hostile_params_never_panic` stays green.

## Why it matters
Reports where the numbers come from a spreadsheet and the narrative from an agent.…

title: Comments in headers, footers, notes and text boxes are missing from the comment list, balloons and Next/Previous
author: squaredcow
body:
A comment anchored in a header (and, by the same code path, a footer, footnote, endnote or text box) is in the Comments pane, but:

- it has **no balloon** on the page, although its text is tinted as commented;
- `review.comments` reports it with `"anchor": null`, so **Go to** does nothing;
- **Next / Previous Comment** never reach it.

The likely cause is that `comment_list` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs`) scans only the body story. `list_comments`, `nav_comment` and the balloons (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`) all use that list.

### Reproduce (main at 86adfd3)

Steps: type "Body text with a comment on it.", select "comment", New Comment. Then Insert › Header "Header text", select it, New Comment. Close the header and press Ctrl+Home.

**Balloons:** "Header text" is tinted, but only the body comment gets a balloon.

![Header text tinted, only the body comment has a balloon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/squaredcow/wordcraft/proof-assets/comments-outside-body/main-1-balloons.png)

**Comments pane:** the header comment is listed, but its Go to has no anchor to go to.

![Comments pane lists both comments](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/squaredcow/wordcraft/proof-assets/comments-outside-body/main-2-pane.png)

**Commands** (`ui_shot` / `wordcraft-cli run --template blank --print`, same steps):

```
review.comments:     [{"id":0,"anchor":{"story":"body","path":[0],"off":17},…},
                      {"id":1,"anchor":null,"text":"Comment in the header",…}]
review.nextComment:  {"anchor":{"story":"body","path":[0],"off":17},…}
review.nextComment:  {"anchor":{"story":"body","path":[0],"off":17},…}   ← never reaches the header comment
```

### Expected

Comments in every story are listed with their anchor and get a balloon, and Go to and Next/Previous reach them in reading order.

Follow-up to #1345 / #1565.

— sent on behalf of @squaredcow by Claude Code

title: Comments: the pages between the first and last page of a comment aren't shaded
author: seif9116
body:
Split from #2314.

Seen in WordCraft 0.7.0 and on main (86adfd3), on Linux.

## Steps

1. In a new document, type enough paragraphs of made-up text ("Alpha paragraph one.", "Beta paragraph two." and so on) to fill four pages.
2. Select from the first page to the last and add a comment (Review › New Comment).

## What happens

The second and third pages aren't shaded at all, and stay plain until something on them changes.

## Expected

As in Word 365, every page of the range is shaded.

## Where

- Page pictures are cached by a fingerprint of the page's paragraphs (`page_content_key` in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`). Adding a comment changes none of the paragraphs on a page wholly inside the range, so that page is never drawn again.
- The shade is worked out one paragraph at a time from the markers inside it (`lines` in `crates/layout/src/display.rs`, #2314), so a page with no marker on it has nothing to shade.

title: Recover page opens after a clean close and renders black with unreadable buttons
author: python2121
body:
## What happened
On Steam Deck (SteamOS, KDE Plasma desktop mode), WordCraft reopened after a normal close and went straight to **File → Recover**, as if the previous session had ended uncleanly. It hadn't.

The Recover page then rendered in a broken dark style:
- The nav pane and page background are pure black, unlike the rest of Backstage.
- The two action buttons (**Continue without restoring**, **Refresh**) draw as blank white pills. Their labels can't be read.
- The page says **"No recovery copies."**, yet the auto-open only fires when `recovery_documents()` is non-empty. So either the list emptied between the check and the paint, or a stale copy triggered it and then vanished.

Screenshot (reporter's machine): `~/Pictures/Screenshots/Screenshot_20261015_191345.png`. It shows the black Recover page with the unlabeled white buttons.

## Likely causes
1. **Black fill is hard-coded, not themed.** `crates/ui-egui/src/backstage.rs` uses `egui::Color32::BLACK` for both the nav panel (~L36) and the page frame (~L139) when `backstage_page == "recover"` (from #586). The buttons keep the light theme's visuals, so the text ends up white on white. This isn't a KDE theme problem; colours should come from `theme::Tokens`.
2. **False "unsafe close" detection.** `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` (~L1824) opens Recover whenever `recovery_ready()` and `!recovery_documents().is_empty()` on first tick. Recovery copies don't seem to be cleared on a clean exit, possibly when the window is closed by the WM/KDE close button or by logout, so the next launch treats them as crash leftovers.

## Expected
- A clean close (window ✕, File → Close, quit) leaves no recovery copies, and the next launch opens normally.
- Recover only auto-opens when there really is something to restore, and it doesn't show "No recovery copies." after auto-opening.
- The Recover page uses theme tokens in light and dark themes. Every button label is readable.

## Acceptance

title: Discord button / hyperlinks: "No valid browsers detected" on SteamOS
author: python2121
body:
## What happened
Clicking the **Discord** title-bar button (or **Discord community** in Backstage) does nothing on Steam Deck. The log shows:

```
2026-10-16T02:14:08.500Z WARN  [main] egui_winit: Failed to open url: No valid browsers detected. You can specify one in BROWSER environment variable
```

The system does have a working default browser. Links open fine from other apps, and `xdg-open https://…` works.

## Where
- `ui.discord` sets `canvas.open_url` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` ~L1496). It's then opened through `ctx.open_url(egui::OpenUrl::new_tab(url))` (~L2034). egui-winit passes it to the `webbrowser` crate.
- The same path handles Ctrl+click hyperlinks in documents (`canvas.rs` ~L2289), so those are probably broken here too.

## Likely cause
The `webbrowser` crate's Linux detection doesn't find a browser on SteamOS. The default browser there is usually a Flatpak (Firefox/Chrome), which isn't on `PATH`. The app may also be running inside a distrobox/container, where `xdg-open` is a shim. When `BROWSER` is unset, `webbrowser` gives up instead of relying on `xdg-open` / the XDG Desktop Portal.

## Proposed fix
- On Linux/BSD, open URLs ourselves: try the `org.freedesktop.portal.OpenURI` portal, then `xdg-open`, then `gio open`, and only then fall back to `webbrowser`. Run it off the UI thread, and never panic.
- If every method fails, show a non-blocking notice with the URL and a Copy button, instead of only logging a warning.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Discord button and document hyperlinks open the default browser on SteamOS (Flatpak browser, `BROWSER` unset).
- [ ] Failure shows the URL to the user (copyable) instead of failing silently.

Environment: Steam Deck, SteamOS (kernel 6.18 neptune), KDE Plasma, build from `main` @ 86adfd3.

title: Agent API: expose position units and support guarded text replacement
author: david-priest
body:
We are using WordCraft 0.7.0 on macOS to revise a manuscript while its author reviews comments in the same document. Structured inspection, comment access and live editing make this workflow practical. However, a client-side position error produced incorrect edits in the visible document.
The agent calculated character offsets instead of UTF-8 byte offsets, including hidden comment markers. We recovered through Undo and verified restoration against a checkpoint. Correctly calculated byte offsets worked.
This request complements existing work:
- [#1302](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/issues/1302) proposes agent workflow guidance. Position handling should be covered there.
- Draft [#1432](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/1432) already addresses live attachment, independent selection and stale-target protection. Its documentation explicitly leaves atomic read–select–edit operations for future work.
- This is separate from the ambiguous-delivery and timeout problems in [#1326](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/issues/1326) and [#1331](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/issues/1331); neither was implicated in our incident.
Minimal reproduction
1. Create a paragraph containing Prefix β text. Strategy views show selections. End.
2. Select Strategy views show selections. and add a comment.
3. Inspect the document and retrieve document.paragraph.
In our installed version:
- Document inspection returns visible text without comment-marker characters.
- Paragraph details include U+FFFC placeholders for the comment’s start and end.
- The reported paragraph length is 58 bytes, including those markers.
- Replacing End. using offsets 54–58 works correctly.
A client deriving positions from the visible text, or using a language’s ordinary string length, can target the wrong content. The exposed select.range command schema says {anchor: Pos, focus: Pos} without explaining these units.

title: Regression/Bug: Right Alt (`AltGr`) triggers Ribbon / KeyTips navigation instead of inserting diacritics on Linux / Wayland (related to #1748)
author: mkarpik79
body:
Hi,

I would like to add crucial technical details and diagnostics regarding issue #1748 (inability to type Polish characters using Right Alt).

### Environment

* **OS:** Linux (openSUSE Tumbleweed, kernel 6.x)
* **Display Server:** Wayland
* **Architecture:** x86_64
* **Binary version:** 0.7.0 (fc419188)

---

### Root Cause Analysis

Under Linux with a Polish keyboard layout, pressing **Right Alt (`AltGr`)** generates:

* Key code: `108`
* Symbol: `sym: ISO_Level3_Shift (65027)`
* Modifier mask: **`Mod5`** (Level 3 shift) — **not `Mod1**`.

Here is the exact event captured via `wev` (Wayland Event Viewer) comparing Left Alt vs Right Alt:

**1. Left Alt (`Alt_L`) — correct menu modifier:**

```text
[wl_keyboard] key: key: 64; state: 1 (pressed); sym: Alt_L (65513)
[wl_keyboard] modifiers: depressed: 00000008: Mod1

```

**2. Right Alt (`ISO_Level3_Shift`) — diacritic composer:**

```text
[wl_keyboard] key: key: 108; state: 1 (pressed); sym: ISO_Level3_Shift (65027)
[wl_keyboard] modifiers: depressed: 00000080: Mod5

```

### The Problem in WordCraft

The application's event loop appears to trigger the Ribbon / KeyTips navigation accelerators by checking:

1. `event.physical_key == KeyCode::AltRight` (or treating both `AltLeft` and `AltRight` identically), or
2. `input.modifiers.alt()` without verifying whether `ISO_Level3_Shift` / `Mod5` is active.

Because of this:

1. Pressing `Right Alt` immediately grabs focus to the ribbon navigation.
2. The subsequent keypress (e.g. `s`, `l`, `z`) is intercepted as a ribbon accelerator rather than being combined into Unicode characters (`ś`, `ł`, `ż`).

---

### Suggested Fix

* **Strict KeyCode check:** Restrict ribbon / menu accelerator activation strictly to `KeyCode::AltLeft` (or when `sym == XK_Alt_L`).
* **Modifier validation:** If checking modifier states, ignore the Alt activation if `ModifiersState` includes `ISO_Level3_Shift` / `Mod5` / `AltGraph`.

This will allow users on European / multi-level keyboard layouts (…

title: DFKai-SB (標楷體, kaiu.ttf) renders with broken/misplaced strokes: TrueType "tricky font" needs glyph hinting programs executed
author: delphicchen
body:
## Summary

Text set in **DFKai-SB / 標楷體** (`kaiu.ttf`, the standard Traditional Chinese Kai font that ships with Windows and is used in a huge number of Taiwanese .docx files) renders with missing and misplaced strokes in WordCraft, both on screen and in `wordcraft-cli render` / PDF export. Characters such as 永, 的, 中, 文 come out visibly broken. The same text renders correctly in LibreOffice, browsers and every other FreeType-based app on the same machine.

## Cause

`kaiu.ttf` is a so-called **"tricky" font**. Its CJK glyphs are composites of a small set of stroke components. Each glyph carries TrueType bytecode (plus a ~37 KB `fpgm`) that scales and moves those components into place. Without running the glyph program, the components stay at their raw positions and the character falls apart.

For example (fontTools, `kaiu.ttf` version 5.02):

```
中  composite, 4+ components, 39 bytes of glyph instructions
永  composite, 4+ components, 60 bytes of glyph instructions
的  composite, 4+ components, 75 bytes of glyph instructions
```

FreeType keeps a hard-coded list of such fonts and **always runs the TrueType hinting interpreter for them, even when hinting is otherwise disabled** (`tt_check_trickyness` in `src/truetype/ttobjs.c`; family names include `DFKaiShu`, `DFKai-SB`, `DFKaiSho-SB`, `MingLiU`, `PMingLiU`, `DFHei`, `DFMincho`, `DLC`, ...). WordCraft does its own font loading and rasterising (fontdb + vello_cpu, no FreeType), and it looks like glyph programs are never executed, so these fonts break.

New-style `mingliu.ttc` / PMingLiU from current Windows renders fine. I only see the problem with DFKai-SB, but older MingLiU builds and the other DynaComware fonts on FreeType's list would be affected the same way.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install `kaiu.ttf` (from a Windows installation) into `/usr/local/share/fonts/` or `~/.local/share/fonts/`.
2. Create a document with the text `標楷體測試 永遠的中文字` and set the font to `標楷體` (or `DFKai-SB`). The result is the same with ei…

author: javierjrueda
body:
**Version:** WordCraft 0.7.0, macOS universal build (started with `--control 7981`), macOS 26

### What happens
When the WordCraft window is not the frontmost app, the control methods `ui.key` and `ui.text` (and the MCP `key` tool) return `{"queued": true}`, but nothing happens in the document. Pointer input works in the same state: `ui.click` on a ribbon tab switches tabs.

This affects agents driving the live app over MCP. These tools are normally called from a terminal or another app, so WordCraft is usually in the background.

### Steps (window behind another app)
```json
{"method": "engine.execute", "params": {"command": "select.text", "params": {"text": "Alcance", "occurrence": 1}}}
{"method": "ui.key", "params": {"key": "b", "cmd": true}}
```
- The reply is `{"queued": true}`, but the text is not bold and `ui.inspect` still reports `"dirty": false`.
- `ui.text {"text": "Z"}` with a selection does not type anything either.
- `ui.inspect` reports `"focused": false`. `ui.focus` returns `{}`, but `focused` stays `false` and the window is not raised.
- `ui.click {x, y}` on the Insert tab switches the ribbon to Insert, so pointer injection works.
- `engine.execute format.bold` works.

### Same steps, WordCraft frontmost
After `osascript -e 'tell application "WordCraft" to activate'`, a double-click on the word with `ui.click` followed by `ui.key {"key":"b","cmd":true}` makes it bold, and `focused` is `true`.

### Notes
- `keys::global_shortcuts` should handle Mod+B even when the canvas isn't focused (`is_global_shortcut` is true for `command`). So the synthetic key events seem to be dropped, or never reach `ctx.input().events`, while the OS window is inactive. They are queued in `raw_input_hook`.
- Possible fix: route `ui.key` with modifiers through the keymap directly (`dispatch`) and `ui.text` to the canvas, instead of going through egui input that depends on window focus. Alternatively, make `ui.focus` really give focus to the canvas without OS window focus. At …

title: DOCX save drops block content controls with w:docPartObj (Word's Table of Contents wrapper)
author: moldluca
body:
## Summary

Saving a `.docx` drops block-level content controls whose `w:sdtPr` holds a `w:docPartObj` (building-block gallery), such as the `Table of Contents` wrapper that Word puts around every inserted TOC. The `w:sdt` / `w:sdtPr` / `w:sdtContent` wrapper disappears and its paragraphs are written as plain body paragraphs. The TOC field inside survives.

A plain rich-text block content control (`w:alias` + `w:tag` + `w:richText`) with the same content is kept, so the loss looks specific to `docPartObj`.

## Version

`wordcraft-cli 0.7.0`, macOS universal build.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Build the minimal document below (stdlib Python, nothing else needed).
2. `wordcraft-cli convert toc-sdt.docx toc-sdt-rt.docx`
3. Count `w:sdt` elements in `word/document.xml` of both files.

```python

W = 'xmlns:w="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main"'
ct = '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?><Types xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/content-types"><Default Extension="rels" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-package.relationships+xml"/><Default Extension="xml" ContentType="application/xml"/><Override PartName="/word/document.xml" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document.main+xml"/></Types>'
rels = '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?><Relationships xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships"><Relationship Id="rId1" Type="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/officeDocument" Target="word/document.xml"/></Relationships>'

title: macOS: offer and install app updates when a Craft app opens (community tool: CraftUpdater)
author: ParthLad03
body:
## Summary

On macOS, the Craft apps don't tell you when a new version is out, and updating means downloading the new `.dmg` and dragging it into Applications again. (PdfCraft's **Help ▸ Check for updates** reports a new version and links to the release page, but doesn't install it. WordCraft and DeckCraft have nothing.) This is the macOS side of #201.

I built a small tool that fixes this for every Craft app at once, and I'd like to offer it to Artcraft: **https://github.com/ParthLad03/craft-updater**

Would you be willing to adopt it as a repository under `storytold`? I can transfer the repo to you, or adapt it to wherever you'd rather it lived.

## What it does

- When a Craft app (any bundle ID `ai.storyteller.*`) **starts**, CraftUpdater asks GitHub for that app's latest release (`storytold/<app>`).
- If it's newer, a popup asks right away: **Update** or **Cancel**. Nothing is downloaded unless you click Update.
- **Update** downloads `<app>-<version>-macos-universal.dmg` with a progress window while you keep working. Once it passes the checks below, a second popup offers **Restart Now** or **Later**.
  - **Restart Now** quits the app the normal way (so it asks to save), swaps in the new version and reopens it.
  - **Later** installs it when you quit the app.
- **Nothing runs in the background.** Each app starts a fresh log file in `~/Library/Application Support/<App>/logs/` at launch. A `launchd` agent watches those folders (`WatchPaths`) and starts CraftUpdater only then. It exits when it's done.

## Security

The installed app is replaced only after **all** of these pass on the exact copy that gets installed:

1. SHA-256 matches the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`
2. Same bundle ID as the installed app
3. `codesign --verify --deep --strict`
4. TeamIdentifier is Artcraft's (`DJ6XS33FX8`)
5. Gatekeeper accepts it (`spctl --assess`, i.e. notarized)

If anything fails, the installed app is left untouched. The swap is a single `replaceItemAt` on the same volume. The t…

title: Recovery: a document with large pictures never gets a recovery copy, and each failed attempt writes 256 MB
author: arcanii
body:
On `main` (eae2421), a document whose recovery snapshot is over `MAX_BYTES` (256 MiB of JSON) never gets a recovery copy. Each attempt fails at the cap, deletes its temporary file, and is tried again at the next tick. So WordCraft writes 256 MB to disk every 11–12 s for as long as the document has unsaved changes, even after typing stops.

**How to see it.** A synthetic `.docx` of 92 MB: 89 pages, 20 PNG pictures of 2400×1800. A release build of the desktop app with a profile of its own (`WORDCRAFT_PROFILE_DIR`), driven over the control channel on macOS 27.0.1 (Apple M3 Max). Bytes written come from `proc_pid_rusage` (`ri_diskio_byteswritten`).

| | Written to disk in a minute | Recovery copy at the end |
|---|---|---|
| Opened, not edited | 0 MB | none needed |
| Typing for a minute | 1,280 MB, 256 MB every 11–12 s | none |
| Typing for 5 s, then nothing | 1,280 MB | none |
| A 74-page text document, typing | 1 MB | made |

The error is shown on File › Recover. Nothing goes to the log. Memory is fine: the footprint while typing stays at what opening took.

**Why.**
- **The JSON is too big.** As `docs/recovery.md` says, "JSON stores binary parts as byte arrays", at about 3.6 characters a byte. This document's 92 MB of pictures need about 330 MB, so `Limited` stops the write at 256 MB.
- **A failure retries forever.** `Recovery::poll` clears `revision` on the error, so the next `tick` writes again whether the document changed or not.
- **No previous copy to fall back on.** `docs/recovery.md` says "Over-limit writes report an error and retain the previous valid copy", but a document that never fitted has no previous copy.

So a document with more than about 70 MB of pictures, or other binary parts, has no crash protection.

**What the open PRs change.**
- **#2101** stores parts as base64, about 1.33 characters a byte. This document would fit, at about 125 MB. But documents with more than about 190 MB of parts would still fail the same way. And every snapshot that succ…

body:
## Summary

On Arch Linux, allow Wordcraft to automatically discover all system fonts that have been indexed by `fc-cache`, so users don’t need to add fonts one by one manually.

## Use case

I’m using Arch Linux and have already built the font index with `fc-cache`. Currently I have to manually add each font to Wordcraft. It would be much more convenient if the app could read the font list from fontconfig automatically on startup or via a one-click refresh button.

## Proposed solution

1. Auto enumerate fonts from fontconfig (using `fc-list` / fontconfig library) on Linux (Arch included).

Many Linux desktop apps use fontconfig to get system fonts natively. Reusing fontconfig can avoid handling font file paths manually and keep font list in sync with system.

title: Feature request: expose the command API to JavaScript in the web build (WebMCP / browser agents)
author: johancoppens
body:
## What

Let JavaScript on the page drive the web build with the same commands the control channel and the
MCP server already use, for example a function exported from the wasm module:

```js
const result = await window.wordcraft.runCommand({ command: "text.insert", params: { text: "Hello" } });
```

It would take the same JSON request as the control protocol and resolve with the same JSON
response, including errors. Next to `runCommand`, a `listCommands()` (the ids, params and help that
`tools/list` already gives agents) and `inspectDocument()` would cover what an agent needs to work
without screenshots.

## Why

WordCraft is built for agents: every action is a command, and `wordcraft-cli mcp --connect` drives
the running desktop app. In the browser there is no way in. The web build only exports its start
function, and a page can't open a TCP port, so an agent working in the browser has to read the
canvas from screenshots and click by coordinates.

Browsers are getting a standard place to plug this in: **WebMCP**, where a page registers tools that
the browser's own agent can call (`document.modelContext`, formerly `navigator.modelContext`; behind
a flag and an origin trial in Chrome, with Gemini in Chrome announced as a consumer). With a JS entry
point, a few lines on the hosting page can register WordCraft's commands as WebMCP tools. Gemini in
Chrome, Claude in Chrome or any other browser agent could then write and edit documents in the tab
the user is already looking at, with no install and no local server.

Our use case: we host the web builds of the Craft apps for a school's Chromebooks, where nothing can
be installed. The desktop MCP server can't run there, so this would be the only way for agents to
use the apps on those devices.

## A possible shape

- On desktop, `control_server.rs` turns lines from the TCP socket into `ControlRequest`s on a
  channel that the app drains every frame. The web build could fill the same kind of channel from an
  exported `#[wa…

title: Dutch spelling and hyphenation (nl, nl-BE, nl-NL)
author: johancoppens
body:
This works out the spelling part of storytold/artcraft#2217 (Dutch missing in the interface and in spelling and grammar) for WordCraft. The same applies to DeckCraft and DesignCraft.

We're a school group in Flanders serving the web builds to our students' Chromebooks. Students write in Dutch, so the spelling check is one of the first things they'll notice.

WordCraft already checks spelling by each run's language (English and Polish, with more languages in `crates/proof`) and hyphenates with per-language patterns in `assets/hyphenation` (English, Italian, Polish, Portuguese). This asks to add Dutch to both.

## What's needed

- **A Dutch spelling dictionary.** The official spelling is shared by Belgium and the Netherlands (Taalunie, the Groene Boekje), but each region has its own words. Runs tagged `nl-BE` would accept Belgian words, `nl-NL` Netherlands words, and plain `nl` the shared list.
- **Dutch hyphenation patterns**, the same for both regions.
- **Dutch grammar checks** later, if the grammar layer that English and Polish have can take another language.

## Possible sources

The OpenTaal word list (opentaal.org) is the usual open source for Dutch spelling and marks regional words. Its licence would need checking against the suite's rules for bundled data. Dutch hyphenation patterns are also published openly (for example in the TeX hyphenation patterns).

## Help offered

We can test the spelling check with Flemish texts once it's in.

title: [Feature Request] Support for Field Codes (Ctrl+F9 / Shift+F9) and DISPLAYBARCODE for QR Code generation
author: joseferreira-alt
body:
### Describe the Feature
I would like to request support for Microsoft Word's dynamic field codes, specifically the `Ctrl + F9` (insert field), `Shift + F9` / `Alt + F9` (toggle field codes), and `F9` (update field) shortcuts. 

### What is the specific use case?
My primary goal is to natively generate **QR Codes** inside documents without using third-party add-ins, exactly how it works in MS Word using the `DISPLAYBARCODE` field syntax:
`{ DISPLAYBARCODE "https://example.com" QR \q 3 }`

### Why is this important for WordCraft?
WordCraft aims for complete parity with Microsoft Word. Many users rely on the native `DISPLAYBARCODE` feature to dynamically generate QR codes for links, marketing materials, and dynamic paperwork. 

To make this work seamlessly, WordCraft needs:
1. Keyboard shortcut listeners for handling field brackets `{ }` via `Ctrl + F9`.
2. Toggling logic via `Shift + F9` / `Alt + F9` to switch between code view and the rendered element.
3. A rendering engine extension (or a Rust crate dependency like `qrcode`) to draw the QR code image when `DISPLAYBARCODE ... QR` is triggered inside a field.

Thank you for the amazing work on this project!

title: Draw Table and Eraser: strokes, outside borders and other differences from Word
author: rabis7575
body:
**Description**
Table Layout › Draw › Eraser works for a single click between two cells, but otherwise it doesn't behave like Word's eraser. Checked against Word (2019, Windows) with a new 4×4 table:

| | Word | WordCraft now |
|---|---|---|
| Drag | A thin red rectangle follows the pointer and every cell border it touches shows thick; on release they are all erased, in one undo step. Across a row's vertical lines the row's cells merge; along a horizontal line each column merges down on its own; corner to corner the cells become one; down the table's outside that side hides | Only the point where the button is released counts: one border |
| A border on the table's outside (also in a 1×1 table) | Hidden (its gridline shows) | "there's no border between two cells there" |
| Hovering, button up | Nothing is highlighted | The border under the pointer turns red |
| Esc during a drag | Drops the drag; the eraser stays on | Turns the eraser off |
| A click off the table | Turns the eraser off | An error on the status bar; the eraser stays on |

title: Mail merge: letters 2+ start 24 pt lower because the record break is appended to the last paragraph
author: Xharig
body:
**Version:** WordCraft 0.7.0 (latest release), Windows 11 x64, portable build

### What happens
After **Finish & Merge** every letter except the first starts lower on its page. In a three-record merge the first heading is at y = 64 pt on page 1 and at y = 88 pt on pages 2 and 3 (measured on `wordcraft-cli render … --page N --scale 1`). For letters printed for window envelopes this moves the address out of the window.

### Cause (from the merged .docx)
The merge separates records with a page break **inside the last run of the previous record's last paragraph**:

```xml
<w:p><w:pPr><w:spacing w:before="0" w:after="480"/>…</w:pPr>
  <w:r>…<w:t>Xharig</w:t><w:br w:type="page"/></w:r>
</w:p>
<w:p><w:pPr><w:spacing w:before="0" w:after="360"/>…</w:pPr> <!-- first paragraph of record 2 -->
```

The rest of that paragraph continues on the next page, so record 2 begins below it. The offset (24 pt) equals that paragraph's space after (`w:after="480"`).

### Counter-test
Same merged file, but the two `<w:br w:type="page"/>` removed and `<w:pageBreakBefore/>` added to the first paragraph of records 2 and 3 → all three letters start at y = 64 pt.

### Expected
Every merged letter is laid out exactly like the first. Word's *Finish & Merge → Edit Individual Documents* separates the records with *Section Break (Next Page)*, so each letter starts on a fresh page with nothing carried over.

### Steps
1. Blank document, letter with merge fields (`mailings.start {kind: letters}`, `mailings.recipients {path: recipients.csv}` with 3 rows, `mailings.insertField`), last paragraph with space after > 0
2. `mailings.finish {path: merged.docx}`
3. Render pages 1 and 2 → page 2 content starts lower by the last paragraph's space after

title: Recovery: a document with more than about 70 MB of pictures never gets a recovery copy
author: arcanii
body:
Split from #2456.

On `main` (eae2421), a document whose recovery snapshot is over `MAX_BYTES` (256 MiB of JSON) never gets a recovery copy. With pictures as byte arrays, that is any document with more than about 70 MB of pictures or other binary parts. It has no crash protection at all.

**How to see it.** A synthetic `.docx` of 92 MB: 89 pages, 20 PNG pictures of 2400×1800. A release build of the desktop app with a profile of its own (`WORDCRAFT_PROFILE_DIR`), driven over the control channel on macOS 27.0.1. Typing into it for a minute leaves the recovery folder empty. A 74-page text document typed into the same way gets its copy. The error is shown on File › Recover; nothing goes to the log.

**Why.** As `docs/recovery.md` says, "JSON stores binary parts as byte arrays", at about 3.6 characters a byte. This document's pictures need about 330 MB, so `Limited` stops the write at 256 MB and the temporary file is deleted. The same document says "Over-limit writes report an error and retain the previous valid copy", but a document that never fitted has no previous copy.

**#2101** stores parts as base64, about 1.33 characters a byte. This document would then fit, at about 125 MB, but documents with more than about 190 MB of parts would still get no copy. Every copy would also still write, then read back and decode, every picture at every interval.

**A proposal: keep each binary part once per record.**
- **Parts as files.** Each media and passthrough part becomes a file in the record folder, `parts/<sha256>`. It is written once (temporary file, sync, rename), the first time a snapshot needs it. The JSON names it (`{"part": "<sha256>", "len": N}`) instead of holding the bytes.
- **Small snapshots.** A snapshot then writes the document's structure plus any parts new since the last generation: a few hundred KB per snapshot while typing into this document, instead of everything.
- **Cheaper validation.** Decode the JSON and check that every named part exists with the righ…

title: Recovery: a failed snapshot is retried at every interval, writing up to 256 MB each time
author: arcanii
body:
Split from #2456.

On `main` (eae2421), a recovery snapshot that fails is tried again at every interval for as long as the document has unsaved changes, even if nothing has changed since. When the failure is the size limit (`MAX_BYTES`, 256 MiB), each attempt writes the full 256 MB before failing.

**How to see it.** A synthetic `.docx` of 92 MB with 20 pictures, whose snapshot is over the limit (see #2624). A release build of the desktop app on macOS 27.0.1, with a profile of its own (`WORDCRAFT_PROFILE_DIR`), driven over the control channel. Bytes written come from `proc_pid_rusage` (`ri_diskio_byteswritten`).

| | Written to disk in a minute |
|---|---|
| Opened, not edited | 0 MB |
| Typing for a minute | 1,280 MB: 256 MB every 11–12 s |
| Typing for 5 s, then nothing | 1,280 MB: 256 MB every 11–12 s |

The writes go on until the document is saved or closed.

**Why.** `Recovery::poll` sets `revision` to `None` when the worker reports an error. `tick` writes whenever the document is dirty and `revision` differs from the session's, so a failed snapshot is repeated every `INTERVAL`, changes or not. `docs/recovery.md` says snapshots happen "only when its revision changes".

**#2102** paces snapshots by what they cost, failed ones included. The attempts would come less often, but they would still go on.

**A suggestion:** don't try again after a failure until the document changes, by keeping `revision` when the error comes from the snapshot itself (a size limit, the folder or disk budget). A document that can't be copied then costs one failed attempt per change, not one every interval. Failures that may clear by themselves, such as a lock held for a moment, could keep retrying, paced as #2102 does.

Not checked: Windows and Linux. The logic is the same on every platform.

### Title:

### Problem / Context
When moving documents or citation libraries over from Microsoft Word to Wordcraft, users currently have to re-enter references and citation metadata manually. title: Spell checking for Greek (el-GR)
author: TrakterDaok
body:
## Summary

Greek (el-GR) can be selected as a document/proofing language, but no spell checking happens for Greek text: misspelled Greek words are not underlined and the spelling check reports nothing. I'd like to request Greek spelling support.

## Environment

- WordCraft 0.7.0 (fc419188), AppImage `wordcraft-0.7.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage`
- Ubuntu, GNOME
- Greek Hunspell dictionary installed: `hunspell-el` (`/usr/share/hunspell/el_GR.aff`, `/usr/share/hunspell/el_GR.dic`)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install `hunspell-el` (`sudo apt install hunspell-el`).
2. Open WordCraft, set the language to Greek (Review → Language → Greek).
3. Type a misspelled Greek word, e.g. `καλημερσ` or `σπιτη`.

**Expected:** the word is underlined and suggestions are offered, using the installed el_GR dictionary.
**Actual:** no spelling errors are reported for Greek text.

From what I can tell, the Hunspell-based spelling currently covers only a few languages (English, Polish, Bulgarian, Portuguese, Italian, Croatian), and the system el_GR dictionary is not used even though the dictionary search paths include `/usr/share/hunspell`.

## Things specific to Greek worth handling

- **Accents in capitals:** Greek text in all caps is normally written without accents (`ΚΑΛΗΜΕΡΑ` for `καλημέρα`). Words in capitals should be matched while ignoring the tonos/dialytika, otherwise every all-caps word will be flagged.
- **Final sigma:** `ς` at the end of a word and `σ` elsewhere; case-folding should treat `Σ`/`σ`/`ς` correctly.
- **Elision with apostrophe:** forms like `σ' αγαπώ`, `απ' όλα`, `τ' όνομα` are correct and shouldn't be flagged.
- **Greek question mark:** `;` (and U+037E) ends a sentence, and `·` (ano teleia, U+0387) is punctuation, not part of a word.
- **Hyphenation:** a Greek hyphenation dictionary (`hyph_el_GR.dic`, package `hyphen-el`) is also available if hyphenation support is added for Greek.

Thank you for WordCraft!

title: LanguageTool API key: credential-store calls block the UI thread (Keychain prompt freezes the window)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Follow-up to #2627 (#764).

## Problem

#2627 keeps the LanguageTool API key in the system's credential store through the `keyring` crate (`crates/ui-egui/src/secrets.rs`, `OsStore`). Every store call runs on the egui UI thread and waits for the answer:

- `WordApp::load_secrets` calls `store.get(LANGUAGE_TOOL_KEY)` from `apply_prefs`, i.e. at startup in `load_prefs` (`apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs`).
- `WordApp::sync_secrets` calls `store.set(...)` or `store.delete(...)`. It runs from `save_prefs`, which also runs when the window closes.
- `secrets::os_store()` calls `keyring::Entry::store_status()` while `services()` is built.

These calls can take a long time:

- **macOS:** the Keychain may show "WordCraft wants to use your confidential information…" and wait until the user clicks. Until then the window can't redraw.
- **Linux/BSD:** the Secret Service goes over D-Bus. A slow or locked keyring (GNOME Keyring unlock prompt, KWallet starting up, a hung D-Bus) blocks the window until it answers or times out.
- **Windows:** usually fast, but the same blocking path.

To the user it looks like WordCraft froze, at startup, after changing the key in File › Options, or when closing.

## Proposal

Move the store calls off the UI thread:

1. A small background worker (a thread with a channel, like `wordcraft_languagetool::Worker`) owns the `SecretStore` and runs `get` / `set` / `delete`.
2. The UI sends it a request and goes on. Each frame it polls for results, and asks for a repaint when one arrives.
3. While a request is in flight, `LtKeyPlace` shows a pending state. File › Options shows "Saving the API key…" (or "Reading…"), and LanguageTool checking waits for the key instead of running without it.
4. When the call fails, the result comes back as today's `LtKeyError` (`Store`, `NotRemoved`, `Lost`), and File › Options shows the message. The key stays in `ui.json` as it does now. A failure is never fatal.
5. `ui.json` is written only after the store confirms a move (`languag…

Part of #2669 (shared root cause: `odt::export` writes from the reduced `Flow` model, so this can't be fixed inside the current writer without carrying more of the document through `Flow`).

title: Parity: RTL paragraphs in HTML, ODT and RTF (formats.rtl)
author: vangel76
body:
Word exports a right-to-left paragraph (Word's `Left-to-Right / Right-to-Left Text Direction`, OOXML `w:bidi`) as `dir="rtl"` in HTML, `style:writing-mode="rl-tb"` in ODT and `\dir\rtldir` in RTF, and reads them back. WordCraft's `doc.para.bidi`/section RTL exists but the text formats drop it silently: an RTL Hebrew/Arabic paragraph copied through HTML or pasted from an .odt/.rtf file loses its direction.

Plan:
- `wordcraft_formats::model` carries a paragraph's RTL flag
- html: write/read `dir="rtl"` on paragraph elements
- odt: write/read `style:writing-mode="rl-tb"`
- rtf: write/read `\dir\rtldir`
- round-trip regression tests in `crates/formats`

title: Parity: tracked style-definition changes (styles.modify, w:stylePrChange)
author: vangel76
body:
Gap #5 (formatting revisions, #41) in docs/gaps.md: the rest it names as missing is tracked style-definition changes.

## What happens today

Track Changes is on, and Modify Style (or Update Style to Match Selection) changes what a style means, so every paragraph using the style changes. Nothing is recorded: `w:stylePrChange` (ECMA-376 §17.13.5.25) is not read, not saved, and style edits while tracking make no tracked change. Saving a tracked document to .docx shows styles.xml without any `w:stylePrChange`, and Word shows no revision for the style.

Word records the style definition as it was before the change: accepting keeps the new definition, rejecting restores the old one.

## Steps to reproduce (synthetic)

1. New document, `review.trackChanges {"value": true}`.
2. `styles.modify {"style": "Heading1", "chr": {"bold": true}}` — Heading 1 becomes bold.
3. `review.changes` lists no change; `text.insert` + `review.acceptSelection` shows nothing to accept for the style.
4. Save as .docx: `word/styles.xml` has no `w:stylePrChange`.

## Plan

- `Style` gains `fmt_change` (the style as it was before the change, keyed by the same revision as other formatting revisions).
- `fmt_revisions::record` compares the style sheets before and after a mutating command, so `styles.modify` and `styles.updateToMatch` (and any command that edits a style definition) record the change; a later change by the same author keeps the definition before their first one, as Word does.
- Accept/reject: accepting keeps the current definition; rejecting restores the old one. `review.changes` lists the change at the document start (like table changes), so the Reviewing Pane, navigation and balloons show it.
- DOCX: `w:stylePrChange` (its `w:id`/`w:author`/`w:date` and the `w:style` before it) is read and written, reusing the existing style writer/reader.

I am working on this. PR follows.

title: SmartArt Text Pane: Tab does not demote items although the Demote button works
author: earlvanze
body:
The SmartArt Text Pane does not demote an item when Tab is pressed, while the Demote button works. Reported on Arch Linux with Hyprland; application version was not provided. This is a user report corroborated by source inspection, not a locally reproduced UI test.

Source report: <https://discord.com/channels/1359579021108842617/1558921592585715862/1560984996536262738>

Steps:
1. Insert an editable SmartArt graphic with multiple items and open its Text Pane.
2. Focus an item that can be demoted (for example, the second top-level item).
3. Press Tab, then compare with clicking Demote.

Expected: Tab demotes the focused item, and Shift+Tab promotes it, respecting the existing hierarchy limits and preserving editing focus.
Actual reported: Tab does not demote; the Demote button works.

Current upstream `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs_smart_art.rs::text_pane` handles Enter and exposes Promote/Demote buttons, but has no Tab/Shift+Tab handling. Inspected source blob: `544720b012967f136e3467bd4dae08bc79222bd8`.

Related work: #503 introduced the pane. Open PRs #2170 and #2512 address typing/shape selection, and #2365 addresses identifiers and whitespace; none covers this shortcut in the reviewed changes. Issue #2467 concerns selecting/editing SmartArt elements, which is distinct from keyboard demotion in the working text pane.

Suggested acceptance checks: Tab/Shift+Tab dispatch the existing SmartArt level commands for the focused item, preserve its text/focus, respect first-item/depth limits, and support undo without editing document text outside the pane.

title: DOCX: a missing font ignores the font table's w:altName (Word draws Museo Sans 300 in Calibri, WordCraft in Arial: 53 pages vs 26)
author: Nghiathan13
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @Nghiathan13._

**Version:** `main` at `eae2421`, `wordcraft-cli` on Windows 11. Reference: Microsoft Word 2024 for Windows (16.0.17932), exporting to PDF.

## Problem

When a document asks for a font that isn't installed, Word uses the alternate name the document's font table gives for it (`w:font/w:altName`, ECMA-376 §17.8.3.1). WordCraft never reads `w:altName`, so it falls back to its own generic list and the text is set in a different face. Line breaks and page counts then move.

## Real-world file

[`go_math_grade4_guide/input.docx`](https://github.com/sverrejb/docxide-pdf/blob/main/tests/fixtures/scraped/go_math_grade4_guide/input.docx) from docxide-pdf's scraped corpus (Apache-2.0). Its body text is in `Museo Sans 300`, which isn't installed, and the font table says:

```xml
<w:font w:name="Museo Sans 300"><w:altName w:val="Calibri"/>…<w:family w:val="modern"/>…</w:font>
```

| | Font used for the body (embedded in the PDF) | Pages |
|---|---|---|
| Word 2024 | Calibri | **26** |
| WordCraft | Arial | **53** |

## Synthetic reproduction

Three paragraphs of the same original text, each in a font no machine has:

| Paragraph | Font table entry | Word 2024 draws it in | WordCraft draws it in |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `WordCraft Missing Face A`, `altName` Courier New, family modern | **Courier New** | Arial |
| B | `WordCraft Missing Face B`, `altName` Times New Roman, family **swiss** | **Times New Roman** | Arial |
| C (control) | `WordCraft Missing Face C`, no `altName`, family swiss | Calibri | Arial |

B shows that `altName` takes precedence over the font's family class. (Word still reports the requested name, `WordCraft Missing Face A/B/C`, as the run's font; only the rendering uses the substitute.)

The fixture is a minimal package (`document.xml`, `fontTable.xml`, `settings.xml` with compatibility mode 15); the font table is:

title: Parity: Chart Design — axis and series formatting (chart.axis, chart.series)
author: vangel76
body:
## Parity: Chart Design — axis and series formatting (`chart.axis`, `chart.series`)

Gap 13 in `docs/gaps.md` ("Charts and SmartArt editing") says charts WordCraft makes are editable,
but there is **no axis formatting and no series formatting**: axis titles, axis minimum/maximum,
tick-label number formats, gridlines and tick labels on or off, axis lines, series fill, line
width, markers, smooth lines and per-series data labels are all missing — `crates/engine/src/cmd/chart.rs`
has only type, data, title, legend and dataLabels, and the writer emits fixed defaults for the axes.

Word's Chart Design tab has Add Chart Element ▸ Axes, ▸ Axis Titles, ▸ Gridlines and Format ▸ Format
Current Selection (series). These are the formatting power users reach for.

## Plan (clean-room, from ECMA-376 Part 1 §21.2 and public OOXML docs)

1. Model (`crates/doc/src/chart.rs`): `ChartSpec` gains a category axis and a value axis

title: Home › Borders in a table draws paragraph borders inside each cell instead of cell borders
author: rabis7575
body:
With the caret or a selection in a table, Home › Paragraph › Borders (Bottom, Top, All, Outside…) gives each paragraph in the cells its own border, drawn inside the cell and offset from the table's grid. Expected: the lines go on the cells, as Table Design › Borders (`table.borders`) does. Use: a line under a header row or a box around a few cells straight from the Home tab.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Insert › Table, 3×3.
2. Select the second row (or put the caret in B2).
3. Home › Paragraph › Borders ▾ › All Borders (or Bottom Border, Outside Borders…).

Result: every cell of the row gets short lines of its own inside it, a little in from the cell's edges, so the table looks doubled. The cells' borders don't change; the paragraphs get `w:pBdr` on save.

## Not the same as
- #2428 — the **Borders and Shading… dialog** in a table (Apply to Cell / Table, the button in Table Properties). This issue is about the **quick items of the Borders menu**, which don't go through the dialog.
- #1279 — paragraphs **outside tables**: an outside border over several paragraphs draws lines between them (fixed in layout by #1172). Here the paragraph border is the wrong thing to set in the first place.

## Cause
The Home menu runs `para.borders` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/para.rs`, `fn borders`), which always sets paragraph borders (`ParaProps::borders`), also in a table cell. The layout draws them around the paragraph, inside the cell margins.

## What would fix it
- In `para.borders`, when the selection is in a table (caret in a cell, or cells selected), apply the side to the cells instead, by handing the call to `table.borders` with the same `kind`, `width` and `color` (the Home kinds map one to one; `inside` = inside horizontal and vertical). `horizontalLine` and `sides` stay paragraph borders.
- Calling `table.borders` through the command registry keeps the change inside `para.rs`. The ribbon (`ribbon.rs`) and `cmd/table.rs` don't need to change, and several open PRs touch both (#2012…

title: Layout: no line break after a hyphen before a digit (Word breaks "2016-" / "2022"; WordCraft moves "2016-2022" whole or splits it inside the number)
author: Nghiathan13
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @Nghiathan13._

**Version:** `main` at `eae2421`, `wordcraft-cli` on Windows 11. Reference: Microsoft Word 2024 for Windows (16.0.17932), exporting to PDF.

## Problem

Word can break a line right after a hyphen-minus (`-`, U+002D) that is followed by a digit. WordCraft never breaks there. A range like `2016-2022` moves to the next line as one piece, and when it doesn't fit there either, it is split inside the number (`2016-202` / `2`) where Word breaks after the hyphen.

## Real-world file

[`transition_to_work_deed/input.docx`](https://github.com/sverrejb/docxide-pdf/blob/main/tests/fixtures/scraped/transition_to_work_deed/input.docx) from docxide-pdf's scraped corpus (Apache-2.0). Its title is "Transition to Work Deed 2016-2022":

| | Line 1 | Line 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Word 2024 | Transition to Work Deed 2016- | 2022 |
| WordCraft | Transition to Work Deed | 2016-2022 |

Across the 159 files of that corpus, Word's PDFs break after a `-` followed by a digit at least 19 times in 10 documents: section numbers (`36-12(2) and 104-` / `1AA(2)`), file references (`538-04-1-1-2/596-` / `24-69`) and URLs. WordCraft can make none of these breaks.

## Synthetic reproduction

One paragraph per width: 24 pt text, the right indent growing by 60 twips per paragraph. Each line break pattern seen across the sweep, leaving out the narrowest widths where both programs break between characters:

| Text | Word 2024 | WordCraft |
|---|---|---|
| `Deed 2016-2022` | `Deed 2016-` / `2022` → `Deed` / `2016-2022` → `Deed` / `2016-` / `2022` | `Deed` / `2016-2022` → `Deed` / `2016-202` / `2` |
| `Deed abcd-2022` | `Deed abcd-` / `2022` → `Deed` / `abcd-2022` → `Deed` / `abcd-` / `2022` | `Deed` / `abcd-2022` → `Deed` / `abcd-202` / `2` → `abcd-20` / `22` |

title: Home › Borders: the menu has no icons, and the button always applies Bottom Border instead of the last border chosen
author: Nghiathan13
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @Nghiathan13._

**Version:** `main` at `eae2421`.

## Problem

Home › Paragraph › Borders (`crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs`, the `split(… "borders" …)` call):

1. **The drop-down is text only.** Bottom, Top, Left, Right, No, All, Outside and Inside Borders are plain labels, so you have to read each one to find the side you want. In Word each choice has a small picture of the box with that side drawn. The menu's own button already has an icon (`"borders"` in `crates/ui-egui/src/icons.rs`: a dotted grid with the bottom edge in the accent colour), but its entries don't.
2. **The button always applies Bottom Border.** Its command is fixed at `para.borders {"kind": "bottom"}`. In Word the button takes on the last border chosen from its menu and applies that one, so the same border can be put on several paragraphs with one click each. WordCraft already does this for the Shading button next to it (`app.canvas.last_shading`, `Remember::Shading`).

## Proposed

- Eight original icons drawn in code in `icons.rs`, in the same style as the existing `borders` icon (20×20 grid, a dotted box, the chosen sides in the accent colour): bottom, top, left, right, none, all, outside, inside. No external asset files, so nothing new for `ATTRIBUTION.md`.
- Each menu entry shows its icon. That needs a menu item with an icon; #2142 adds such a helper (`mi_icon`) for the Shapes menu, and I'll reuse it rather than add a second one.
- The button remembers the last kind chosen (default Bottom, as now), applies it, and shows that kind's icon, like Shading remembers its colour.
- Horizontal Line and Borders and Shading… keep their current behaviour.

Light and dark themes checked with `ui_shot`.

## Not in scope

- Table Design › Borders (`table.borders`), which #2204 is reworking.
- Home › Borders inside a table (#2710).

title: Windows: AccessKit panic "Focused ID is not in the node list" closes the window
author: lawlabs
body:
## What happened

On Windows the WordCraft window exits with a panic in AccessKit. The document is not what fails. The same panic happened on the stock sample window, including while that window was sitting idle.

```
panic at accesskit_consumer-0.35.0\src\tree.rs:71:13:
Focused ID #5743185116967667151 is not in the node list
```

The process then exits with code 101.

## Environment

- Windows 10/11 (win32 10.0.26300)
- WordCraft 0.7.0, upstream commit `eae2421` (2026-10-15, "Merge pull request #2307 from dylanmtaylor/ci/nix-workflow")
- egui / eframe 0.36.2
- accesskit_consumer 0.35.0
- `eframe` is built with the `accesskit` feature (`apps/wordcraft/Cargo.toml`)
- Graphics: DirectX 12, Intel Iris Xe

## When it happened

The window was started with the sample document (`wordcraft --sample`). The panic showed up more than once, with no single click that always causes it:

- about 18 seconds after launch
- about 4 minutes after launch
- after the sample window had been open for about 7 hours, with no command in the log immediately before the panic

Log excerpt from the long run (`%APPDATA%\WordCraft\logs\wordcraft.log`):

```
2026-10-17T09:07:16.404Z INFO  wordcraft: WordCraft 0.7.0 (dev)
2026-10-17T16:11:13.572Z ERROR wordcraft::logging: panic at ...\accesskit_consumer-0.35.0\src\tree.rs:71:13: Focused ID #5743185116967667151 is not in the node list
```

An earlier line in that log says Zotero was not running. The process kept going for hours after that warning. The AccessKit panic is a separate event.

## Why this looks like an egui / AccessKit issue

`accesskit_consumer::tree::State::validate_global` panics when the focused node id is not in the current tree. egui is the side that sends that focus id. AccessKit treats a mismatched update as a contract violation and panics on the UI thread, so the whole window dies. `Session::run` does not catch it, because the panic is outside a command.

I do not have a reliable click-by-click reproduction. It is intermittent.

title: Layout tests: use a fixed set of fonts instead of the installed ones
author: rabis7575
body: The layout tests measure lines and pages with whatever fonts the machine has, so each font set breaks different tests: on FreeBSD two failed with no system fonts, and with the fonts the VM has now four others fail (#2069). Worth doing: have the tests load only a fixed font set and skip the system fonts, for example Carlito (OFL) from craft-fonts, which has Calibri's metrics, so values measured in Word still hold; web-platform-tests do this with the Ahem font and Flutter with its own test font. Then every OS gives the same lines, and new tests needn't measure their room from the layout as #2078 does.

title: Home › Underline drop-down: line previews, Dot-dot-dash, None, More Underlines… and Underline Color
author: Nghiathan13
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @Nghiathan13._

**Version:** `main` at `eae2421`.

## Problem

Home › Font › Underline's drop-down (`crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs`, the `split(… "underline" …)` call) is a list of words: Single, Double, Thick, Dotted, Dashed, Dot-dash, Wave, Words only. Next to Word's:

1. **No previews.** You read "Dot-dash" and have to imagine the line. In Word each entry is a sample of the line itself.
2. **Dot-dot-dash is missing**, though `format.underline` already accepts `"style": "dotDotDash"` and the renderer draws it.
3. **No None.** The only way to remove an underline from the menu is the button itself, which toggles.
4. **No More Underlines…**, which in Word opens the Font dialog (`format.fontDialog` exists).
5. **No Underline Color.** The model already has `CharProps::underline_color` (read from and written to DOCX), but no command or menu sets it. The feature catalog (`crates/engine/src/catalog.rs`) lists Underline and Double Underline, but not Underline Color.

## Proposed

- **Previews drawn in code**: each style entry shows a short sample of its own line (single, double, thick, dotted, dashed, dot-dash, dot-dot-dash, wave), in the theme's text colour so it reads in light and dark. They are our own drawings of the line styles, not icons, so there are no asset files. Words only stays a text entry.
- **None** runs `format.underline {"value": false}`.
- **More Underlines…** runs `format.fontDialog`.
- **Underline Color ▸** opens the same colour drop-down as Font Color (Automatic, theme and standard colours, More Colors…). It runs a new command `format.underlineColor {"color": "RRGGBB" | "auto"}`, which sets or clears the direct underline colour and leaves the underline style alone. The command gets a catalog row (`Home|Font|Underline Color|format.underlineColor`), params documentation and engine tests, including `hostile_params_never_panic`.

title: [WC-03] MCP bridge sends the control key to any loopback peer
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from the supplied `WordCraft-AUDIT.md` security and robustness audit of WordCraft 0.7.0 at [`eae2421`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706) (2026-10-17). Upstream main matched this revision when checked before filing.

**Audit severity:** Medium. **Audit confidence:** Confirmed (code) / Plausible (exploit).

The evidence, timings and reproduction outcomes below are those recorded by the audit; this filing pass did not rerun builds, benchmarks or exploit inputs. Proposed changes and regression tests are suggestions, not applied or verified fixes. Where the audit extrapolates resource use, that estimate is not a measured process abort.

**Source locations at the audited revision:** [crates/mcp/src/backend.rs:75](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L75-L77).

**Evidence.** `crates/mcp/src/backend.rs:75-77`:
```rust
fn may_send_key(addr: &str, peer: Option<SocketAddr>) -> bool {
    is_loopback_addr(addr) && peer.is_some_and(|p| p.ip().to_canonical().is_loopback())
}
```
`reconnect` (`:108-118`) iterates `addr.to_socket_addrs()` and takes the first address that accepts. The app binds **only** `127.0.0.1` (`apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs:40`). The unit test at `backend.rs:266-267` explicitly accepts `("localhost:7981", "[::1]:7981")`.

**Scenario.** On a multi-user Linux or macOS host, user B binds `[::1]:7981`, which needs no privileges. User A runs `wordcraft-cli mcp --connect localhost:7981`, and `localhost` resolves to `::1` first. The bridge reads A's 0600 key file and sends the key to B's listener. B replays it to `127.0.0.1:7981` and fully controls A's running app: open and save files (WC-01), and `ui.screenshot {path}`.

**Fix.**
```diff
-is_loopback_addr(addr) && peer.is_some_and(|p| p.ip().to_canonical().is_loopback())
+peer.is_some_and(|p| p.ip().to_canonical() == IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::LOCALHOST))
```

title: [WC-04] ODT `<text:s text:c>` has no total expansion budget
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from the supplied `WordCraft-AUDIT.md` security and robustness audit of WordCraft 0.7.0 at [`eae2421`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706) (2026-10-17). Upstream main matched this revision when checked before filing.

**Audit severity:** High. **Audit confidence:** Confirmed (repro).

The evidence, timings and reproduction outcomes below are those recorded by the audit; this filing pass did not rerun builds, benchmarks or exploit inputs. Proposed changes and regression tests are suggestions, not applied or verified fixes. Where the audit extrapolates resource use, that estimate is not a measured process abort.

**Source locations at the audited revision:** [crates/formats/src/odt.rs:1675](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/formats/src/odt.rs#L1675-L1678).

**Evidence.** `crates/formats/src/odt.rs:1675-1678`:
```rust
"s" => {
    let n = get(a, "text:c").and_then(|v| v.parse::<usize>().ok()).unwrap_or(1).clamp(1, 1000);
    self.push_text(&" ".repeat(n));
}
```
Each tag is clamped, but nothing limits the total. `content.xml` may be 256 MB (`MAX_ENTRY`, `odt.rs:31`) and compresses about 1000:1.

**Repro** (debug CLI, `wordcraft-cli convert x.odt x.txt`):

| `<text:s text:c="1000"/>` × | .odt size | peak working set |
|---|---|---|
| 20,000 | 1.5 KB | 41 MB |
| 100,000 | 6.0 KB | 138 MB |

Growth is linear, about 23,000× amplification. A file of about 600 KB extrapolates to roughly 13 GB of spaces, and `to_doc`/`clean_text` copy it again. The result is an OOM abort that `catch_unwind` cannot catch.

**Fix.** Add a per-document expansion budget in the ODT `Body`:
```diff
-let n = …clamp(1, 1000);
-self.push_text(&" ".repeat(n));
+let n = …clamp(1, 1000).min(self.space_budget);
+self.space_budget -= n;              // e.g. start at 4 MiB
+if n > 0 { self.push_text(&" ".repeat(n)); }
```
