title: [WC-05] Markdown table rows padded to header width before any cap
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from the supplied `WordCraft-AUDIT.md` security and robustness audit of WordCraft 0.7.0 at [`eae2421`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706) (2026-10-17). Upstream main matched this revision when checked before filing.

**Audit severity:** High. **Audit confidence:** Confirmed (repro).

The evidence, timings and reproduction outcomes below are those recorded by the audit; this filing pass did not rerun builds, benchmarks or exploit inputs. Proposed changes and regression tests are suggestions, not applied or verified fixes. Where the audit extrapolates resource use, that estimate is not a measured process abort.

**Source locations at the audited revision:** [crates/formats/src/markdown.rs:386](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/formats/src/markdown.rs#L386-L403).

**Evidence.** `crates/formats/src/markdown.rs:386-403`:
```rust
let mut cells = split_row(l);
cells.resize(aligns.len(), String::new());
table.rows.push(cells.iter().zip(&aligns).map(|(s, a)| cell(s, false, *a)).collect());
```
`MAX_COLS`/`MAX_ROWS` are applied later, in `model::Builder::table`, after every `Cell{Para}` has been allocated.

**Repro:**

| header cols × rows of `\|` | .md size | peak |
|---|---|---|
| 2000 × 200 | 8.6 KB | 155 MB |
| 4000 × 200 | 16.6 KB | 289 MB |
| 4000 × 400 | 17.2 KB | 566 MB |

That is about 350 B per padded cell. A 100 KB file (20k columns × 20k rows) needs over 100 GB, so the process aborts.

**Fix.**
```diff
+if aligns.len() > model::MAX_COLS { aligns.truncate(model::MAX_COLS); }
 …
 while let Some(l) = lines.get(i) {
+    if table.rows.len() >= model::MAX_ROWS { i += 1; continue; }
```

**Test.** For `format!("{}|\n{}|\n{}", "|a".repeat(50_000), "|-".repeat(50_000), "|\n".repeat(10_000))`, assert `cols() <= MAX_COLS` and that peak allocation stays small.

title: [WC-06] No attribute cap per XML element in the docx reader
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from the supplied `WordCraft-AUDIT.md` security and robustness audit of WordCraft 0.7.0 at [`eae2421`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706) (2026-10-17). Upstream main matched this revision when checked before filing.

**Audit severity:** High. **Audit confidence:** Confirmed (repro).

The evidence, timings and reproduction outcomes below are those recorded by the audit; this filing pass did not rerun builds, benchmarks or exploit inputs. Proposed changes and regression tests are suggestions, not applied or verified fixes. Where the audit extrapolates resource use, that estimate is not a measured process abort.

**Source locations at the audited revision:** [crates/docx/src/xml.rs:303](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/docx/src/xml.rs#L303-L343).

**Evidence.** `crates/docx/src/xml.rs:303-343`:
```rust
for a in e.attributes().with_checks(false) {   // duplicates allowed
    …
    el.attrs.push((aname, val));
```
The only caps are `MAX_ELEMENTS = 8_000_000` and `MAX_DEPTH = 256`. The main tree lives for the whole read (`read/mod.rs:136`), and chart and diagram trees are cached together (`read/mod.rs:664-671`).

**Repro.** One `<w:p a="" …>` with 2,000,000 attributes gives a 15 KB `.docx` and a 150 MB peak. The part may be 256 MB, which is about 50M attributes and an extrapolated 3.7 GB or more (with Vec doubling, about 5-7 GB). That is fatal on wasm32 (4 GB address space) and on low-RAM machines.

**Fix.**
```diff
+pub const MAX_ATTRS: usize = 1024;
 for a in e.attributes().with_checks(false) {
+    if el.attrs.len() >= MAX_ATTRS {
+        return Err(DocxError::Limit("too many attributes on one element".into()));
+    }
```
Also charge elements, attributes and text bytes against one package-wide node budget.

**Test.** `assert!(matches!(xml::parse(&flood(200_000)), Err(DocxError::Limit(_))))`.

title: [WC-11] Uncapped `.doc` style tab stops, re-applied per child style
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from the supplied `WordCraft-AUDIT.md` security and robustness audit of WordCraft 0.7.0 at [`eae2421`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706) (2026-10-17). Upstream main matched this revision when checked before filing.

**Audit severity:** Medium. **Audit confidence:** Confirmed (trace).

The evidence, timings and reproduction outcomes below are those recorded by the audit; this filing pass did not rerun builds, benchmarks or exploit inputs. Proposed changes and regression tests are suggestions, not applied or verified fixes. Where the audit extrapolates resource use, that estimate is not a measured process abort.

**Source locations at the audited revision:** [crates/docbin/src/fmt.rs:193](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/docbin/src/fmt.rs#L193-L239).

**Evidence.** `crates/docbin/src/fmt.rs:193-239`:
```rust
for k in 0..add {   // add ≤ 64 per sprm, but sprms per papx are unbounded
    …
    tabs.retain(|t| (t.pos - pos).abs() > 0.05);
    tabs.push(TabStop { pos, align, leader });
}
tabs.sort_by(|a, b| a.pos.total_cmp(&b.pos));
```
The tab list has no cap (Word allows 64). `stylesheet` (`fmt.rs:355-358`) re-walks the whole base chain for each of up to 4,096 styles.

**Scenario.** A base style with about 330 `sprmPChgTabsPapx` entries gives about 21k tabs, about 2.3e8 comparisons per application, then × 4,096 child styles. That is minutes of CPU and about 1 GB of `TabStop`s from roughly 140 KB of Table stream.

**Fix.** `if tabs.len() >= 64 { break; }`. Also resolve each style once (parent's resolved properties plus its own grpprl), memoised by `istd`.

**Test.** See the reviewer's sketch: a 64 KB papx base plus 4,095 children must give `stylesheet()` in under 2 s with every `tabs.len() <= 64`.

```rust
for (c, mut props) in result {
    props.link = Some(target.clone());
    pb.push(c, props);           // push compares CharProps (incl. the link String) with the previous run
}
```
Neither `FieldBuild.instr` nor `sep` is capped beyond the global character budget (up to 64M chars).

title: [WC-13] `.doc` per-anchor clones of picture alt text and whole groups
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from the supplied `WordCraft-AUDIT.md` security and robustness audit of WordCraft 0.7.0 at [`eae2421`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706) (2026-10-17). Upstream main matched this revision when checked before filing.

**Audit severity:** Medium. **Audit confidence:** Confirmed (trace).

The evidence, timings and reproduction outcomes below are those recorded by the audit; this filing pass did not rerun builds, benchmarks or exploit inputs. Proposed changes and regression tests are suggestions, not applied or verified fixes. Where the audit extrapolates resource use, that estimate is not a measured process abort.

**Source locations at the audited revision:** [crates/docbin/src/lib.rs:496](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/docbin/src/lib.rs#L496-L522), [crates/docbin/src/drawing.rs:318](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/docbin/src/drawing.rs#L318-L349).

**Evidence.**
- `crates/docbin/src/lib.rs:496-512` with `media.rs:71-72` (`hit.clone()`): every `\x01` anchor pointing at one cached picture copies its alt text (up to 4,096 UTF-16 units).
- `drawing.rs:318-349`: up to 20k anchors may all reference one group spid with 1,000 children, so the group is rebuilt and cloned per anchor (`lib.rs:519-522`).

**Scenario.**
- A 100 KB stream of `\x01` gives about 200k anchors × 12 KB, roughly 2.4 GB.
- 20k anchors × 1,000 group children gives about 20M `GroupChild`s, over 5 GB.

**Fix.** Anchor each spid once (`HashSet<u32>`). Charge the heap cost of each emitted object (alt length, child count) against the walk budget. Cap the total number of group children per document.

title: [WC-14] Failed decompression and DIB decode work is not charged in `.doc`
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from the supplied `WordCraft-AUDIT.md` security and robustness audit of WordCraft 0.7.0 at [`eae2421`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706) (2026-10-17). Upstream main matched this revision when checked before filing.

**Audit severity:** Medium. **Audit confidence:** Confirmed (trace).

The evidence, timings and reproduction outcomes below are those recorded by the audit; this filing pass did not rerun builds, benchmarks or exploit inputs. Proposed changes and regression tests are suggestions, not applied or verified fixes. Where the audit extrapolates resource use, that estimate is not a measured process abort.

Related: closed #1334 concerned repeated rejected inline pictures/ODT entries. This report concerns the distinct OfficeArt BLIP-store path, aliasing via different FBSEs and failed-work accounting.

**Source locations at the audited revision:** [crates/docbin/src/officeart.rs:155](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/docbin/src/officeart.rs#L155-L158).

**Evidence.** `crates/docbin/src/officeart.rs:155-158`:
```rust
miniz_oxide::inflate::decompress_to_vec_zlib_with_limit(raw, want).ok()?
```
A failed inflation (`HasMoreOutput`) is cached per `pib` but never charged to the media `total`. Up to 5,000 FBSEs may point at the same delay-stream record, and each one is inflated again. Separately, DIB→PNG (`officeart.rs:181-221`) is charged only for the compressed PNG output. A ~100-byte RLE8 DIB can declare 9000×9000 (243 MB decoded).

**Scenario.** 5,000 × 64 MB inflations is about 320 GB of decompression work, many minutes of CPU, from a file under 1 MB.

**Fix.** Keep a per-document decode-work budget (e.g. 512 MB) charged with `want`, or with `w*h*4` for DIBs, *before* each attempt, whether or not it succeeds. Also cache results by `(fo_delay, size)`.

author: PierrunoYT
body: Reported from the supplied `WordCraft-AUDIT.md` security and robustness audit of WordCraft 0.7.0 at [`eae2421`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706) (2026-10-17). Proposed changes and regression tests are suggestions, not applied or verified fixes. Where the audit extrapolates resource use, that estimate is not a measured process abort. Related: #1336 covers unmatched backtick/bracket lookahead. These are separate emphasis-format back-scans and HTML anchor suffix lowercasing hotspots. **Source locations at the audited revision:** [crates/formats/src/markdown.rs:1017](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/formats/src/markdown.rs#L1017-L1025). **Evidence.** - `crates/formats/src/markdown.rs:1017-1025`: `base_of` scans backwards for a `Text` node, once per `Delim`. - `:871`: `r.to_ascii_lowercase().starts_with("")` copies and lowercases the whole rest of the paragraph for every ``. **Repro.** - `*_` × N: 5k → 0.16 s, 10k → 0.26 s, 20k → 1.01 s. - `` × N: 5k → 0.06 s, 10k → 0.11 s, 20k → 0.36 s. title: [WC-18] Embedded font faces uncapped
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from the supplied `WordCraft-AUDIT.md` security and robustness audit of WordCraft 0.7.0 at [`eae2421`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706) (2026-10-17). Upstream main matched this revision when checked before filing.

**Audit severity:** Medium. **Audit confidence:** Confirmed (trace).

The evidence, timings and reproduction outcomes below are those recorded by the audit; this filing pass did not rerun builds, benchmarks or exploit inputs. Proposed changes and regression tests are suggestions, not applied or verified fixes. Where the audit extrapolates resource use, that estimate is not a measured process abort.

**Source locations at the audited revision:** [crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs:768](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs#L768-L795).

**Evidence.** `crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs:789-795`:
```rust
Ok(FileRef::Collection(c)) => c.len(),
…
(0..count).filter_map(|i| skrifa::FontRef::from_index(data, i).ok().map(|f| font_faces(&f, i))).flatten().collect()
```
`font_faces` adds one face per `fvar` named instance, with an O(n²) `named.iter().any(..)` dedupe (`:768-771`). `MAX_FACES_PER_FILE = 256` (`user.rs:27`) is enforced only for user-installed fonts, not for `add_document_fonts` (`:1082-1097`). The resulting faces are kept in the process-global FontDb for the rest of the session.

**Scenario.** A 50 MB TTC declaring millions of faces that all point at one table directory, or one variable font with 65,535 named instances. Opening the document hangs or runs out of memory.

**Fix.** Apply `count.min(MAX_FACES_PER_FILE)` in `enumerate_faces`, `.take(256)` on named instances, and a `HashSet` for the dedupe.

title: [WC-20] PDF export does not filter hyperlink schemes
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from the supplied `WordCraft-AUDIT.md` security and robustness audit of WordCraft 0.7.0 at [`eae2421`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706) (2026-10-17). Upstream main matched this revision when checked before filing.

**Evidence.** `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs:1466-1471`:
```rust
let url = target.trim();
if url.is_empty() { continue; }
Target::Action(Action::Link(LinkAction::new(url.to_string())))
```
Every other exporter filters through `wordcraft_doc::link::is_safe_href` (`html.rs:1032`, `markdown.rs:1182`, `odt.rs:362`, `rtf.rs:179`, `latex.rs:324`).

**Scenario.** A hostile docx carries `\\attacker\share\x` or `file:///C:/Users/Public/evil.exe` as link targets. The victim converts it to PDF and shares the PDF. Recipients who click get an NTLM leak (UNC on Windows) or a local file launch in permissive viewers. A `javascript:` URI is passed through too.

**Fix.**
```diff
-if url.is_empty() { continue; }
+if url.is_empty() || !wordcraft_doc::link::is_safe_href(url) { continue; }
```

**Test.** Export links `javascript:alert(1)` and `\\h\s`; assert the PDF bytes contain neither `/URI (javascript` nor `\\\\h`.

title: [WC-23] Failed zip entries are not charged against the total
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from the supplied `WordCraft-AUDIT.md` security and robustness audit of WordCraft 0.7.0 at [`eae2421`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706) (2026-10-17). Upstream main matched this revision when checked before filing.

**Audit severity:** Medium. **Audit confidence:** Plausible.

The evidence, timings and reproduction outcomes below are those recorded by the audit; this filing pass did not rerun builds, benchmarks or exploit inputs. Proposed changes and regression tests are suggestions, not applied or verified fixes. Where the audit extrapolates resource use, that estimate is not a measured process abort.

**Source locations at the audited revision:** [crates/docx/src/package.rs:191](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/docx/src/package.rs#L191-L201).

**Evidence.** `crates/docx/src/package.rs:191-201`: on a `read_to_end` error the loop `continue`s *before* `total += buf.len()`. zip 3.0.0 does not reject overlapping entries, and its CRC check fails only at EOF.

**Scenario.** 20,000 central-directory entries (`MAX_ENTRIES`) all point at one 250 KB deflate stream that inflates to 256 MB and carries a bad CRC. Every entry is inflated in full and then discarded, about 5 TB of inflation from a 2-3 MB file.

**Fix.** Charge `buf.len()` before checking the result, and reject repeated `data_start()` offsets with a `HashSet<u64>`. Also report unreadable parts to the caller, instead of only logging them, because they are silently lost on save.

**Source locations at the audited revision:** [crates/layout/src/styleref.rs:265](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/layout/src/styleref.rs#L265-L283), [crates/layout/src/fields.rs:72](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/layout/src/fields.rs#L72-L83).

**Evidence.** `crates/layout/src/styleref.rs:265-283`: `eval` scans backwards from `first` and then forwards over all body entries. It is called for every header STYLEREF on every page, twice (cache key at `fields.rs:72-83`, then `field_text_on`), across up to 3 layout passes.

**Scenario.** 1,000 `STYLEREF "X"` fields where no paragraph uses style X, with 100k paragraphs over 2k pages, is about 4e11 steps per layout.

**Fix.** Precompute a sorted entry index per style and binary-search it. Cap the number of STYLEREF fields evaluated per header.

**Evidence.** `crates/engine/src/cmd/mailings.rs:917,940-997`. `MAX_MERGED_BLOCKS` counts only top-level blocks. Records are capped at 100,000 (`:543`). Each record deep-copies the body through `merge_blocks`.

author: PierrunoYT
body:

Proposed changes and regression tests are suggestions, not applied or verified fixes. Where the audit extrapolates resource use, that estimate is not a measured process abort.

**Source locations at the audited revision:** [crates/doc/src/link.rs:7](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/doc/src/link.rs#L7-L10), [crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs:2288](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs#L2288).

- **WC-28: link allow-list checks the prefix only.** `crates/doc/src/link.rs:7-10` uses `url.split_once(':')` plus a scheme compare, and passes the raw string to `ctx.open_url` → `webbrowser`. `webbrowser` 1.2.4 falls back to `from_file_path` when `Url::parse` fails. A link such as `http://x:99999/../../../../home/u/Downloads/evil.html` therefore becomes a local `file://` path. On Linux, when no browser is found, it may go to `gio open`/`kde-open`.

  - Fix: parse with `url::Url`, require `http`/`https` with a host (or `mailto`), and pass `parsed.as_str()`.

**Suggested validation:** Use malformed http/https URLs and supported valid web/mail links with a mocked opener; invalid URLs must be rejected before an OS call.

title: Windows: UNC and device paths in command parameters are canonicalised before the automation-root check (outbound SMB / NTLM leak)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium (Windows NetNTLMv2 credential leak to an attacker-controlled SMB/WebDAV host). **Confidence:** Confirmed by code trace.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/engine/src/file_access.rs:203-213`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/engine/src/file_access.rs#L203-L213): `resolve()` calls `std::fs::canonicalize(at)` and `std::fs::symlink_metadata(at)` on the raw caller-supplied path *before* checking `inside()` against the configured automation roots:
  ```rust
  let absolute = std::path::absolute(path).map_err(|e| format!("{path}: {e}"))?;
  loop {
      match std::fs::canonicalize(at) { // CreateFileW on \\host\share triggers SMB/WebDAV auth
  ```
- Without roots in force, [`crates/engine/src/io.rs:349-354`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/engine/src/io.rs#L349-L354) touches the path directly.

title: MCP bridge (`--connect`): control key is sent to any loopback peer (`[::1]`, `127.0.0.x`) while the app binds only `127.0.0.1`
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium (control-key disclosure to another local user on multi-user systems). **Confidence:** Confirmed in code; exploit plausible on shared hosts.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/mcp/src/backend.rs:75-77`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L75-L77):
  ```rust
  fn may_send_key(addr: &str, peer: Option<SocketAddr>) -> bool {
      is_loopback_addr(addr) && peer.is_some_and(|p| p.ip().to_canonical().is_loopback())
  }
  ```
- [`crates/mcp/src/backend.rs:108-118`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L108-L118): `reconnect` iterates `addr.to_socket_addrs()` and connects to the first address that accepts.
- [`apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs:40`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs#L40): the desktop app binds *only* `127.0.0.1:<port>`, never `[::1]` or `127.0.0.2`.
- [`crates/mcp/src/backend.rs:266-267`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L266-L267): the existing unit test explicitly permits `("localhost:7981", "[::1]:7981")`.

## Conditions and impact
On a multi-user host where `localhost` resolves to `::1` and `127.0.0.1`, an unprivileged local user B can bind `[::1]:7981` (or `127.0.0.2:7981` on Linux) while user A's WordCraft listens on `127.0.0.1:7981`. When user A runs `wordcraft-cli mcp --connect localhost:7981`, the bridge reads A's `0600` key file and transmits the key to B's listener. B can then replay the key to `127.0.0.1:7981` and take full control of A's session.

## Recommended remediation
Require `peer.is_some_and(|p| p.ip().to_canonical() == IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::LOCALHOST))` in `may_send_key`, and resolve `localhost` to `127.0.0.1` only when connecting to the local control server.

title: ODT reader: `<text:s text:c="1000"/>` space expansion has no per-document budget (6 KB file → 138 MB, ~23,000× amplification)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** High (out-of-memory abort from a tiny `.odt` file, uncatchable by `catch_unwind`). **Confidence:** Confirmed, reproduced (6.0 KB `.odt` → 138 MB peak working set).

## Source evidence
- [`crates/formats/src/odt.rs:1675-1678`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/formats/src/odt.rs#L1675-L1678):
  ```rust
  "s" => {
      let n = get(a, "text:c").and_then(|v| v.parse::<usize>().ok()).unwrap_or(1).clamp(1, 1000);
      self.push_text(&" ".repeat(n));
  }
  ```
- [`crates/formats/src/odt.rs:31`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706/crates/formats/src/odt.rs#L31): `content.xml` may be up to `MAX_ENTRY = 256 * 1024 * 1024` bytes after deflate, and each `<text:s text:c="1000"/>` (22 bytes of XML) appends 1,000 spaces with no cumulative budget.

## Conditions and impact
Reproduction with `wordcraft-cli convert x.odt x.txt`:
- 20,000 × `<text:s text:c="1000"/>` (1.5 KB `.odt`) → 41 MB peak RSS in 0.11 s.
- 100,000 × `<text:s text:c="1000"/>` (6.0 KB `.odt`) → 138 MB peak RSS in 0.26 s.

Growth is linear at ~23,000× amplification; a ~600 KB `.odt` extrapolates to ~13 GB of spaces (copied again in `to_doc` / `clean_text`), aborting the process and losing unsaved work in open windows.

## Recommended remediation
Track a per-document space-expansion budget (e.g. 4 MiB) in the ODT `Body` state (and/or enforce a shared total-character cap in `formats::model::Builder`), clamping `n` to the remaining budget.

## Suggested regression test
An ODT paragraph containing 200,000 `<text:s text:c="1000"/>` tags imports without panicking or exceeding the total character budget (e.g. total text length ≤ 16 MiB).


---

title: Format Painter: double-click should keep it on (sticky), and the button should show armed vs. sticky state
author: miltonjrd
body:
### Summary

The Format Painter has a sticky mode in the engine (edit.formatPainter with {"sticky": true}), but the ribbon can't reach it. In Word, double-clicking the Format Painter button keeps it on until you press Esc or click the button again. Here, a double-click does nothing useful, and a single click and a sticky painter look the same.

### Current behavior

- crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs always calls edit.formatPainter with {}, so sticky is only reachable from the CLI, MCP or the control channel.
- With a double-click, egui fires clicked() on both clicks. The first arms the painter and the second toggles it off, so it ends up off.
- The button uses the same "checked" look whether the painter is armed once or sticky.

### Expected behavior

- Single click: arms the painter for one use. The button shows a blue border only. It turns off after the formatting is applied.
- Double-click: keeps the painter on across multiple applications. The button shows the full checked look (blue fill and border).
- Turning it off: Esc or another click on the button.

title: Inline text box with "Resize shape to fit text" (a:spAutoFit) keeps its stale saved height and pushes content onto a blank page
author: Menonro
body:
An inline text box with **Resize shape to fit text** (`a:spAutoFit` in `wps:bodyPr`) keeps the height saved in the file instead of fitting its text. When the saved height is larger than the text needs, the box takes room that Word doesn't give it, and the content after it moves to the next page. In the attached case a paragraph holding only a page break is pushed over the page edge, so WordCraft prints a blank page that Word doesn't have.

This is the inline counterpart of #2533, which fits floating text boxes and notes that "linked, inline and vertical auto-fit sizing remain unchanged". #843 reads `spAutoFit` but doesn't resize the shape.

### Environment

- WordCraft `main` at `eae2421`, built from source, Linux x86_64, `wordcraft-cli convert repro.docx repro.pdf`
- Reference: Word for Windows (Microsoft 365) 16.0.20527, File › Save As › PDF
- Also checked: LibreOffice 26.2.4

### Steps

1. Run the script below (Python 3, standard library only). It writes `repro.docx`: 34 lines of text, an inline rounded-rectangle text box with three short lines inside and `a:spAutoFit` on, saved with a height of 10 cm (`wp:extent`/`a:ext` `cy="3600000"`), an empty paragraph, a paragraph holding only a page break, then one line of text.
2. `wordcraft-cli convert repro.docx repro.pdf`
3. Open `repro.docx` in Word and save it as PDF.

### Expected (Word)

2 pages. The box shrinks to its three lines (73 pt tall), the page break paragraph fits on page 1, and "Second page text." is on page 2.

### Actual (WordCraft)

3 pages. The box is drawn at its saved 10 cm (283 pt), the empty paragraph and the page break paragraph no longer fit on page 1, the break starts on page 2, and "Second page text." lands on page 3. Page 2 is blank.

title: Option to keep character count visible in the status bar
author: earlvanze
body:
A WordCraft user asks whether the symbols/character count can remain permanently visible while writing.

Current behavior: in v0.7.0 and the current upstream status-bar implementation, the bar displays word counts. Clicking that count opens the Word Count dialog, which includes characters with and without spaces. I found no persistent character-count display setting in the status-bar implementation.

title: Feature Request: Support Drag-and-Drop to Move Selected Text
author: TheSoumyaSarkar
body:
I would like to suggest adding drag-and-drop functionality for moving selected text within a WordCraft document, similar to Microsoft Word.

Currently, users should be able to move text using cut-and-paste operations. Drag-and-drop would provide a faster and more intuitive alternative for rearranging paragraphs, sentences, and other text content.

Proposed Behaviour

Select a word, sentence, paragraph, or block of text.

Click and hold the selected text.

Drag it to the desired position within the document.

Release the mouse button to move the selected text to that location.

The moved text should retain its original formatting, including font styles, bold, italic, underline, text colour, and other supported formatting.

Expected Features

Move selected text: Drag selected text to another position in the same document.

Preserve formatting: Retain the original formatting when moving text.

Clear insertion indicator: Display a caret or visual indicator showing where the text will be inserted.

Reliable selection behaviour: Distinguish dragging selected text from ordinary text selection.

Undo support: Allow users to reverse the operation using Ctrl+Z.

Steps to Reproduce

Open a document containing multiple paragraphs.

Select a word, sentence, or paragraph.

Attempt to drag the selected text to another location.

Observe whether the text can be moved directly using drag-and-drop.

Why This Feature Would Be Useful

Drag-and-drop text editing would make document rearrangement faster, reduce repetitive cut-and-paste operations, and improve the overall editing experience for users working with long documents.

This request concerns moving already-selected text, rather than the existing behaviour for selecting text by dragging the mouse.

Thank you for considering this enhancement!

title: Feature Request: Add Live Preview During Drag-and-Drop of Text and Tables
author: TheSoumyaSarkar
body:
I would like to suggest adding a live visual preview when dragging and dropping text or tables within a WordCraft document, similar to the intuitive editing experience available in Microsoft Word.

When rearranging document content, users should be able to see where the selected content will be inserted before releasing the mouse button. This would make editing more predictable and help prevent accidental changes to document layout.

Proposed Features

1. Live Preview While Dragging Text

When a user selects text and drags it to another location, WordCraft should provide a visual preview of the intended insertion position and, where practical, the resulting placement of the text.

2. Live Preview While Dragging Tables

When dragging a table or moving it to another position, WordCraft should provide a clear visual indication of where the table will be placed.

3. Clear Insertion Indicator

Display a visible insertion marker, caret, highlighted drop position, or other suitable visual cue that updates as the mouse moves.

4. Automatic Layout Feedback

Where technically feasible, update the preview to reflect how surrounding paragraphs, tables, and page layout will be affected by the proposed placement.

5. Safe Drag-and-Drop Behaviour

The document should only be modified when the user releases the mouse button at a valid drop location. Pressing Esc should cancel the operation where supported.

Expected Behaviour

Select text or initiate a supported table drag operation.

Hold the mouse button and move the content towards the desired destination.

See a live visual indication of the proposed placement.

Release the mouse button to confirm the operation, or cancel it to leave the document unchanged.

Why This Feature Would Be Useful

Live previews would make document editing more intuitive, especially when working with long documents, multiple paragraphs, and complex tables. They would reduce placement errors, improve precision, and make drag-and-drop operations easier …

title: Feature Request: Support Non-Contiguous Text Selection Using Ctrl + Mouse
author: TheSoumyaSarkar
body:
I would like to suggest adding support for selecting multiple non-contiguous text ranges within a WordCraft document using the Ctrl key and mouse selection, similar to advanced text-selection functionality in desktop word processors.

Currently, selecting text in a document generally involves selecting one continuous range at a time. The ability to select multiple separate ranges would make it easier to edit or format specific words and passages scattered throughout a document.

Proposed Behaviour

1. Multiple Text Selections

Allow users to hold Ctrl and select additional text ranges without losing their previous selections.

2. Non-Contiguous Selection

Users should be able to select separate words, phrases, sentences, or text ranges in different paragraphs of the same document.

3. Apply Formatting to All Selected Ranges

Where supported by the document editor, users should be able to apply formatting such as bold, italic, underline, font colour, or other compatible formatting to all selected ranges simultaneously.

4. Preserve Existing Selections

Selecting an additional range should preserve previously selected ranges until the user clears the selection or starts a normal selection operation.

5. Clear Visual Feedback

All selected ranges should remain visibly highlighted so users can identify exactly which parts of the document will be affected by an editing operation.

6. Reliable Editing Behaviour

Keyboard shortcuts, formatting commands, and other editing operations should behave predictably when multiple ranges are selected. Unsupported operations should be handled gracefully without damaging document content.

Steps to Reproduce

Open a document containing multiple paragraphs.

Select a word or phrase in the first paragraph.

Hold Ctrl and attempt to select another word or phrase in a different paragraph.

Observe whether the first selection remains active while the second selection is made.

Why This Feature Would Be Useful

Non-contiguous text selection…

title: Feature Request: Support Deleting Selected Table Rows and Columns with Backspace
author: TheSoumyaSarkar
body:
I would like to suggest improving table editing in WordCraft by allowing users to delete entire selected table rows or columns using the Backspace key.

Currently, when a row or column is selected in a table, pressing the Delete key clears the text inside the selected cells but leaves the table structure intact. Users must use a separate table command to remove the selected rows or columns.

It would be useful to have a keyboard shortcut for deleting the selected rows or columns directly.

Proposed Behaviour

1. Delete Selected Rows

When one or more complete table rows are selected, pressing Backspace should delete the selected rows, including their cells and associated table structure.

2. Delete Selected Columns

When one or more complete table columns are selected, pressing Backspace should delete the selected columns, including their cells and associated table structure.

3. Preserve Existing Delete Behaviour

Pressing Delete should continue to clear the contents of selected cells without removing the rows or columns, preserving the distinction between clearing content and deleting table structure.

4. Context-Aware Keyboard Behaviour

Backspace should delete rows or columns only when the corresponding table selection is active. When editing ordinary text or when no complete row or column is selected, Backspace should retain its normal behaviour.

5. Undo Support

Users should be able to restore deleted rows or columns using Ctrl+Z.

Steps to Reproduce

Insert a table into a WordCraft document.

Select an entire row or column.

Press the Delete key and observe that the cell contents are cleared while the table structure remains.

Look for a convenient keyboard shortcut to delete the selected rows or columns directly.

Expected Behaviour

When an entire table row or column is selected, pressing Backspace should remove the selected table structure rather than merely clearing the text inside its cells.

Why This Feature Would Be Useful

This enhancement would make…

title: Feature Request: Fully Clear Contents of Selected Table Rows and Columns Using Delete
author: TheSoumyaSarkar
body:
I would like to suggest improving the Delete key behaviour when working with tables in WordCraft.

Currently, when I select a table row or column and press Delete, the visible text is removed, but residual paragraph marks, empty paragraphs, or unwanted spacing may remain inside the cells. As a result, the cells can still appear to contain blank lines or unnecessary vertical spacing instead of becoming completely empty.

Expected Behaviour

When one or more complete table rows or columns are selected and the user presses Delete:

Clear all text and other removable content from the selected cells.

Remove residual empty paragraphs or unnecessary paragraph spacing left behind by the deletion.

Reset the affected cells to a clean, empty state while preserving the table structure, row and column dimensions, and existing table formatting where possible.

Keep the selected rows and columns in the table rather than deleting the table structure.

Important Distinction

Delete: Clear the contents of selected cells completely while retaining the selected rows and columns.

Backspace (proposed separate feature): Delete the selected rows or columns from the table structure.

Steps to Reproduce

Insert a table into a WordCraft document.

Enter text into several cells, including content with multiple paragraphs or line breaks.

Select an entire row or column.

Press Delete.

Observe whether empty paragraphs, residual spacing, or other unwanted content remains in the cells.

Why This Feature Would Be Useful

This improvement would make table editing more predictable and prevent unwanted blank lines or excess spacing when clearing multiple cells. It would be especially useful when restructuring tables, reusing existing table layouts, or preparing professional documents.

Thank you for considering this enhancement!

title: Portuguese spelling is silently off with the standard pt_BR Hunspell dictionary (SET ISO8859-1 unsupported)
author: andresilvareis
body:
### What happens

With the Brazilian Portuguese dictionary installed (VERO 3.2.0, Arch AUR package `hunspell-pt-br`, files `/usr/share/hunspell/pt_BR.{aff,dic}`), text marked as Português (Brasil) gets no spelling marks at all. `review.issues` returns `[]` for text full of obvious mistakes (`orcamento`, `esperavamos`, `area`).

The only trace is in the log:

```
WARN [main] wordcraft_proof::pt: Portuguese spelling: unsupported encoding ISO8859-1
```

### Cause

`pt_BR.aff` starts with `SET ISO8859-1`. `hunspell::decode` (crates/proof/src/hunspell.rs) only accepts UTF-8, ISO-8859-2, KOI8-R and Windows-1251, so the Portuguese dictionary falls back to an empty one. This still holds on `main`.

**Why #786 didn't hit it:** it was measured on Debian's VERO 3.2, which Debian ships converted to UTF-8 (`FLAG UTF-8`). The original VERO, the LibreOffice extension `veroptbrv320aoc.oxt`, declares `SET ISO8859-1`. That is what the Arch AUR package installs as-is, and what a "download from LibreOffice's collection" flow (#1698) would fetch too.

### Workaround (confirms the cause)

A UTF-8 copy in `~/.local/share/hunspell` is picked up and spelling works:

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.local/share/hunspell
iconv -f ISO-8859-1 -t UTF-8 /usr/share/hunspell/pt_BR.aff | sed 's/^SET ISO8859-1/SET UTF-8/' > ~/.local/share/hunspell/pt_BR.aff
iconv -f ISO-8859-1 -t UTF-8 /usr/share/hunspell/pt_BR.dic > ~/.local/share/hunspell/pt_BR.dic
```

After restarting, 6 of 7 test mistakes were flagged with the right suggestions (suites→suítes, preve→prevê, area→área, orcamento→orçamento, esperavamos→esperávamos, churasqueira→churrasqueira).

### Suggested fix

Decode `ISO8859-1` / `ISO-8859-1` in `hunspell::decode`. Each byte maps to the code point of the same value, so it is a one-liner next to `decode_latin2`. ISO-8859-15 would be cheap to add too.

### Environment

title: Proofing hint: tell "dictionary found but unreadable" apart from "no dictionary"
author: andresilvareis
body:
### What happens

#1441 (for #1167) adds a status-bar hint when Polish or Portuguese has no dictionary. `missing_dictionary` decides that through `has_dictionary()`, which is `!dictionary().is_empty()`. When a dictionary file **is** installed but fails to load, `load_installed` also falls back to an empty dictionary: unsupported `SET` encoding (#2824), file over the size cap, or a parse error.

So, reading `main`, the user would see "Portuguese (no dictionary)" and a tooltip pointing to the folders where the file already is. They would reinstall it and nothing would change. The real reason is only in the log (`Portuguese spelling: unsupported encoding ISO8859-1`).

### Suggestion

Keep the load error, e.g. `Result`/`Option<String>` beside the cached dictionary. In the status bar, show "Portuguese (dictionary unreadable)", with a tooltip giving the file path and the reason. Show the same in the Proofing options pane that lists the dictionary each language found (#1084).

### Environment

Seen on WordCraft 0.7.0 (Arch Linux) with the ISO-8859-1 `pt_BR` dictionary from #2824. The status-bar behaviour above is from reading `main` (#1441), not from a build of it.

title: wordcraft-cli audit: report hidden information in .docx before sharing
author: ejbarraza
body:
Word documents routinely carry information the sender doesn't know is there: author names on tracked changes and comments, creator / last-modified-by in core properties, hidden text, VBA macros, orphaned package parts. WordCraft honors w:removePersonalInformation / w:removeDateAndTime on save (#1062), but there is no way to see what's in a file — especially one from Word — before sharing it.

Proposal: `wordcraft-cli audit <file>` scans the raw OPC package, reports findings as machine-readable JSON with stable finding IDs, and exits nonzero when findings exist (CI-gate usable). v1 finding classes: author PII (revisions, comments, core/app properties), hidden text (w:vanish), active content (VBA project, embedded OLE — visibility, not blocking), orphan package parts.

Out of scope for v1: sanitizing (strip flagged content with a before/after report) — follow-up.

Fixtures will be synthetic, built from ECMA-376 (no Word-produced files committed, per the clean-room rule).

title: Add musl Linux builds (Alpine Linux, Void musl)
author: vinod2807
body:
### What I'd like

A musl-linked Linux build, so WordCraft runs on musl distributions — **Alpine Linux** (the most widely used musl distro, and the base of a great many container images) and **Void Linux's musl variant**. None of the currently published Linux artifacts can be used on either.

### Why the current artifacts don't work there

The Linux tarball does contain both binaries:

```
$ tar tzf wordcraft-0.8.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz | grep /bin/
wordcraft-0.8.0-linux-x86_64/bin/wordcraft
wordcraft-0.8.0-linux-x86_64/bin/wordcraft-cli
```

…but both are linked against glibc:

```
$ file .../bin/wordcraft
  ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, x86-64, version 1 (SYSV), dynamically linked,
  interpreter /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, for GNU/Linux 3.2.0, stripped

$ readelf -d .../bin/wordcraft | grep NEEDED
  (NEEDED) Shared library: [libgcc_s.so.1]
  (NEEDED) Shared library: [libm.so.6]
  (NEEDED) Shared library: [libc.so.6]
  (NEEDED) Shared library: [ld-linux-x86-64.so.2]

$ .../bin/wordcraft --version
/bin/ash: .../bin/wordcraft: not found        # Alpine 3.24, i.e. musl
```

`/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2` is glibc's loader; a musl system provides `/lib/ld-musl-x86_64.so.1` instead, so the kernel cannot start the process, and the shell reports that as the very confusing "not found" — which reads like a missing file rather than an ABI mismatch. The same applies to the `.deb`, the `.rpm`, the AppImage (glibc + FUSE) and the Flatpak. `gcompat` is only a partial shim, not a real answer for a GUI application.

### The trap worth avoiding: a static musl build cannot open a window

This is the part that costs a build cycle, so it is worth writing down.

Rust's `*-unknown-linux-musl` targets **link statically by default**. A naive musl build compiles, and `wordcraft-cli` works, but the GUI never comes up:

```
Error: WinitEventLoop(Os(OsError {
    ... XNotSupported(LibraryOpenError(OpenError { kind: Library,
    detail: "opening library failed (Dynamic loading not supported); .…

title: Home › Bullets › Change List Level: show each level as a drawn preview, not Level 1…9 text
author: Nghiathan13
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @Nghiathan13._

**Version:** `feat/2786-define-new-bullet` at `0cf56f2` (the branch for #2786, which adds the menu).

## Problem

Home › Paragraph › Bullets › **Change List Level ›** (added for #2786 in `crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs`) is nine plain text items, "Level 1" to "Level 9".

Steps: type two lines, put the second in a bullet list, Increase Indent it to level 2, open Bullets ▾ › Change List Level.

- **Now:** a column of words, "Level 1 … Level 9". You can't see what a level will look like (which bullet, how far in) before you pick it, and nothing tells you which level the paragraph is at.
- **Word:** each entry is a small picture of that level: the level's bullet (or number) at its position, followed by a line of text, each level further in, and the paragraph's current level is highlighted.

## Proposed

- Each of the nine entries is a small bordered tile drawn in code: the level's own bullet or number for the caret's list, at that level's aligned-at position, then a grey line from its text position, so the tiles step in as the levels deepen.
- The bullet is drawn through `crate::previews::glyph` (laid out like document text), so a Symbol/Wingdings bullet shows the character the page will, not a box.
- The paragraph's current level is highlighted (selected), as galleries are.
- A click still runs `para.listLevel {"level": n}`; programmatic use doesn't change.
- Accessibility: each tile is named "Level N" (and reports selected), so tests and screen readers still find it.
- Light and dark themes: the tile uses the gallery page tint, so it isn't the brightest thing on a dark interface.
- Our own drawing; nothing taken from Word beyond the feature's name and what it does. No new asset files or strings.

## Not in scope

- The Numbering drop-down and the Multilevel List drop-down's "Change to Level" items could reuse the tiles later; separate change.

title: [Bug]: WordArt elements from Word 2007 (.docx) are missing / not rendered

body:
### Summary
When opening a `.docx` document created in Microsoft Word 2007 that contains WordArt objects, the WordArt is completely missing from the document canvas (no text, effect, or placeholder is rendered).

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Create or obtain a `.docx` document in Microsoft Word 2007 containing a WordArt element (legacy VML / `v:textpath`).
2. Open the file in WordCraft.
3. Observe the page where the WordArt should appear.

### Expected Behavior
The WordArt object should be parsed and rendered with its stylized text, warp/curve effects, and fill according to the document's specification.

### Actual Behavior
The WordArt element is entirely absent. The canvas shows blank space or moves adjacent paragraphs up as if the element does not exist.

### Technical Context / Suspected Cause
Word 2007 typically encodes WordArt as legacy VML objects inside `<w:pict>` using `<v:shape>` and `<v:textpath>` (before the transition to DrawingML text effects introduced in Word 2010). WordCraft appears to skip or fail to parse this VML shape / textpath structure during document load.

title: Render: thick borders stick out past the corners on screen (round line caps)
author: dfgodvan
body:
On the canvas, table borders and other rules are stroked with kurbo's default round caps, so every rule extends half its width past its end point. With thick borders (3 pt and up) each corner gets a rounded blob that sticks out over the neighbouring border; with thin borders it is too small to notice.

The PDF export draws the same rules with butt caps (`LineCap::Butt` in `crates/pdf`), so screen and PDF differ. Word and LibreOffice draw borders with flat ends.

**Repro:** a table with 3 pt single borders. Zoom in on any corner on screen and compare it with the exported PDF: on screen the horizontal border ends in a half-disc beyond the vertical one.

**Cause:** `Draw::Line` in `crates/render/src/lib.rs` builds `kurbo::Stroke::new(w)` without setting caps, and kurbo defaults to `Cap::Round`. The `Double` style has the same default.

title: Thai Distributed paragraph alignment (w:jc="thaiDistribute")
author: pakiat
body:
Word has a separate paragraph alignment for Thai: **Thai Distributed** (Home › Paragraph, Ctrl+Shift+J; OOXML `w:jc w:val="thaiDistribute"`). It is the standard alignment for Thai official and government documents.

Unlike Justify, which only stretches spaces, Thai Distributed also spreads the extra width between Thai characters/clusters when a line has few or no spaces, so lines fill the measure evenly. The last line of the paragraph is not stretched.

**Current behaviour (0.8.0):** WordCraft has no Thai Distributed option, and a DOCX using `thaiDistribute` is not shown or kept as such.

**Expected:**
1. Thai Distributed alignment on the ribbon/paragraph dialog, distinct from Distribute
2. Read and write `thaiDistribute` in DOCX (direct, style, and table-style properties) without changing it to Justify/Distribute
3. Layout that spreads space between Thai grapheme clusters, never inside a cluster (combining vowels and tone marks stay on their base)

This depends on correct Thai word-boundary line breaking (#1548). PR #1713 includes a ThaiDistribute implementation, but it is a draft that also covers line breaking and other changes; a separate issue would let this feature be tracked on its own.

title: Ruler margin handles on even pages of mirrored (Book fold / Mirror margins) layouts edit the wrong stored margin
author: dkhlapov
body:
Found in review of #2414 (CodeRabbit, withdrawn there as pre-existing; it already affects Mirror margins).

On an even page of a mirrored layout, `mirror_even_pages` moves the text area so its visible left edge is controlled by `margin_right`. The ruler's left handle still calls `dragged_margin(MarginEdge::Left, ...)` and emits `{"left": ...}`, which `layout.margins` writes to `margin_left`, so the visible left edge does not move while the opposite stored margin changes.

Expected: on even mirrored pages map each visual horizontal edge to its stored edge (visual left -> `margin_right`, visual right -> `margin_left`, gutter-aware), reflect the drag coordinate, and emit the mapped edge name. Touches `ruler_drag_margin` and the related ruler-handle update path in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`. Needs a regression test.

title: RTF writer can't keep the prior list kind of a tracked paragraph-format change (numbered <-> bulleted)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Found in review of #2088 (CodeRabbit asked for a follow-up).

The RTF writer in `crates/formats/src/rtf.rs` supports only one list definition per paragraph. When a tracked formatting change switches a paragraph between a numbered and a bulleted list, the document model now keeps a separate old list instance (`Builder::para` in `crates/formats/src/model.rs`), but the writer cannot export the prior list definition, so the old list kind is lost on RTF save. It likewise doesn't write the old paragraph spacing or borders of such a change.

Expected: the writer emits the prior list/spacing/border state of a tracked paragraph change so reject after an RTF round-trip restores it. Needs a round-trip test.

title: Linux X11/XWayland: Vietnamese input garbled when fcitx5 sends forwarded BackSpace over XIM
author: nguyenphivn
body:
With a Vietnamese fcitx5 engine that fixes a word by forwarding BackSpace keys and then committing the new text, WordCraft on X11/XWayland (XIM) ends up with wrong text. Other XIM clients get it right.

Environment: WordCraft 0.8.0 (linux-x86_64 tarball); fcitx5 with the Ngó Sen engine 1.5.2 (https://github.com/ngosen/ngosen), Telex, default "Sen" mode. Seen on Linux Mint 22.3 Cinnamon (X11, fcitx5 5.1.7) and Ubuntu 26.04 GNOME Wayland (fcitx5 5.1.19, WordCraft on XWayland, the default).

Steps:
1. Open a blank document, turn on Vietnamese.
2. Type the keys `tieengs vieetj cos daaus` (Telex for "tiếng việt có dấu").

Expected: `tiếng việt có dấu`
Actual (two runs on Mint): `tiêiees viêieejcó dâấ`, `Tiêến việt có dâấ`

Checks, same keys sent the same way:
- GTK3 text view forced to XIM (`GTK_IM_MODULE=xim`): correct, 3/3.
- WordCraft with `WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND=1` on GNOME: correct, 2/2.
- WordCraft on XIM with the engine in preedit mode (no forwarded keys): correct, 2/2.

Suggestion: on a Wayland session, prefer the native backend (text-input-v3) when an input method is running, e.g. when `XMODIFIERS` or `GTK_IM_MODULE`/`QT_IM_MODULE` is set, and keep XWayland as the opt-in for file drag-and-drop (see also #2184). With `WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND=1` the same keys came out right, and XWayland is also behind #1169, #1382, #1240 and #1956. On GNOME the native window had only the fallback buttons and no title bar, which may be a reason to keep XWayland there.

X11 sessions only have XIM, so the garbling above still needs a fix there.

title: Dimmed header/footer: overlapping lines darken where they meet
author: dfgodvan
body:
While the body is being edited, headers and footers are drawn dimmed. Where two of their lines overlap, the overlap comes out darker than the lines themselves: a table in the header gets near-black squares where its borders cross, and borders shared by neighbouring cells are a darker grey than the outer ones.

![Crossing of two header table borders while the body is edited](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dfgodvan/wordcraft/assets/dimmed-header-overlap/before-crossing.png)

**Repro:** put a table with single borders in the header, then click into the body. Zoom in on a point where two borders cross: it is much darker than the borders around it. Double-click into the header (no dimming) or export to PDF and the crossing is the same tone as the lines.

**Expected:** the dimmed header looks like the undimmed header faded as one picture, as in Word: every line the same tone, crossings included.

**Cause:** `page_display` (`crates/layout/src/display.rs`) gives every header/footer draw item the dimming alpha (0.45) on its own, so wherever items overlap the alpha is applied more than once (0.55² of the background left at a crossing instead of 0.55).

title: Table cell: a word after a slash ("/заполняется") is split between two letters instead of wrapping whole
author: Menonro
body:
In a narrow table cell, a word that follows a slash (`/word`) is split between two letters instead of moving to the next line whole. Word and LibreOffice wrap the word whole; WordCraft fills the line letter by letter. A control cell with the same text and no slash wraps correctly.

### Environment

- WordCraft `main` at `7333a30`, built from source, Linux x86_64, `wordcraft-cli convert repro_break_in_word.docx out.pdf` (also reproduces with #2912 and #1760 merged)
- Reference: Word for Windows (Microsoft 365) 16.0.20527, Save As › PDF; LibreOffice 26.2.4

### Steps

1. Run `make_repro_break_in_word.py` below (Python 3, standard library only). It writes `repro_break_in_word.docx`: a fixed-layout table with two 1800-twip cells, Arial 7 pt, centred. Cell 1 is a Kazakh/Russian caption whose Russian part follows a slash: `… толтырылады /заполняется в случае …`; the slash is in its own run (` /`) and the text around it is italic. Cell 2 is the same text without the slash.
2. `wordcraft-cli convert repro_break_in_word.docx out.pdf`
3. Open the same file in Word and save it as PDF.

### Expected (Word, LibreOffice)

Cell 1: `ЖСН енгізілмеген / жағдайда толтырылады / /заполняется в случае / неприсвоения ИИН` — `/заполняется` moves to the next line whole.

### Actual (WordCraft)

Cell 1: `ЖСН енгізілмеген / жағдайда / толтырылады /заполн / яется в случае / неприсвоения ИИН` — the word is split after `/заполн`.

Cell 2 (no slash) wraps the same as in Word and LibreOffice.

| Cell 1, lines | |
|---|---|
| Word 16.0.20527 | `…толтырылады` / `/заполняется в случае` |
| LibreOffice 26.2.4 | `…толтырылады` / `/заполняется в случае` |
| WordCraft `7333a30` | `…толтырылады /заполн` / `яется в случае` |

Sweeping the cell width from 1500 to 2150 twips moves the split point (`/за|полняется`, `/зап|олняется`, `/запо|лняется` …), so the slash seems to make the rest of the word breakable anywhere.

title: Roman page numbers in the footer show as digits when the body shows the page count
author: dfgodvan
body:
## Summary
A section whose pages are numbered in lower-case roman (`w:pgNumType w:fmt="lowerRoman"`) shows its page numbers as digits in the footer ("2" instead of "ii") when the body has a NUMPAGES or SECTIONPAGES field (for example an "N pages" line on the title page). Without the body field the footer is right.

## Reproduce
Two sections, with a PAGE field in the footer. The second section restarts at 1 in lower-case roman. The first paragraph of the body is `{NUMPAGES} pages`. On main, every page of the second section whose roman number has more than one letter shows digits ("2", "3", "4", "6" … "10"). Single-letter pages such as "v" look right only because the digit and the letter have the same length.

## Cause
`Fields::page_key` (the cache key of a paragraph with page fields) holds the page number, the totals, the section and the bookmarks, but not the number format. Paginating lays the footer out to know where the body ends, before the section's number format is set in the field context, so in decimal. When the body shows page totals, the pass with the right totals gives that layout the same key as the page's own footer, and the decimal layout is drawn.

title: macOS Zoom (picture-in-picture lens) does not follow the caret while typing in the document
author: filo3108
body:
> Note: I'm not a developer. I used an AI assistant (Claude) to investigate the problem and write this report.

## Summary

With macOS Zoom set to follow keyboard focus, the zoom lens does not move with the text caret when typing in a WordCraft document. In TextEdit, Pages and Electron apps on the same machine, the lens follows the caret.

The cause is how the document canvas is exposed to macOS accessibility. WordCraft gives the canvas `Role::Document`. AccessKit maps that to an `AXGroup` (subrole `AXDocument`), and because `Document` doesn't support the read-only state, AccessKit treats the node as read-only, so `AXValue` is not settable. Zoom queries the caret position correctly but only follows the insertion point of elements it considers **editable text**, so it ignores the canvas.

## Environment

- WordCraft 0.7.0 (`fc419188`), arm64
- macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), external 3440×1440 display
- Zoom: picture-in-picture style, "Follow keyboard focus" enabled

## Steps to reproduce

1. Turn on Zoom in picture-in-picture mode (System Settings › Accessibility › Zoom).
2. Open a document in WordCraft and type a long line of text.
3. Watch the zoom lens.

**Expected:** the lens follows the caret, as it does in TextEdit or Pages.
**Actual:** the lens stays where it is.

## What we measured

**1. WordCraft's AccessKit output is correct.** Querying WordCraft from an external `AXUIElement` client:

- The focused element is `AXGroup` / `AXDocument`, with `AXSelectedTextRange`, `AXNumberOfCharacters`, `AXBoundsForRange`, `AXLineForIndex`, `AXRangeForLine`, `AXStringForRange` and `AXAttributedStringForRange`.
- `AXSelectedTextRange` advances with every keystroke, and `AXBoundsForRange` returns correct screen rectangles that move with the caret.
- `AXSelectedTextChanged` and `AXValueChanged` are posted on every keystroke. Their userInfo is empty, but NSTextView's is empty too, so that is not the difference.

1. OS and WordCraft commit (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`)
2. Exact build command
3. File type and a safe-to-share fixture
4. Whether a blank/new document opens
5. Log output or stack trace from the hang

The app must remain responsive or show bounded progress while opening documents; it must not hang.

title: File › Info: Custom document properties dialog
author: maxm11
body:
The UI half of #1798, split out so the fix isn't mixed with a feature (as suggested by @midasmatterhorn in #1798). Field evaluation is covered separately by #1851.

**Gap:** WordCraft reads and writes custom document properties (they survive DOCX round-trips and `file.properties` exposes them), but there is no way for a user to see or edit them in the app. Word's path is File › Info › Properties › Advanced Properties › Custom.

**Scope (v1):**
- A `CustomProperties` dialog opened from the File › Info properties area via an "Advanced Properties…" / "Custom" entry.
- List existing custom properties with Add, Edit and Delete, using a small name/value form.
- Text properties only; Word's number/date/yes-no types are out of scope for v1 (documented in the parity docs).
- Backed by the existing `file.properties` command (`custom` object) and `doc.custom_props` — no second storage format.
- OK applies everything as one undo step, marks the document dirty and refreshes the File › Info fields; Cancel changes nothing.
- Names/values validated with the existing engine limits; errors surface in the dialog; hostile/empty/duplicate names never panic.

**Out of scope:** DOCPROPERTY field evaluation (#1851), header/footer field refresh (#1706 / #1780), non-text property types, document-management integration.

Refs #1798
Refs #1851

title: References › Insert Table of Figures always lists Figures: no way to build a list of Tables (or Equations / custom labels)
author: benandez
body:
## Problem
**References › Captions › Insert Table of Figures** always builds the list for the **Figure** caption label. There's no way in the interface to build a **list of tables** from "Table" captions, or a list for "Equation" or a custom label from **New Label…**.

The engine already supports it. Only the UI is missing:
- `references.tableOfFigures` takes `{"label"?: "Figure|Table|Equation"}` and builds `TOC \c "<label>"` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/citations.rs:315-320` at d588e0b8).
- The ribbon button always sends `json!({})` (`crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs:1863-1867`), so the label defaults to Figure.

A workaround is only possible through automation/MCP: `references.tableOfFigures {"label":"Table"}`.

## Expected (Word behaviour)
**Insert Table of Figures** opens a dialog with:
- **Caption label:** Figure / Table / Equation / any user label.
- Include label and number, show page numbers, right-align page numbers, tab leader.
- **Update Table** refreshes whichever list the caret is in.

That lets a document have both a "List of Figures" and a "List of Tables", which is common in reports and theses.

## Notes
- The `params` hint lists only Figure, Table and Equation. User labels from New Label… (kept in the interface settings) should be accepted as well.
- Related: #2940 (cross-reference to a caption with a custom label), #426 (TOF refresh, closed).

title: Typing creates ~50 threads per second: render_region builds a new multi-threaded RenderContext (and rayon pool) on every call
author: bConcreteFriend3
body:
## What happens

While typing, WordCraft creates and throws away about 50 threads per second. Each one is a rayon worker that starts, spin-waits in `cthread_yield`, and exits.

| | Idle | Typing steadily |
|---|---|---|
| Threads seen in a 15 s sample | 7 | 828 (800 of them rayon workers) |
| Busy CPU spent spin-waiting | 0% | 28% |

A separate 60 s session of typing, formatting and scrolling showed 1,882 threads and 45% of busy CPU spent spin-waiting. It is not a startup effect: the 15 s sample above was taken almost 7 minutes after launch.

This may be part of #1621 (high CPU on a 4-core i5) and #2442 (typing latency that depends on Turbo Boost). On an 8-core M3 the spinning workers land on idle cores and typing feels fine, but on a 4-core machine they compete with the UI thread.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open WordCraft 0.8.0 (release DMG) on macOS with a new blank document.
2. Type steadily, and while typing run:
   `sample $(pgrep -x WordCraft) 15 5 -file out.txt`
3. Count the threads in the sample:
   `grep -cE '^    [0-9]+ Thread_[0-9]+' out.txt`
   Typing gives several hundred; idle gives under 10.

## Where it comes from

The stack that creates the threads, from the sample (demangled and trimmed):

```
wordcraft_ui_egui::canvas::show
  wordcraft_render::render_region
    vello_cpu::render::RenderContext::new_with
      vello_cpu::dispatch::multi_threaded::MultiThreadedDispatcher::new
        rayon_core::registry::Registry::new
          std::thread::spawn
```

So `render_region` seems to build a new multi-threaded `RenderContext` on each call, and each one starts its own rayon thread pool that spins up, does a little work and is torn down.

## Possible fix

Keep one `RenderContext`, or at least one thread pool, alive across frames and reuse it instead of constructing a new one per call. A test that counts threads created while typing would catch it if it comes back.

## Environment

- WordCraft 0.8.0, `wordcraft-0.8.0-macos-universal.dmg`
- macOS 27.2, MacB…

title: Tabs dialog shows a blank list box when the paragraph has no custom tab stops
author: SlavenDj
body:
**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs_para.rs` (`tabs()`), the list frame at :209-294.

**What happens:** Format › Paragraph › Tabs (or double-clicking the ruler) on a paragraph with no custom tab stops shows a bordered box with nothing inside. A fresh paragraph has no stops, so this is the default state, not an edge case.

**Expected:** an empty-state hint inside the box, like the Bookmark dialog's "The document has no bookmarks yet." or the Customize Keyboard keys list's "(none)".

**Why:** the frame + `ScrollArea` at :209-294 only render `f.stops`; there is no `if f.stops.is_empty()` branch.

title: Styles pane offers Delete for built-in styles, which the command then refuses
author: SlavenDj
body:
**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/panes.rs:346` (the Styles pane row context menu) vs `crates/engine/src/cmd/para.rs:1110`.

**What happens:** right-clicking a built-in style (Normal, Heading 1, …) in the Styles pane shows a clickable **Delete**. Clicking it runs `styles.delete`, which refuses with "`…` is a built-in style and can't be deleted" (`para.rs:1110`). Word greys Delete out for built-in styles.

**Expected:** Delete disabled for built-in styles. The pane's row tuples are `(id, name, is_char)` (:315-323) and don't carry the `builtin` flag yet, so it needs exposing.

**Contrast:** the table-style menu already gates this — `ribbon.rs:2487` uses `can_modify`/`can_delete`.

title: File browser Open/Save button hardcodes white text and the light brand blue (broken in dark theme)
author: SlavenDj
body:
**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/file_browser.rs:447`.

**What happens:** the built-in file browser's Open/Save button is drawn with `egui::Color32::WHITE` text over a hardcoded `APP_COLOR` (`#3B5BDB`, the light-theme brand blue). In the dark theme it stays a bright light-theme blue, out of step with the rest of the dark chrome, and bypasses the theme accent.

**Expected:** `t.accent` + `t.on_accent` (or the shared `widgets::primary_button()`), which already adapt per theme.

**Related:** #1906 was the same pattern (forced white text on a themed dialog).

title: SmartArt Pyramid preview draws white band separators on the dark card
author: SlavenDj
body:
**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs_smart_art.rs:101` (`preview()`, the `SmartArtLayout::Pyramid` arm).

**What happens:** every other layout uses the passed `line` colour (`Stroke::new(1.0, line)`), but Pyramid hardcodes `Color32::WHITE` for the separators between its three bands. The preview sits on the themed card (`t.input`), which is near-black in dark mode, so the white separators are a bright, non-adapting element.

**Expected:** use the same `line` parameter as the sibling layouts so it follows the theme.

title: WordArt reflection preview swatch uses a fixed light grey in the dark ribbon menu
author: SlavenDj
body:
**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/wordart_menus.rs:51` (`paint_style`).

**What happens:** the "reflection" bar under the previewed letter is drawn with `Color32::from_gray(190)`, a fixed light grey. The swatch sits on the themed menu surface (`t.menu`, `#2B2B2B` in dark mode), so the reflection bar stays light and no longer reads as a faded reflection of the themed text.

**Expected:** derive it from the theme text colour (a faded/dimmed variant) so it adapts like the `shadow` case just above it (`from_black_alpha`, :45).

title: File browser shows a blank list box for an empty folder or a filter that matches nothing
author: SlavenDj
body:
**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/file_browser.rs:361-391` (the entries frame + `ScrollArea::show_rows`), message block at `:398-409`.

**What happens:** `navigate` lists the folder filtered by the chosen type filter (`:184`, `:179`). An empty folder, or a folder with no file matching the selected type filter, yields zero rows, so the bordered box is blank.

**Expected:** an empty-state message. The `message` match at `:398` only covers `NotFound` / `Replace` / read error / `truncated` — not the empty case. A simple "No items to show." would do.

title: Mini toolbar highlight swatches do not return the keyboard to the document
author: SlavenDj
body:
**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/mini_toolbar.rs:288` (`highlight_menu`).

**What happens:** picking a highlight colour swatch runs `app.run("format.highlight", …)` directly, so keyboard focus stays in the (closed) popup layer. Popups are excluded from the `refocus_after_chrome_click` safety net (`lib.rs:2000`), so typing then goes nowhere until the document is clicked again.

**Contrast:** the "No Color" button a few lines below (`:296`) uses `widgets::run_from_ribbon`, which sets `canvas.want_focus = true`. The swatch above should too.

**Related:** #1902 was the same class (Clipboard pane Delete).

title: Mini toolbar font colour Automatic does not return the keyboard to the document
author: SlavenDj
body:
**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/mini_toolbar.rs:308` (`font_color_menu`, the "Automatic" item).

**What happens:** choosing "Automatic" runs `app.run("format.color", …)` directly inside the popup; focus is not handed back to the document, so the next keystrokes are lost until it is clicked.

**Expected:** `widgets::run_from_ribbon(app, "format.color", …)` (what the ribbon uses), which restores `canvas.want_focus`.

**Related:** #1902.

title: Undo-history popup row does not return the keyboard to the document
author: SlavenDj
body:
**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/chrome.rs:177` (`undo_list`, the click handler).

**What happens:** clicking an Undo-history row runs `app.run("edit.undoTo", …)` from inside the popup and never restores document focus. Because the popup layer is excluded from the `refocus_after_chrome_click` safety net (`lib.rs:2000`), the document is left unfocused.

**Expected:** set `canvas.want_focus = true` (or route through `widgets::run_from_ribbon`) like the ribbon's undo buttons.

**Related:** #1902, and #1903 for the same popup's footer.

title: Ctrl+V doesn't paste a clipboard picture when Ctrl is released before V
author: jcagudelo12
body:
**Environment:** Ubuntu, GNOME Shell 50.1, Wayland, built from source (main @ d588e0b8)
**Steps**
1. Copy a picture (Print Screen, or "Copy image" in Firefox).
2. In WordCraft press Left Ctrl+V, releasing Ctrl slightly before V (the natural one-hand motion).
**Expected:** the picture is pasted.
**Actual:** nothing happens; you have to press it again, which feels like a delay. Releasing V
first (e.g. with Right Ctrl) pastes immediately (~15 ms). Right-click > Paste always works.
**Cause:** egui-winit swallows the Mod+V press, so WordCraft pastes a picture on V's *release*
(`crates/ui-egui/src/keys.rs:277`), and `is_paste_release` requires `modifiers.command` at that
moment. Instrumented log:
    suelta Ctrl          02:57:19.606
    V released cmd=false 02:57:19.675 -> paste_keys=false, nothing pasted
**Proposed fix:** a plain V press arrives as a Key event; a Mod+V press doesn't (egui-winit eats
it). So on V's release, if no V press was seen, treat it as Mod+V using the modifiers held while
Ctrl was down (to keep Mod+Shift+V / Mod+Alt+V apart). I can open a PR with a regression test.

title: Feature request: Select Text with Similar Formatting
author: peterw5000
body:
Word has a "Select Text with Similar Formatting" command. On Windows it's under Home > Editing > Select, and on macOS it's in the Styles pane. It looks at the formatting where the cursor is, and selects all the text in the document with the same formatting - usually the base style plus any direct formatting.

It would be great to have this in WordCraft, in the same places as Word (the Select dropdown and the Styles pane).

### How it works in Word
1. Put the cursor in some text, or select some.
2. Run the command.
3. Everything in the document with the same formatting gets selected, so you can change it all at once (apply a style, clear formatting, delete it, and so on).

### Matching
Word seems to compare the style plus direct formatting such as bold, italic, font, size and colour, but the Windows and Mac entry points may differ slightly (style only vs style plus direct formatting). If the selection covers mixed formatting, I think Word uses whatever is at the start of the selection.

### Why I'd use it
Mainly for tidying up documents that came from somewhere else. A common case is a document where someone has made headings by hand with bold and a bigger font. With this command, you can select all of them in one go and apply a proper Heading style. Find and replace with formatting can do it, but it's slower and fiddlier.

### Nice to have
- The same command available through `wordcraft-cli` / MCP.
- A count of how many matches were selected.

title: Page borders: `w:offsetFrom` is ignored when laying out
author: antoaster
body:
WordCraft 0.8.0 (Flatpak, Linux). Page borders are always placed `w:space` points from the page edge, whatever `w:offsetFrom` says.

**Repro:** an A4 page with 72pt margins and this border:

```xml
<w:pgBorders w:display="allPages" w:offsetFrom="text">
  <w:top w:val="single" w:sz="8" w:space="24" w:color="000000"/>
  <!-- left, bottom, right the same -->
</w:pgBorders>
```

| | Border distance from page edge |
|---|---|
| Expected (`offsetFrom="text"`: margin 72pt − space 24pt) | 48pt |
| LibreOffice 24.2.7 | 47pt |
| WordCraft 0.8.0 (screen and `wordcraft-cli convert` → PDF) | 24pt |

The same happens with no `w:offsetFrom` at all, which ECMA-376 §17.6.10 defines as measuring from the text.

_Edited to split out the saving problem into #3075 (and the related missing feature, first-page-only borders, into #3076)._

Cause, as far as I can tell: `crates/docx/src/read/props.rs` reads `w:pgBorders` with the shared `borders()` helper, which keeps only the sides (line 713 at 117aea3), and layout (`page_border_rules` in `crates/layout/src/lib.rs`) always measures from the page edge.

I have a fix with tests (including mirrored margins) and will open a PR for it, together with #3075.

title: Page borders: saving writes w:offsetFrom="text" and drops w:display and w:zOrder
author: antoaster
body:
WordCraft 0.8.0 (Flatpak, Linux). Split out of #3073 (layout ignoring `w:offsetFrom`).

Saving rewrites a section's page border settings: `w:offsetFrom` is always written as `"text"`, and `w:display` and `w:zOrder` are dropped.

**Repro:** a document whose `w:sectPr` has

```xml
<w:pgBorders w:display="firstPage" w:offsetFrom="page" w:zOrder="back">
  <w:top w:val="single" w:sz="8" w:space="24" w:color="000000"/>
  <!-- left, bottom, right the same -->
</w:pgBorders>
```

`wordcraft-cli convert in.docx out.docx` writes it back as

```xml
<w:pgBorders w:offsetFrom="text">
```

so in Word the border moves (it's now measured from the text instead of the page edge), shows on every page instead of the first only, and is drawn in front of the text instead of behind it.

Expected: the three attributes are kept as read (ECMA-376 §17.6.10). Borders created in WordCraft, which it draws from the page edge, should save as `w:offsetFrom="page"`.

The writer hardcodes `("w:offsetFrom", "text")` in `crates/docx/src/write/story.rs`, and the reader (`crates/docx/src/read/props.rs`, the `w:pgBorders` arm) keeps only the four sides.

Showing borders on the first page only, or on every page except the first, is a separate feature that WordCraft doesn't have yet (filed separately); this ticket is only about not losing the setting.

title: Page borders: first page only, or every page except the first (w:display)
author: antoaster
body:
Word's Page Borders dialog can apply a page border to **This section – First page only** or **This section – All except first page**, as well as to the whole document or this section. A common use is a decorative border on a cover page only. Files store the choice as `w:pgBorders/@w:display` (`allPages`, `firstPage`, `notFirstPage`; ECMA-376 §17.6.10).

WordCraft 0.8.0 has neither part:

- **Layout** draws page borders on every page of the section whatever `w:display` says, so a Word file with a cover-page-only border shows it on every page.
- **Borders and Shading › Page Border** and `design.pageBorders` only offer this section or the whole document (`applyTo: "section" | "document"`).

Expected: borders follow `w:display` on screen, in PDF export and in printing, and the dialog and command can set it (for example `applyTo: "firstPage" | "notFirstPage"`).

Keeping the attribute on save is #3075; this ticket is the feature itself.

title: PDF export is not reproducible: the same document twice gives different bytes
author: Hamza0101
body:
**Type:** Bug (minor)

Converting one document to PDF twice gives two different files, so a PDF cannot be checked by its hash, cached by content, or compared between runs.

**Version.** `wordcraft-cli` built from `main` at `117aea3`, macOS 26 (aarch64).

**Steps to reproduce**

```sh
printf 'Hello from a reproducibility check.\n' > in.txt
wordcraft-cli convert in.txt out1.pdf
sleep 2
wordcraft-cli convert in.txt out2.pdf
cmp out1.pdf out2.pdf
```

**Actual.** 88 bytes differ, the files are the same size, and the pages are identical:

```
/ModDate(D:20261019091517Z)        vs  …091519Z)
/CreationDate(D:20261019091517Z)   vs  …091519Z)
<xmp:ModifyDate>…T09:15:17+00:00   vs  …09:15:19+00:00
<xmpMM:InstanceID>…                vs  …
```

**Expected.** Either the export records no clock time when the document carries none, or there is a way to pin it — `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, as the [reproducible-builds specification](https://reproducible-builds.org/specs/source-date-epoch/) defines it, is the usual one and what VectorCraft adopted in storytold/vectorcraft#2947.

**Notes, and where I got stuck**

- The instance id is not a separate problem: krilla derives it with `stable_hash_base64(pdf.as_bytes())`, so it differs only because the timestamps do and would follow them once pinned.
- `wordcraft-cli info in.txt` reports `created: ''`, so the document carries no creation date of its own — the date in the PDF comes from the export.
- I tried the obvious site, `metadata()` in `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs`, where `let date = parse_iso(&c.created).or_else(|| now_unix().map(civil))` looks like the fallback in question. Making that honour `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` did **not** change the exported dates, which says the dates reaching the file come from somewhere else on the `convert` path. I did not want to guess further and send a change that looks right and does nothing.

So this is a report rather than a patch: the symptom is reproducible and the mechanism is clear, but the date's real source on …
