title: Feature request: direct EPUB import
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## Request

Add a way to open EPUB (.epub) files directly as editable WordCraft documents, symmetric to the EPUB 3 export added in #2815 (closes #2265). #2815's description explicitly notes "Export only; EPUB import remains open."

## Scope

Import a reflowable EPUB 3 (OCF ZIP: `META-INF/container.xml` → OPF package document → spine-ordered XHTML content documents + manifest images) into the existing flow/document model:

- Read the OPF manifest and spine for reading order, media types and `dc:title"/`dc:creator`/`dc:language` metadata.
- Parse each spine XHTML content document and concatenate into one document, resolving manifest images through an image loader backed by the ZIP archive.
- Document what is out of scope for a first pass (EPUB 2/NCX-only packages, DRM, scripted/fixed-layout EPUBs) rather than silently mis-handling them.

I've read `crates/formats/src/epub.rs` (the exporter) and `crates/formats/src/odt.rs`/`crates/formats/src/html.rs`: the existing `html::parse_with`/`ImageLoader` abstraction and the ODT importer's `zip::ZipArchive` handling look directly reusable, so this shouldn't need a new parsing approach — written from the public EPUB 3.3/OCF specs, same as the exporter.

## Not proposed

No external or GPL-licensed conversion tool (e.g. pandoc) — per AGENTS.md's clean-room rule, this would be a native Rust implementation only.

title: ODF format as default format
author: Thatoo
body:
ODF is the ISO-standardised open document format championed by LibreOffice and mandated by public administrations across the EU. Xordcraft is positioned as an open alternative to proprietary office suites, making robust ODF support a strategic requirement, not just a feature request.

Supporting ODF is an important part of supporting the open source movement. The "Save" and "Save as..." dialogues should include a note above the file type drop-down that encourages people to choose ODF (it could be the default format). This will gradually increase awareness among end-users about open standards.

In comparison, keeping proprietary ooxml format would not fully help people free themselves from corporate's software.

title: [Windows Jump List] Opening a recent document from taskbar right-click context menu opens "Recover Documents" dark screen
author: psign04
body:
### Environment
- **OS:** Windows 11
- **App Version:** WordCraft v0.8.0

### Describe the Bug
When launching WordCraft directly, recent documents display fine on the home screen and open normally.
However, right-clicking the WordCraft icon on the Windows taskbar/Jump List and selecting a recent document opens the app on a black screen displaying **"Recover Documents"** instead of loading the document directly.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Open WordCraft, edit/save a document, and close the application.
2. Right-click the WordCraft icon on the Windows taskbar (or Jump List in the Start menu).
3. Click on the recent file that was just closed.
4. WordCraft launches, but instead of opening the document workspace, it displays a dark/black screen with the "Recover Documents" dialog/view.

### Expected Behavior
Selecting a recent document from the Windows taskbar context menu should pass the file path argument cleanly and open the document workspace directly.

### Possible Root Cause
When invoked via Windows Jump List, the file path is passed as a command-line argument (`wordcraft.exe "path\to\file"`). The engine seems to handle file argument loading during initial startup before the document manager/layout thread is fully initialized, causing it to assume an ungraceful shutdown/crash and falling back to document recovery.

title: Options › Language always says spelling is checked in English (United States)
author: jvspier
body:
**What happens:** File › Options › Language, under *Proofing language*, always says "Spelling and grammar are checked in English (United States).", whatever language the text is in. ```rust
note(ui, "Spelling and grammar are checked in English (United States).");
```

**Suggested fix:** name the language at the caret, as the status bar does:
```rust
let lang = crate::ribbon::caret_language(app);
ui.label(RichText::new(crate::i18n::fmt(tl!("Spelling and grammar are checked in {lang}."), &[("lang", &lang)])).small().weak());
```
plus the new sentence in the catalogs (Dutch: "Spelling en grammatica worden gecontroleerd in het {lang}."). I run this locally and it shows the right language.

(Found and written up with help from Claude Code.)

title: CLI: `run` without `--file` creates a Letter page whatever the region (WORDCRAFT_REGION and the locale are ignored)
author: great-horn
body:
**What happens**

`wordcraft-cli --help` says documents created by the CLI use the region's paper, read from `LC_ALL` / `LC_PAPER` / `LANG` or the platform, and that `WORDCRAFT_REGION` forces it. `convert` from a text file follows this, but `run` without `--file` always writes a Letter page.

**Steps** (wordcraft-cli 0.8.0, macOS 27.0.1 with region Switzerland; same result on Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 with `LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8`)

```sh
for e in WORDCRAFT_REGION=fr-CH WORDCRAFT_REGION=en-GB LC_ALL=fr_CH.UTF-8 LC_PAPER=de_DE.UTF-8 LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8; do
  env $e wordcraft-cli run --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"x"}' --save region.docx >/dev/null
  echo "$e: $(unzip -p region.docx word/document.xml | grep -o '<w:pgSz[^>]*>')"
done
```

Every line prints `<w:pgSz w:w="12240" w:h="15840"/>` (Letter). For comparison:

```sh
printf 'Bonjour\n' > in.txt
WORDCRAFT_REGION=fr-CH wordcraft-cli convert in.txt fromtxt.docx
unzip -p fromtxt.docx word/document.xml | grep -o '<w:pgSz[^>]*>'
# <w:pgSz w:w="11906" w:h="16838"/>   (A4, as documented)
```

**Expected:** `run` without `--file` picks the paper the same way as `convert`: A4 for `fr-CH`, `en-GB` and `de_DE`.

**Also:** the default language in `styles.xml` stays `en-US` for every region tried. I'm not sure that is meant to follow the region, but if it is, it doesn't.

**Workaround:** start the command list with `--cmd 'layout.size={"name":"A4"}' --cmd 'review.language={"lang":"fr-CH","default":true}'`.

title: Windows, NVDA/UIA: focus never reaches the ribbon, Tab types into the document, names and heading roles missing (0.8.0)
author: devinprater
body:
# WordCraft 0.8.0 on Windows: screen-reader and keyboard findings

Reporter: R. D. T. Prater, a blind user who writes for a living and reads the screen with a braille display.
Build: WordCraft 0.8.0, `wordcraft-0.8.0-windows-x64-portable.zip`, Windows 11 x64, Authenticode signature `Valid`, `CN=Learning Machines Inc`.
Method: Windows UI Automation, the same API that NVDA, Narrator and JAWS read. I am blind, so I have not run a screen reader myself here. Every statement below was measured by reading the accessibility tree and by sending keystrokes, then reading the tree again.

It relates to #1012 and the "not yet tried with real screen readers" note in `docs/gaps.md` (item 18). Two things are better than the roadmap suggests, one is worse, and one is a separate defect.

## What works

1. The document canvas is exposed well. `ControlType.Document` supports `TextPattern` and `ValuePattern`. The Studio handbook sample read back 2,022 characters as continuous text, and the tree carries a `List` with `ListItem` children, a `Table` with `DataItem` cells, and `Hyperlink` nodes. That matches the AccessKit work in #488.
2. The File page, ribbon tab names and most ribbon command names are exposed with proper roles. Tabs are `Button` with names `File`, `Home`, `Insert`, `Draw`, `Design`, `Layout`, `References`, `Mailings`, `Review`, `View`, `Developer`, `Zotero`, `Help`. Commands such as `Paste (?V)`, `Bold`, `Find`, `Replace`, `Text Effects and Typography` and the Styles gallery tiles are named as well.

## What is missing

3. Fifty-three controls take keyboard focus and have no accessible name at all. They are the font name box, the font size box, both font-size arrows, every colour and underline-style dropdown, the style gallery's scroll arrows, the quick access toolbar, the title-bar search box, the zoom slider and its buttons, and the ruler's tab selector. A screen reader has nothing to say for a control with no name.
4. The document's structure does not reach a screen re…

title: Dragging a picture near the bottom of page moves it off the page
author: RatkoR
body: A document with two pages of text and a picture on page 1. Drag the picture down toward the bottom of page 1: instead of landing where it's dropped, it ends up far below, outside page 1. It is still part of page 1, so it's cut off at the page edge and appears to sit "under" page 2. You can see its blue selection box over page 2, but no picture, just white space. Steps to reproduce 1. Type =lorem() and press Enter twice, so there are two pages of text. 2. Insert a picture on page 1. 3. Drag it a few lines down: it lands where it's dropped. 4. Drag it further down, so its bottom goes past the end of page 1: the part past the edge is cut off. 5. Drag it again, near the bottom of page 1: it jumps off the page. Only its selection box shows, over page 2. Expected: the picture lands where it's dropped. Actual: it is anchored to a page-1 paragraph with a vertical offset that puts it hundreds of points below the bottom of page 1.

title: Windows screen reader: keyboard focus never enters the ribbon; Tab and keytip letters edit the document
author: devinprater
body:
Split from #3164 at the maintainers' request.

With a screen reader or keyboard alone, the ribbon cannot be reached. From the document, Tab never moves focus out of the page: twice in a row it inserted two tab characters (text length 5, 6, 7).

Alt followed by the tab keytip letter `H` does switch the tab visually (a screenshot shows Home selected and command badges P, C, O, F, B, I, U over the buttons), but keyboard focus never moves: `AutomationElement.FocusedElement` stays `Document 'Document1'` through Alt, Alt+H and a following Tab. The next Tab goes back into the text and inserts a tab character, and a keytip letter typed while the badges are showing also lands in the document.

So a blind user cannot walk the ribbon, cannot tell what a keytip letter did, and the keystrokes meant to explore it edit the document.

Suggested fix: make ribbon tabs and command buttons focusable widgets with a Tab/arrow focus ring, keep the canvas from handling Tab while that ring is active, expose the active tab as a selected tab/button node, return focus to the canvas on Escape, and swallow Tab and unbadged keys while keytips are showing (`keytips::handle_key`, `crates/ui-egui/src/keytips.rs`).

Related: #1012, #3164.

title: Windows screen reader: 53 keyboard-focusable controls have no accessible name
author: devinprater
body:
Split from #3164 at the maintainers' request.

Measured on the Home tab with the sample document open: the window has 115 keyboard-focusable elements and 53 of them have no `Name` at all (46%).

The unnamed ones include the font name box and the font size box (both `Edit`, 201 px and 54 px wide), every colour and underline-style dropdown, the style gallery's scroll arrows, the quick access toolbar, the title-bar search box, the zoom slider and its buttons, and the ruler's tab selector.

A screen reader has nothing to announce when focus lands on any of them, so the user hears only "edit" or "custom".

Suggested fix: give each a name through `widget_info` (most already have a tooltip or a nearby label string), report the font size box's value, and name the zoom slider.

Related: #3164.

title: Screen readers: the document exposes no heading, paragraph, cell or image roles or text
author: devinprater
body:
Split from #3164 at the maintainers' request.

The canvas node is a `Document` with a `TextPattern` that returns the page as one string (2,022 characters from the Studio handbook sample). Under it the tree is only `Group`, `Text`, `List`, `ListItem`, `Table` and `DataItem` nodes, none of them named and none carrying their own text.

There is no `Heading` (with level), `Paragraph`, `Cell`, `Row` or `Image` role, so a screen reader can read the page as a block of text but cannot move by heading, hear "heading level 2", or know that a table cell is a cell or a picture is a picture. `crates/ui-egui/src/a11y.rs` builds this tree.

Suggested fix: set `Role::Heading` with `set_level`, `Role::Paragraph` on body paragraphs, `Role::Cell`/`Row` on tables, `Role::Image` with a label on pictures and charts, and put each paragraph's text on its node.

Related: #488, #3164.

title: Windows screen reader: the document reports IsReadOnly=true, so NVDA does not echo typed characters
author: devinprater
body:
Split from #3164 at the maintainers' request.

NVDA reads the page with the arrow keys but says nothing while typing. The document states it is read-only:

- `IUIAutomationValuePattern::IsReadOnly` on the document element is **True**.
- `ITextRangeProvider::GetAttributeValue(UIA_IsReadOnlyAttributeId)` is **True**.
- NVDA's developer info: `role: DOCUMENT`, `states: FOCUSABLE, FOCUSED, READONLY`.

The document is editable: typing changes the text and `ValuePattern.Value` returns the new text. NVDA does not speak typed characters in a field it believes is read-only.

The font name and font size `Edit` elements in the same window report `IsReadOnly = False`, so the flag is specific to the document node. Nothing in `wordcraft-ui-egui`, egui 0.36.2 or craft-ui calls `set_read_only`, and accesskit's flag defaults to false, so it is worth finding what sets it.

Suggested fix: `clear_read_only()` where `a11y::expose` sets the document node's role and label (`crates/ui-egui/src/a11y.rs`), plus a test that `ValuePattern.IsReadOnly` is false on the document.

Related: #3164.

title: Save Changes: Tab from Save skips Don't Save (focus order is the reverse of the visual order)
author: devinprater
body:
Split from #3164 at the maintainers' request.

With the Save Changes prompt open, focus starts on Save. Tab does not reach Don't Save; Shift+Tab does.

In the `Dialog::SaveChanges` arm of `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs` the buttons are created as Cancel, Don't Save, Save inside a `right_to_left` layout. The screen reads Save, Don't Save, Cancel, but egui's focus order follows creation order, so Tab from Save leaves the row instead of moving to Don't Save.

Suggested fix: create the three buttons in visual order (Save, Don't Save, Cancel) and right-align the group, or set the focus order explicitly. A test that Tab from Save lands on Don't Save would cover it.

Related: #3164.

title: Launch: no control takes focus, so NVDA announces only "WordCraft window"; start-page tiles are unnamed text
author: devinprater
body:
Split from #3164 at the maintainers' request.

Opening WordCraft leaves focus on the window itself, so a screen reader user hears the title and nothing about what is on screen.

Measured on the start page:

- The `Window` element is `focusable = True` and was focused at launch.
- No descendant of the window had keyboard focus (`HasKeyboardFocus` count: 0).
- NVDA's developer info: `name: 'WordCraft'`, `role: WINDOW`, `states: FOCUSABLE, FOCUSED`, `TextInfo: displayModel.DisplayModelTextInfo` (the offscreen model, so there is no text to read).

No greeting, no Blank document, no templates and no recent files are announced. The template tiles are `Text` elements inside unnamed `Custom` containers (`home_page` and `template_tile` in `crates/ui-egui/src/backstage.rs`), so even if focus reached one, there is no button role and no name to announce.

Suggested fix: on the first frame of the start page, request focus on the first tile and give each tile a `Button` role with its name and selected state; when a document opens, request focus on the canvas. A test asserting a named, focused control exists after the first frame would cover it.

Related: #3164.

title: Proposal: adopt Phosphor Icons for the interface icon set
author: DailyXplorer
body:
## What Phosphor Icons is
[Phosphor Icons](https://phosphoricons.com) is an open-source icon family ([source](https://github.com/phosphor-icons/core), MIT). It has 1,500+ icons in six weights (Thin, Light, Regular, Bold, Fill, Duotone), drawn on a 256×256 grid with a consistent stroke and optical sizing. The Regular weight matches WordCraft's current line-art style. The SVGs are small, vector, and use `currentColor`, so they can follow the theme.

## Proposal
Adopt Phosphor Regular as the base icon set, starting with the File sidebar shown below. Keep the hand-drawn set for Word-specific commands where Phosphor has no faithful equivalent. A full replacement would lose meaning for commands such as Track Changes, Format Painter, Character Border, Enclose Characters, SmartArt, WordArt, mail merge and equations.

## Screenshots
English interface. Left: the current File sidebar with the drawn icons (the sidebar proposed in #3183). Right: the same sidebar with Phosphor Regular icons. The right panel is a mockup; the SVGs are not integrated yet.

![Current drawn icons vs Phosphor Icons](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DailyXplorer/wordcraft/pr-assets/wordcraft-phosphor-sidebar.png)

## Scope
- Start with the File sidebar: Back, Home, New, Open, Info, Recover, Save, Save As, Print, Export, Close, Options.
- Keep `icons::paint(name, …)`; add a mapping table with a Phosphor glyph and a drawn fallback.
- Land the sidebar first, then decide whether the work goes per tab or per area.

## Integration options
- Vendor the Regular SVGs (MIT, add a row to `ATTRIBUTION.md`) and draw their paths or rasterise them at build time.
- Embed the Phosphor font and draw glyphs.
- The SVG route keeps the current vector rendering and theme colours.

## Open questions
- Regular, Bold or Fill weight at the 17–18 px ribbon size?
- Which Phosphor glyphs for Back and Recover? The mockup uses `arrow-left` and `clock-counter-clockwise`; `arrow-u-left-up` and `arrow-counter-clockwise` are alternative…

title: Integral operators (∫ ∬ ∭ ∮) don't grow with a tall operand in display equations; Word and LibreOffice draw them taller
author: gabgart
body:
## Summary

In a display equation, the integral operators (∫, ∬, ∭, ∮) are drawn at the size of a normal letter and do not grow with their operand. Word draws them tall enough to match the integrand, and LibreOffice also draws them taller. Delimiters, radicals, ∑ and ∏ look the same in the three programs, so this seems specific to how the integral operators are sized.

The test file was created by WordCraft itself and saved as `.docx`, so this is not about importing a file from another program: the same file looks right in Word and worse in WordCraft.

## Environment

- WordCraft 0.8.0 (macOS 27.0.1); the page was rendered with `wordcraft-cli` 0.8.0
- Microsoft Word for Mac 16.114 (Spanish UI), for comparison
- LibreOffice 26.2.3.2, for comparison

## Steps to reproduce

Create a new document and insert these as display equations (I used LaTeX input):

1. `\int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{\sin x}{x}\,dx = \frac{\pi}{2}`
2. `\int_{0}^{1} \frac{\frac{a}{b}+\frac{c}{d}}{\frac{e}{f}}\,dx`
3. `\iint_{D} f(x,y)\,dA \quad \iiint_{V} \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}\,dV \quad \oint_{C} \vec{F}\cdot d\vec{r}`

WordCraft shows equations 1 and 2 in its linear format as `∫_0^∞▒((sin⁡x)/x dx)=π/2` and `∫_0^1▒((a/b+c/d)/(e/f) dx)`.

## Expected

As in Word: the integral sign is taller, and in equation 2 it spans most of the stacked fraction. The limits sit at the bottom and top of the sign.

## Actual

In WordCraft the integral sign stays about as tall as a letter. In equation 2 it is much shorter than the fraction next to it. ∬, ∭ and ∮ are small too.

## Notes

- Delimiters (`\left( … \right)` with stacked fractions), matrices, `\sqrt` with a fraction inside, ∑ and ∏ match Word in this document, so the stretching code for those works.
- The `m:nary` elements WordCraft writes only carry `m:ctrlPr` in `m:naryPr` (for example, no `m:grow`), so Word chooses the size by itself.
- Related: #2662 ("Respect the font minimum height for display operators") covers the minimum display height of n-…

body:

Its `word/document.xml` (full file, reformatted):

```xml
<w:document xmlns:w="...">
  <w:body>
    <w:tbl>
      <w:tblPr><w:tblW w:w="0" w:type="auto"/></w:tblPr>
      <w:sdt>

title: Inserting a Table of Contents leaves the caret inside its own title, not after it like Word
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## What happens

After `references.toc` (Insert › Table of Contents) builds the table, the caret is left at offset 0 of the TOC's own `TOCHeading` paragraph — literally right before the "Contents" title text — instead of in a fresh paragraph after the table.

Confirmed against real Microsoft 365 Word (16.0.20527.20054): clicking Insert › Table of Contents › Automatic Table 1 on a document with no headings yet (Word warns but still creates an empty table) leaves the caret in a clean new paragraph immediately below the table's "No table of contents entries found." line — typing right away lands cleanly after the table, never inside it.

## Why it matters

This is the natural next step after inserting a TOC at the top of a new document: write the title, then start typing headings and body text. In WordCraft today, anything typed right after `references.toc` lands *inside* the TOC's own title paragraph instead. Concretely:

```
wordcraft-cli run --template blank --cmd 'references.toc={"levels":2}' --print

shows the selection left at `{"path":[0],"off":0}` — the very start of the paragraph holding "Contents".

Continuing to type a heading and some body text there, then calling "Update Table" later (a completely ordinary workflow: insert the TOC placeholder first, write the document, update the table at the end) corrupts the document: the TOC's own "Contents" title text ends up stripped out and spliced onto an unrelated paragraph elsewhere, while the `TOCHeading` paragraph itself goes blank. Minimal repro:

title: Bibliography, Table of Figures, Table of Authorities and Index all leave the caret inside their own title (same bug as #3227's TOC)
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## What

Follow-up to #3227 (fixed in #3228): the same caret-placement bug exists in every sibling of `references.toc` — **Bibliography**, **Table of Figures**, **Table of Authorities**, and (through `references.index`'s first-creation path) **Index**. All four share `generated_list` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/citations.rs`, which builds the title paragraph, the field and the entries but never moves the selection afterward.

```
wordcraft-cli run --template blank --cmd 'references.bibliography={}' --print
# references.bibliography: {"anchor":{"off":0,"path":[0],...}}  <- inside "References", not after it
```

Same four commands, same result — the caret lands at offset 0 of the generated list's own title paragraph:

```
wordcraft-cli run --template blank --cmd 'references.tableOfAuthorities={}' --print
wordcraft-cli run --template blank --cmd 'references.caption={"label":"Figure","text":"A plan"}' --cmd 'caret.docStart={}' --cmd 'references.tableOfFigures={}' --print
wordcraft-cli run --template blank --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"Kiln"}' --cmd 'select.all={}' --cmd 'references.markEntry={}' --cmd 'caret.docStart={}' --cmd 'references.index={}' --print
```

## Why it matters

Exactly the #3227 scenario, just for a different References-tab button: insert the list, then keep writing the document. Anything typed right after inserting a Bibliography/Table of Figures/Table of Authorities/Index lands inside the list's own title paragraph instead of after it, and a later "Update" call on that list can splice stray text out of its title and into whatever body content happens to end up adjacent.

## Fix

Working on the same fix as #3228: move the selection to a paragraph right after the generated list's entries once `generated_list` finishes building it, reusing one that's already there or inserting an empty one if the list ends the document.

title: Closing a .md document: "Save" in the close-changes dialog can never succeed, with no clear warning
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## What happens

Editing a `.md` (or any other format `save()` doesn't mark as fully saved — see below) document and trying to close it traps you in a loop: the "Do you want to save changes?" dialog's **Save** button writes the file correctly, but the document never stops being "Edited", so closing is silently refused every time, with the only explanation a small, easy-to-miss status-bar line that appears *after* the dialog has already closed.

**Steps to reproduce** (confirmed with `wordcraft-cli`/the desktop app, official v0.8.0 release):
1. Open or create a `.md` document, type something, press `Ctrl+W` (File › Close) or the window's close button.
2. The "Do you want to save changes to `name.md`?" dialog appears (screenshot: the exact same dialog a real user hit, attached in the linked discussion). Click **Save**.
3. The dialog closes — but you're dropped right back into the editor, title bar still reads "`name` — Edited", and closing again immediately re-triggers the same dialog. This repeats forever; **Save** can never actually close the document.
4. The *only* indication of what's going on is a small line of blue text in the bottom status bar: "That format doesn't keep everything, so the document is still open. Save it as a Word document (.docx) to go on." — which most people never see, because their attention was on the dialog that just closed, not the status bar.

I independently reproduced this exact flow via the control protocol (`ui.key` for the real `Ctrl+S` / `Ctrl+W` shortcuts, not scripted `engine.execute`, so it goes through the same code path a mouse-and-keyboard user hits) and confirmed:
- `file.save` on the `.md` path **does** write the file correctly with the latest content every time (verified on disk).
- `Session::dirty` **never** clears for a `.md` save — `crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs`'s `save()` only clears `dirty` for `["docx", "docm", "dotx", "dotm", "odt", "rtf", "json", "xml"]`; `md` isn't in that list.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`'s `s…

title: Markdown import doesn't support task lists, reference-style links, or footnotes — they leak through as literal text
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## Summary

`crates/formats/src/markdown.rs` documents its import coverage as "a CommonMark subset plus GitHub tables and strikethrough" ([markdown.rs:1-9](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/main/crates/formats/src/markdown.rs#L1-L9)). Three widely-used constructs aren't in that list and, confirmed empirically, aren't parsed at all — they pass through import as literal text instead of being converted or erroring:

1. **GFM task lists** — `- [ ]` / `- [x]`
2. **Reference-style links** — `[text][ref]` with a separate `[ref]: url` definition line
3. **Footnotes** — `[^1]` with a separate `[^1]: content` definition line

None of these round-trip as intended; the raw markdown syntax ends up as visible document text.

## Repro

Input (`test.md`):
```markdown
- [ ] Unchecked task
- [x] Checked task

Reference link: [click here][ref1]
Footnote: some text[^1]

[ref1]: https://example.com/ref
[^1]: Footnote body
```

Imported and converted to plain text (`wordcraft-cli text test.md`):
```
•	[ ] Unchecked task
•	[x] Checked task
Reference link: [click here][ref1] Footnote: some text[^1]
[ref1]: https://example.com/ref [^1]: Footnote body
```

Observed:
- Task list markers are not recognized as checkboxes — they render as a bullet followed by literal `[ ]`/`[x]` text.
- The reference link `[click here][ref1]` is not resolved against its `[ref1]: url` definition — both the link and the definition line survive as plain text in the document body (the definition line isn't even consumed/hidden, it becomes a stray paragraph).
- The footnote marker `[^1]` and its `[^1]: ...` definition behave the same way — no footnote is created, both bits of syntax become visible text.

By contrast, inline links (`[text](url)`) and autolinks (`<https://...>`) both work correctly, and `data:`-URI images are converted to real pictures as documented — so this isn't a general inline-parsing gap, just these three constructs.

## Why it matters

- Task lists are extremely common in real-world ma…

title: DOCX: w:linkStyles makes Word restyle a document from the local Normal.dotm
author: pick2510
body:
## What Word does

`w:settings/w:linkStyles` (ECMA-376 §17.15.1.55, "Automatically update document styles") makes Word replace the document's styles with those of the attached template when it opens the file. For most documents that's the user's own Normal.dotm. WordCraft follows the styles in the file and never reads Word templates (#377). A document with this setting can therefore paginate differently from Word, and Word's result depends on the template installed on the machine.

## Observed in Word for Mac

Compatibility mode 15, with Word's stock Normal.dotm. The synthetic document's `docDefaults` have spacing after 160 and line 259. Its Normal style sets after 0 and line 240 (single), and the default font is Times New Roman 12 pt. Values are read back through AppleScript (`space after` / `line spacing` of each paragraph's format, and `name of font object`):

| paragraph | without `w:linkStyles` | with `w:linkStyles` |
|---|---|---|
| no direct spacing | after 0, line 12 pt (single), Times New Roman | **after 8, line 13.9 pt (1.16), Aptos** |
| direct `<w:spacing w:line="360" w:lineRule="auto"/>` | after 0, line 18 | **after 8**, line 18 |
| style based on Normal with its own `w:after="100"` | after 5 | after 5 |
| direct `<w:spacing w:after="0" …/>` | after 0 | **after 8** |

So Word swaps Normal for the template's Normal (Aptos, 8 pt after, line 13.9 pt at 12 pt, about 1.16). Spacing a style sets itself survives. In this probe, Word even replaced a direct `w:after="0"`.

## Real-world effect

In a private corpus of 180 real manuscripts compared page by page with Word for Mac, 2 documents carry `w:linkStyles`. One of them comes out 3 pages shorter in WordCraft than in Word. title: A large copied picture does not paste into another document (the clipboard's HTML limit)
author: albayazid
body:
## Description

A picture copied in WordCraft travels to another document as HTML: the picture's bytes, base64-encoded, inside a `data:` URI. The clipboard and the paste path cap that HTML at 16 MiB, so a picture whose HTML is longer than that is dropped on the way in — pasting it into another document inserts nothing, while the same document still pastes the picture.

The picture should travel as the picture, the way Word does it: the system clipboard carries the picture itself, so the size of the HTML is not the limit on which pictures travel.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Put a large picture in a document — a PNG of about 12 MB or more (a photo pasted as PNG, a scan, a CAD drawing).
2. Copy the picture.
3. Open another document (File › Open, or a second window) and paste (Ctrl+V).

## Expected behavior

The picture is inserted at the cursor position.

## Actual behavior

Nothing is pasted. The paste reports what the clipboard holds — the HTML is on it, but too long to read — and no picture arrives.

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| The same document | The picture is pasted (WordCraft's own copy holds it) |
| Another document, picture under ~12 MB | The picture is pasted, as HTML |
| Another document, picture over ~12 MB | Nothing is pasted |

## Where the limit is

- `MAX_PASTE_BYTES` (16 MiB) in `crates/engine/src/cmd/paste.rs` caps what a paste may carry.
- The clipboard reader drops a longer HTML: `apps/wordcraft/src/clipboard.rs` reads the clipboard's HTML and filters it by the same cap.
- `rich_fragment` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/paste.rs` refuses a longer HTML as well, and a picture-only copy has no text to fall back on.

Measured on the engine's paste path, with a picture carried as HTML:

| Picture | PNG | HTML | Pasted |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 × 400 | 625 KiB | 834 KiB | yes |
| 1200 × 1200 | 5,626 KiB | 7,502 KiB | yes |
| 2000 × 2000 | 15,628 KiB | 20,837 KiB | no |
| 2400 × 2400 | 22,504 KiB | 30,005 KiB | no |

## What works / doesn't work

| Scenario…

title: select.text and edit.find find nothing in the main text while the caret is in a footnote
author: chazmaniandinkle
body:
## Summary
When the caret is inside a footnote, `select.text` fails with "not found" and `edit.find` reports 0
matches for text that exists in the main document. This is easy to hit headlessly because
`references.footnote` always leaves the caret in the note.

## Version / OS
wordcraft-cli 0.8.0, Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)

## Repro
```
wordcraft-cli run --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"Main sentence."}' \
  --cmd 'references.footnote={"text":"Note text."}' \
  --cmd 'edit.find={"text":"Main"}' \
  --cmd 'select.text={"text":"Main"}' --print
```

## Expected
"Main" is found in the main text (Word's Find covers the main document as well as notes), or, if the
search is meant to be limited to one story, the command docs say so and/or the commands accept a
`story` parameter.

## Actual
```
text.insert: {"anchor":{"off":14,"path":[0],"story":"body"},"focus":{"off":14,"path":[0],"story":"body"}}
references.footnote: {"id":1}
edit.find: {"count":0,"matches":[]}
wordcraft-cli: select.text: `Main` not found
```
(exit code 1)

## Workaround
Move the caret back to the main text first, e.g.
`--cmd 'caret.set={"pos":{"path":[0],"off":14,"story":"body"}}'`; after that `select.text` finds
"Main" and `caret.docEnd` goes to the end of the main text.

title: edit.replaceAll / edit.replace / edit.find accept a missing `text` and ignore unknown parameter names
author: chazmaniandinkle
body:
## Summary
`edit.replaceAll` documents `{"text": string, "with": string, ...}`, but a call with misspelled keys
(`find`/`replace`) or with no parameters at all succeeds with `{"replaced":0}`. The same holds for
`edit.replace` and `edit.find`. Other commands do validate required parameters (`text.insert` without
`text` fails with "bad parameters: `text` (string) is required"), so a typo in a find/replace call is
indistinguishable from "no matches". More generally, unknown keys are ignored by every command tried
(`matchcase` instead of `matchCase`, `para.heading1={"bogus":1}`, `text.insert={"text":"!","bogus":1}`),
which makes silent misconfiguration easy for CLI/MCP callers.

## Version / OS
wordcraft-cli 0.8.0, Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)

## Repro
```
wordcraft-cli run --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"cat cat"}' \
  --cmd 'edit.replaceAll={"find":"cat","replace":"dog"}' \
  --cmd 'edit.replaceAll={}' \
  --cmd 'edit.find={}' \
  --cmd 'edit.replace={"find":"cat","replace":"dog"}' \
  --cmd 'edit.replaceAll={"text":"cat","with":"dog","matchcase":true}' --print
```

## Expected
The calls without `text` fail like `text.insert` does ("bad parameters: `text` (string) is required").
Ideally unknown keys are rejected too, or at least reported (e.g. "unknown parameter `find`").

## Actual
```
text.insert: {"anchor":{"off":7,"path":[0],"story":"body"},"focus":{"off":7,"path":[0],"story":"body"}}
edit.replaceAll: {"replaced":0}
edit.replaceAll: {"replaced":0}
edit.find: {"count":0}
edit.replace: {"remaining":0}
edit.replaceAll: {"replaced":2}
```
Exit code 0; the misspelled `matchcase` in the last call is silently ignored.

## Workaround
Use the exact documented names from `wordcraft-cli commands --json` (`text`, `with`, `matchCase`, ...)
and treat `replaced: 0` as a possible parameter error.

title: Plain text, Markdown, HTML and RTF exports drop footnotes (reference mark and note text)
author: chazmaniandinkle
body:
## Summary
A footnote vanishes completely when the document is exported to `.txt`, `.md`, `.html` or `.rtf`
(and from `wordcraft-cli text`): neither the reference mark nor the note text is written, although
the footnote is in the .docx (`inspect` lists it under `parts`).

## Version / OS
wordcraft-cli 0.8.0, Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)

## Repro
```
wordcraft-cli run --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"Main sentence."}' \
  --cmd 'references.footnote={"text":"Note text."}' --save fn.docx
wordcraft-cli text fn.docx
wordcraft-cli convert fn.docx fn.md   && cat fn.md
wordcraft-cli convert fn.docx fn.html && grep -c "Note text" fn.html
wordcraft-cli convert fn.docx fn.rtf  && grep -c "Note text" fn.rtf
wordcraft-cli inspect fn.docx
```

## Expected
The note is kept in each format, e.g. a reference mark plus the notes after the text in plain text,
`[^1]` / `[^1]: Note text.` in Markdown, a linked note list in HTML, `{\footnote ...}` in RTF.

## Actual
```
$ wordcraft-cli text fn.docx
Main sentence.
$ cat fn.md
Main sentence.
$ grep -c "Note text" fn.html
0
$ grep -c "Note text" fn.rtf
0
$ wordcraft-cli inspect fn.docx
... "parts": [{"id": 1, "kind": "footnote", "text": " Note text."}] ...
```
`convert --markup` to .md gives the same output.

## Workaround
Export to .docx or PDF, which keep footnotes.

title: Control channel: file.new, file.open, file.recover and the mailings merges silently discard unsaved work
author: matstrange
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at `9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770`. **Severity:** Medium (data loss). **Confidence:** high — reproduced at runtime against a worktree at this commit, with and without a candidate fix.

## Root cause and evidence
[`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:110-121`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770/crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs#L110-L121) is the control channel's unsaved-work guard. It refuses a command only when the id is exactly `file.close` and the document is dirty:

```rust
if id == "file.close" && app.session.dirty {
    return Some("the document has unsaved changes: save it first, or pass {\"force\": true} to discard them and close");
}
// Comment text still being typed is unsaved work too (#1348): replacing the document would drop it.
(crate::discards_document(id, params) && crate::panes::has_comment_drafts(app))
    .then_some("a comment is still being edited: finish it first, or pass {\"force\": true} to discard it")
```

The interactive path uses the full list of commands that replace the document (`discards_document`, [`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:2647`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L2647)): `file.new`, `file.close`, `file.open` with a path, `file.recover` with `restore`, `mailings.labels`, `mailings.envelopes` and `mailings.finish`. The control channel applies that list only to *comment drafts*, never to a dirty document — so every other document-replacing command replaces the document with no question at all.

[`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:282-285`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770/crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs#L282-L285) has the same gap for `app.quit`: it sets `quit_requested`, and `close_requested` returns true as soon as that flag is set, so the Save prompt never appears.

title: The privacy options, the properties and the inspector's removals change a protected document
author: matstrange
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at `9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770`. **Severity:** Medium (editing restrictions). **Confidence:** high — reproduced at runtime against a worktree at this commit, with and without a candidate fix.

## Root cause and evidence
[`crates/engine/src/cmd/protect.rs:206-208`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770/crates/engine/src/cmd/protect.rs#L206-L208) waves through every file command by prefix:

```rust
fn always_allowed(id: &str) -> bool {
    id == "review.restrict" || id.starts_with("file.") || id == "edit.undo" || id == "edit.redo"
}
```

`always_allowed` is consulted before any mode check, so a `file.*` command is allowed in every protection mode, and the post-check that would roll a change back is skipped for it as well. Three of those commands change the open document:

- `file.privacyOptions` ([`crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:134`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770/crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L134)) writes `doc.settings.remove_personal_info` and `doc.settings.remove_date_time`. Its own comment says the change is "refused on a protected document"; it is not.
- `file.properties` ([`crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:124`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770/crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L124)) rewrites `doc.core` and the custom properties.
- `file.inspect` with `{"remove": [...]}` ([`crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs:462`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770/crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs#L462)) deletes hidden text, comments, revisions and headers straight from the document.

title: The post-check after a command doesn't compare the document's settings or metadata
author: matstrange
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at `9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770`. **Severity:** Medium (editing restrictions). **Confidence:** high — reproduced at runtime against a worktree at this commit.

## Root cause and evidence
[`outside_unchanged`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770/crates/engine/src/cmd/protect.rs#L318) is the post-check that rolls a command back when it changed anything outside the editable regions. It compares the last section, the per-paragraph sections, the style defaults, the pre-existing styles, and — through `outside()` — the text, the run formatting, the paragraph marks, the inline objects and the table/row/cell properties outside the editable regions, in every story.

It does not compare:

- `doc.settings` (the whole struct, which derives `PartialEq`, [`crates/doc/src/lib.rs:488`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770/crates/doc/src/lib.rs#L488)),
- `doc.core` and `doc.custom_props`,
- `doc.comments[*].resolved` (the flag; the comment's text is a part and is compared),
- `doc.numbering`,
- `doc.sources`.

It also permits a *new* style to be added, deliberately: `b.styles.iter().all(|st| a.get(&st.id) == Some(st))` only requires the old ones to be unchanged.

## Conditions and realistic impact
On a protected document with an editable exception, a command that changes the metadata is accepted and never rolled back. Reproduced on a worktree at this commit:

```

s.run("review.restrict", &json!({"mode": "readOnly"}))?;
s.run("file.properties", &json!({"title": "Forged title"}))?;
// Ok(...), s.doc.core.title == "Forged title"
```

The same holds for the list definitions and the bibliography sources: redefining a list changes what the protected paragraphs look like without tripping the check.

title: file.setAuthor changes the identity a named exception range is checked against on a protected document
author: matstrange
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at `9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770`. **Severity:** Medium (editing restrictions). **Confidence:** high — reproduced at runtime against a worktree at this commit.

## Root cause and evidence
[`file.setAuthor`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770/crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L127) sets `s.author`. That identity is what `editable_by` compares a named exception range against ([`crates/engine/src/cmd/protect.rs:51`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770/crates/engine/src/cmd/protect.rs#L51)):

```rust
fn editable_by(r: &PermRange, author: &str) -> bool {
    r.everyone() || (!r.editor.is_empty() && r.editor.eq_ignore_ascii_case(author.trim()))
}
```

It is also the author recorded on new tracked changes and comments. Because `always_allowed` waves through every `file.*` id, the command runs on a protected document.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Reproduced on a worktree at this commit, on a read-only protected document:

```
s.run("file.setAuthor", &json!({"name": "Alice"}))?;
// Ok(...), s.author == "Alice"
```

A script can therefore name itself after the editor of a `w:permStart w:ed="…"` range and edit inside it, and can put its revisions and comments in someone else's name.

## Recommended remediation
Refuse the change while the document is protected, using the idiom the file already has for `developer.properties` ("stop protection before …"). Changing the user name is a preference in Word and is allowed there; refusing it under protection is this project's deliberate choice, because the name says who may edit what.

## Suggested regression tests
On a protected document `file.setAuthor` is refused and the author is unchanged; on an unprotected document it still works.

title: A file command can change or stop a password-less protection
author: matstrange
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at `9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770`. **Severity:** Medium (editing restrictions). **Confidence:** high — reproduced at runtime against a worktree at this commit.

## Root cause and evidence
In `restrict` ([`crates/engine/src/cmd/protect.rs:78-100`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770/crates/engine/src/cmd/protect.rs#L78-L100)) the guard that stops the protection of a protected document from changing reads:

```rust
if enforced(&s.doc) && !s.doc.settings.protect_hash.is_empty() {
    return Err(CmdError::Disabled("the document is protected with a password: stop protection first".into()));
}
```

So it only applies when the document has a *password*. A password-less protected document can have its mode changed, and `file.protect {"mode": "none"}` stops it outright. `file.protect` forwards only `{"mode": …}` to `review.restrict` ([`crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs:464`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770/crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs#L464)).

## Conditions and realistic impact
Reproduced on a worktree at this commit:

```
s.run("review.restrict", &json!({"mode": "readOnly"}))?;   // no password
s.run("file.protect", &json!({"mode": "none"}))?;
// Ok(...), s.doc.settings.protection == None
```

A script can strip a user's protection and then edit the document freely, with no record. A password-protected document is safe: the password check refuses it (verified as a control).

The same guard is why the *mode* of a protected document can be switched (for instance read-only to comments) without stopping the protection first, which Word does not allow.

## Recommended remediation
The protection of a protected document should only change through the explicit Stop Protection path — `review.restrict {"stop": true}`, which is what the pane's Stop Protection button sends — and not through a command that mere…

title: Version snapshots survive a document switch
author: matstrange
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at `9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770`. **Severity:** Medium (data integrity). **Confidence:** high — reproduced at runtime against a worktree at this commit.

## Root cause and evidence
[`Session::versions`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770/crates/engine/src/session.rs#L443) holds the version snapshots, and [`set_document`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770/crates/engine/src/session.rs#L1105) resets almost everything about the open document — the document id, the document, the selection, the undo history, the password, the file name — but not the snapshots.

`file.versions` is a pure command, so nothing about it is checked.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A snapshot taken of one document survives `file.new`, `file.open`, `file.newFromTemplate` and `file.recover`, and `file.versions {"restore": index}` then puts the previous document's content into the open one. Reproduced on a worktree at this commit:

```
let mut s = Session::new(Document::from_text("First document."));
s.run("file.versions", &json!({"save": "snapshot"}))?;
s.run("file.new", &json!({}))?;
s.run("file.versions", &json!({"restore": 0}))?;
// s.doc.plain_text(Body) == "First document."   (the new document got the old one's text)
```

The restore also does not go through `set_document`, so it does not reset the selection or the merge state the way a document switch does.

## Recommended remediation
A version snapshot belongs to the document it was taken from: `set_document` should clear them, so a restore can only ever bring back a version of the document that is open. Every caller of `set_document` replaces the document with a different one, so none of them loses anything it needs.

## Suggested regression tests
After `file.new` and after `file.open`, a snapshot taken in the previous document is gone and cannot be restored;…

title: DOCX: an inline table right after a text-anchored floating table (tblpY=1, tblOverlap=never) is drawn over it, not below it
author: dpkruse
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @dpkruse (Kruse Legal)._

**Version:** WordCraft v0.8.0 (web build). Also seen on `main` at 9b4b948, and on `main` + #1760.

## Summary

A table laid out in the flow, directly after a **floating** table anchored to the text with a tiny offset, is drawn **over** the floating table instead of below it.

The floating table has `w:tblpPr w:vertAnchor="text" w:tblpY="1"`, no `tblpX` or `horzAnchor`, `w:tblOverlap w:val="never"`, and fills the column. Word places it 1 twip below the preceding content and starts the next flowed content below it. WordCraft starts the following inline table at the floating table's own top.

## Where to see it (a public court form, blank)

- **Form:** the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia's *Application for Consent Orders kit*, the Word version: https://www.fcfcoa.gov.au/fl/forms/app-consent-kit
  - Direct download: https://www.fcfcoa.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-12/consent_orders_kit_0625v3.docx
- **Page:** numbered 6 in the form ("Part D About the children").
  - Body element 274 is the floating table: items 21–22 up to "Child 1".
  - Body element 275 is the inline table that follows directly: item 22's "Child 2" block.
- **Expected (Word):** "Child 2" sits below "Child 1", lower down the page.
- **Actual (WordCraft):** the "Child 2" block is drawn at the top of the page, over item 21's table and its footnotes, and its own place below "Child 1" is left empty. The rest of the document follows on from there.

## Related

- **#2666** ("account for table gridBefore and clear floats for flow tables") contains a fix for exactly this case. See its `a_flow_table_starts_below_a_floating_table` test, with `vertAnchor="text" tblpY="1"`. It is open and currently conflicting.
- **#1760** fixes the gridBefore tables on the same form, and overlaps #2666's other half.
- **Not the same as:** #2732 (late, page-relative floats) and #2463 / #2359 (a float taller than the page).

title: [Bug] HTML clipboard paste ignores embedded web images () while direct image paste succeeds
author: psign04
body: ## Summary When copying formatted text containing images from a web browser into WordCraft, text layout and formatting are pasted correctly, but inline images (`` tags) are dropped/omitted. Pasting the image independently via Special Paste / Direct Paste works as expected, indicating an issue with how HTML clipboard payload images are fetched or resolved. ## Environment - **OS:** Windows 10 / 11 - **App Version:** WordCraft v0.8.0 ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open a web article containing both formatted text and an inline image in a web browser. 2. Select all content (text + image) and press `Ctrl + C`. 3. Open a new document in WordCraft. 4. Paste the content using standard paste (`Ctrl + V`). 5. Observe that text and formatting are pasted, but the image is missing. 6. title: [Feature Request] Thai text support: Dictionary-based line wrapping and Thai Distributed justification (thaiDistribute)
author: jjnikom576
body:
### Summary
Currently, Thai text in WordCraft cannot wrap properly and Thai justification (`w:jc w:val="thaiDistribute"`) is not fully supported, as noted in `docs/layout-parity.md`:
> *"Khmer, Thai and Lao still wrap only at spaces (need a dictionary)"*
> *"Distributed / Thai distributed alignment | 🟡 | read; layout untested"*

Because Thai is written without spaces between words (Scriptio continua), spaces only denote clause or sentence boundaries. Without a dictionary-based word segmentation engine, Thai lines currently only break at spaces, leading to severely broken layouts.

### Current Behavior
1. **Line Breaking**: Lines only wrap at explicit ASCII/Unicode spaces, often resulting in sentences overflowing margins or huge unnatural gaps.
2. **Justification**: 
   - `crates/docx/src/read/props.rs` maps `"thaiDistribute"` to generic `Align::Distribute`.
   - `crates/layout/src/para.rs` distributes excess width equally across all character clusters indiscriminately, which breaks Thai cluster spacing and looks unnatural compared to Microsoft Word.
   - On save, `Align::Distribute` writes back `w:jc w:val="distribute"` instead of preserving `thaiDistribute`.

### Expected Behavior (Word Parity)
1. **Word-based line breaking**: Thai text should break at word boundaries according to Unicode standard rules (UAX #14 with dictionary-based segmentation).
2. **Thai Distributed (`w:jc w:val="thaiDistribute"`)**:
   - In Microsoft Word, "Thai Distributed" (กระจายแบบไทย) achieves flush left and right margins by first distributing spacing between segmented words (inter-word), and secondarily applying subtle proportional inter-character tracking across clusters without detaching vowels and tone marks.

### Proposed Pure-Rust Implementation
To avoid C/C++ FFI dependencies (like `libthai`), WordCraft can leverage the official Unicode **[ICU4X](https://github.com/unicode-org/icu4x)** pure-Rust crate:
- **Crate**: [`icu_segmenter`](https://crates.io/crates/icu_segmenter) (or the u…

title: [Bug] Paste formatted text: Line 1 inherits target document font size, while Line 2+ retains original source font size
author: psign04
body:
## Summary
When pasting formatted text copied from an external source (e.g., digitized book page or formatted document), the first line incorrectly inherits the default font size of the destination document, whereas the second line (and subsequent lines) retains the original font size from the source.

## Environment
- **OS:** Windows 10 / 11
- **App Version:** WordCraft v0.8.0

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Copy a multi-line excerpt of formatted text from a source (e.g., PDF, web reader, or formatted text document) that uses a distinct font size (e.g., 14pt).
2. Open a document in WordCraft where default body text is set to a different size (e.g., 11pt).
3. Paste the copied text using standard paste (`Ctrl + V`).
4. Observe the font size of the pasted lines.

## Expected Behavior
The pasted text should maintain consistent styling across all lines—either fully inheriting the target document's formatting (if pasting plain text) or fully preserving the source formatting across all lines.

## Actual Behavior
- **Line 1:** Takes on the default font size of the target WordCraft document.
- **Line 2 (and onwards):** Retains the actual/original font size from the source payload.

## Additional Context / Root Cause Hypothesis
Likely a style-parser or range-application bug during clipboard import: the first paragraph/line range gets overridden by the active target paragraph style before the source run properties are applied to subsequent nodes/lines.

title: Language › Detect language automatically does nothing
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## What I found

Review › Language has a "Detect language automatically" checkbox (`crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs_layout.rs:487`, `ui.checkbox(&mut f.detect, tl!("Detect language automatically"));`), on by default (`Session::prefs.detect_language: bool`, `crates/engine/src/session.rs:526`, default `true`). Its doc comment says exactly what it's meant to do: "Language › Detect language automatically (per user, as in Word)".

Toggling it does get wired through to the preference (`tools.language`'s `detect` param, `crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs:765-785`, sets `s.prefs.detect_language`), and the dialog reads it back correctly to show the checkbox state. But I couldn't find anywhere that `detect_language` is actually *read* to do anything besides populate/report that one checkbox — it's set, stored, and shown, and that's it. I searched both `crates/engine` and `crates/ui-egui` for every reference to it; the only other "detect_language" in the codebase is `speech::detect_language(text)`, which is a completely separate thing — it's a script/alphabet detector used only for picking a Read Aloud voice, not for assigning a proofing language to typed text.

The real Microsoft Word feature this checkbox is named after auto-switches the proofing language per run as you type, based on the script/characters you're typing (so switching from an English sentence to a Russian one mid-document gets the right spell-checker without the user manually reopening Review › Language each time). Here, nothing does that — the checkbox is on by default and looks like it should already be doing this, but it's a no-op.

## Where this came from

Spotted this while following up on #3226: the reporter there confirmed Russian spellcheck itself works correctly once the language is manually selected in Review › Language, but has to be re-selected every time the keyboard layout/script changes in a mixed-language document — which is exactly what "Detect language automatically" should be preventing, if it work…

title: Right-clicking a link leaves the hover tooltip over the context menu, hiding Cut / Copy / Paste / Font…
author: SlavenDj
body:
### What happens

Hover a hyperlink, then right-click it without moving the pointer. The hyperlink's hover tooltip (the target URL plus "⌘+Click to follow link") stays open on top of the context menu. Because tooltips are drawn above menus, the tooltip covers the menu's first items: `Cut`, `Copy`, `Paste`, the separator and `Font…` are hidden, and the menu only shows `Paragraph…`, `Link…` and `New Comment`.

It is most obvious with a long URL (a Facebook or newsletter link with tracking parameters wraps to eight lines and is about 500 px wide, hiding most of the menu).

### Expected

Opening the context menu dismisses the link tooltip, so the whole menu is visible and clickable, as in Word.

### Where

`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, at the end of `mouse()`: the tooltip is shown whenever the pointer hovers a link and is not dragging. It never checks `app.canvas.context_menu_open`, unlike the mini toolbar (`crates/ui-egui/src/mini_toolbar.rs:116`), which stands down while the menu owns the pointer.

### Fix

Suppress the link tooltip while the context menu is open (and while the secondary button is opening it), with a kittest regression: hover a link, assert the tooltip is showing, right-click, assert the menu is open and the tooltip is gone.

title: AutoSave: clicking the label doesn't toggle the switch, and double-clicking the text selects it
author: SlavenDj
body:
### What happens

In the title bar the AutoSave switch is drawn next to a plain text label. They look like one setting, but they behave as two separate things:

- Clicking the **AutoSave** text does nothing; only the 30 × 16 switch reacts.
- Double-clicking the text selects it like document text: "AutoSave" is highlighted, and `⌘C` copies it to the clipboard. The rest of the title bar is chrome, not content.

### Expected

The text and the switch are one control, as in Word: clicking either the label or the switch toggles AutoSave, and the label's text can't be selected.

### Where

`crates/ui-egui/src/chrome.rs`, `title_bar()`: the label is a separate `ui.label(...)` (selectable by default, `style.interaction.selectable_labels`), and the switch is an independent `allocate_exact_size(..., Sense::click())`.

### Fix

Make the label part of the switch: `Label::selectable(false).sense(Sense::click())`, share the hover tooltip, and toggle when either the label or the switch is clicked. Regression tests: clicking the label toggles AutoSave, and double-clicking it + Copy leaves the clipboard alone.

title: Link tooltip: add a gap between the URL and the "Click to follow link" hint
author: SlavenDj
body:
### What happens

The hyperlink hover tooltip shows the target URL, a newline and "⌘+Click to follow link" as one label. The URL wraps to many lines and the hint sits flush under the last line, so the tooltip reads as one dense block: there is no visual separation between the address and the instruction.

### Expected

The URL and the hint are visually distinct: a small gap (and/or a faint divider) between them, with the hint in secondary text. Long URLs still wrap the same way, and the tooltip's width is unchanged.

### Where

`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, the tooltip body is a single `ui.label(tip)` where `tip` is `format!("{target}\n{key}+Click to follow link")`.

### Note

This edits the same block as #3369 (right-clicking a link hides the tooltip), which is open and green; this should land after it to avoid a conflict.

### Acceptance

- A visible gap between the URL and the follow instruction (theme spacing, not a hardcoded pixel if avoidable).
- Hint styled as secondary text.
- Right-click still dismisses the tooltip (#3369).
- A kittest check that the tooltip has two separate text nodes/rows.

title: Show a site icon (favicon) in the hyperlink hover tooltip
author: SlavenDj
body:
**Nice-to-have / low priority.** Word's tooltip has no favicon, so this is deliberate polish, not a parity gap.

### Summary

The hyperlink hover tooltip now shows the URL and a secondary "⌘/Ctrl+Click to follow link" line (#3373). Show the destination site's icon to the left of the URL, as browsers do, so long or tracking-heavy links are recognisable at a glance.

There is no favicon cache, site metadata or HTTP client in the repo today. The tooltip is in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` (`link_tip`).

### Proposed behaviour

- 16×16 icon left of the URL, top-aligned with the first line; URL and hint unchanged.
- Known icon → show it; otherwise the existing hand-drawn `"link"` glyph (`crates/ui-egui/src/icons.rs`).
- Only `http`/`https` targets are eligible; in-document bookmarks, `mailto:` and invalid targets keep the glyph.
- Decorative only: no click action, no alt text that changes the link's accessible name. A favicon is **not** a trust signal; the URL stays the source of truth.

### Phased approach

**Stage 1 — no network (recommended first PR):** icon slot + vector fallback only. No cache, no URL parsing, no setting, no new dependency. Does not show real favicons yet.

**Stage 2 — opt-in fetch (separate PR, owner sign-off):** bounded in-memory cache keyed by normalized `https` origin, and a native-only fetcher behind a **default-off** setting. Off by default → behaviour identical to stage 1.

### Privacy and safety (stage 2 requirements)

- Default off; with it off, zero network requests (tested with a fake transport).
- Hover dwell (~500 ms), once per origin per session; never on open/render/print/export/screenshot/headless; negative cache.
- `https:` only, default port, `/favicon.ico` only; no page HTML, no `Referer`, no cookies, fixed User-Agent.
- Refuse localhost, loopback/private/link-local/metadata IPs, `.local`, single-label hosts, IP literals — before DNS and again after resolution/redirects.
- At most one same-registrable-domain redirect; ~2 s connec…

title: Live layout label while resizing a picture: "Moves to page 3" / "Pushes the next picture to page 4"
author: SlavenDj
body:
### Context

Resizing a picture re-paginates the document, but the user only finds out after releasing the handle. Growing a picture by a couple of lines can push its own paragraph — and everything after it — onto the next page, often off-screen. The canvas shows the resize preview (`crates/ui-egui/src/objects.rs`) but says nothing about the layout consequence, and the drop does one silent relayout.

The engine already has what is needed to predict this cheaply:

- `Session::layout()` is a cached whole-document layout (`crates/engine/src/session.rs`), warm enough to re-run during a drag (~1.4 ms for 188 pages per the README).
- `Document` is cheap to clone (`body: Vec<Arc<Block>>`), so a speculative pass can run on a copy with no document mutation, no undo step and no dirty flag.
- The layout cache key includes the paragraph `rev` and a hash of the wrap exclusions, so touching the resized picture's paragraph invalidates exactly what changed.
- `arrange.bounds` already clamps the committed size (`min_size`, `MAX_OFFSET`).

### Desired behaviour

While dragging a **resize handle on a body picture**:

- A small label follows the pointer, to its right by default; it flips to the left when there is no room and is clamped vertically to the window.
- The label appears only when the predicted layout differs from the current one. Nothing is shown after the drop — no toast, no summary.
- If the picture's own page changes: `Moves to page 3`, or `Moves up to page 2`.
- Otherwise, if following content crosses a page, name **only the first item whose page changes**, in reading order: `Pushes the next picture to page 4`, `Pulls the next picture up to page 2`, `Pushes the next table to page 4`, `Pushes the text after it to page 4`. The chain reaction is implied.
- Hidden while the drag is below its movement threshold, on release, on Esc, and when the pointer leaves the canvas viewport.
- Correct with explicit page breaks, section breaks and restarted page numbering: the number show…

title: Picture right-click: "Save as Picture…" to save the image to disk
author: SlavenDj
body:
### Problem

There is no way to save a picture out of a document. Right-clicking a picture offers **Change Picture…**, **Reset Picture** and **Size and Crop…**, but nothing like Word's **Save as Picture…**. The only ways to get the image are copying it and pasting it somewhere else (which is currently broken — #3328 / #2909), or renaming the `.docx` to `.zip` and digging through `word/media/`.

I would like to save the image straight to my device without going through the clipboard.

### Desired behaviour

- Right-click a picture → **Save as Picture…**, next to **Change Picture…** and **Reset Picture** (Word has the same item there).
- It opens the usual Save dialog with a suggested name and the picture's own extension, then writes the picture file.
- The picture is saved in its **original format and original bytes** (a JPEG stays a JPEG, a PNG stays a PNG), at its original resolution — not a screenshot of the page and not re-compressed.
- A `picture.saveAs` command with `{"path": "..."}` does the same for scripts; without a path it asks the UI for one, as `file.exportPdf` does (#2313).
- The command is available only when exactly one picture is selected.
- The status bar confirms where the file went.

### Why this is small

The document already keeps every picture's original encoded bytes in `Document::media: BTreeMap<String, Arc<Vec<u8>>>`, and each picture stores the key in `InlineObject::Image { media, .. }`. Saving is:

1. find the selected picture's media key,
2. look the bytes up,
3. write them to the chosen path.

No document-model change, no re-encoding, no layout work, no new dependency. The Save dialog and the “command takes a path / UI command asks for one” pattern already exist for PDF and PNG export.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Right-clicking a picture shows **Save as Picture…**; it is absent for shapes, text boxes, tables and text selections.
- [ ] Choosing it opens a Save dialog with a sensible suggested name (document name or picture name) and t…

title: Comments: a long comment's card and balloon grow without limit, hiding the comments after it
author: squaredcow
body:
Seen on `main` (e3bb06a), macOS, with headless `ui_shot`.

## Steps

1. In a new document, type "Alpha paragraph one." and "Beta paragraph two." as two paragraphs.
2. Select "Alpha" and add a long comment: about 7,500 characters, or 200 short lines.

A comment's card is as tall as its text, with no limit.

title: CI: check dependency licences, sources and advisories with cargo-deny
author: Nghiathan13
body:
Nothing in WordCraft's CI checks the licences, sources or security advisories of its dependencies. `main` (e3bb06a2) has no `deny.toml`, `cargo xtask ci` has no deny/audit step, and none of the workflows runs cargo-deny or cargo-audit. WordCraft is `MIT OR Apache-2.0`, so a copyleft dependency would change what the shipped binaries can be released under, and the repo already keeps GPL/LGPL/AGPL code out of its own source. Today a dependency update (e.g. Dependabot's grouped Cargo PR, #2973 with 19 crates) can bring in a copyleft licence, a git source outside storytold, or a crate with a RUSTSEC advisory, and nothing flags it.

### Earlier work
- #2839 (WC-40 from the #2744 audit) added a `deny.toml` and `cargo xtask deny`, and reported `cargo deny check` passing on its branch, where zip had already been upgraded (`advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`, 40 duplicate-version warnings). Its author closed it unmerged on 2026-10-18 ("no longer working on this"). It also bundled the zip 3 → 9 upgrade, overflow checks and lint changes.
- #2744's checklist item "Add a project-specific cargo-deny policy for permitted licenses and git sources, and schedule dependency advisory checks" was never done; the tracker was closed as not planned.
- #1365 recommended running the advisory tool in CI, and #2401 left it out as "a separate CI decision".

### Current state (cargo-deny 0.20.2 on main e3bb06a2, using #2839's `deny.toml`)
`advisories FAILED, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`
- **Licences and sources pass** under #2839's allow-list, so the policy can be turned on without changing any dependency.
- **Advisories fail on `zip` 3.0.0** (used by `wordcraft-docx` and `wordcraft-formats`): RUSTSEC-2026-0367, 0368 and 0369, all about `ZipArchive::extract` / `ZipStreamReader::extract`. Nothing in `crates/`, `apps/` or `xtask/` calls either, because parts are read into memory, so these don't look reachable. The check still fails on them until zip is upgraded or they're ignored…

title: [Feature Request] Add eye-protection color scheme / soft paper background presets (similar to WPS Office)
author: momefan
body:
1. Feature Description
Requesting a built-in "Eye Protection Mode" or paper background color preset option (similar to the soft green/bean-paste and warm cream tints found in WPS Office and other modern document editors) for the reading and editing interface.

2. Use Case / Motivation
Reduced Eye Strain: Spending hours reading or editing documents against a stark white background (#FFFFFF) under bright screens causes noticeable eye fatigue, particularly during extended evening work or low-light environments.

Familiar Alternative: Popular office suites like WPS Office offer a signature eye-protection green (soft pastel green/sage tint) and warm sepia tones that significantly soften screen glare and improve reading comfort.

Accessibility & Customization: While dark mode exists, many users prefer a soft, low-contrast paper tint (e.g., pale green, warm beige, or soft gray) over a full dark theme because it maintains traditional document aesthetics while easing visual strain.

3. Proposed Solution
Quick Preset Toggles: Add an "Eye Protection / Page Background" option to the toolbar or appearance settings with common presets:

Eye Protection Green (Soft pastel green tint, e.g., #CCE8CF or similar soft hex)

Warm Sepia / Cream (Soft parchment tint for reading)

Cool Slate / Soft Gray (Low-glare neutral gray)

Persistent Setting: Allow users to set a default background color for the workspace canvas that can be toggled on/off independently of the exported document styling (so the background tint helps the user's eyes while drafting, but doesn't force a colored background when printing or exporting to PDF).

4. Additional Context
Inspiration: WPS Office's eye-protection mode is widely appreciated by students, teachers, and professionals who spend long hours reviewing long-form Chinese/English text.

title: [Bug Report] [WordCraft] Ink strokes are drawn behind table cell shading when the stroke starts above the table
author: ravenmyrrdin
body: **What happens** Ink drawn with the Draw tab's pen disappears wherever it crosses a shaded table cell, but only when the stroke was started *above* the table. A stroke started *below* the table is drawn on top of everything, as expected. In the screenshot: - The **black** strokes were drawn top to bottom, starting in the paragraph above the table. They are hidden in the dark header row and in the light-blue shaded rows ("Etching press", "Large-format printer"), and only visible in the white rows and outside the table. - The **green** stroke was drawn bottom to top, starting below the numbered list. It is visible over every row, including the shaded ones. **Expected** Ink is always drawn in front of the document content (text, tables, shading), regardless of where or in which direction the stroke was drawn, as in Word. **Likely cause** The stroke seems to be painted together with the paragraph it is anchored to (where the stroke starts), so content that comes later in the document, like the table's cell shading, is painted over it. A stroke anchored after the table is painted last and ends up on top. The problem persists after saving and reopening the .docx, so it is either stored that way in the file or reproduced from the anchor on load. Worth checking how the same file looks in Word. **Steps to reproduce** 1. Insert a table with shaded cells (e.g. a table style with banded rows), with a paragraph above and below it. 2. Draw tab › Pen: draw a vertical stroke starting in the paragraph above the table, down through the table. 3. Draw a second stroke starting below the table, up through it. 4. The first stroke is hidden behind the shaded cells; the second is drawn on top. 5. Save, close and reopen: unchanged. **Environment** - WordCraft 0.9.0 - Windows 11

title: Inconsistent justification in mixed Chinese and Latin text
author: sch401
body: ### Observed behavior With Justify selected, paragraphs containing Chinese text, Latin text, and numbers sometimes show: - Excessively wide spaces, especially between numbers and units such as `405 mV` and `0.6 V`. - Uneven right edges on wrapped lines before the paragraph’s final line. ### Possible cause analyzed by Chatgpt: In the [justification logic in break_lines()](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/e05b7fe86f3b85454000dffc321de638d7009817/crates/layout/src/para.rs#L2456-L2493): - When ordinary spaces exist, all remaining width is distributed across them using `slack / spaces.len()`, potentially creating large gaps. - When no ordinary spaces exist, the spacing adjustment runs only for `Align::Distribute`, leaving `Align::Justify` unchanged. This may explain both behaviors.

title: Tables: per-cell padding (w:tcMar) is ignored, text sits on the cell border
author: michaelkrisper
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @michaelkrisper._

**Version:** WordCraft 0.9.0, Linux x86_64 release tarball (headless `wordcraft-cli`). Reference: Microsoft Word, export to PDF.

## What happens

In Word you can give individual table cells their own inner padding (Table Properties → Cell → Options → cell margins). WordCraft ignores this per-cell padding. The text sits directly on the cell border instead of being inset.

The table in the example sets the table-wide left/right padding to 0, as many corporate templates do, and gives every cell its own 0.25 cm (7.2 pt) left/right padding. In Word the text is inset by 7.2 pt. In WordCraft it starts right at the cell edge, so the first column's text lines up with the page margin.

Because every cell loses 14.4 pt of padding, text wraps differently than in Word. That shifts row heights and page breaks.

## How to reproduce

1. Open `repro-table-hyphen-slash-wrap.docx` (attached).
2. Export to PDF and compare with `repro-table-hyphen-slash-wrap_word.pdf` (Word export, attached).

| | First-column text starts at |
|---|---|
| Word | x = 63.9 pt (page margin 56.7 + 7.2 padding) |
| WordCraft | x = 56.7 pt (on the page margin) |

## Technical notes

- `w:tblPr/w:tblCellMar` sets left/right = 0. Each `w:tcPr/w:tcMar` sets left/right = 144 twips and top/bottom = 72 twips.
- Expected: `w:tcMar` takes precedence over `w:tblCellMar` for that cell (ECMA-376 §17.4.42).
- The same file also shows a separate line-break issue (hyphen before `/`), which is reported on its own.

Attached: `repro-table-hyphen-slash-wrap.docx`, `repro-table-hyphen-slash-wrap_word.pdf`, `wordcraft-table-hyphen-slash-wrap.pdf`

title: Layout: no line break after a hyphen before a slash ("Data-/Privacy"), so auto-fit tables widen the column instead of wrapping like Word
author: michaelkrisper
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @michaelkrisper._

**Version:** WordCraft 0.9.0, Linux x86_64 release tarball (headless `wordcraft-cli`). Reference: Microsoft Word, export to PDF.

## What happens

A table cell contains a compound word with a hyphen followed by a slash, such as `Dataprotection-/Secrecyviolation`. Word wraps it onto two lines (`Dataprotection-` / `/Secrecyviolation`) and keeps the column narrow. WordCraft never breaks there. It treats the whole compound as one unbreakable word and widens the column so that it fits on one line.

In an auto-fit table the widened column takes its space from the neighbouring column. All the long text in that neighbouring column then wraps into more lines than in Word, and the page breaks shift.

## Why it matters

We found this in a real 158-page Word document that has this kind of compound in a 4-column table. Together with the cell-padding bug #3407, the tables there wrap differently from Word, and the text at the end of the page differs from Word's PDF on 83 of 158 pages.

## How to reproduce

1. Open `repro-table-hyphen-slash-wrap.docx` (attached). It contains one small auto-fit table, and row T3 has the compound in column C.
2. Export to PDF, or render page 1.
3. Compare with `repro-table-hyphen-slash-wrap_word.pdf` (the same file exported by Word, attached).

| | Column C, row T3 | Columns start at (pt) |
|---|---|---|
| Word | `Dataprotection-` / `/Secrecyviolation` | 63.9 / 90.0 / 143.2 / 250.3 |
| WordCraft | `Dataprotection-/Secrecyviolation` (one line) | 56.7 / 82.8 / 146.3 / 304.6 |

Column D is about 54 pt narrower in WordCraft. The small offset in the first two columns comes from a separate bug (cell padding, #3407).

## Technical notes

- Related: #2712, where Word also breaks after a hyphen that UAX #14 does not allow a break after (there: before a digit; here: before `/`, where rule LB13 forbids a break before a slash). It is probably the same root cause: Word always offers a break…
