```
Syntax Error: Suspects object is wrong type (boolean)
```

The PDF itself is valid. WordCraft writes `/MarkInfo <</Marked true/Suspects false>>`, which matches the spec. The warning comes from a quirk in poppler, which only accepts `/Suspects` when it is `true`. Still, it makes WordCraft's PDFs look broken in validation scripts and logs.

Word avoids it by leaving the key out when it is false. Its PDFs contain `/MarkInfo <</Marked true>>`, and pdfinfo reports `Suspects: no` without a warning.

**Proposal:** only write `/Suspects` when it is `true`.

## How to check

Export any document to PDF and run `pdfinfo out.pdf`. The attached `wordcraft-*.pdf` shows the warning, and the attached `*_word.pdf` does not.
[repro-footer-right-tab_word.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33760935/repro-footer-right-tab_word.pdf)
[wordcraft-footer-right-tab.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33760936/wordcraft-footer-right-tab.pdf)

title: A document with many relationships takes minutes to open
author: matstrange
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at `9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770`. **Severity:** Medium (a document takes minutes to open). **Confidence:** high — reproduced at runtime against a worktree at this commit, with and without a candidate fix.

## Root cause and evidence
[`crates/docx/src/read/embed.rs:102-121`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770/crates/docx/src/read/embed.rs#L102-L121) keeps the parts of a package that WordCraft neither models nor writes, so that saving carries them over unchanged. To skip a relationship the main document's markup already refers to, it looks for that relationship's id in the main document's part:

```rust
let main = pkg.get(&self.main).unwrap_or_default();
let referenced = |id: &str| {
    let needle = format!("\"{id}\"");
    main.windows(needle.len()).any(|w| w == needle.as_bytes())
};
...
if HANDLED_RELS.contains(&tail)
    || (owner == "D" && referenced(&rel.id))
```

That is a full pass over the part, once per relationship. The reader's limits are `MAX_PART = 256 MiB` for one part (`crates/docx/src/package.rs:11`) and `MAX_EMBEDDED_RELS = 1024` for the relationships of one part (`crates/docx/src/package.rs:119`), so the worst case is about 256 GiB of byte comparisons for one document.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Measured on this commit, with a 64 MiB main part and a relationship type the reader doesn't model (so every relationship is looked for):

| relationships | open time |
|---|---|
| 4 | 1.05 s |
| 64 | 14.33 s |
| 256 | 57.70 s |
| 1024 | 223.97 s |

The cost is linear in the number of relationships and in the size of the part, so the open costs the part's size times the relationships' number, where the parse of the same part costs the part's size once. With 1024 relationships the scan is 200 times the parse.

The main part is a zip entry, so it compresses: the file above is **70 KB on disk** and takes 3 minutes 44 to open. …

title: A word with no break opportunity in it makes the layout quadratic
author: matstrange
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at `9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770`. **Severity:** Medium (a document takes minutes to lay out). **Confidence:** high — reproduced at runtime against a worktree at this commit, with and without a candidate fix.

## Root cause and evidence
[`crates/layout/src/para.rs:2192-2202`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/9b4b948c6ecf29401e01ad58626d3c1983b83770/crates/layout/src/para.rs#L2192-L2202) measures the word that starts at a line, to tell whether it fits the full line beside a floating object:

```rust
let word: f32 = (c0..n)
    .filter_map(|k| pl.clusters.get(k).map(|c| (k, c)))
    .scan(false, |done, (k, c)| {
        let end = c.break_after && pl.hyph_after.binary_search(&(k as u32)).is_err();
        (!std::mem::replace(done, end)).then_some(c)
    })
    .filter(|c| c.kind != ClKind::Space)
    .map(|c| c.adv)
    .sum();
let full = base_right - row_lo;
skip = narrowed && skipped < 50 && word <= full + 0.01;
```

The `scan` ends at the first cluster it doesn't yield, so the word is the clusters up to the first break opportunity. But the scan walks `c0..n` — to the end of the paragraph — and the iterator it is built on keeps going, so the walk costs the rest of the paragraph however short the word is. A word with no break opportunity in it gives a line per word's worth of characters, and each of those lines walks the paragraph again.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Measured on this commit, laying out one paragraph of one word with no break opportunity in it:

| word length | layout time |
|---|---|
| 1 MiB | 29.42 s |
| 2 MiB | 118.47 s |
| 4 MiB | 472.34 s |

The same text as ordinary prose lays out in 0.39 s for a megabyte — 76 times faster — because a space ends the word and the scan stops there. So the cost is the length of the word squared, and only a word with no break opportunity in it pays it.

title: A start override restarts every level of a shared list, renumbering the whole document's headings
author: urbanij
body:
## Summary

When two numbering instances (`w:num`) share one abstract list (`w:abstractNum`) and the second one carries `w:lvlOverride/w:startOverride` on several levels, WordCraft applies **all** of that instance's start overrides the first time the instance is used — at whatever level that first paragraph is. The counters are kept per abstract list, so this resets levels the instance never used, including the top one: every heading after that point is numbered from 1 again.

Word restarts only the level being used. Its table of contents (cached in the same file) and its own heading numbers keep counting.

## Where

`crates/doc/src/numbering.rs`, `Counters::next_label`:

```rust
if let Entry::Vacant(e) = self.seen.entry(num) {   // first use of the num, any level
    e.insert(true);
    for (l, start) in &n.start_overrides {         // every level it overrides
        if let Some(s) = st.get_mut(*l as usize) { // shared per abstract list
            *s = start.saturating_sub(1);
        }
    }
}
```

## Reproduce (document shape)

A common heading setup produced by Word templates:

- `styles.xml`: `Heading1`–`Heading4` use `numId 1`, `Heading5`–`Heading9` use `numId 8`.
- `numbering.xml`:

  ```xml
  <w:num w:numId="1"><w:abstractNumId w:val="12"/></w:num>
  <w:num w:numId="8"><w:abstractNumId w:val="12"/>
    <w:lvlOverride w:ilvl="0"><w:startOverride w:val="1"/></w:lvlOverride>
    <!-- … the same for ilvl 1 to 8 -->
  </w:num>
  ```

- Body: chapters 1–5 (Heading 1), with sections down to Heading 4; then, inside chapter 5, the document's first Heading 5 or deeper; then chapters 6–12.

Converted with `wordcraft-cli convert in.docx out.pdf`:

| | Chapter 6 | A section of chapter 6 | Last chapter |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Word (and the file's own cached TOC) | `6` | `6.3.2.1` | `12` |
| WordCraft | `1` | `1.3.2.1` | `7` |

The table of contents in WordCraft's output is right (it is the field's cached text); the body headings disagree with it from the first dee…

title: Opening a .dotx from the file manager edits the template; Save overwrites it instead of saving a new .docx
author: benandez
body:
## What happened
Double-clicking a Word template (`.dotx`) in the file manager (Linux, KDE; the path arrives through the document portal) opens WordCraft with the template file itself as the open document. Then **Save** (Ctrl+S) writes back to the `.dotx` instead of asking for a new `.docx`. You can overwrite the template without noticing, and the new document never gets saved as a plain document.

## Expected (Word's observed behaviour)
When you open a template from the shell (double-click or the default **New** verb), you get a new **untitled document based on the template**:
- the document has no path, the title shows `Document1` and so on, and Save opens Save As with **Word Document (.docx)** as the default type
- the template is recorded as the attached template (`settings.attached_template`)
- the template file on disk is never modified

**File › Open** on a `.dotx`/`.dotm` still opens the template itself for editing. That's Word's way to edit a template, so only the shell-launch path changes.

## Where
- No open path treats `.dotx`/`.dotm` as "new from template". `crates/engine/src/io.rs` lists `dotx` as a plain open/save format, so the launch argument goes through a normal open and `Session` keeps the `.dotx` path.
- Same for `.dotm`, and probably `.dot`.

## Repro
1. Take any `.dotx`, double-click it (or run `wordcraft path/to/T.dotx`).
2. Type something and press Ctrl+S.
3. The template is overwritten. Expected: Save As opens for a new `.docx`.

Seen on 0.8.0, Linux (CachyOS, KDE). Not checked on Windows or macOS.

title: A document with many content controls takes seconds to save
author: matstrange
body:
**A document with many content controls takes seconds to save, and the time grows with the square of the number of controls.**

A form-shaped document — one content control per paragraph, or a control around every two paragraphs — saves in quadratic time:

| Controls | Save time |
|---|---|
| 8,000 | 0.23 s |
| 16,000 | 0.93 s |
| 32,000 | 3.70 s |
| 64,000 | 14.7 s |

Doubling the controls quadruples the time.

Two loops in the DOCX writer (`crates/docx/src/write/sdt.rs`) cause it:

- The plan that decides where each control is written collects the inline markers of every control in one set, then, for each paragraph, looks for that paragraph's markers by filtering the whole set. The cost of one paragraph's answer is therefore the size of the whole document's marker set, so the save costs paragraphs × markers.
- To find the block-level controls that clash (one that opens in the block another closes in), every control is compared with every other control.

What it costs: a questionnaire or a template with tens of thousands of fields takes seconds to save, while the file itself is small — the time is spent scanning, not on the file's size.

The fix groups the markers by paragraph once (so a paragraph's markers are a lookup rather than a filter over every marker) and groups the block-level controls by the block they end in (so the clash test is a sweep rather than a comparison against every control). What is written does not change: the same packages come out byte for byte.

Tests: `crates/docx/tests/content_control_save_cost.rs`.

title: Windows: [Bug] Ruler fails to update and display column subdivisions (2, 3, or multi-column layouts)
author: gmatiasfriske
body:
### Bug Description
When text or a document section is formatted into multiple columns (e.g., 2 columns, 3 columns, or custom multi-column layouts), the horizontal ruler at the top of the editor fails to update its visualization. 

Instead of splitting to reflect the individual column widths, margins, and gutter gaps, the ruler remains strictly static as a single-column continuum across the entire page width.

---

### Expected Behavior
The horizontal ruler should dynamically adapt to the active section layout where the cursor is positioned:
1. **Column Breakouts:** Visually divide the active scale into separate segments corresponding to Column 1, Column 2, Column 3, etc.
2. **Gutter Space Rendering:** Display dead spaces/margins (gutters) between columns clearly on the ruler track.
3. **Interactive Column Indents:** Allow adjustment of indents/margins specific to each column directly via ruler drag markers.

---

### Impact
This is a major layout visibility bug for users working with multi-column documents (such as newsletters, flyers, or formatted books). Without visual column indicators on the ruler, it is impossible to accurately align text elements, tab stops, or column-specific indents.

title: FILENAME field does not appear in WordCraft 0.9.0 on Windows and Linux
author: earlvanze
body:
## Community report

WordCraft **0.9.0**, reproduced by the reporter on **Windows 11** and **Linux Mint**: inserting **FILENAME** does not produce the expected filename. TIME, DATE, PAGE and NUMPAGES work.

Source: <https://discord.com/channels/1359579021108842617/1558921592585715862/1562448551374495831>

## Expected

In a saved document, inserting FILENAME displays its filename. Save As and field-update behavior should remain consistent. Unsaved-document behavior should be defined separately.

## Source inspection, not runtime reproduction

The v0.9.0 release supports FILENAME in the field dialog. `crates/layout/src/fields.rs` evaluates it from `FieldCtx.filename` when the cached result is empty. However, the layout `FieldCtx` initializer in `crates/layout/src/lib.rs` supplies title and author and leaves filename at `Default::default()`. `insert.field` defaults the cached result to an empty string. This suggests a missing filename context path rather than a missing field command; please verify end to end.

Reporter has not confirmed whether the tested document had already been saved, or whether the field is inserted but invisible versus rejected by the dialog. No runtime reproduction or fix is claimed.

## Suggested verification

- Insert FILENAME into a named saved DOCX on Windows and Linux, in body and header/footer.
- Check initial display, explicit field update, save/reopen and Save As rename.
- Check unsaved documents and existing cached FILENAME results separately.
- Add focused regression coverage for filename propagation without regressing the working fields.

Duplicate check: searched existing issues and open PRs for FILENAME/field; filename-dialog and file.rename reports describe separate behavior.

title: Opening or creating new file in the same window closes currently open document.
author: cute-johnny
body:
## Description

When a document is already open, using **File → New** or **File → Open** loads the new document into the existing window. The currently open document is closed, instead of the new one opening in a separate window.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open any document.
2. Click **File** (top-left corner).
3. Select **New** or **Open**.
4. Create or choose a document.

## Expected behavior

The new or opened document appears in a new window, and the original document stays open.

## Actual behavior

No new window is created. The new document replaces the current one, which is closed.

## Why this matters

Users don't expect their current work to close when they open another file. This can cause confusion and may lead to lost work.

title: Mouse cursor disappears on Wayland (Flatpak): winit "Failed to set cursor" warnings
author: antoinemenini
body:
### Environment
- WordCraft 0.8.0 (f2e15cf8), Flatpak (user install, `ai.storyteller.wordcraft`, stable)
- Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME, Wayland session
- System cursor theme: `DMZ-White` (`gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface cursor-theme`)
- Flatpak permissions: `sockets=x11;wayland;fallback-x11;`, `devices=dri;`, `filesystems=xdg-documents;xdg-pictures;`

### Problem
The mouse cursor often disappears while using the app, typically after some time, when the cursor shape changes (e.g. text cursor, arrow, pointer). The pointer stays invisible, although clicks still work.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Launch with `flatpak run ai.storyteller.wordcraft` on a GNOME/Wayland session.
2. Use the app normally, moving the cursor between the document area, the ribbon and menus.
3. After a while the cursor becomes invisible.

### Logs
Every cursor shape change fails, including `Default`:

```
WARN [main] winit::platform_impl::linux::wayland::window::state: Failed to set cursor to Default
WARN [main] winit::platform_impl::linux::wayland::window::state: Failed to set cursor to Text
WARN [main] winit::platform_impl::linux::wayland::window::state: Failed to set cursor to Pointer
```

Also present at startup:

```
WARN [?] zbus::proxy: Failed to populate properties cache via GetAll: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.ServiceUnknown
```

### Workaround
Setting the cursor theme explicitly fixes it:

```
flatpak run --env=XCURSOR_THEME=DMZ-White --env=XCURSOR_SIZE=24 ai.storyteller.wordcraft
```

### Hypothesis (unverified)
Inside the Flatpak sandbox, winit cannot determine or load the cursor theme (no `XCURSOR_THEME` in the environment, and the settings lookup over D-Bus seems to fail), so setting any cursor fails.

### Suggested fix
Set a default `XCURSOR_THEME` / `XCURSOR_SIZE` in the Flatpak manifest `finish-args`, or fall back to egui/winit's custom cursor handling when the theme cannot be loaded.

title: DOCX: saving drops the East Asian language of w:lang (w:eastAsia)
author: Fubeo
body:
### What happens

Opening a `.docx` and saving it drops the East Asian language of `w:lang` (`w:eastAsia`, ISO/IEC 29500-1 §17.3.2.20). `w:val` and `w:bidi` are kept. This happens in the document defaults, in styles and in runs. Nothing warns about it, so a Japanese, Chinese or Korean document saved by WordCraft loses the language Word uses for its East Asian text.

### Steps to reproduce

A minimal package. `word/styles.xml`:

```xml
<w:docDefaults><w:rPrDefault><w:rPr>
  <w:lang w:val="en-US" w:eastAsia="ja-JP" w:bidi="ar-SA"/>
</w:rPr></w:rPrDefault></w:docDefaults>
```

`word/document.xml`:

```xml
<w:p><w:r><w:rPr><w:lang w:val="en-US" w:eastAsia="zh-CN"/></w:rPr><w:t>Hello 你好</w:t></w:r></w:p>
```

Then `wordcraft_docx::read` followed by `wordcraft_docx::write`.

### Expected

```xml
<w:lang w:val="en-US" w:eastAsia="ja-JP" w:bidi="ar-SA"/>   <!-- styles.xml -->
<w:lang w:val="en-US" w:eastAsia="zh-CN"/>                  <!-- document.xml -->
```

### Actual

```xml
<w:lang w:val="en-US" w:bidi="ar-SA"/>   <!-- styles.xml -->
<w:lang w:val="en-US"/>                  <!-- document.xml -->
```

A run whose `w:lang` carries only `w:eastAsia` loses the whole element.

### Where

On `main` (e05b7fe), `crates/docx/src/read/props.rs` reads only `w:val` into `CharProps::lang` and `w:bidi` into `lang_bidi`. `crates/docx/src/write/props.rs` (`match (&c.lang, &c.lang_bidi)`) writes only those two. `CharProps` has no field for the East Asian language. A `lang_ea` next to `lang_bidi`, read, written, merged and inherited the same way, would fix it.

Reproduced with v0.9.0 (2e6db0bd). The code above is unchanged on `main`.

Found by a round-trip check that compares the elements and attributes of each part before and after a save. The same check also shows `w:tblInd w:w="0"` dropped from the `TableNormal` style. That one is harmless because 0 is the default, so I'm only mentioning it.

title: WordCraft: Hard to exit bulleted lists
author: jasonvey
body:
I noticed today in WordCraft that it's near impossible to exit a bulleted list. In Word all you have to do is hit enter twice and you're out of the list and back into paragraph mode. To insert a line break into a bulleted list while staying in the list, you have to hit Ctrl + Enter

In Wordcraft, hitting enter multiple times just keeps inserting empty bullets. 

Hitting the bulleted list button also doesn't end the list as it should; it eliminates the bullets from the whole list. In Word to eliminate bullets from the whole list you'd have to highlight the list and hit the bulleted list button. Simply hitting the button itself would turn off bullets for the current line and moving forward.

I believe, iirc, that I was able to get out of the list by double-clicking below it to force-insert the cursor there. But I had to mess around for awhile to figure that out and it's not a great workaround for a word processor.

title: Ribbon: offer a layout that uses available width on wide displays
author: earlvanze
body:
A user asks how to make the ribbon controls fill the horizontal space on a 2K display. Their screenshot shows the ribbon groups occupying the left portion of the window, with substantial empty space on the right.

Source: <https://discord.com/channels/1359579021108842617/1558921592585715862/1562468484959699076>

Current behavior and available workaround:
- File → Options → General → Interface size can enlarge the ribbon, menus and dialogs together; it is separate from document zoom.
- The ribbon uses the available panel width, but its control groups retain their native widths. `crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon_fit.rs` adapts groups to narrower space rather than stretching them across a wide window.
- I found no dedicated stretch-to-fill setting in the current source or the roadmap/gaps documents.

Requested improvement: consider an optional wide-display ribbon layout that uses the available horizontal space more effectively, while keeping controls readable and grouped consistently. Simply making the panel background full-width does not address the screenshot.

The user's release/build, operating system and display scaling are unknown. This is a layout/usage request based on the screenshot and source inspection, not a reproduced runtime defect. Existing issues about small toolbar icons (#988, #2863), compact ribbon layout (#619), and narrow-window overlap (#1110), plus spacing PR #1751, cover related but different behavior.

author: albayazid
body:
## Description

Follow-up to #3172. The first slice of it — the ribbon's font name and size boxes and the dropdown arrows beside them — is fixed in #3476. The rest of the Home tab's keyboard-focusable elements still have no accessible name, so a screen reader has nothing to announce when focus lands on them.

Measured the way the original report measured it — every keyboard-focusable element of the Home tab and its name, through the AccessKit tree:

What is left, grouped by what it is:

- **The quick access toolbar's buttons** (AutoSave, Save, Undo, Redo and the rest) — the ribbon's own buttons are named, these are not.

title: Change Case ignores the text's language: Turkish `istanbul` becomes `Istanbul`, not `İstanbul`
author: SlavenDj
body:
## What to build

`format.changeCase` should apply the same language-aware case mapping as AutoCorrect (#1923, PR #2009) for Turkish, Azerbaijani, and Crimean Tatar. Today it uses locale-independent uppercase/lowercase, so a Turkish run changes `i` to `I` instead of `İ`, and `I` to `i` instead of `ı`. The existing `is_turkic`, `upper_char`, and `lower_char` helpers used by AutoCorrect already define the mapping; Change Case should share them rather than duplicate the rules.

The effective language of each run (`w:lang`, through character style, paragraph style, and document defaults, else the editing language) decides its mapping. All five Change Case modes are in scope: sentence case, lowercase, UPPERCASE, Capitalize Each Word, and tOGGLE cASE.

Observable behavior:

- Turkish selected, `istanbul` → Capitalize Each Word → `İstanbul`
- Turkish selected, `IŞIK` → lowercase → `ışık`
- Turkish selected, `istanbul` → UPPERCASE → `İSTANBUL`
- English selected, `istanbul` → Capitalize Each Word → `Istanbul` (unchanged)
- A mixed-language selection applies each run's own mapping
- The surrounding text's formatting, selection, and one undo step are preserved as today

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All five Change Case modes use the run's effective language when mapping `i`/`İ` and `I`/`ı`; Turkish, Azerbaijani, and Crimean Tatar follow the same rules as AutoCorrect.
- [ ] English and other non-Turkic languages keep the current Unicode-default mapping.
- [ ] A selection spanning runs with different languages maps each run by its own language.
- [ ] Sentence and title case still capitalize the first letter after the same boundaries as today; only the letter mapping changes.
- [ ] Existing Change Case behavior (selection, formatting runs, Track Changes, content-control refusal, undo grouping) is unchanged.
- [ ] Engine tests cover Turkish uppercase, lowercase, title, sentence, toggle, an Azerbaijani/Crimean Tatar case, a mixed-language run, and an English control; the existing…

title: Change Case picker with Original and mini-toolbar access
author: SlavenDj
body:
## What to build

WordCraft's Change Case is only a ribbon drop-down, and `Shift+F3` cycles the text invisibly. Add a single Change Case picker that shows the available cases and makes the reset explicit. The picker is opened by `Shift+F3`, the ribbon Aa button, a new mini-toolbar Aa button, and the right-click menu. It lists the cases in a fixed order and applies only after the user chooses.

The picker order is fixed for v1:

1. Original
2. Sentence case
3. lowercase
4. UPPERCASE
5. Capitalize Each Word
6. tOGGLE cASE

`Shift+F3` opens the picker with the mode that would have been applied next already highlighted; pressing Enter applies it. Pressing `Shift+F3` again while the picker is open moves the highlight. Arrow keys, Home/End, Enter, Esc, and the mouse work while the picker is open. Esc and Original close without changing the text. Applying uses the existing Change Case command, so it remains one undo step and keeps Track Changes and content-control behaviour.

The text must not change while the highlight moves. Live previews of every variant are out of scope for v1 because stable variants would need to be computed from the original snapshot rather than the current text.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Shift+F3` opens the Change Case picker instead of changing the text immediately; the text is unchanged while the picker is open.

title: Change Case › Sentence case capitalizes after decimal points
author: SlavenDj
body:
### Summary
`format.changeCase` with `{"mode":"sentence"}` capitalizes the first letter after every `.` — including decimal points.

### Reproduction
```sh
W=target/debug/wordcraft-cli
$W run --template blank \
  --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"one 3.14 apples and two 2.5 pears."}' \
  --cmd 'select.all' \
  --cmd 'format.changeCase={"mode":"sentence"}' \
  --save /tmp/sentence.docx
$W text /tmp/sentence.docx
```

Actual:
```text
One 3.14 Apples and two 2.5 Pears.
```

Expected:
```text
One 3.14 apples and two 2.5 pears.
```

### Cause
In `crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs` (the sentence-case branch around lines 610–629), `up` is set for every `.` with no check for the surrounding characters. A digit following the period does not clear `up`, so the next letter is capitalized.

### Fix
Do not treat a period between two digits as a sentence boundary. Add a regression test next to the existing `change_case` tests.

title: Date pictures ignore uppercase D and Y
author: SlavenDj
body:
### Summary
The date-picture formatter recognizes only lowercase `d` and `y`, although Word's date-time format switch accepts either case for the day and year codes. Uppercase letters are emitted literally.

### Reproduction
```sh
W=target/debug/wordcraft-cli
$W run --template blank --cmd 'insert.dateTime={"format":"MM/DD/YYYY"}' --save /tmp/date1.docx
$W text /tmp/date1.docx

$W run --template blank --cmd 'insert.dateTime={"format":"D MMMM YYYY"}' --save /tmp/date2.docx
$W text /tmp/date2.docx
```

Actual (on 2026-10-21):
```text
10/DD/YYYY
D October YYYY
```

Expected:
```text
10/21/2026
21 October 2026
```

### Cause
In `crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs` (around lines 845–854), the match arms handle `'y'` and `'d'` only. Word documents commonly use uppercase `D` and `Y`, and Microsoft's date-picture documentation says both cases are valid.

### Fix
Match `'y' | 'Y'` and `'d' | 'D'`. Add regression tests for both cases.

title: Date pictures do not zero-pad hh on the 12-hour clock
author: SlavenDj
body:
### Summary
The lowercase `hh` date-time instruction does not pad a single-digit 12-hour clock hour. `HH` is padded correctly.

### Reproduction
```sh
W=target/debug/wordcraft-cli
$W run --template blank --cmd 'insert.dateTime={"format":"hh:mm"}' --save /tmp/time.docx
$W text /tmp/time.docx
```

Actual at 17:27:
```text
5:27
```

Expected:
```text
05:27
```

### Cause
In `crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs` (around lines 855–858), the `'h'` arm always emits the unpadded 12-hour value. There is no `('h', 2..)` arm, unlike `'H'`.

### Fix
Add a padded `hh` arm that uses the 12-hour value. Add tests for `h`, `hh`, `H`, and `HH`.

title: Date pictures mishandle quoted literals and bare a
author: SlavenDj
body:
### Summary
Date pictures keep the single quotes around literal text, and a bare `a` is treated as the AM/PM token. Word treats `'...'` as literal text and only recognizes `am/pm` or `AM/PM` as the day-period token.

### Reproduction
```sh
W=target/debug/wordcraft-cli
$W run --template blank --cmd 'insert.dateTime={"format":"yyyy 'Q'"}' --save /tmp/dateq.docx
$W text /tmp/dateq.docx

$W run --template blank --cmd 'insert.dateTime={"format":"yyyy a"}' --save /tmp/datea.docx
$W text /tmp/datea.docx
```

Actual:
```text
2026 'Q'
2026 PM
```

Expected:
```text
2026 Q
2026 a
```

### Cause
In `crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs` (around lines 843–866), the fallback copies quote characters literally, and the `('a' | 'A', _)` arm always emits AM/PM. The existing five-character `am/pm` check above already handles the real token.

### Fix
Parse a quoted group and emit its contents without the quotes. Remove the bare `a`/`A` arm so those characters fall through as literals. Add tests for quoted text and a bare `a`.

title: Format Page Numbers clears the section Start at value
author: SlavenDj
body:
### Summary
`layout.pageNumberFormat` always writes `page_num_start`, even when the caller only supplies a format. Changing the number format therefore clears an existing “Start at” value.

### Reproduction
```sh
W=target/debug/wordcraft-cli
$W run --template blank   --cmd 'layout.pageNumberFormat={"start":5}'   --cmd 'layout.pageNumberFormat={"format":"lowerRoman"}'   --save /tmp/pagenum.docx
$W inspect /tmp/pagenum.docx | grep -E 'pageNum'
```

Actual:
```json
"pageNumFormat": "lowerRoman",
"pageNumStart": null,
```

Expected: `pageNumStart` stays `5`.

The ribbon's “Format Page Numbers…” menu item currently sends `{}` and also clears the value; that dead menu item is tracked separately in #1443, but the data loss remains even when a caller supplies only `format`.

### Cause
In `crates/engine/src/cmd/page.rs` (around lines 73–85), `x.page_num_start = start;` runs unconditionally.

### Fix
Assign `page_num_start` only when the `start` key is present. Keep an explicit `null` as the way to clear it. Add a test for changing only `format`.

title: Cell Margins resets the sides that are not passed
author: SlavenDj
body:
### Summary
`table.cellMargins` rebuilds the whole margin array from defaults, so setting one side silently resets the other three.

### Reproduction
```sh
W=target/debug/wordcraft-cli
$W run --template blank   --cmd 'insert.table={"rows":1,"cols":1}'   --cmd 'table.cellMargins={"top":20}'   --cmd 'table.cellMargins={"left":10}'   --save /tmp/margins.docx
unzip -p /tmp/margins.docx word/document.xml | grep -o '<w:tblCellMar>.*</w:tblCellMar>'
```

Actual:
```xml
<w:tblCellMar><w:top w:w="0" .../><w:left w:w="200" .../><w:bottom w:w="0" .../><w:right w:w="108" .../></w:tblCellMar>
```

Expected: `top` stays 20pt (400 twips) and `right` stays at its previous value.

### Cause
In `crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs` (around lines 630–637), missing keys fall back to `0`/`5.4` instead of the table's current `cell_margins`.

### Fix
Start from the table's current margins and overwrite only the supplied sides. Add a test that changes one side twice.

title: Bookmark names are validated by bytes and accept invalid characters
author: SlavenDj
body:
### Summary
`insert.bookmark` validates the 40-character limit with `str::len()` (bytes) and only rejects spaces and a leading ASCII digit. It rejects valid 27-character Unicode names and accepts names Word rejects, such as `a&b` and `a!b`. (A leading `_` is intentionally valid: Word's own hidden bookmarks are `_Ref…`/`_GoBack`, and the Bookmark dialog hides `_`-prefixed names behind a checkbox.)

### Reproduction
```sh
W=target/debug/wordcraft-cli

# 27 characters, 51 UTF-8 bytes
$W run --template blank --cmd 'insert.bookmark={"name":"быстрый_доступ_к_документам"}' --save /tmp/bm.docx
# error: bookmark names ... at most 40 characters

for n in 'a&b' 'a!b'; do
  $W run --template blank --cmd "insert.bookmark={"name":"$n"}" --save /tmp/bm.docx
done
# both are accepted
```

Expected: the 27-character Cyrillic name is accepted; `a&b` and `a!b` are rejected. User-facing Word bookmark names contain only letters, digits, and underscores and are at most 40 characters; a leading `_` stays allowed for hidden bookmarks.

### Cause
In `crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs` (around lines 460–462), `bookmark_name_ok` uses `name.len()` and a minimal character check. The doc comment already says “40 characters”.

### Fix
Count characters with `chars().count()`, require the first character to be a letter or `_`, and reject characters that are not alphanumeric or `_`. Add tests for Unicode names, hidden `_`-leading names, and invalid punctuation.

title: HTML export drops ordered-list start numbers
author: SlavenDj
body:
### Summary
DOCX lists that start at a value other than 1 are exported to HTML as a plain `<ol>`. Opening that HTML or converting it to PDF restarts the list at 1.

### Reproduction
```sh
W=target/debug/wordcraft-cli
$W run --template blank   --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"five"}'   --cmd 'text.newParagraph'   --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"six"}'   --cmd 'select.all'   --cmd 'para.defineNumber={"start":5}'   --save /tmp/list.docx
$W convert /tmp/list.docx /tmp/list.html
$W convert /tmp/list.html /tmp/list.pdf
pdftotext -layout /tmp/list.pdf -
```

Actual: `<ol>` in the HTML and `1. Five / 2. six` in the PDF.
Expected: `<ol start="5">` and `5. Five / 6. six`.

### Cause
In `crates/formats/src/html.rs` (around line 1679), the list stack stores only `(ordered, li_open)` and always writes `<ol>`.

### Fix
Carry the list start in the stack and emit it on the opening `<ol>`; close and reopen when it changes. Add an HTML round-trip test.

title: HTML import ignores ordered-list start numbers
author: SlavenDj
body:
### Summary HTML ordered lists with a `start` attribute or per-item `value` are imported starting at 1. Separate adjacent `
    ` elements also merge into one continuous list. ### Reproduction ```sh W=target/debug/wordcraft-cli printf '
    1. a
    2. b
    ' > /tmp/list.html $W convert /tmp/list.html /tmp/list.docx $W text /tmp/list.docx ``` Actual: ```text 1. a 2. b ``` Expected: ```text 3. a 7. b ``` ### Cause In `crates/formats/src/html.rs`, `ElKind::List(bool)` stores only the ordered flag, and the paragraph builder hardcodes `start: 1` (around line 806). The parser has the attributes but does not carry them. ### Fix Store the start value on the open list element and copy it into `ListInfo.start`. Per-item `value` needs a per-item override or a new list group; split adjacent `
      `s into separate groups. Add round-trip tests.

title: ODT and TeX exports restart ordered lists at 1
author: SlavenDj
body:
### Summary
Ordered lists that start at a value other than 1 are written to ODT and TeX without their start value. Converting the result back shows 1, 2, … instead of the original numbers.

### Reproduction
```sh
W=target/debug/wordcraft-cli
$W run --template blank   --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"five"}'   --cmd 'text.newParagraph'   --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"six"}'   --cmd 'select.all'   --cmd 'para.defineNumber={"start":5}'   --save /tmp/list.docx

for ext in odt tex; do
  $W convert /tmp/list.docx /tmp/list.$ext
  $W convert /tmp/list.$ext /tmp/list-$ext.pdf
  pdftotext -layout /tmp/list-$ext.pdf -
done
```

Actual: `1. Five / 2. six` from both formats.
Expected: `5. Five / 6. six`.

### Cause
The ODT writer emits `<text:list-item>` without `text:start-value` (`crates/formats/src/odt.rs`, around line 559), and the TeX writer emits `\begin{enumerate}` without a counter override (`crates/formats/src/latex.rs`, around line 123). The start value is available on the paragraph's `ListInfo`.

### Fix
Write `text:start-value="5"` on the first ODT item and `\setcounter{enumi}{4}` after the first TeX `enumerate`. Add round-trip tests. RTF has the same symptom but needs list overrides, so it is out of scope for this issue.

title: Read Aloud on Windows: stop starting PowerShell for every sentence
author: d-0-t
body:
## TLDR Abstract
Windows Read Aloud starts a new PowerShell process for every sentence, so every sentence waits about 1.5 seconds before it can speak. A persistent host started once per reading cuts that wait to about 16 milliseconds after the first sentence.  
The change keeps the same voices and settings, adds no dependencies, and falls back to today's path if the host fails. A one-sentence document will not feel faster; a page or a chapter will.

## Description

I'm a writer and a reader. Read Aloud, an accessibility feature, is the reason I would use WordCraft, and the default Windows voice is the version most people will meet first. Right now that voice has a long pause before every sentence, which makes a long document hard to listen to. It feels like the app has to wake up for every sentence.

Read Aloud should work on a fresh Windows install. While there are other PRs meant to extend Read Aloud, asking people to install additional software, download models, or sign up for a cloud voice, only helps superusers.

On my machine, speaking just `"Hi."` takes 2.8 seconds from launching PowerShell to the process exiting. A 59-character sentence takes 5.4 seconds. Most of that time is not speech. It is PowerShell starting, loading System.Speech, creating a SpeechSynthesizer, speaking one sentence, and exiting. Then the next sentence does it all again.

The numbers below come from Windows PowerShell 5.1 and System Speech at rate 0, with the default English voice.  
"Today" is the current path. "One persistent host" is the proposed path.

| What I measured | Time |
|---|---:|
| Today: start PowerShell to the first sound (`"Hi."`) | 1.50 to 1.56 s |
| Today: start to the end of `"Hi."` | 2.84 s |
| Today: start to the end of a 59-character sentence | 5.38 s |
| One persistent host: start to ready | 1.56 to 1.62 s, once per reading |
| One persistent host: next sentence to the first sound | ~16 ms |
| One persistent host: next sentence to the end of `"Hi."` | 1.24 s |
| …

title: DOCX: saving regenerates the theme and drops a few attributes (table style indent, rFonts hint, annotationRef, dc:language)
author: Fubeo
body:
### What happens

Opening a `.docx` and saving it without changes loses a few things outside the text. Nothing warns about them. The biggest one is the theme: `word/theme/theme1.xml` is rebuilt from a small model, so most of the original theme is replaced.

Each case below is a minimal package (`[Content_Types].xml`, `_rels/.rels`, `word/document.xml` with one paragraph, plus the part shown), passed through `wordcraft_docx::read` and then `wordcraft_docx::write`. Reproduced with v0.9.0 (2e6db0bd).

### 1. The theme is regenerated

Input `word/theme/theme1.xml` (shortened):

```xml
<a:theme name="LibreOffice">
  <a:themeElements>
    <a:clrScheme name="Mio">…</a:clrScheme>
    <a:fontScheme name="LibreOffice">
      <a:majorFont>
        <a:latin typeface="DejaVu Sans" pitchFamily="2" charset="0"/>
        <a:ea typeface="Noto Sans CJK SC"/>
        <a:cs typeface="Noto Sans Arabic"/>
      </a:majorFont>
      …
    </a:fontScheme>
    <a:fmtScheme name="Office">
      …
      <a:lnStyleLst>
        <a:ln w="6350">…</a:ln><a:ln w="6350">…</a:ln><a:ln w="6350">…</a:ln>
      </a:lnStyleLst>
      …
    </a:fmtScheme>
  </a:themeElements>
</a:theme>
```

Output:

```xml
<a:clrScheme name="LibreOffice">…</a:clrScheme>
<a:majorFont>
  <a:latin typeface="DejaVu Sans"/>
  <a:ea typeface=""/>
  <a:cs typeface=""/>
</a:majorFont>
…
<a:lnStyleLst>
  <a:ln w="6350" …/><a:ln w="12700" …/><a:ln w="19050" …/>
</a:lnStyleLst>
```

- the East Asian and complex script theme fonts (`a:ea`, `a:cs`) become empty, so text that uses the theme font for those scripts changes font. The reader already reads `a:cs` for rendering (`pc.major_cs`), but it's not kept in the model;
- `pitchFamily` and `charset` of the theme fonts are dropped;
- the colour scheme takes the theme's name;
- the format scheme (fills, lines, effects, background fills) is replaced by a fixed minimal one. Shapes and charts that point at a theme style (`a:lnRef idx="2"` and so on) then draw with other widths and fills. T…

title: [BUG][ODT] `Keep with next paragraph` option doesn't behave as expected when opening .odt files
author: hmslima
body:
While version 0.9.0 (2e6db0bd) of WordCraft successfully recognizes the ODT `Keep with next paragraph` property _(resolving the core issue from https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/issues/2813)_, it does not behave as expected during pagination.

**Sample file**
Take the following .odt file:
[Keep with next paragraph.odt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33794459/Keep.with.next.paragraph.odt)

File content:
> Line 1 keeps with the next line
> Line 2 keeps with the next line
> Line 3
> Line 4
> Line 5

Only the first two lines have the `Keep with next paragraph` option enabled

**Expected behavior**
In LibreOffice, when we add newer content or blank lines before this initial content in a way that these initial  lines are pushed to the next page, once the `Line 3` goes to the next page, the previous two lines that have the `Keep with next paragraph` option follow the third line. That's also the behavior in WordCraft with its own .docx files.

**Actual behavior in WordCraft with an ODT file**
When opening this same .odt file in WordCraft 0.9.0 (2e6db0bd) and adding content above, the moment `Line 3` is pushed to the next page, the previous two lines fail to follow together. While WordCraft correctly recognizes that the first two lines have the `Keep with next` optio enabled, they do not pull along with the third line _(though, notably, the first line still correctly follows the second line)_.

title: Fedora: a Thai run with Latin is drawn in two fonts again (#1549); the pinned craft-fonts has no Thai face
author: MatRanc
body:

## Summary
On Fedora, the release build still draws a Thai run with Latin text in two fonts, which is the bug #1549 fixed. The fix needs one face that covers Thai and Latin. Fedora's Thai fonts are Thai-only, and the craft-fonts commit that CI and releases pin (`8dcdacd5`, `CRAFT_FONTS_REF` in `ci.yml` and `release.yml`) has no Thai font. Noto Sans Thai, which does cover Latin, landed in craft-fonts later (storytold/craft-fonts#18, 2026-10-11) as "the apps' fallback for Thai where no Thai font is installed".

title: Caret skips the last character of the line above a wrapped inline equation
author: supikachu
body: ## Environment - WordCraft 0.9.0 (dev build from `main`; still reproduces at `8e986366`) - Windows 10 x64, 100% zoom, default page setup - No IME involved; reproduces with plain ASCII text - `wordcraft.log`: no errors or panics ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open a new blank document with the default page setup at 100% zoom. 2. Type `This is an inline formula, This is an inline formula,` and leave the caret at the end. 3. Press `Alt+=` to insert an inline equation. Set the input format to LaTeX and paste: ```latex \cos{\alpha}+\cos{\beta}=2\cos{\frac{1}{2}\left(\alpha+\beta\right)}\cos{\frac{1}{2}\left(\alpha-\beta\right)} ``` 4. Press Enter to build the equation up. (This report is about the built-up inline equation, not the linear editing view from #3461.) 5. title: macOS Vietnamese IME: need to press Space twice to commit composed syllables
author: WillemTruong
body:
Summary

 On macOS, when using a Vietnamese input method (e.g., built-in "Tiếng Việt" Telex/VNI, or GoTiengViet), typing a composed syllable requires pressing Space twice. The first Space is meant to commit the IME composition (tru → type ng →
 Space → trưng), but WordCraft treats it as a normal punctuation word boundary and ignores it.

 Root cause

 WordCraft already handles IME pre-edit/commit events (ImeEvent::Preedit → ime_preedit in crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs), but the AutoCorrect/space logic in crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs triggers on a space as a word boundary even while
 IME composition is active:

 ```rust
   fn autocorrect_word(s: &mut Session, on_enter: bool) -> Result<(), CmdError> {
       let Some(last) ... = ... else { return Ok(()); };
       // space / punctuation trigger autocorrect even during active Vietnamese IME composition
       if !(on_enter || last == ' ' || ",.;:!?".contains(last)) { return Ok(()); }
       ...
   }
 ```

 In Vietnamese IMEs, Space is the commit key — it should not trigger AutoCorrect until the syllable is committed.

 Proposed fix

 Gate AutoCorrect and normal Text/Space insertion behind ime_composing state:

 1. Track composition state (ime_preedit.is_empty() + an explicit ime_composing flag).
 2. In canvas_events() (crates/ui-egui/src/keys.rs), skip Event::Text and Key::Space while ime_composing is true.
 3. Reset ime_composing = false on ImeEvent::Commit, WindowFocused(false), or any focus-losing event.
 4. After commit, run AutoCorrect normally.

 This is a minimal change localized to the UI event loop (keys.rs) and the autocorrect trigger (tools.rs). It won't affect other languages' typing behavior.

 Reproduction

 1. Add a Vietnamese keyboard in System Settings → Keyboard → Input Sources (e.g., "Tiếng Việt - Gõ Đơn" Telex).
 2. Switch to it, open WordCraft.
 3. Type truong → trường (with tone marks via Telex rules).
 4. Press Space to commit → observe the space is consumed and the next word requires another Sp…

title: [Feature Request] [WordCraft] Clear a direct paragraph property (null in para.set is ignored)
author: forhadkhan
body:
## Environment
- WordCraft 0.9.0 (`wordcraft-cli --version`), Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64, .deb from ArtCraft Launcher 0.6.1
- Driven by an MCP client over stdio: `wordcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root <dir> --automation-write-root <dir>`

## Steps
1. `new_document` `{"template":"blank"}`, then `type_text` `{"text":"First"}`
2. `execute` `para.set` `{"props":{"spaceBefore":48}}`
3. `inspect_document`: the block has `"props":{"spaceBefore":48.0}`
4. `execute` `para.set` `{"props":{"spaceBefore":null}}` (no error)
5. `inspect_document`: the block still has `"spaceBefore":48.0`

## Actual
`null` is accepted and ignored. Setting `0` makes an explicit zero, which is different from "inherit from the style". New paragraphs made with `text.newParagraph` inherit the direct properties (after `para.set` with `spaceBefore` 48 and `pageBreakBefore` true on "First", the next paragraph "Second" has both too), so a one-off value carries to every later paragraph, and there is no command to take it off.

## Expected / request
A way to remove a direct paragraph property so it falls back to the style: `null` in `para.set` meaning "unset", or a command such as `para.clearDirect` that takes a list of property names (or all of them). `format.clear` covers characters; there is no paragraph counterpart that I could find in `list_commands`.

Near: #3069 (select text with similar formatting).

title: [FEATURE REQUEST] — Add "Synonyms" to Right-Click Context Menu
author: CasaAmarillaRoja
body:
**1. Summary / User Story**
As a user writing documents, I want to be able to right-click a word and see a list of synonyms so I can easily vary my vocabulary without opening an external browser or dictionary app.

**2. Proposed Behavior**

* **Trigger:** The user right-clicks on a specific word in the document.
* **UI Addition:** The context menu includes a new item called "Synonyms" (featuring a flyout/sub-menu).
* **Action:** Hovering over or clicking "Synonyms" displays a list of alternative words generated by the software's thesaurus dictionary.
* **Resolution:** Clicking one of the suggested alternative words automatically replaces the original word in the text.

**3. Acceptance Criteria (Edge Cases)**
To ensure a smooth user experience, the implementation should handle the following:

* **Formatting Preservation:** The newly inserted word should match the font, size, and styling (bold, italics) of the original word.
* **Capitalization:** The replacement word should match the original word's capitalization (e.g., replacing *“Happy”* should result in *“Joyful”*, not *“joyful”*).
* **Punctuation:** Replacing a word should not delete adjacent punctuation (e.g., right-clicking "sad," and replacing it should result in "upset,").
* **Empty States:** If no synonyms are found for the selected word in the active language, the "Synonyms" menu item should be greyed out or display "No suggestions available."

title: DOCX: patterned shading (w:shd pct80, pct25, solid with a fill) is drawn as the plain fill colour, so pct80 on white comes out white
author: dpkruse
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @dpkruse (Kruse Legal)._

**Version:** `main` at 8e98636 (0.9.0 + merged PRs, wordcraft-cli and the web editor built on macOS from that commit); also v0.9.0.

## Summary

Patterned shading (`w:shd` with `w:val="pctNN"`, and `solid` when a fill is also given) is drawn as the plain `w:fill` colour. The pattern colour is ignored, so the Australian family court's forms lose their Part heading bars: `<w:shd w:val="pct80" w:color="auto" w:fill="FFFFFF"/>` is a dark grey bar in Word (80% black over white) and plain white in WordCraft.

## Repro

One table, shading on the right-hand cells (`word/document.xml`, synthetic):

```xml
<w:tc><w:tcPr><w:shd w:val="pct80" w:color="auto"   w:fill="FFFFFF"/></w:tcPr>…Lorem ipsum…</w:tc>
<w:tc><w:tcPr><w:shd w:val="pct25" w:color="auto"   w:fill="FFFFFF"/></w:tcPr>…Lorem ipsum…</w:tc>
<w:tc><w:tcPr><w:shd w:val="pct50" w:color="FF0000" w:fill="FFFFFF"/></w:tcPr>…Lorem ipsum…</w:tc>
<w:tc><w:tcPr><w:shd w:val="solid" w:color="auto"   w:fill="FFFFFF"/></w:tcPr>…Lorem ipsum…</w:tc>
```

| `w:shd` | Word (365, PDF via Graph) | WordCraft |
|---|---|---|
| `pct80`, auto on FFFFFF | dark grey `333333`, text white | white |
| `pct25`, auto on FFFFFF | grey `BFBFBF` | white |
| `pct50`, FF0000 on FFFFFF | pink `FF8080` | white |
| `solid`, auto, fill FFFFFF | black, text white | white |

Word draws a percentage pattern as the pattern colour (`w:color`, `auto` = black) over the fill (`w:fill`, `auto` = white) at that percentage: in effect `fill × (1 − p) + color × p`. `solid` is p = 1, so the fill is not seen at all.

Real documents: the FCFCOA's published forms, for example the *Notice of address for service* (https://www.fcfcoa.gov.au/fl/forms; Part C) and the *Affidavit – Family law* (Part A), where each Part's heading is a black and grey bar made with `pct80`/`pct25`. 10 of the court's 12 most-used forms use this; the other Part headings in the same forms use `clear` fills and draw corr…

title: DOCX: malformed document.xml is silently truncated (exit 0), and saving makes the loss permanent
author: otsouvalas
body:
**Version:** wordcraft 0.9.0 (2e6db0bd), Linux x86_64 (.deb)

If `word/document.xml` is not well-formed, WordCraft opens the file anyway. It drops everything after the first error, gives no warning and exits with status 0. Saving the file then writes the truncated text as a valid DOCX, so the lost text is gone for good.

LibreOffice 24.2 refuses to load the same files ("source file could not be loaded"), so the user at least knows something is wrong.

#2778 described this parser behaviour (`check_end_names = false`, auto-closing unclosed elements, stopping at the first complete root). It assumed the behaviour was "not reachable from files today". It is reachable from files, through the DOCX reader.

### Results

| `document.xml` body | `wordcraft-cli text` | exit |
|---|---|---|
| `<w:t>a <- b</w:t>` (valid control) | `a <- b` | 0 |
| `<w:t>before a <- b after</w:t>` then `<w:p>…last paragraph…</w:p>` | `before a ` (the rest of the run and the whole last paragraph are missing) | **0** |
| a second `<w:p>` left unclosed, then a third paragraph | `first`, `second` (`third` is missing) | **0** |

title: Find/Replace ^b: text moves before section break but break remains (user report)
author: earlvanze
body:
A user reports that replacing a section break moves the following page’s text before the break while leaving the break present.

Source: <https://discord.com/channels/1359579021108842617/1558921592585715862/1562788022469001276> (2026-10-22 11:21 UTC).

The report follows instructions to find `^b` (Special > Section Break), leave Replace with empty, disable wildcards and regular expressions, then use Find Next and Replace. The user says: “When I click replace the section break is not getting deleted but instead the text in next page appears before the section break”. A screenshot is attached to the source message.

Expected: replacing the matched section break with empty text removes the boundary without losing text; Undo restores it.

This is a user report, not independently reproduced. The exact version, OS, document, Track Changes state, and actual Find options are not yet verified.

Related: #2127 was closed by merged PR #2133. That fix covers shared paragraph-join deletion logic and Backspace/Delete, including a final-paragraph case; it does not by itself verify this reported Find/Replace workflow. This could be an older build, tracked-deletion behavior, or another edge case. Please establish which before treating it as a regression.

Source review: `crates/engine/src/cmd/find_pattern.rs` recognizes section marks; `edit.replace` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs` uses `paste_text`, and untracked Replace All uses `Document::delete_range`. The current local source contains #2133’s section-transfer logic. No source changes or reproduction tests were performed in this monitoring run.

Suggested verification: obtain the version and a minimal non-sensitive document, check Replace and Replace All with Track Changes on/off and a break at the final paragraph, and add a focused regression test if the failure remains on current main.

title: Forms protection makes legacy form fields read only: FORMTEXT can't be typed into, FORMCHECKBOX can't be ticked
author: dpkruse
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @dpkruse (Kruse Legal)._

**Version:** `main` at 8e98636 (`wordcraft-cli` built on macOS from that commit).

## Summary

A document protected for filling in forms (`<w:documentProtection w:edit="forms" w:enforcement="1"/>`) is treated as **read only**. Its legacy form fields can't be filled in: typing into a `FORMTEXT` field and ticking a `FORMCHECKBOX` are both refused with "the document is protected (read only)". Only content controls are fillable (#1309).

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.15.1.29 (`documentProtection`): with `w:edit="forms"`, "allow editing of form fields only". Word works this way. The fixed wording can't be changed, but each legacy text field can be typed into, check boxes tick, drop-downs choose, and Tab moves from field to field.

Real documents: the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia's family law forms (https://www.fcfcoa.gov.au/fl/forms). 11 of the 12 most-used forms enforce this protection, with about 2,000 legacy `FORMTEXT`/`FORMCHECKBOX` fields between them. Opened in WordCraft, none of them can be filled in. #1174 (drawing and keeping these fields) is fixed; this is the editing side.

## Repro (headless)

A synthetic file: a `FORMTEXT` field showing `XXXXX` after "Name: ", a `FORMCHECKBOX` before "Applicant", a line of fixed wording, and `<w:documentProtection w:edit="forms" w:enforcement="1"/>` in `word/settings.xml`.

| Command | Result | Word |
|---|---|---|

| caret at the `FORMCHECKBOX`, `developer.toggleCheckBox` | `… protected (read only)` | ticks the box |
| the same file with `w:enforcement="0"` | `text.insert` works | — |

(Finding or selecting a field's displayed text is a separate problem, without protection too: #3605.)

title: edit.find and select.text don't search a legacy form field's displayed text (FORMTEXT result)
author: dpkruse
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @dpkruse (Kruse Legal)._

**Version:** `main` at 8e98636 (`wordcraft-cli` built on macOS from that commit).

## Summary

`edit.find` and `select.text` don't search the text a legacy form field displays (a `FORMTEXT` field's result). On a filled-in form that text is the answers, so they can't be found or selected, even though `wordcraft-cli text` shows them. Word's Find searches field results.

This is separate from #3603, which is about filling fields in under forms protection. This one happens without any protection.

## Repro (headless, unprotected)

A synthetic file: "Name: " followed by a `FORMTEXT` field whose result is `XXXXX`, then a paragraph "Fixed wording of the form."

```xml
<w:p><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">Name: </w:t></w:r>
  <w:r><w:fldChar w:fldCharType="begin"><w:ffData><w:name w:val="Name1"/><w:enabled/><w:calcOnExit w:val="0"/><w:textInput/></w:ffData></w:fldChar></w:r>
  <w:r><w:instrText xml:space="preserve"> FORMTEXT </w:instrText></w:r><w:r><w:fldChar w:fldCharType="separate"/></w:r>
  <w:r><w:t>XXXXX</w:t></w:r><w:r><w:fldChar w:fldCharType="end"/></w:r></w:p>
```

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `wordcraft-cli text` | `Name: XXXXX` |
| `edit.find={"text":"XXXXX"} --print` | `{"count":0,"matches":[]}` |
| `select.text={"text":"XXXXX"}` | `` `XXXXX` not found `` |
| `edit.find={"text":"Fixed"} --print` | `{"count":1, …}` (ordinary text is found) |

## Expected

As in Word, Find, Select and Replace include the displayed result of fields, with field codes hidden. That covers `FORMTEXT` here, and likely other fields' results too.

## Related

Searched issues and PRs for "find field result", "search field results", "find inside field", "edit.find field", "select.text field": nothing. #3300 and #3270 are about which *stories* Find searches, not field results.

title: [N-02] Object drag preview can create a texture larger than the GPU limit, and wgpu panics outside the command guard
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, findings N-02) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** High (crash of the UI thread). **Status:** Confirmed in code and dependency source at eae2421 (not executed); the code is unchanged at `00bc6a4b`, and the dependency versions are the same (`egui-wgpu` 0.36.2, `wgpu` 30.0.1 in `Cargo.lock`).

let img = wordcraft_render::render_items(&app.session.doc, &items, b.x, b.y, b.w, b.h, scale * ctx.pixels_per_point(), &opts);
let ci = egui::ColorImage::from_rgba_unmultiplied([img.width as usize, img.height as usize], &img.to_straight());

title: [N-03] Hunspell continuation classes make each spell check O(rules²) on the UI thread; a hostile .aff hangs every launch
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, findings N-03) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Medium (persistent UI hang). **Status:** Confirmed by measurement at eae2421; the matching code is unchanged at `00bc6a4b` (the only later changes to `affix.rs` are the U+FE0F flag fixes). Timings: a release harness for the per-word cost, and the debug `wordcraft-cli` (workspace `opt-level=1`) for the end-to-end run.

Related: #2775 (`dictionariesFolder` and the automation roots), #3654 (N-45) / #3655 (N-46) / #3656 (N-47) (other `.aff` suggestion costs).

## Evidence

`suffixed` tries every rule of a matching group, and for each one calls `form_has_flag` ([`affix.rs#L651-L680`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/proof/src/affix.rs#L651-L680)):

```rust
if need == 0 && rules().any(|r| r.cond_matches(&root, true) && self.form_has_flag(&root, r.bit, INNER_CHAIN, excluded)) {
```

`form_has_flag` walks the same groups' rules again ([`affix.rs#L581-L605`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/proof/src/affix.rs#L581-L605)):

```rust
for r in g.rules.iter().filter_map(|&i| self.suffixes.get(i as usize)) {
    if r.cont & bit != 0 && r.cond_matches(&root, true) && self.form_has_flag(&root, r.bit, depth - 1, excluded) {
```

`MAX_CHAIN = 2` bounds the depth, but not the fan-out. A rule with an empty append is indexed under the empty suffix and matches every word, so R such rules cost R² condition checks per word. `MAX_WORD_BYTES` (120) doesn't help: the cost is in rules, not word length. `parse_aff` has no rule cap ([`#L351-L353`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/proof/src/affix.rs#L351-L353)). `forms()` ([`#L709-L745`](https://github.com/s…

title: [N-04] Paragraph::object_at rescans the paragraph on every call, so object loops are quadratic and a 24 KB .docx hangs on open
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, findings N-04) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** High (hang on open, and on later edits and frames). **Status:** Confirmed by repro at eae2421; the code is unchanged at `00bc6a4b`. Timings come from the audit run at eae2421 on the debug `wordcraft-cli` (workspace `opt-level=1`).

Related: #2765 (other docx reader quadratic scans), #3437 (quadratic content-control save, fixed in the writer), #554.

## Evidence

`object_at` counts every U+FFFC before `off` to find the object's index ([`doc/src/para.rs#L1062-L1084`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/doc/src/para.rs#L1062-L1084)):

```rust
fn objects_before(&self, off: usize) -> usize {
    self.text.get(..off).map(|t| t.chars().filter(|c| *c == OBJ).count()).unwrap_or(0)
}
pub fn object_at(&self, off: usize) -> Option<&InlineObject> {
    ...
    self.objects.get(self.objects_before(off))
}
```

About 50 loops use the pattern `for off in p.object_offsets() { p.object_at(off) }`, which is O(objects × paragraph length): the field scan ([`doc/src/fields.rs#L46-L47`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/doc/src/fields.rs#L46-L47)), control events ([`doc/src/control.rs#L315-L316`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/doc/src/control.rs#L315-L316)) and kept markers on every range delete (`#L645`), permission ranges and bookmarks ([`doc/src/lib.rs#L1486-L1487`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/doc/src/lib.rs#L1486-L1487)), and engine commands in `insert.rs`, `references.rs`, `tools.rs`, `review.rs`, `accessibility.rs` and `speech.rs`.

title: [N-05] Style and numbering lookups are linear scans repeated per paragraph and per run: a 61 KB .docx takes 35 s to open
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, findings N-05) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Medium (hang on open and export). **Status:** Confirmed by repro at eae2421; the code is unchanged at `00bc6a4b`. Timings come from the audit run at eae2421 on the debug `wordcraft-cli` (workspace `opt-level=1`).

Related: #2767 (STYLEREF cost, another per-paragraph style walk).

## Evidence

`StyleSheet::get` is a linear search, and `chain` calls it up to 32 times, once per `basedOn` step ([`doc/src/styles.rs#L729-L758`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/doc/src/styles.rs#L729-L758)):

```rust
pub fn get(&self, id: &str) -> Option<&Style> {
    self.styles.iter().find(|s| s.id == id)
}
...
pub fn chain(&self, id: &str) -> Vec<&Style> {
    ...
        if out.len() >= 32 || out.iter().any(|o: &&Style| o.id == s.id) {
    ...
        cur = s.based_on.as_deref().and_then(|b| self.get(b));
```

Paragraph resolution walks the chain, and run resolution walks the paragraph chain again for every run, plus the character style's chain ([`doc/src/resolve.rs#L299-L300`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/doc/src/resolve.rs#L299-L300), [`#L360-L366`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/doc/src/resolve.rs#L360-L366)). This runs in layout, export, word count and docx import.

Numbering is the same. `num` and `abstract_of` are linear searches, and `level` and `next_label` call them several times per label ([`doc/src/numbering.rs#L221-L238`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/doc/src/numbering.rs#L221-L238), [`#L314-L320`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b…

title: [N-12] TOC hyperlinks and Update Fields are quadratic in headings, fields and bookmarks
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, finding N-12) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Medium (DoS / UI hang). **Status:** Confirmed by measurement. The timings below come from the audit run at eae2421 on a debug build; they were not re-measured at upstream main, but the code paths are unchanged.

Related: #2767 (WC-26, STYLEREF cost, closed), #554

## Evidence

1. **TOC with `\h` (hyperlinks, the default).** For every entry, `bookmark_heading` rescans every bookmark in the document to find the next free `_Toc` number:
   [crates/engine/src/cmd/references.rs#L519-L529](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/references.rs#L519-L529), called once per entry from [#L593-L600](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/references.rs#L593-L600)
   ```rust
   let next =
       s.doc.bookmarks().iter().filter_map(|(n, _)| n.strip_prefix("_Toc").and_then(|d| d.parse::<u64>().ok())).max().unwrap_or(0).saturating_add(1);
   ```
   `Document::bookmarks()` walks every paragraph and collects a `Vec<(String, Pos)>`, and each new `_Toc` bookmark makes the next scan longer.
2. **Update Fields.** Inside the per-field loop of `update_fields_in`:
   - `NUMWORDS` recounts the whole document for every field: [#L1020](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/references.rs#L1020) `"NUMWORDS" => updates.push((k, s.doc.word_count().to_string())),`

title: [N-14] Automation can make persistent, cross-document preference changes (AutoCorrect, key bindings, ribbon, author)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, finding N-14) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Medium (persistence / integrity, agent trust boundary). **Status:** Confirmed in the engine; persistence to `ui.json` traced in code.

Related: #2745 (WC-01, agent file access, closed), #2779 (closed), #969, #3279

## Evidence

`tools.autocorrect` (`add`), `tools.customizeKeyboard` (`assign`/`remove`/`reset`), `tools.customizeRibbon` and `file.setAuthor` are ordinary commands, reachable by id from MCP (headless or `--connect`), the control channel and `wordcraft-cli run`. Nothing marks them as user-only ([crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs#L439-L452](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs#L439-L452), [file.rs#L137](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L137)).

title: [N-15] Windows: clipboard picture is decoded by arboard with no size limits before WordCraft's caps (process abort)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, finding N-15) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Medium (crash: allocation failure aborts the process, outside `Session::run`). **Status:** Confirmed via dependency source (arboard 3.6.1, still the locked version at upstream main), not executed.

## Evidence

The paste path asks arboard for decoded pixels on every platform:
[apps/wordcraft/src/clipboard.rs#L99-L124](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/apps/wordcraft/src/clipboard.rs#L99-L124)
```rust
match clipboard.get_image() {
    Ok(image) => Some(ClipboardPicture::Pixels { width: image.width, height: image.height, rgba: image.bytes.into_owned() }),
```
The doc comment says "The UI checks the sizes before inserting anything". Those checks (`crates/ui-egui/src/paste_picture.rs`, `MAX_PIXELS = 50_000_000`) only run after `get_image()` returns.

`Cargo.lock` at upstream main pins `arboard 3.6.1`. Its Windows backend (`src/platform/windows.rs`, around lines 198-230) decodes the registered "PNG" format with `PngDecoder::new(..)` and `CF_DIBV5` with `BmpDecoder::new_without_file_header(..)`. Both then call `DynamicImage::from_decoder(decoder)`. No `image::Limits` are set, so the decoder allocates the full output buffer from the header's width x height before reading any pixel data. On Linux and macOS, arboard goes through paths that keep the `image` crate's default allocation limit, so they are not affected in the same way.

## Conditions and impact

- Platform: Windows desktop app.
- Input: a tiny clipboard item (tens of bytes) whose PNG or DIB header declares very large dimensions. The audit computed about 80 GB requested for a 100,000 x 100,000 16-bit RGBA header.
- Who can place it: any local process, a remote desktop server through clipboard redire…

title: [N-16] IME composition is drawn at an unclamped font size; a large line height panics epaint's glyph atlas
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, finding N-16) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Medium (UI crash outside `Session::run`'s guard). **Status:** Confirmed in code and dependency source (epaint 0.36.2 at upstream main), not executed.

## Evidence

The pre-edit text is laid out at a size derived from the caret height and zoom, with no clamp:
[crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs#L1604](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs#L1604)
```rust
let g = painter.layout_no_wrap(app.canvas.ime_preedit.clone(), regular(c.height * scale * 0.8), Color32::PLACEHOLDER);
```
`regular` is just `FontId::proportional(size)` ([crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs#L627-L629](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs#L627-L629)).

`c.height` is the caret span, which covers the line height. The model allows font sizes up to 1638 pt and Multiple line spacing up to 132x ([crates/doc/src/resolve.rs#L226](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/doc/src/resolve.rs#L226), [#L253](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/doc/src/resolve.rs#L253)). Zoom multiplies that again.

In epaint 0.36.2, a rasterised glyph is placed with `TextureAtlas::allocate`, which asserts:
```rust
assert!(w <= self.image.width(), "Tried to allocate a {} wide glyph in a {} wide texture atlas", ...);
```
(`epaint/src/texture_atlas.rs` around line 226, called from `text/font.rs` around line 283). A glyph taller than the atlas can grow to is then copied pixel by pixel with `image[(x, y)]` indexing past the image's height, which panics too.

title: [N-18] settings.xml merge copies the original prolog verbatim (DTD included) and keeps children by a prefix-blind r:id check
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, finding N-18) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (integrity; DTD/XXE passthrough to other consumers). **Status:** Confirmed in code.

Related: #1034 (introduced the settings merge), #2778 (WC-39, strict XML validation, closed)

## Evidence

On read, the original `word/settings.xml` bytes are stored when they hold children the model doesn't own ([crates/docx/src/read/mod.rs#L1161-L1165](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/read/mod.rs#L1161-L1165)). The XML reader skips a document type declaration silently, so such a part opens normally. On save, `merge` rebuilds the part from the original ([crates/docx/src/write/settings_merge.rs#L257-L316](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/write/settings_merge.rs#L257-L316)):
```rust
let (o_open, o_close, o_kids) = children(orig, "w:settings")?;
...
let root_tag = orig.get(..o_open)?;
...
s.push_str(root_tag);
```
1. **Prolog passthrough.** `root_tag` is everything from byte 0 to the end of the `<w:settings …>` start tag. That is the XML declaration, any comments or processing instructions, and any `<!DOCTYPE …>` with an internal subset. `children()` refuses `<!` only between the root's start and end tags ([#L158-L180](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/write/settings_merge.rs#L158-L180)), although its doc comment says DOCTYPE makes it return `None`.
2. **Prefix-blind reference check.** Unowned children are kept unless their text contains the literal `r:id=` ([#L296-L298](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/write/settings_merge.rs#L296-L298)):

title: [N-19] "Remove personal information" keeps word/people.xml and a stale docProps thumbnail on save
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, finding N-19) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (privacy). **Status:** Confirmed in code.

Related: #1062 (authors, dates and properties under "remove personal information", closed), #3276, #3277

## Evidence

When `w:removePersonalInformation` is on, the writer anonymises comment and revision authors, core properties, and Company/Manager. Examples: [crates/docx/src/write/mod.rs#L1223-L1237](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/write/mod.rs#L1223-L1237) and [#L1287-L1295](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/write/mod.rs#L1287-L1295).

The doc comment names "the thumbnail" as an intended keep.

title: [N-20] insert.field / fields.setCode accept any field instruction from automation, including fields Word acts on (DDE, linked includes)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, finding N-20) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (unsafe output produced on behalf of an agent). **Status:** Confirmed in code. The effect in Word is the documented behaviour of those field types; it was not exercised by the audit.

Related: #2746 (WC-02, UNC paths and NTLM, closed), #2745 (WC-01, closed)

## Evidence

[crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs#L933-L946](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs#L933-L946):
```rust
fn field(s: &mut Session, v: &Value) -> CmdResult {
    let instr = p::req_str(v, "instr")?.trim().to_string();
    if instr.is_empty() || instr.len() > 4096 {
        return Err(CmdError::Params("bad field code".into()));
    }
```
[crates/engine/src/cmd/fields.rs#L154-L163](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/fields.rs#L154-L163) (`fields.setCode`) applies the same length-only check before replacing an existing field's code.

There is no check on the field type. The docx writer writes the instruction back as-is in `w:instrText`/`w:fldSimple`. No code under `crates/engine/src` or `crates/mcp/src` mentions the DDE or INCLUDE* field types.

## Conditions and impact

- Precondition: an agent driving WordCraft through MCP, the control channel or `wordcraft-cli run` is steered by a prompt injection, for example text inside a document it was asked to edit. The agent then inserts or rewrites a field whose type Word acts on when the document is opened or its fields are updated:

title: [N-21] Kept part trees re-emit nested external relationships and macro parts in a .docx save
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, finding N-21) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (sanitisation gap). **Status:** Confirmed in code. The effect in Word was not verified.

Related: #1343 (embedded-object preservation, closed), #1034, #2778 (WC-39, closed)

## Evidence

**Read side.** `keep_unmodelled` filters external relationships only at the root (package and main document): `rels.list.iter().filter(|r| !r.external)` ([crates/docx/src/read/embed.rs#L113](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/read/embed.rs#L113)). `keep_part_tree` then keeps every relationship of every reached part, external ones included, with no type filter ([#L161-L192](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/read/embed.rs#L161-L192)): only internal targets are followed, but every relationship ends up in `kept`.

**Write side.** `copy_tree` re-emits external relationships verbatim and copies every internal target ([crates/docx/src/write/embed.rs#L261-L286](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/write/embed.rs#L261-L286)):
```rust
if r.external {
    rels.add_with_id(&r.id, &r.kind, &r.target, true);
```
Kept embedded objects add their external refs the same way ([#L328-L333](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/write/embed.rs#L328-L333)).

The macro guard covers only the main document's VBA project (`VBA_PROJECT_PART`), dropped when the target flavour can't hold macros ([crates/docx/src/write/mod.rs#L456-L490](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/write/mod.rs#L456-L490)).
