title: [N-23] connectors::reroute is O(connectors x laid-out objects) after every drawing command
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, finding N-23) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (DoS). **Status:** Plausible. The cost is confirmed in code but was not measured.

Related: #2763 (WC-21: this hook runs outside the `catch_unwind` guard, closed)

## Evidence

After every successful `arrange.*`, `shape.*`, `picture.*`, `draw.*` or `insert.shape` command, `Session::run` re-routes glued connectors ([crates/engine/src/session.rs#L1489-L1492](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/session.rs#L1489-L1492)). That is after, not inside, the guarded dispatch at [#L1463](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/session.rs#L1463):
```rust
if crate::cmd::connectors::reroutes_after(id) && crate::cmd::connectors::reroute(self) {
    self.touch();
}
```

`reroute` looks up each connector and both of its glued ends with `layout.object` ([crates/engine/src/cmd/connectors.rs#L93-L112](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/connectors.rs#L93-L112)):
```rust
let hit = layout.object(target, page)?;
...
for pos in conns {
    let Some(hit) = layout.object(&pos, s.page_hint) else { continue };
```
`object` → `find_object` scans the hint page and then linearly every other page's objects until it finds a match ([crates/layout/src/hit.rs#L372-L386](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/layout/src/hit.rs#L372-L386)):
```rust
on(page_hint).or_else(|| (0..self.pages.len()).filter(|i| *i != page_hint).find_map(on))
```
Each connector lookup uses `s.page_hint` (the caret's page), not the connector's own page. For a document whose connectors sit on many pages, almost …

title: [N-24] review.compare / combine: 64 MB LCS table per paragraph pair, with no overall work budget
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, finding N-24) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (DoS). **Status:** Confirmed by measurement. The timings come from the audit run at eae2421 on a debug build; the code is unchanged at upstream main.

## Evidence

[crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs#L1325-L1348](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs#L1325-L1348):
```rust
const MAX_LCS: usize = 4000;
...
let (n, m) = (a.len().min(MAX_LCS), b.len().min(MAX_LCS));
let mut t = vec![vec![0u32; m + 1]; n + 1];
for i in (0..n).rev() {
    for j in (0..m).rev() {
```
- The full O(n·m) table is allocated and filled: up to 4001 x 4001 `u32` ≈ **64 MB and 16M cells** for one call.
- `lcs_ops` runs once over the block list ([#L1218](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs#L1218)).

`MAX_LCS` bounds a single table. Nothing bounds the sum over all pairs.

## Conditions and impact

- Input: two documents with many long, slightly different paragraphs, for example two revisions of a long contract or a generated report. Each paragraph pair up to 4,000 words costs up to 16M cell updates and a fresh 64 MB allocation.

title: [N-25] mailings.labels / envelopes copy an uncapped text line into up to 400 labels
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, finding N-25) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

[crates/engine/src/cmd/mailings.rs#L1358-L1420](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/mailings.rs#L1358-L1420):

```rust
let rows = p::u64(v, "rows").map_or(prod.rows, |n| n.clamp(1, 40) as usize);
let cols = p::u64(v, "cols").map_or(prod.cols, |n| n.clamp(1, 10) as usize);
...

...
                _ => text.clone(),
...

```

title: [N-26] A NUL in the document title panics winit on X11 when it becomes the window title
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, finding N-26) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (UI crash, X11 only). **Status:** Confirmed by code trace on the `.json` path (winit 0.30.13 is still the locked version at upstream main).

## Evidence

For a document with no file path and no file name, the title bar uses the core title as-is ([crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L2052-L2061](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L2052-L2061)):
```rust
None => match &self.session.file_name {
    Some(name) => name.clone(),
    None if self.session.doc.core.title.is_empty() => tl!("Document1").into(),
    None => self.session.doc.core.title.clone(),
},
```
It is sent every time it changes ([#L2419-L2427](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L2419-L2427)):
```rust
ctx.send_viewport_cmd(egui::ViewportCommand::Title(title.clone()));
```
winit 0.30.13's X11 backend converts it with `CString::new(title).expect("Window title contained null byte")` (`src/platform_impl/linux/x11/window.rs:1005`).

Nothing strips control characters from `core.title`:
- `file.properties` sets it from the `title` parameter verbatim ([crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L385-L392](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L385-L392));

title: [N-27] ui.screenshot {path} writes with plain fs::write, bypassing file_access and safe_save
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, finding N-27) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (file write for control-key holders). **Status:** Confirmed in code.

Related: #2745 (WC-01, closed), #2779 (closed), #678 (temp-file names, closed)

## Evidence

The control method passes the caller's path through ([crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs#L255](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs#L255)):
```rust
"ui.screenshot" => Outcome::Screenshot { path: s("path").map(str::to_string) },
```
and the PNG is written with a bare `std::fs::write` ([#L312-L329](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs#L312-L329)):
```rust
#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
{
    if let Err(e) = std::fs::write(path, &png) {
        return json!({"ok": false, "error": format!("{path}: {e}")});
    }
}
```
By contrast, every engine write (for example `file.exportPng`) goes through `io::write_file`, which calls `file_access::check_write` and then writes atomically with `safe_save` ([crates/engine/src/io.rs#L677-L683](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/io.rs#L677-L683)):
```rust
pub fn write_file(path: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), String> {
    crate::file_access::check_write(path)?;
    safe_save::write(std::path::Path::new(path), bytes).map_err(|e| format!("{path}: {e}"))
}
```

## Conditions and impact

- Reachable only by a holder of the running app's control key: a local script or tool, or an agent using the raw control channel. The MCP `screenshot` tool sends no path and gets base64 back, so it is not affected.
- `fs::write` follows symlinks and truncates the existing file in place. The caller can ove…

title: [N-29] Table cell span arithmetic overflows on .json input (insert column / merge cells)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, finding N-29) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (integer overflow; panic in debug, silent wrap in release). **Status:** Confirmed by repro at eae2421 (debug build); the code is unchanged at upstream main.

`CellProps::span` is a plain `u32` with no deserialisation bound ([crates/doc/src/props.rs#L1289-L1290](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/doc/src/props.rs#L1289-L1290)).
```rust
pub fn span(&self) -> usize {
    self.props.span.clamp(1, 63) as usize
}
```
But two edit primitives do unchecked arithmetic on the raw field:
- `insert_col` ([#L194-L197](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/doc/src/table.rs#L194-L197)):
  ```rust
  Some((i, true)) => {
      if let Some(c) = row.cells.get_mut(i) {
          c.props.span += 1;
  ```

  ```rust
  first.props.span += c.props.span.max(1);
  ```

title: [N-35] Progressive-JPEG coefficient buffers are not charged to the decode budget; the crop dialog and picture edits decode with no header check
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, findings N-35) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Medium (High on wasm). **Status:** Partially fixed. At eae2421 a 197-byte 13000 x 13000 CMYK progressive JPEG inside a 7 KB docx peaked at about 1.78 GiB on PDF or PNG export (audit run at eae2421, debug build). Commit 3787af0a (#2001) added a header-time `decode_fits` check to `pdf` and `render`, and that check now refuses this file. Two gaps remain, both found by reading the code and not re-measured.

Related: #1321 (closed; fixed the order of allocation and checking, not the coefficient buffers).

## Evidence

The dependency versions are unchanged at upstream main (`image` 0.25.10, `zune-jpeg` 0.5.15):
- `image` charges only `decoder.total_bytes()`, the output buffer, against `max_alloc` (`io/image_reader_type.rs:319`).
- `zune-jpeg` `mcu_prog.rs:101-106` allocates a full-resolution `Vec<i16>` per component before reading any scan data, and it tolerates missing data.

For CMYK that is 8 B/px of coefficients on top of 3 B/px of output.

**Gap 1, the budget.** [geom/src/pixels.rs#L19-L24](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/geom/src/pixels.rs#L19-L24) charges 8 B/px against 512 MiB, which admits about 67 M px. Both [pdf/src/lib.rs#L1893-L1915](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/pdf/src/lib.rs#L1893-L1915) and [render/src/lib.rs#L204-L223](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/render/src/lib.rs#L204-L223) use it. An 8192 x 8192 CMYK progressive JPEG passes, but the decode needs about 537 MB of coefficients plus 201 MB of output. That is about 1.4x the intended cap.

title: [N-36] TIFF pictures with JPEG-compressed strips bypass every image limit (zune-jpeg default options inside `tiff`)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, findings N-36) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Medium (out-of-memory, dependency). **Status:** Plausible from source; not reproduced (the audit never ran its TIFF generator). Upstream main still pins `tiff` 0.11.3, `zune-jpeg` 0.5.15 and `image` 0.25.10 with the `tiff` feature, and WordCraft still accepts and decodes TIFF.

## Evidence

In `tiff` 0.11.3, `src/decoder/image.rs:585-601` (its default `jpeg` feature is enabled via `image`) decodes each JPEG-compressed strip with a fresh decoder:

```rust
let mut decoder =
    zune_jpeg::JpegDecoder::new(zune_core::bytestream::ZCursor::new(jpeg_data));
let mut options: zune_core::options::DecoderOptions = Default::default();
...
let data = decoder.decode()?;
```

Two things leave this unbounded:
- `DecoderOptions::default()` in zune-core 0.5.3 is `max_width = max_height = 16384` with no memory limit.
- The strip's embedded JPEG dimensions are never compared with the TIFF's declared strip size.

So a TIFF that declares a tiny image can still make each strip allocate up to 16384 x 16384 x components bytes of output. A progressive strip adds coefficient buffers on top (see N-35). `image`'s `Limits` (including the `decode_fits` header budget added for #1321) only see the declared TIFF size.

WordCraft reaches it from:
- `insert.picture`, which accepts TIFF on a header-size check alone. [engine/src/cmd/insert.rs#L230-L242](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs#L230-L242) maps `II*\0`/`MM\0*` to `"tiff"`.
- Every decode that guesses the format from the bytes:
  - PDF export: [pdf/src/lib.rs#L1893-L1906](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/pdf/src/lib.rs#L1893-L1906)
  - rend…

title: [N-37] `picture.corrections` with a subnormal `sharpen` panics inside `image::blur` (aborts the tab on wasm)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, findings N-37) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Medium (panic; process-fatal on wasm). **Status:** Confirmed by reproduction at eae2421 (debug build). The same logic is still present at upstream main, and `image` is still 0.25.10.

## Evidence

[crates/engine/src/cmd/objects.rs#L114-L140](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/objects.rs#L114-L140):

```rust
let sharpen = p::f32(v, "sharpen").unwrap_or(0.0).clamp(-100.0, 100.0);
...
} else if sharpen < 0.0 {
    img = img.blur(-sharpen / 25.0);
}
```

- `p::f32` ([engine/src/lib.rs#L150-L152](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/lib.rs#L150-L152)) only filters out non-finite values, so a subnormal such as `-1e-40` gets through. Any value whose `-sharpen / 25.0` is subnormal or underflows does too.
- `image` 0.25.10 `DynamicImage::blur` (`src/images/dynimage.rs:980-985`) remaps only an exact `0.0`.
- `GaussianBlurParameters::new_from_sigma` (`src/imageops/sample.rs:1199-1203`) then runs `assert!(sigma.is_normal(), "Sigma cannot be NaN, Infinities, subnormal or zero")`.

**Repro (eae2421):** `insert.picture`, then `picture.corrections {"sharpen": -1e-40}`. Result: `panicked at ...imageops/sample.rs:1199:9`.

## Conditions and impact

Any caller of the command can trigger it: an MCP or control-channel client, a CLI `--cmd`, or a front end passing through a computed value.
- **Native:** `Session::run` catches the panic and restores the document, so the result is an error.
- **wasm32:** panics abort, so the tab dies and unsaved work is lost.

This breaks the project's "no panics reachable from params" rule. `hostile_params_never_panic` ([engine/src/tests.rs#L3345-L3369](…

title: [N-38] Picture edits decode before the size check, and Remove Background / the Shadow style scale badly with picture size
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, findings N-38) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Medium (memory exhaustion and long UI stalls). **Status:** Confirmed by measurement at eae2421. The numbers below come from the audit run at eae2421 on a debug build. All three code paths still have the same logic at upstream main.

Related: #3644 (N-35) (the same `load_from_memory` call also misses progressive-JPEG coefficient memory).

## Evidence

**1. The size check runs after decoding.** `adjust_media` ([crates/engine/src/cmd/objects.rs#L1193-L1198](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/objects.rs#L1193-L1198)), which every Picture Format adjustment uses:

```rust
let img = image::load_from_memory(&bytes).map_err(...)?;
if (img.width() as u64) * (img.height() as u64) > 80_000_000 {
    return Err(CmdError::Failed("picture is too large to edit".into()));
}
```

The decode has no dimension limit (only `image`'s default 512 MiB output cap), and the 80 MP refusal only happens after the full decode.

**2. The Remove Background flood-fill stack is O(w*h).** In [objects.rs#L1356-L1401](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/objects.rs#L1356-L1401), every matching pixel pushes four neighbours before checking `seen`, so the stack can hold several entries per pixel on top of the RGBA copy and the `seen` vector.

**3. The Shadow style.** [objects.rs#L1410-L1448](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/objects.rs#L1410-L1448) makes several full RGBA buffers (`out`, `shadow`, `padded`, `blurred`, plus `img.to_rgba8()` twice). It then runs a Gaussian blur with `sigma = max(w, h) / 80`, so the kernel grows wit…

author: PierrunoYT

title: [N-40] Insert/Update Index is quadratic in `XE ... \r bookmark` entries
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, findings N-40) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Medium (UI hang). **Status:** Confirmed by measurement at eae2421 (the timings are from the audit run on a debug build). The code is unchanged at upstream main.

## Evidence

`collect` in [crates/engine/src/cmd/index.rs#L179-L237](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/index.rs#L179-L237) builds a closure that rescans the whole body for each lookup:

```rust
let bookmark_end = |name: &str| {
    s.doc.para_paths(StoryRef::Body).into_iter().find_map(|path| {
        let p = s.doc.para(StoryRef::Body, &path)?;
        let off = p.object_offsets().into_iter().find(|o| matches!(p.object_at(*o),
            Some(InlineObject::BookmarkEnd { name: n }) if n == name))?;
        ...
```

It calls that closure once per `XE` mark that has a `\r` switch, after a linear `starts.iter().find` over every bookmark:

```rust
let range = f.arg('r').and_then(|bm| {
    let a = starts.iter().find(|(n, _)| n == bm).map(|(_, p)| page(p))?;
    let b = bookmark_end(bm).map(|p| page(&p)).unwrap_or(a);
```

So N such marks over a body with N bookmarks cost O(N x body), with `para_paths` re-collected and every paragraph's objects re-enumerated each time. `references.index` and `references.updateIndex` both go through `collect`.

## Conditions and impact

| `XE \r` entries | File size | Time |
|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 4 KB | 0.4 s |
| 2,000 | 7 KB | 1.2 s |
| 4,000 | 12 KB | 4.8 s |
| 8,000 | 23 KB | 20 s |

The time quadruples per doubling, so a 50 KB document should already freeze the UI for minutes. Commands run synchronously on the UI thread, so Insert Index or Update Index on a hostile (or just large, heavily indexed) document blocks the app.

title: [N-42] The table-formula work budget is per field and counts cells, not bytes, so Update Fields can still hang
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, findings N-42) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Medium (UI hang). **Status:** Confirmed by measured scaling at eae2421. The per-field and per-read timings below come from the audit run on a debug build. The totals are extrapolated from them, not measured end to end. The file has had unrelated changes since then, but the budget logic is the same at upstream main.

## Evidence

`MAX_CELL_VISITS = 100_000` bounds one evaluation. Each `evaluate_with` call starts a fresh counter ([crates/engine/src/cmd/table_formula.rs#L22-L53](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/table_formula.rs#L22-L53)):

```rust
let here = Here { t, doc, default_lang, r, c, g: t.grid_col(r, c), visits: std::cell::Cell::new(0) };
```

Each visit costs as much as the cell is large ([#L493-L527](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/table_formula.rs#L493-L527)):

- `cell_number` then rebuilds the whole cell text with `table::cell_text(c)` before `parse_number`.

`update_fields_in` evaluates every `=` field in the document, one after another, each with its own budget ([crates/engine/src/cmd/references.rs#L979-L993](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/references.rs#L979-L993)). `fields.setCode`, `insert.field` and the table formula command ([table.rs#L978](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs#L978)) reach the same evaluator.

title: [N-43] Word 2003 XML export inlines a shared header, footnote or comment once per reference (5.8 KB docx to 239 MB)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, findings N-43) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Medium (out-of-memory on export). **Status:** Confirmed by reproduction at eae2421. The sizes come from the audit run at eae2421 on a debug build. The code is unchanged at upstream main.

## Evidence

`crates/docx/src/wordml2003_write.rs` moves OOXML's separate stories back inline, as WordprocessingML 2003 requires.

- **Headers and footers.** `section` ([#L440-L472](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/wordml2003_write.rs#L440-L472)) re-reads and re-converts the referenced part for every `w:sectPr`, even when every section points at the same header:

```rust
let Some(path) = k.attr("r:id").and_then(|id| rels.by_id(id))...;
let Some(root) = self.pkg.xml(&path).ok().flatten() else { continue };
self.stories += 1;
...
let kids = self.kids(&root, &story_rels, name, depth + 1);
```

- **Notes.** `note` ([#L363-L378](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/wordml2003_write.rs#L363-L378)) converts the whole note again at every `w:footnoteReference` / `w:endnoteReference` with the same id.
- **Comments.** `comment` ([#L387-L410](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/wordml2003_write.rs#L387-L410)) does the same at every `w:commentReference`.

The only bound is `MAX_STORIES = 50_000` ([#L40](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/wordml2003_write.rs#L40)). That caps how many times a story is inlined, not how many bytes the inlining produces.

title: [N-48] Russian hyphenation is quadratic in word length (`out.contains(&cut)` per syllable)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, findings N-48) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Medium (layout hang). **Status:** Confirmed by measurement at eae2421; the code is unchanged at `00bc6a4b`. Timings come from the audit run at eae2421 on a debug build.

Related: #3412 (the separate quadratic long-word scan in `break_lines`; this one is on top of it, in the Russian hyphenator).

## Evidence

[`crates/proof/src/ru/hyphen.rs#L60-L62`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/proof/src/ru/hyphen.rs#L60-L62):

```rust
if cut >= 2 && n - cut >= 2 && !out.contains(&cut) {
    out.push(cut);
}
```

`points` runs once per pair of neighbouring vowels. `out.contains` is a linear scan of the cuts found so far, so a word with V vowels costs O(V²).

The rest of `hyphen_points_in` was already made linear (see `hyphenating_a_long_word_is_linear`, [`hyphen.rs#L686`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/proof/src/hyphen.rs#L686-L686)). author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, findings N-53) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

title: [N-55] Font dialog: typing "NaN" as the size gives a NaN preview font size (clamp keeps NaN), tripping epaint's debug assertion
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md, findings N-55) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (debug-build panic; release builds probably draw an empty or broken preview). **Status:** Found by code reading. This was not run. The line is unchanged at `00bc6a4b` (it moved from `dialogs.rs:1544` to `:1787`), and the pinned epaint is 0.36.2.

## Evidence

[`crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs#L1787-L1790`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs#L1787-L1790):

```rust
let preview_size = size.trim().parse::<f32>().unwrap_or(12.0).clamp(6.0, 72.0);
...
font_id: egui::FontId::new(preview_size, egui::FontFamily::Proportional),
```

Rust's `f32::from_str` accepts `"NaN"` (any case), `"inf"` and `"infinity"`:
- `"NaN"` parses to `Ok(NaN)`, so `unwrap_or` does not replace it;
- `f32::clamp` returns NaN when its input is NaN;
- infinities clamp to 6 or 72, which is fine.

The NaN size goes into the preview `FontId`. When epaint 0.36.2 builds a glyph cache key for that text, it checks the scale with `debug_assert!(0.0 < px_scale_factor && px_scale_factor.is_finite(), ...)` (`epaint/src/text/font.rs`, `GlyphCacheKey::new`). A NaN font size gives a NaN scale, so the assertion fails.

## Conditions and impact

- Open Home › Font (the Font dialog), type `NaN` in the Size box, and let the preview redraw.
- In a debug build: a panic inside the egui frame. The last-resort guard (`Session::run`) covers commands, not UI painting, so the panic ends the app. Only AutoRecover then limits what is lost.
- In a release build: the assertion is compiled out. The preview probably renders nothing or garbage. NaN layout sizes can also spread into the dialog's measurement code.
- The size the dialog applies on OK goes through the command layer's own vali…

title: [WC-22] Two path-read helpers still bypass the bounded regular-file reader
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (residual of WC-22; the original `/dev/zero` and FIFO cases for `file.open` and `insert.picture` are fixed)
Related: #1333, #1690 (both closed)

**Evidence.** `read_document` uses `read_regular_file`, which re-checks the opened handle and bounds the read. Two helpers do not:

- `read_file_capped` checks `metadata(path).is_file()` and the length, then calls `std::fs::read(path)` on the path again ([engine/src/io.rs#L566-L576](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/io.rs#L566-L576)). It is behind `read_file` (pictures, mail-merge data, up to 2 GB), fonts and citation source files. A file swapped or grown after the check is read whole.
- `read_file_head` opens the path with no file-type check ([#L581-L587](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/io.rs#L581-L587)). It runs on save to an `.xml` path (`is_word_2003_file`, [cmd/file.rs#L339-L343](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L339-L343)), so `file.saveAs {"path":"/tmp/fifo.xml"}` blocks in `File::open` until a writer appears.

**Impact.** An agent-supplied path can still hang the MCP server or UI thread (FIFO on save), or read past the size cap (race or growing file).

**Suggested fix.** Implement both helpers on top of `read_regular_file` (open once, check the handle, `take(limit + 1)`). Test: `read_file_head` and `read_file_capped` on a FIFO return an error without blocking.

title: [WC-32] Zotero session keeps every call's method name and error with no cap
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (local denial of service; needs a process on the Zotero port)
Related: #1332 (closed; this code is unchanged since)

**Evidence.** The transport caps one frame at 32 MiB (`MAX_FRAME`, [zotero/src/wire.rs#L15](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/zotero/src/wire.rs#L15)) but not the session. `serve` loops over calls with no call count or byte budget and pushes every error ([zotero/src/client.rs#L99-L128](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/zotero/src/client.rs#L99-L128)):

```rust
out.errors.push(e.clone());
```

The UI keeps each call's method name, whose length is not checked by `Call::parse`, until the session ends ([ui-egui/src/zotero.rs#L166-L170](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/ui-egui/src/zotero.rs#L166-L170)). Each read waits up to an hour (`idle_timeout`, [client.rs#L72](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/zotero/src/client.rs#L72)), and there is no Cancel.

**Impact.** A fake Zotero server can keep the session open and send unknown methods with multi-MiB names. The audit measured about 330 MB retained after 40 calls with 8 MiB names, all parsed on the UI thread.

**Suggested fix.** Cap calls and total bytes per session, truncate stored method names and errors (or keep only counts and the last few), cap the method-name length in `Call::parse`, and offer Cancel. Test: a fake peer sending N oversized calls ends the session with bounded memory.

title: [Audit minor] Page Borders: with the caret in a header, the border goes to the wrong section
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (wrong section changed)

**Evidence.** `design.pageBorders` picks the section from the first index of the caret's path, whatever story the caret is in ([engine/src/cmd/design.rs#L230-L237](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/design.rs#L230-L237)):

```rust
Some("section") | None => vec![s.sel.focus.path.0.first().copied().unwrap_or(0) as usize],
```

In a header, footer, footnote or comment, that index counts blocks of that story, not of the body. The layout commands already map the caret to its section story-aware with `section_index_of_focus` ([cmd/page.rs#L243-L247](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/page.rs#L243-L247)).

**Impact.** With the caret in the header of section 3, Page Borders (applyTo section) changes whichever section holds body block 0 or 1, usually section 1, and leaves section 3 alone.

**Suggested fix.** Use the section-end block of `section_index_of_focus(s)` (as `selected_section_ends` does in `page.rs`). Test: a two-section document, caret in section 2's header, `design.pageBorders {}` changes section 2 only.

title: [Audit minor] Index: an INDEX field inside a table cell or text box is not found, so Insert Index adds a second one
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (duplicate index, index never updated)

**Evidence.** `index_field` only looks at top-level body paragraphs ([engine/src/cmd/index.rs#L128-L136](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/index.rs#L128-L136)):

```rust
s.doc.body.iter().enumerate().find_map(|(i, b)| {
    b.as_para()?.objects.iter().find_map(|o| match o {
```

`update_generated`, which Update Index and Update Fields use, walks `s.doc.body` the same way ([cmd/citations.rs#L914-L924](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/citations.rs#L914-L924)).

**Impact.** An INDEX field in a table cell (common in imported layouts), a text box or a header is never rebuilt, and `references.index` inserts a second index at the caret instead of changing the existing one.

title: [Audit minor] Style Inspector: clearing formatting silently drops pending formatting revisions
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (tracked changes lost without Accept or Reject)

**Evidence.** `styles.inspectorClear` rebuilds the properties from defaults ([engine/src/cmd/inspector.rs#L123-L141](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/inspector.rs#L123-L141)):

```rust
*p = ParaProps { style: p.style.clone(), numbering: p.numbering, ..Default::default() };
```

This discards `ParaProps::num_change` and `fmt_change`, the records of tracked numbering and paragraph-formatting changes. The `characterFormatting` level keeps `ins`, `del`, `lang` and `rtl` but not `CharProps::fmt_change`.

**Impact.** A pending formatting revision vanishes from Review and from the saved file, without being accepted or rejected, and with Track Changes off there is no new revision either.

**Suggested fix.** Carry `num_change` and `fmt_change` through both clear levels, as `ins`/`del` are already carried. Test: a paragraph with a tracked formatting change keeps its revision after `styles.inspectorClear {"level":"paragraphFormatting"}`.

title: [Audit minor] docx writer: text-frame (`w:framePr`) enumerations from a .json document are written unvalidated
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (saved .docx can be schema-invalid)

**Evidence.** The docx reader keeps only allowed values for a frame's wrap, anchors and alignments ([docx/src/read/props.rs#L21-L38](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/read/props.rs#L21-L38)). The writer emits whatever the model holds ([docx/src/write/props.rs#L268-L296](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/write/props.rs#L268-L296)):

```rust
a.push(("w:wrap", &f.wrap));
a.push(("w:vAnchor", &f.v_anchor));
a.push(("w:hAnchor", &f.h_anchor));
```

`TextFrame` keeps them as free `String`s with serde defaults ([doc/src/props.rs#L849-L870](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/doc/src/props.rs#L849-L870)), so a `.json` document with `"frame": {}` gives `w:wrap=""`, and `"wrap": "x"` gives `w:wrap="x"`. `.json` open does not normalise them.

**Impact.** `ST_Wrap`, `ST_VAnchor`, `ST_HAnchor`, `ST_XAlign` and `ST_YAlign` are closed enumerations. A file with an empty or unknown value can make Word report the document as damaged.

**Suggested fix.** Validate on write (fall back to `auto` / `page` / no alignment, as the reader does), or make these fields enums. Test: a `.json` document with an empty `frame` saves a `w:framePr` whose values are all in the allowed sets.

title: [Audit minor] Drawing ids: one shape with id 4294967295 makes every new drawing id collide
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (duplicate ids in saved files; connectors can glue to the wrong shape)

**Evidence.** The reader keeps a file's `wp:docPr id` as the shape's id ([docx/src/read/story.rs#L1572-L1579](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/read/story.rs#L1572-L1579)). The next free id saturates instead of looking for a gap ([doc/src/lib.rs#L1342-L1361](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/doc/src/lib.rs#L1342-L1361)):

```rust
max.saturating_add(1).max(1)
```

With a shape at `u32::MAX`, `next_shape_id()` is `u32::MAX` again. `connectors::ensure_id` gives that id to every shape it glues ([engine/src/cmd/connectors.rs#L169-L177](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/connectors.rs#L169-L177)), and the writer's fresh `docPr` ids also stay at `u32::MAX` (`next_docpr`, [docx/src/write/mod.rs#L626-L629](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/write/mod.rs#L626-L629), starting from `next_shape_id() - 1` at [#L159](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/write/mod.rs#L159)).

**Impact.** A crafted (or merely unusual) `.docx` makes later connectors attach to whichever shape is found first with that id, and the saved file has many drawings with the same `docPr` id, which other consumers may reject or repair.

**Suggested fix.** When the maximum is `u32::MAX`, search for the lowest unused id (or renumber on open). Test: a document with a shape at `u32::MAX` plus two new shapes glued by connectors gives three distinct ids and distinct `doc…

title: [Audit minor] PDF export: a glyph id above 65535 reaches an `unwrap()` in krilla (aborts the tab on wasm)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (Plausible: needs a font whose cmap maps to a glyph id above 65535; not reproduced)

**Evidence.** Shaping returns 32-bit glyph ids: harfrust's `glyph_id`, and the skrifa charmap fallback's `g.to_u32()` ([fonts/src/lib.rs#L218-L237](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/fonts/src/lib.rs#L218-L237)). A format-12 cmap can map a character to any 32-bit id. PDF export passes them on unchecked as `GlyphId::new(g.gid)` ([pdf/src/lib.rs#L1484](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/pdf/src/lib.rs#L1484), [#L1710](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/pdf/src/lib.rs#L1710), [#L1760](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/pdf/src/lib.rs#L1760)). The pinned krilla (craft-libs `c3487320`) then does, in `vendor/krilla/src/text/cid.rs` line 161:

```rust
.remap(u16::try_from(glyph_id.to_u32()).unwrap());
```

Natively, `write::guard` catches the panic and the export fails. On wasm32 (`panic = "abort"`) the tab is lost with any unsaved work.

**Suggested fix.** Drop or replace (with .notdef) glyph ids above `u16::MAX` before building `KrillaGlyph`s, and report it upstream in craft-libs. Test: a glyph run with gid 70000 exports without panicking.

title: [Audit minor] Italian grammar: the capital-at-sentence-start rule never fires after the first sentence
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (missing grammar marks)

**Evidence.** `sentence_capitals` passes the whole rest of the paragraph to `ends_sentence` instead of the gap between two words ([proof/src/it/grammar.rs#L211-L221](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/proof/src/it/grammar.rs#L211-L221)):

```rust
after_end = ends_sentence(text.get(*b..).unwrap_or(""), w);
```

`ends_sentence` returns true only when what follows the full stop is whitespace and quotes or brackets ([#L152-L163](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/proof/src/it/grammar.rs#L152-L163)). With the next words included, that is false everywhere except at the paragraph's end. Portuguese, Polish, Croatian and Russian pass the gap `text.get(pb..a)` ([pt/grammar.rs#L133-L145](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/proof/src/pt/grammar.rs#L133-L145)).

**Impact.** "Vado a Roma. oggi piove." gets no "Maiuscola a inizio frase" mark on `oggi`. Only the paragraph's first word is checked.

**Suggested fix.** Pass the gap between the previous word and the current one, as the other languages do. Test: `check("Vado a Roma. oggi piove.")` reports the capital rule on `oggi`, and `"Il dott. rossi"` still doesn't.

title: [Audit minor] Page parameters: `max(1) as usize - 1` underflows on 32-bit and wasm
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (debug panic or wrong page on 32-bit targets only)

**Evidence.** Three page parameters are cast from `u64` to `usize` before the subtraction:

- `ui.render` / `render.page` in MCP, outside `Session::run`'s guard ([mcp/src/lib.rs#L49](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/mcp/src/lib.rs#L49));
- `file.exportPng` ([engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L371](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L371));
- `edit.goto` ([engine/src/cmd/edit.rs#L738](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs#L738)).

```rust
let page = p::u64(v, "page").unwrap_or(1).max(1) as usize - 1;
```

On wasm32 or i686, `{"page": 4294967296}` truncates to 0 and `0 - 1` panics in debug builds (wraps in release); `4294967297` silently selects page 1.

**Suggested fix.** `usize::try_from(p.max(1)).unwrap_or(usize::MAX).saturating_sub(1)` at all three sites. Test: each command with `page` = 2^32 returns an error or the last page, never page 1.

title: [Audit minor] Comment commands truncate `id` with `as u32`, so a large id acts on another comment
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (wrong comment deleted, replied to or resolved)
Related: #1690 (reported this among five defects; closed, the code is unchanged)

**Evidence.** Three comment commands cast the `u64` parameter ([engine/src/cmd/review.rs#L24](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs#L24), [#L165](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs#L165), [#L292](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs#L292)):

```rust
let id = p::u64(v, "id").map(|x| x as u32).or_else(|| comment_at_caret(s)) ...
```

**Impact.** `{"id": 4294967296}` from MCP, the control channel or the CLI targets comment 0 instead of failing; `4294967301` targets comment 5. `review.deleteComment` then deletes the wrong comment.

**Suggested fix.** `p::u64(v, "id").and_then(|x| u32::try_from(x).ok())`, as `review.editComment` already does, and return a params error when it doesn't fit. Test: each of the three commands with `id + 2^32` errors and leaves the comment unchanged.

title: [Audit minor] .json open doesn't reconcile inline objects with their U+FFFC markers
author: PierrunoYT

title: [Audit minor] Group: grouping more than 1,000 objects silently loses the rest
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (objects lost on save and on Ungroup)

**Evidence.** `arrange.group` builds the group's children from every picked object with no count check ([engine/src/cmd/objects.rs#L1512-L1585](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/objects.rs#L1512-L1585)). Everything that reads a group stops at `MAX_GROUP_CHILDREN` (1,000):

- drawing and Ungroup go through `group_rects` ([doc/src/para.rs#L754-L755](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/doc/src/para.rs#L754-L755)): `children.iter().take(MAX_GROUP_CHILDREN)`;
- the docx writer ([docx/src/write/story.rs#L752](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/write/story.rs#L752)).

The drawing-canvas command already refuses past the cap ([cmd/canvas.rs#L79](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/canvas.rs#L79)).

**Impact.** Selecting 1,001 or more floating objects (or nesting groups) and grouping them shows 1,000; saving or ungrouping drops the others for good.

**Suggested fix.** Refuse `arrange.group` when the flattened member count exceeds `MAX_GROUP_CHILDREN`, with a clear message. Test: grouping 1,001 shapes is refused and the document is unchanged.

title: [Audit minor] Read Aloud: `tidy()` is quadratic on nested brackets, and sentences without spaces are never split
author: PierrunoYT

title: [Audit minor] Mail merge Rules: IF / SKIPIF text is put into the field code without escaping quotes
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (broken field from ordinary text; no privilege gain)

**Evidence.** `mailings.rules` interpolates `value`, `then` and `else` between double quotes as they are ([engine/src/cmd/mailings.rs#L405-L421](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/mailings.rs#L405-L421)):

```rust
"IF" => format!(
    "IF {{ MERGEFIELD {} }} = \"{}\" \"{}\" \"{}\"",
    quote(p::str(v, "field").unwrap_or("Field")),
    p::str(v, "value").unwrap_or(""),
    p::str(v, "then").unwrap_or(""),
```

Only the field name goes through `quote`. SKIPIF and NEXTIF interpolate `value` the same way.

**Impact.** `"then": "Dear \"friend\""` or a value containing `"` ends the argument early, so the IF compares or prints the wrong text and the merge result is wrong.

**Suggested fix.** Escape `"` and `\` in the three arguments as field-code text (`\"`, `\\`) and make sure `FieldCode::parse` reads them back. Test: a rule whose `then` holds quotes round-trips through `FieldCode::parse` with the same text.

title: [Audit minor] settings.xml merge: a `>` inside an attribute value makes the scan fail, and the kept settings are dropped on save
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (silent loss of round-tripped settings)

**Evidence.** `children` finds the end of each tag with the next `>`, without skipping quoted attribute values ([docx/src/write/settings_merge.rs#L185](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/write/settings_merge.rs#L185), in `children` at [#L158-L212](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/write/settings_merge.rs#L158-L212)):

```rust
let gt = at + tail.find('>')? + 1;
```

`>` is legal unescaped in an XML attribute value. For `<w:docVar w:name="a" w:val="x>y"/>`, the tag ends early, does not end in `/>`, and is counted as an open element, so the depth never returns to 0 and `children` gives `None`. `has_unowned` then reports nothing to keep, and `merge` falls back to the generated part.

**Impact.** Every setting WordCraft doesn't model (document variables, compatibility options, rsids, schema references) is dropped from `settings.xml` on save, with no warning.

**Suggested fix.** Skip over `"..."` and `'...'` when looking for the tag's `>` (or scan with the XML reader). Test: a settings part with a `>` in a `w:docVar` value keeps that `w:docVar` after a save.

title: [Audit minor] VML path parser builds one command entry per letter before any cap applies
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (memory amplification on .docx open)

**Evidence.** `vml_commands` reads up to `MAX_VML_PATH` (1 Mi) characters and pushes a `(String, Vec<f64>)` for every command letter ([docx/src/read/freeform.rs#L243-L272](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/read/freeform.rs#L243-L272)):

```rust
out.push((cmd, Vec::new()));
```

Only the parameter count is capped (`MAX_VML_PARAMS`). The point and path caps (`d.full()`) apply afterwards, while `vml_path` iterates the finished list ([#L130-L133](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/read/freeform.rs#L130-L133)).

**Impact.** A `path` attribute of 1 MiB of letters (for example `xxxx...`) allocates about a million small Strings and Vecs, tens of MB for a single shape, and the work repeats for every shape carrying such a path.

**Suggested fix.** Stream the commands into `Draw` (stop when `full()`), or cap the number of commands (for example at `MAX_VML_PARAMS`), and keep the command as a `&'static str` or small enum instead of a `String`. Test: a 1 MiB path of letters parses with bounded allocation.

title: [Audit minor] Web build: dropped files are read whole, with no size or count cap
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (tab out of memory on wasm32)
Related: #1333 (closed; paste and file-picker reads are now capped, drops are not)

**Evidence.** Every dropped file is read in full and queued, with no limit on its size or on how many are dropped ([apps/wordcraft-web/src/web.rs#L118-L131](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/apps/wordcraft-web/src/web.rs#L118-L131)):

```rust
for f in dropped {
    ...
    match f.bytes_async().await {
        Ok(bytes) => {
            inbox.lock()...push((name, bytes));
```

Pasted pictures are capped at 200 MB each and 20 per paste, and picked fonts by `MAX_PENDING_PICKED_BYTES` ([#L162-L266](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/apps/wordcraft-web/src/web.rs#L162-L266)); drops have neither.

**Impact.** Dropping a multi-GB file, or many files at once, exhausts the wasm32 heap (4 GiB) and aborts the tab, losing unsaved work.

**Suggested fix.** Check `size()` before reading (the same 2 GB document ceiling as native, or lower on web), cap the number of files per drop, and bound the bytes waiting in the inbox. Test: a drop over the cap is refused with a status message and nothing is read.

title: [Audit minor] MCP server: stdio requests and bridge replies are read as unbounded lines
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (memory exhaustion of the MCP process)
Related: #1331 (closed; these reads are unchanged), #2747

**Evidence.** The stdio loop uses `lines()` ([mcp/src/server.rs#L62](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/mcp/src/server.rs#L62)), and the `--connect` bridge reads the app's reply with `read_line` ([mcp/src/backend.rs#L152](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L152)):

```rust
let mut reply = String::new();
if reader.read_line(&mut reply)? == 0 {
```

The app's own control server bounds each line (`take(MAX_LINE + 1)`, [apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs#L145-L151](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs#L145-L151)).

**Impact.** A process holding the bridge port (the WC-03 loopback case) or a misbehaving client can send a line with no newline and grow the buffer until allocation fails, which aborts the MCP server.

**Suggested fix.** Read with `take(limit + 1)` and `read_until`, as `control_server::read_line` does; the reply limit has to allow large results (screenshots, `document.inspect`). Test: an over-long line gets an error reply and the server keeps serving.

title: [Audit minor] Control server: one thread per connection with no cap, created before authentication
author: PierrunoYT

title: [Audit minor] Fonts embedded in one document stay loaded and are used by every later document
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (cross-document font substitution; memory not released)
Related: #1171 (embedded fonts support, closed)

**Evidence.** On every open, the document's embedded fonts go into the process-global font database ([engine/src/io.rs#L174-L182](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/io.rs#L174-L182)):

```rust
wordcraft_fonts::FontDb::global().add_document_fonts(files);
```

`add_document_fonts` adds them "for this run" and nothing removes them when the document is closed or replaced ([fonts/src/fontdb/user.rs#L245-L259](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/fonts/src/fontdb/user.rs#L245-L259)). Faces are leaked deliberately (`FaceRef::of`, [fonts/src/fontdb.rs#L93-L118](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs#L93-L118)).

**Impact.** After opening document A that embeds a face named, say, "Corporate Sans", document B asking for that family (not installed) lays out, renders and exports to PDF with A's font, which can carry different glyphs for the same characters. Installed faces are not overridden. Each opened document's fonts also stay in memory until exit.

**Suggested fix.** Scope embedded faces to the document that brought them (a per-document overlay consulted before the global database), or at least drop a document's faces when no open document references them. Test: open A with an embedded family, then B using the same family name without embedding it: B falls back as if A had never been opened.

title: [Audit minor] Agile decryption: replaced spin-hash buffers and the AES key schedule are not wiped
author: PierrunoYT

title: [Audit minor] Legacy .doc RC4 decryption: the UTF-16 password and derived keys are not wiped
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (hygiene; password-equivalent data left in freed memory)

**Evidence.** The RC4 path passes a temporary UTF-16 copy of the password straight to MD5 and never clears it ([docbin/src/crypt.rs#L263-L275](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docbin/src/crypt.rs#L263-L275)):

```rust
let h0 = md5(&utf16le(password));
...
let base = md5(&buf)[..5].to_vec();
```

The CryptoAPI path does clear its copy (`pw.fill(0)`, [#L335-L337](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docbin/src/crypt.rs#L335-L337)). In both paths, `h0`, the 336-byte `buf` built from it, the derived `base` kept in `Cipher::Rc4` for the whole read, and each per-block key from `block_key` are plain `Vec`s or arrays that are dropped without clearing.

**Suggested fix.** Hold the UTF-16 password, `h0`, `buf`, `base` and the block keys in `Zeroizing` (as `docx/src/crypt.rs` does for agile encryption), and clear the RC4 state on drop. Test: a unit test that both paths still decrypt the existing fixtures.

title: [Audit minor] .doc reader: bookmark names longer than 40 characters desync the bookmark table
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (wrong or missing bookmark names on .doc open)
Related: #2744 (listed in the WC-40 checklist, not filed on its own)

**Evidence.** `sttb_strings` clamps each string's length but then advances by the clamped length, not by the stored one ([docbin/src/notes.rs#L104-L115](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docbin/src/notes.rs#L104-L115)):

```rust
let cch = cch.min(40);
let chars = b.get(at..at + cch * 2)?;
at += cch * 2;
```

For a name of 41 or more UTF-16 units, the rest of that name is read as the next entry's length and text. The function also assumes the extended (UTF-16) form and ignores `cbExtra` from the header ([#L93-L103](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docbin/src/notes.rs#L93-L103)), so a table with extra data per entry is misread too.

**Impact.** Every bookmark after a long name gets a garbage name or is lost, and REF / PAGEREF fields pointing at them break.

**Suggested fix.** Advance by the stored `cch` (truncate only the kept text), honour `fExtend` (0xFFFF) and skip `cbExtra` bytes after each string. Test: an SttbfBkmk with a 50-character name followed by a short one reads both names.

title: [Audit minor] docx writer re-emits part names from the input file without OPC part-name validation
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Reported from a read-only security and robustness audit (AUDIT.md) of WordCraft at eae2421, re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) before filing.

**Severity:** Low (hardening; a hazard for other tools that extract the saved file; traced in code, not reproduced end to end)
Related: #2744 (listed in the WC-40 checklist, not filed on its own)

**Evidence.** Part names are taken from the zip entry names as they are, only stripped of a leading `/` ([docx/src/package.rs#L219](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/package.rs#L219)). Kept parts (embedded objects, custom XML, unmodelled parts) are written back under their original name when it is free ([docx/src/write/embed.rs#L123-L130](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/write/embed.rs#L123-L130)):

```rust
if !Self::reserved(&lower) && self.taken.insert(lower) {
    return orig.to_string();
}
```

`resolve` normalises `..` segments split on `/`, but a backslash is not a separator there, so `word/..\..\x.bin` stays one segment and is written to the saved zip unchanged.

**Impact.** A saved `.docx` can carry entries named like `word/..\..\x`, which extractors that treat `\` as a separator (some Windows tools) may write outside their target folder. WordCraft itself never extracts to disk.

**Suggested fix.** Validate kept part names against the OPC part-name rules (ECMA-376 Part 2: no backslash, no empty or dot segments, no percent-encoded separators) and rename or drop the others on write. Test: a package with a part named `word/a\b.bin` saves it under a valid name.

title: Security and robustness audit follow-up: finding tracker (N-01 to N-56, re-filed WC-01 to WC-40 and 2026-10-13 audit, minor)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Tracker for the second security and robustness audit of WordCraft (AUDIT.md). The audit was run read-only at [`eae2421`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/eae242176108d328c5dd81fbc10370c51ab90706). Every finding below was re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d) and against existing issues before filing. Findings that are fixed upstream or already tracked were not refiled (see the end of this list). Each report covers one problem; this issue only links them.

The audit found no first-party `unsafe`, no memory-safety defect and no code execution. Most reports are availability bugs: small inputs that abort the process on allocation or hang the UI thread, crash paths outside `Session::run`'s guard, and writer/reader mismatches that produce files WordCraft can't reopen. Security-relevant reports describe the defect class, preconditions and fix without exploit walk-throughs.

## High

- [ ] **N-01**: #3611: Picture Styles / Picture Border size the output image from the input with no cap: a 39 KB PNG makes the process abort
- [ ] **N-02**: #3612: Object drag preview can create a texture larger than the GPU limit, and wgpu panics outside the command guard
- [ ] **N-04**: #3614: Paragraph::object_at rescans the paragraph on every call, so object loops are quadratic and a 24 KB .docx hangs on open
- [ ] **N-33**: #3642: A hostile CFB header makes `cfb` build a multi-GiB FAT before validating it (reached by the encryption sniff)
- [ ] **N-34**: #3643: A ragged equation matrix is padded to rows x max-cols on save, so `document.xml` grows quadratically

## Medium

- [ ] **N-03**: #3613: Hunspell continuation classes make each spell check O(rules²) on the UI thread; a hostile .aff hangs every launch
- [ ] **N-05**: #3615: Style and numbering lookups are linear scans repeated per paragraph and per run: a 61 KB .docx takes 35 s to open
- [ ] **N-06**: #3616: Select Recipients h…

title: [Feature Request] Ctrl + Shft + Backspace to delete last sentence
author: Atlas-Karalis
body: As a Linux user I've been using LibreOffice for my document writing and one feature I've gotten used to is **Control + Shift + backspace** to delete the entire last sentence. I understand that Wordcraft is primarily intended to offer feature parity with Microsoft Word, and this particular feature is not one it offers, however I think it's worth mentioning to the devs.

title: [WC-01a] Headless `wordcraft-cli mcp` gives agents unconfined file access unless roots are passed
author: PierrunoYT

title: [WC-01b] The desktop app's control channel (`wordcraft --control`, `mcp --connect`) cannot confine file access
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-01), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #2745 (and its duplicate #2779) (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** High (audit, as part of WC-01). **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b` (documented limitation; confirmed in code).

Related: #769, #3582, #3635.

## Evidence

The CLI refuses roots together with `--connect`, because the app on the other end would not apply them:
[`apps/wordcraft-cli/src/main.rs#L570-L576`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/apps/wordcraft-cli/src/main.rs#L570-L576)
```rust
let connect = arg_value(&rest, "--connect");
if roots.is_some() && connect.is_some() {
    return Err(
        "mcp: --automation-read-root and --automation-write-root confine the headless server; a running app is not confined by them"
```
The docs confirm it: "WordCraft's desktop app has no equivalent flags yet, so a running app (`wordcraft --control`) is not confined" ([`docs/mcp.md#L87-L89`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/docs/mcp.md#L87-L89)).

`engine::file_access` is not used anywhere in `apps/wordcraft/src` or `crates/ui-egui/src` (`git grep file_access upstream/main -- apps/wordcraft/src crates/ui-egui/src` returns nothing). So commands arriving over the control server ([`apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs#L40`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs#L40)) run with the same unconfined `check_read`/`check_write` as the person at the keyboard ([`crates/engine/src/file_access.rs#L183-L191`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/file_access.rs#L183-L191)).

title: [WC-01c] `file.exportPng` writes PNG bytes to any path, with no `.png` extension check
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-01), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #2745 (and its duplicate #2779) (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Medium on its own (part of the High WC-01 in the audit: it is the one automation write that is not limited to document extensions). **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`.

Related: #3635 (`ui.screenshot {path}` has the same any-path write, through plain `fs::write`).

## Evidence

[`crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L365-L383`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L365-L383)
```rust
fn export_png(s: &mut Session, v: &Value) -> CmdResult {
    let Some(path) = p::str(v, "path") else { … };
    …
    let png = img.to_png();
    crate::io::write_file(path, &png).map_err(CmdError::Failed)?;
```
`io::write_file` only applies `check_write` (unconfined by default) and then replaces the target atomically ([`crates/engine/src/io.rs#L677-L683`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/io.rs#L677-L683)). Nothing checks the extension. By contrast, `file.save` refuses unknown extensions (noted in the audit's re-verification), so this is the one export that can replace a file of any kind.

The command is registered as pure and callable from automation ([`file.rs#L106-L108`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L106-L108)).

## Conditions and impact

An agent steered by text in a document, or any caller of the control channel or MCP `execute`, can replace any file the user can write (configuration, scripts, notes) with PNG data. The content is a rendered page, not attacker-chosen text, so this destroys data rather than …

title: [WC-02a] Windows: the automation-root check opens a network path before rejecting it
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-02), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #2746 (and its duplicate #2780) (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Medium (audit). Windows only. **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b` (`file_access.rs` has not changed since eae2421). Confirmed in code; no live SMB test was run.

Related: #769, #3628 (fields that reach other machines).

## Evidence

`AutomationRoots::check` resolves the caller's path before it compares it with the root:
[`crates/engine/src/file_access.rs#L98`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/file_access.rs#L98)
```rust
if inside(&resolve(path)?, folder) {
```
`resolve` makes the raw path absolute, then calls `canonicalize` and `symlink_metadata` on it and on each parent:
[`crates/engine/src/file_access.rs#L203-L219`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/file_access.rs#L203-L219)
```rust
let absolute = std::path::absolute(path)…?;
…
loop {
    match std::fs::canonicalize(at) {
        …
        Err(e) => match std::fs::symlink_metadata(at) {
```
The only lexical filter before that is the reserved device-name check ([L199-L202](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/file_access.rs#L199-L202)). UNC, verbatim-UNC (`\\?\UNC\…`) and device-namespace prefixes are not rejected first.

## Conditions and impact

On Windows, `canonicalize` and `symlink_metadata` open the path. For a UNC path this makes the system contact the named host over SMB (or WebDAV), and it may send the signed-in user's NTLM challenge response automatically. A host that receives this can try to crack or relay it.

This happens while roots are in force, …

title: [WC-02b] Windows: `templates::is_network_path` misses NT-namespace (`\??\`) UNC paths in a document's attached template
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-02), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #2746 (and its duplicate #2780) (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Medium per the audit for WC-02; this variant has a narrow precondition (see below). Windows only. **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`. Confirmed in code. The audit checked that Rust std passes `\??\` paths through to `CreateFileW`, but ran no live SMB test.

Related: #3628.

## Evidence

The helper that keeps template paths from reaching another machine only looks at the first two characters:
[`crates/engine/src/cmd/templates.rs#L243-L246`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/templates.rs#L243-L246)
```rust
pub(crate) fn is_network_path(p: &str) -> bool {
    let b = p.as_bytes();
    matches!((b.first(), b.get(1)), (Some(b'\\' | b'/'), Some(b'\\' | b'/')))
}
```
A path in the NT object namespace starts with `\??\`. Its second character is `?`, so a `\??\UNC\…` path is not seen as remote. The test list at [L500-L509](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/templates.rs#L500-L509) covers the `\\`, `//`, `\\?\UNC\` and `file://host` forms, but not this one.

`local_path` relies on this check ([L228-L232](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/templates.rs#L228-L232)). `update_styles` falls back to the document's own `attached_template` when no `path` is given ([L91-L98](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/templates.rs#L91-L98)). The same helper also guards `user_templates.rs:92` and `options.rs:260`.

title: [WC-03] MCP bridge sends the control key to any loopback peer, while the app listens only on 127.0.0.1
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-03), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #2747 (and its duplicate #2781) (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Low (the audit's re-verification lowered it from Medium: it needs a multi-user host and a `--connect` address other than `127.0.0.1`). **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b` (`backend.rs` unchanged since eae2421).

Related: #3686 (control server connection handling).

## Evidence

The key may go to any loopback peer:
[`crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L73-L77`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L73-L77)
```rust
fn may_send_key(addr: &str, peer: Option<SocketAddr>) -> bool {
    is_loopback_addr(addr) && peer.is_some_and(|p| p.ip().to_canonical().is_loopback())
}
```
`reconnect` tries each address `--connect` resolves to and keeps the first that accepts ([L108-L126](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L108-L126)). `is_loopback_addr` accepts all of 127.0.0.0/8, `::1` and `localhost` ([L58-L71](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L58-L71)). The desktop app, however, binds only `127.0.0.1` ([`apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs#L40`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs#L40)). The unit test explicitly allows sending the key to `[::1]` for `localhost` and to `127.0.0.2` ([L260-L270](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L260-L270)).
