title: [WC-04] ODT import: `<text:s text:c>` is capped per tag but has no total budget (11.6 KB file to 1.2 GB)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-04), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #2748 (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** High (audit). **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`. Measurements are from the audit run at eae2421 on a debug build; the code path is unchanged.

## Evidence

[`crates/formats/src/odt.rs#L2062-L2065`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/formats/src/odt.rs#L2062-L2065)
```rust
"s" => {
    let n = get(a, "text:c").and_then(|v| v.trim().parse::<usize>().ok()).unwrap_or(1).clamp(1, 1000);
    self.push_text(&" ".repeat(n));
}
```
Each `<text:s>` adds up to 1,000 spaces, and nothing limits how many such tags a document may contain. `content.xml` may inflate to 256 MB ([`MAX_ENTRY`, L32](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/formats/src/odt.rs#L32)), and a run of identical tags compresses extremely well. `push_text` appends straight into the paragraph ([L1895-L1908](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/formats/src/odt.rs#L1895-L1908)). The `formats` crate has no document-wide character budget.

## Conditions and impact

Input shape: one paragraph holding a long run of `<text:s text:c="1000"/>` tags.

| tags | .odt size | result (audit, debug build) |
|---|---|---|
| 20,000 | 1.5 KB | 41 MB peak |
| 100,000 | 6.0 KB | 138 MB peak |
| 200,000 | 11.6 KB | 6.5 s, 1.21 GB peak |

That is about 100,000 times the file size, and growth is linear. A file of a few hundred KB extrapolates past available memory, and `to_doc` / text clean-up copy the text again. An allocation failure aborts the process, which the command guard's `catch_unwind` cannot catch. Opening the file loses unsaved work in…

title: [WC-05] Markdown import pads every table row to the header width before the row/column caps (33.6 KB to 2.28 GB)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-05), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #2749 (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** High (audit). **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`. Measurements are from the audit run at eae2421 on a debug build; the code path is unchanged.

Related: #3616 (the same pad-to-header pattern in Select Recipients).

## Evidence

[`crates/formats/src/markdown.rs#L508-L524`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/formats/src/markdown.rs#L508-L524)
```rust
let head = split_row(t);
if head.len() == aligns.len() {
    …
    while let Some(l) = lines.get(i) {
        …
        let mut cells = split_row(l);
        cells.resize(aligns.len(), String::new());
        table.rows.push(cells.iter().zip(&aligns).map(|(s, a)| cell(s, false, *a)).collect());
```
Every body row, even one that is just `|`, is padded to the header's column count, and each padded cell becomes a full `Cell { blocks: vec![FBlock::Para(..)] }` through `parse_inlines`. The table caps only apply later, in `model::Builder`, once every cell has been allocated:
[`crates/formats/src/model.rs#L733-L737`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/formats/src/model.rs#L733-L737)
```rust
let rows: Vec<&Vec<Cell>> = t.rows.iter().filter(|r| !r.is_empty()).take(wordcraft_doc::table::MAX_ROWS).collect();
…
let cols = t.cols().clamp(1, wordcraft_doc::table::MAX_COLS);
```

## Conditions and impact

Input shape: a header row and delimiter row with many columns, followed by many near-empty body rows. The cost is header columns times body rows, at about 350 bytes per padded cell.

| columns x rows | .md size | peak (audit, debug build) |
|---|---|---|
| 2000 x 200 | 8.6 KB | 155 MB |
| 4000 x…

title: [WC-06] docx XML reader has no per-element attribute cap (59 KB .docx to 611 MB)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-06), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #2750 (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** High (audit). **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`. Measurements are from the audit run at eae2421 on a debug build; the code path is unchanged.

## Evidence

[`crates/docx/src/xml.rs#L302-L342`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/xml.rs#L302-L342)
```rust
let mut el = El { name, attrs: Vec::new(), kids: Vec::new() };
for a in e.attributes().with_checks(false) {
    …
    el.attrs.push((aname, val));
}
```
`with_checks(false)` also accepts duplicate attribute names. The reader's only limits are element count and depth ([L15-L17](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/xml.rs#L15-L17)):
```rust
pub const MAX_DEPTH: usize = 256;
pub const MAX_ELEMENTS: usize = 8_000_000;
```
Each attribute costs two owned `String`s plus the `Vec` slot. The whole tree of `document.xml` stays alive for the full read, and parsed chart and diagram trees are cached alongside it.

## Conditions and impact

Input shape: one element (for example one `w:p`) carrying millions of short attributes. Deflate compresses that to almost nothing.

| attributes | .docx size | peak (audit, debug build) |
|---|---|---|
| 2,000,000 | 15 KB | 150 MB |
| 8,000,000 | 59 KB | 611 MB |

That is about 76 bytes per attribute. A part may inflate to 256 MB, which allows tens of millions of attributes and several GB with `Vec` doubling. That is fatal on wasm32 (4 GB address space) and on low-memory machines, and an allocation failure aborts outside `catch_unwind`. It is reached by opening any `.docx`.

## Suggested fix

```rust
pub const MAX_ATTRS: usize = 1024;
…
…

title: [WC-07] WOFF1 fonts are decompressed before the 128 MB size cap (per-table `origLength` is trusted)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-07), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #2751 (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** High (audit). **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b` (still `wuff` 0.2.9 in `Cargo.lock`). Confirmed by tracing into the dependency; not reproduced at runtime.

## Evidence

[`crates/fonts/src/fontdb/user.rs#L150-L156`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/fonts/src/fontdb/user.rs#L150-L156)
```rust
let decoded = match sniff(bytes).ok_or(UserFontError::NotAFont)? {
    …
    FontFormat::Woff => unwrap_web_font(|| wuff::decompress_woff1(bytes))?,
    FontFormat::Woff2 => unwrap_web_font(|| wuff::decompress_woff2(bytes))?,
};
if decoded.len() > MAX_DECODED_BYTES {   // 128 MB, checked only afterwards
```
In `wuff` 0.2.9, `decompress_woff1` handles each compressed table with `decompress_z(data, table.orig_length as usize)`, which starts with `Vec::with_capacity(size_hint)`, and appends the result to one output buffer. `orig_length` is a `u32` taken from the file's table directory. Neither the per-table sizes nor their sum (or the header's `totalSfntSize`) is checked against any limit before decoding. WOFF2 is bounded inside `wuff`; WOFF1 is not.

The input file is capped at 50 MB (`MAX_FONT_FILE_BYTES`), but deflate reaches about 1000:1 on uniform data. Fonts embedded in a document are decoded on every open ([`crates/engine/src/io.rs#L177`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/io.rs#L177)), and user-installed fonts go through the same function.

## Conditions and impact

Input shape: a document that embeds a WOFF1 font whose tables declare `origLength` near 4 GB, with highly compressible table data behind them. Opening it res…

title: [WC-14a] .doc import: a failed metafile inflation is not charged to the media budget, so 5,000 BLIP entries can each inflate 64 MB
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-14), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #2758 (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Medium (CPU denial of service on open) **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`; `officeart.rs` and `media.rs` are unchanged since eae2421. Confirmed by code trace.

Related: #1334 (closed)

## Evidence

A compressed EMF/WMF/PICT BLIP is inflated with a limit of up to `MAX_METAFILE` (64 MB). When the stream would produce more than that, or is corrupt, `decompress_to_vec_zlib_with_limit` returns an error and the `?` returns `None`, so the work done is thrown away:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docbin/src/officeart.rs#L147-L164

```rust
let cap = limit.min(MAX_METAFILE);
let bytes = if compression == 0 {
    let want = if cb_size > 0 { cb_size.min(cap) } else { cap };
    miniz_oxide::inflate::decompress_to_vec_zlib_with_limit(raw, want).ok()?
```

The caller caches the failure per BLIP-store index (`pib`) but only successful output is added to `total`. Nothing charges the attempt:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docbin/src/media.rs#L104-L131

```rust
let room = self.limit.saturating_sub(self.total);
let key = officeart::fbse_blip(fbse, delay, room).and_then(|b| self.insert(b.bytes, b.ext, b.placeholder));
self.by_bse.insert(pib, key.clone());
```

`MAX_PICTURES` is 5,000 (`media.rs:17`), and the cache key is the store index, not the record location (`foDelay`). Many FBSE entries can point at the same delay-stream record, and each one inflates it again.

## Conditions and impact

Opening a hostile `.doc` file. 5,000 store entries pointing at one compressed metafile that inflates past 64 MB give up to about 5,000 × 64 MB = 3…

title: [WC-14b] .doc import: DIB-to-PNG conversion charges only the PNG output, so a tiny RLE bitmap can decode about 243 MB per picture
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-14), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #2758 (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Medium (CPU and memory denial of service on open) **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`; `officeart.rs` and `media.rs` are unchanged since eae2421. Confirmed by code trace.

Related: #1334 (closed)

## Evidence

A DIB BLIP is wrapped in a BMP header, decoded, and re-encoded as PNG. The decode is allowed up to 16,384 px per side and `max_alloc` of 256 MB (or the remaining media budget). Only the encoded PNG bytes are later charged to the media `total`:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docbin/src/officeart.rs#L181-L221

```rust
let mut limits = image::Limits::default();
limits.max_image_width = Some(MAX_DIB_SIDE);
limits.max_image_height = Some(MAX_DIB_SIDE);
limits.max_alloc = Some((256 << 20).min(limit as u64));
...
match reader.decode() {
    Ok(img) if image::codecs::png::PngEncoder::new(&mut png).write_image(img.as_bytes(), ...).is_ok() =>
```

The check `file_size <= limit` (`:199`) is on the *compressed* DIB size. Then `Pictures::insert` adds only `png.bytes.len()` to `total` (`media.rs:119-131`).

## Conditions and impact

Opening a hostile `.doc` file. An RLE8 DIB of about 100 bytes can declare 9000 × 9000 pixels, which is about 243 MB once decoded. That is under the 256 MB `max_alloc`, so it decodes. A uniform image then compresses to a small PNG, so the media budget barely moves. Each distinct BLIP-store entry (up to `MAX_PICTURES` = 5,000) repeats a 243 MB allocation, a full decode and a full PNG encode. That is minutes of CPU and repeated large transient allocations from a small file.

- Before decoding, read the declared width and height (`into_dimensi…

body: Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-17), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). title: [WC-18] Fonts embedded in a document: collection face count and variable-font named instances are enumerated without a cap
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-18), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #2761 (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Medium (hang or out-of-memory on open) **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`. Confirmed by code trace.

Related: #3687 (embedded fonts stay loaded for later documents)

## Evidence

`enumerate_faces` takes the face count straight from a TrueType collection header. Other enumerators in the same file clamp it to `MAX_FACES` (256, `fontdb.rs:450-454`); this one does not:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs#L859-L866

```rust
let count = match FileRef::new(data) {
    Ok(FileRef::Font(_)) => 1,
    Ok(FileRef::Collection(c)) => c.len(),
    Err(_) => 0,
};
(0..count).filter_map(|i| skrifa::FontRef::from_index(data, i).ok().map(|f| font_faces(&f, i))).flatten().collect()
```

`font_faces` adds one face per `fvar` named instance (up to 65,535), with a linear dedupe per instance, so it is O(n²):

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs#L828-L839

```rust
for ni in f.named_instances().iter() {
    let Some(style) = name(f, &[ni.subfamily_name_id()]) else { continue };
    if named.iter().any(|n| n.style.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&style)) {
```

Document fonts go through `add_document_fonts` → `add_fonts`. It builds a face for every entry, and then checks each new face against every face already in the process-wide database (`fontdb.rs:1171-1195`). `MAX_FACES_PER_FILE` (256) is checked only for user-installed fonts, and only *after* the full enumeration (`fontdb/user.rs:269-275`).

- a TTC whose header lists milli…

title: [WC-21c] `hostile_params_never_panic` has no large-input junk (huge strings, huge counts) and no time or memory budget per command

body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-21), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #2763 (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Low (test coverage gap for resource exhaustion through command params) **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`; the junk set is unchanged since eae2421.

Related: #3633, #3641

## Evidence

The whole junk set is six small values:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/tests.rs#L3347-L3354

```rust
let junk = [
    json!(null),
    json!({}),
    json!({"text": 5, "size": "x", "path": [], "pos": {"block": 9999, "off": 99999}}),
    json!({"value": -1e308, "rows": 1e9}),
    json!({"width": 1e-9, "height": 1e30, "top": -1e9, "left": 1e9}),
    json!({"section": {"pageW": -1e308, ...}}),
];
```

What is missing:
- There is no long string anywhere (`text`, `name`, `label`, `find`, `replace`, `title`).
- Most count-like keys are absent: `count`, `copies`, `times`, `cols`, `level`, `page`, `from`/`to`, `id`.
- Each command runs once on a fresh sample document. There is no wall-clock or allocation bound, so a command that loops 1e9 times, or allocates gigabytes for a huge `count`, passes once it finishes.

## Conditions and impact

The CLI, the control channel and MCP agents pass parameters to commands verbatim. Several of the newer audit's reports are this kind of bug: #3633 (labels/envelopes copy an uncapped line into up to 400 labels) and #3641 (`edit.pasteSpecial` queues about 144 MB per call). A large-parameter junk set with a budget is the kind of check that finds them. Today CI cannot catch a regression that reintroduces one.

## Suggested fix

- Add a size-oriented junk set, for example:
  - every common count key set to `1e9` and to `u32::MAX`;
  - every common string key set …

title: [WC-21e] Web build: `wasm32-unknown-unknown` aborts on panic, so `Session::run`'s `catch_unwind` guard does nothing there
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-21), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #2763 (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Medium (every command panic is fatal on the web build) **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`. Confirmed: no panic strategy or unwinding support is configured for the web target.

Related: #3646, #3674

## Evidence

The never-crash design relies on unwinding:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/session.rs#L1463-L1470

```rust
let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| crate::cmd::column::dispatch(self, id, mutates, run, params)));
```

The `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target's spec has `"panic-strategy": "abort"`, which the audit confirmed. Nothing in the repository changes that:
- the workspace `Cargo.toml` profiles (`Cargo.toml:94-104`) set no `panic` option;
- `.cargo/config.toml` only defines the `xtask` alias;
- `apps/wordcraft-web` builds with the default target.

On that target, a panic calls the panic hook and then traps. `catch_unwind` never sees an `Err`. The same applies to the WOFF decoder guard (`fonts/src/fontdb/user.rs:167`) and the Zotero bridge guard (`zotero/src/bridge.rs:185`).

## Conditions and impact

Any panic reachable from a command or a file open on the web build aborts the WebAssembly instance, and with it the editor tab. The document state in that instance is lost, and the web app turns AutoRecover off (`app.autosave = false`, `apps/wordcraft-web/src/web.rs:67`), so nothing can be restored.

Several open reports already describe panics that "abort the tab on wasm" (#3646, #3674). On native builds the guard would turn those panics into errors; on the web build each one is a crash. The `CLAUDE.md` statement that `Session::run`…

title: [WC-24b] Flat OPC open: `with_scope` rescans the part's root start tag once per inherited namespace declaration
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-24), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #2765 (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Medium (hang on open) **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`. Confirmed by code trace.

Related: #1353 (closed)

## Evidence

When an inline XML part of a Flat OPC (`.xml`) document is extracted, the namespaces declared on the enclosing `pkg:package`, `pkg:part` and `pkg:xmlData` elements are copied onto the part's root element. For each inherited declaration, the code scans the whole root start tag to see whether the part already declares it:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/docx/src/flat.rs#L334-L358

```rust
let tag_end = rest.iter().position(|b| *b == b'>').unwrap_or(rest.len());
let tag = rest.get(..tag_end).unwrap_or_default();
...
for (k, v) in decls.iter().rev() {
    let declared = tag.windows(k.len() + 1).any(|w| w.get(..k.len()) == Some(k.as_bytes()) && matches!(w.last(), Some(b'=' | b' ')));
```

Each of the three scope levels keeps up to 256 declarations (`ns_decls`, `flat.rs:321-330`, pushed at `:180-182`), so there can be up to 768 inherited declarations. The root start tag is bounded only by the part size limit, hundreds of MB.

## Conditions and impact

Opening a crafted Flat OPC file:
- the package elements carry hundreds of distinct `xmlns:` declarations;
- an inline part's root element has a start tag that is very long (for example padded with attributes) and contains none of them.

The cost is up to 768 × tag length comparisons per part, for example about 2e11 for a 250 MB tag, on the thread opening the file.

## Suggested fix

- Parse the root start tag once (for example with `quick_xml`'s attribute iterator, as `ns_decls` already does), and collect its declare…

title: [WC-30] Web build: followed hyperlinks open with window.open(url, "_blank") and keep window.opener
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-30), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #2771 (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Low (reverse tabnabbing on the web build) **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`. Confirmed from source (WordCraft and eframe 0.36.2); no browser test was run.

## Evidence

A Ctrl/Cmd-clicked document link (http, https or mailto) goes to `ctx.open_url` with `new_tab`, on every target including wasm:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs#L2665-L2666
https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L2416-L2418

```rust
if let Some(url) = self.canvas.open_url.take() {
    ctx.open_url(egui::OpenUrl::new_tab(url));
}
```

The locked eframe is 0.36.2 ([Cargo.lock#L1076-L1077](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/Cargo.lock#L1076-L1077)). On the web, its `app_runner.rs` passes that command to `web::open_url` (`eframe-0.36.2/src/web/mod.rs:351-356`), which opens the URL with no window features:

```rust
let name = if new_tab { "_blank" } else { "_self" };
web_sys::window()?.open_with_url_and_target(url, name).ok()?;
```

`check_write` resolves the path with links followed, including a link in the final component, and compares that resolved path with the root:

title: [WC-38c] HTML export: font names are written into the CSS font-family string with only single quotes removed
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-38, HTML font-family), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #2777 (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Low (CSS declaration injection inside one `style` attribute) **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`. Confirmed from source; the audit's re-check found that the attribute itself can't be closed (`"` is entity-escaped), so the impact is limited to CSS inside that attribute.

Related: #2759 (closed; unbounded font-name length, a different problem)

## Evidence

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/formats/src/html.rs#L1697-L1703

```rust
if let Some(fam) = &f.font {
    css.push(format!("font-family:'{}'", esc(&fam.replace('\'', ""))));
}
if !css.is_empty() {
    open.push_str(&format!("<span style=\"{}\">", css.join(";")));
```

`esc` only escapes HTML (`& < > "`). It leaves newlines, backslashes, semicolons and other characters that matter to CSS unchanged:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/formats/src/html.rs#L1609-L1623

The font name comes from the document. For example, the docx reader takes `w:rFonts/@w:ascii` with only an emptiness check (`crates/docx/src/read/props.rs:229-235`). The RTF, ODT and HTML importers and `.json` documents also carry names as given.

## Conditions and impact

A document whose run font name contains CSS-significant characters (a newline, which XML can carry as a character reference, or a backslash escape) is exported to HTML (`file.saveAs` / `wordcraft-cli convert … .html`). Inside a quoted CSS string, an unescaped newline ends it as a bad string. The CSS parser then recovers at the next `;`, so the rest of the font name is parsed as further declarations on the same `<span>`. A hos…

title: [WC-38d] RTF export: a semicolon in a font name ends the \fonttbl entry early, so the name is truncated on reopen
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-38, RTF font names), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #2777 (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Low (round-trip correctness; the audit's re-check found no injection, because `{`, `}` and `\` are escaped) **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`. Confirmed from source.

## Evidence

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/formats/src/rtf.rs#L759-L764

```rust
for (i, f) in w.t.fonts.iter().enumerate() {
    let fam = if model::is_mono(f) { "\\fmodern" } else { "\\fswiss" };
    out.push_str(&format!("{{\\f{i}{fam}\\fcharset0 {};}}", esc(f)));
}
```

`esc` handles `\`, `{`, `}`, tabs, line breaks and non-ASCII, but writes `;` through unchanged:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/formats/src/rtf.rs#L44-L70

In a font table entry, `;` ends the font name. The importer reads it that way too: `Dest::FontTbl` commits the name at the first `;`.

Two more details:
- `esc` turns a `\n` in a font name into `\line `, which is not meaningful inside `\fonttbl` either.
- Two different names that share a prefix up to the `;` read back as the same font name.

## Conditions and impact

A document with a run font name that contains `;` is saved as RTF. This can happen with a docx `w:rFonts` value or a `.json` document. When the file is reopened (in WordCraft or another RTF reader), the font name is cut at the `;`, and the remainder of the entry is ignored or read as text. The run is then shown in a different font. This is formatting loss, not code execution, and it is unlikely with real font names. But it is a silent writer/reader mismatch.

## Suggested fix

In the font-table loop, sanitise the name before `esc`:
- Drop `;` (or repl…

title: [WC-40d] wordcraft-control-key is the only production crate root without the never-panic clippy deny
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-40, lint follow-ups), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously listed in tracker #2744 (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Info (rule gap; no panic path found today) **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`. Confirmed from source.

## Evidence

`AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` (line 16) require every production crate root to carry:

```rust
#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]
```

At `00bc6a4b`, every `crates/*/src/lib.rs` and `apps/*/src/main.rs` has it (for example [geom/src/lib.rs#L7](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/geom/src/lib.rs#L7)), except `wordcraft-control-key`:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/control-key/src/lib.rs#L1-L4

```rust
//! The control channel's key file, one rule for the app (which writes it) and the MCP bridge
//! (which reads it): `<settings>/control-key.<instance>`. See `docs/control-protocol.md`, Keys.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
```

The workspace lint table doesn't cover these lints either. It only sets `unsafe_code = "forbid"` plus `dbg_macro`/`todo` as warnings:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/Cargo.toml#L85-L92

## Conditions and impact

The crate is linked into the desktop app, which writes the key file, and into the MCP bridge, which reads it. These are security-relevant paths: a panic there would take down the bridge or the app outside `Session::run`'s guard. Its current non-test code has no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`. title: [WC-40e] xtask does not inherit the workspace lints, so unsafe_code = "forbid" doesn't apply to it
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the security and robustness audit of WordCraft at eae2421 (finding WC-40, lint follow-ups), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously listed in tracker #2744 (closed as not planned without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Info (uniformity; xtask is a developer tool and is not shipped) **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`. Confirmed from source.

Related: #974 (CI enforcement of `cargo xtask ci`)

## Evidence

The workspace forbids `unsafe` and warns on `dbg!`/`todo!`:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/Cargo.toml#L85-L92

```toml
[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "forbid"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
dbg_macro = "warn"
todo = "warn"
```

Every crate and app opts in with `[lints] workspace = true` (for example [crates/control-key/Cargo.toml](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/control-key/Cargo.toml)). `xtask/Cargo.toml` has no `[lints]` table:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/xtask/Cargo.toml#L1-L9

```toml
[package]
name = "xtask"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
publish = false

[dependencies]
serde_json = { workspace = true }
```

## Conditions and impact

xtask has no `unsafe` today. But it runs on every developer's and agent's machine as part of `cargo xtask ci`, and it is the code that enforces the project's gates (assets, layers, parity floor, wasm). If `unsafe` or a leftover `dbg!` were added there, nothing would flag it, unlike in every other workspace member.

## Suggested fix

Add the following to `xtask/Cargo.toml`, then fix any warnings that clippy `-D warnings` reports for xtask:

```toml
[lints]
workspace = true
```

- Extend `cargo xtask layers` (or add a small check) so that every worksp…

Previously filed as #1317 (closed by the author without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** High (document integrity). **Status:** static review, not run. Related: open PR #1925 (not merged), #3632 (Compare work budget, a different problem).

## Evidence
`compare` opens the revised file as a full `Document` but takes only its body. [crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs#L1207-L1208](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs#L1207-L1208):

```rust
let old: Vec<Arc<Block>> = s.doc.body.clone();
let new: Vec<Arc<Block>> = revised.body.clone();
```

Revised blocks are then pushed into the result as they are ([#L1236-L1240](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs#L1236-L1240), [#L1259-L1261](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs#L1259-L1261)), and the result becomes `s.doc.body` ([#L1273](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs#L1273)). Nothing in `compare` (L1179-L1281) reads `revised.media`, `revised.parts`, `revised.styles`, the numbering definitions or `revised.revisions`.

The copied blocks keep the revised document's identifiers:
- media keys of pictures
- part ids of footnotes, endnotes and text boxes
- style ids
- list `numId`s
- revision indices already in the revised file

These ids are resolved against the original document's tables.

Compare an original with a revised file that adds a picture, a footnote, a new style or a new list. The same happens when both files use the same id for different things, which is common, …

title: [A13-1323a] Zotero bridge edits the document directly, bypassing Restrict Editing and content-control locks
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the read-only source audit of 2026-10-13 (upstream 159b84f), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #1323 (closed by the author without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** High (application editing restrictions; not a cryptographic control). **Status:** static review, not run. Related: open PR #2002 (not merged), #3753 (A13-1323b) (tracked changes), #3276 (other paths that change a protected document).

## Evidence
Restrict Editing is enforced in `Session::run`, but only for registered commands that mutate. Each such command is checked before it runs, and the regions outside the editable exceptions are compared after it ([crates/engine/src/session.rs#L1391-L1477](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/session.rs#L1391-L1477)):

```rust
let guard = if spec.mutates { crate::cmd::protect::check_before(self, id, params)? } else { false };
```

author: PierrunoYT
body:

title: [A13-1331b] Control channel and MCP bridge: writes have no timeout and replies no overall deadline
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the read-only source audit of 2026-10-13 (upstream 159b84f), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #1331 (closed by the author without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Low (local availability; loopback only). **Status:** static review, not run. Related: open PR #2596 (not merged), #3685 (unbounded line length, not time), #3686 (connection cap), #3699 (port held by another process).

## Evidence
No socket in the control path sets a write timeout. `git grep set_write_timeout` at `00bc6a4b` finds nothing in `apps/` or `crates/`.

**App side.** Replies are written with a blocking `writeln!` ([apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs#L217-L222](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs#L217-L222)). After authentication, the read deadline is removed for good (`set_deadline(None)`, [#L229-L232](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs#L229-L232)). An authenticated client that stops reading a large reply (a screenshot, `document.inspect`) parks the connection thread in `write` with no limit.

**Bridge side.** `Remote::roundtrip` writes without a timeout. For the reply, it relies on a per-read timeout ([crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L117](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L117), [#L144-L156](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L144-L156)):

```rust
s.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(90))).ok();
...
writer.write_all(line.as_bytes())?;
...
if reader.read_line(&mut reply)? == 0 {
```

`set_read_timeout` bounds each `read` call, not the whole `read_line`. A peer that sends a byte every few seconds keeps one reply open in…

title: [A13-1341a] Layout stops breaking a paragraph after 200,000 lines, so the rest of its text is never shown, printed or exported
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the read-only source audit of 2026-10-13 (upstream 159b84f), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #1341 (closed by the author without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Low (silent loss of rendered text in an extreme paragraph; the model keeps the text) **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`. Static review only. PR #1927 proposed a fix but is still open and unmerged.

Related: #1341 (closed), #1927 (open PR)

## Evidence

`break_lines` fills `pl.lines` for one paragraph and simply leaves the loop once it holds more than 200,000 lines:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/layout/src/para.rs#L2638-L2640

```rust
        if lines.len() > 200_000 {
            break;
        }
```

The function is `break_lines` ([para.rs#L1987](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/layout/src/para.rs#L1987)). Nothing records that the paragraph was cut short. The clusters after the last line therefore get no line, are not painted, are not hit-testable, and are not in PDF/PNG output or page counts. The text is still in the document model, so a .docx save keeps it. What the user sees and prints no longer matches the file.

## Conditions and impact

One paragraph that breaks into more than 200,000 lines: a long run of manual line breaks (Shift+Enter, `w:br`), or several megabytes of text in a very narrow column or table cell. This is rare in normal writing, but it can come from generated or converted documents. When it happens, the end of the paragraph and anything placed by it simply vanish from the page, and nothing says so. PDF export (`file.exportPdf`, `wordcraft-cli convert`) then produces an incomplete document while reporting success.

The cap itself is a reasonable guard. The problem is that it is silent.

title: [A13-1341b] Finish & Merge stops at 200,000 merged blocks and reports success without saying records were left out
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the read-only source audit of 2026-10-13 (upstream 159b84f), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #1341 (closed by the author without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Medium (recipients silently missing from a merge) **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`. Static review only. PR #1927 proposed a fix but is still open and unmerged.

Related: #1341 (closed), #1927 (open PR), #3731 (memory cost of the same loop; a different problem)

## Evidence

`finish` builds one copy of the body per record. Once the output holds more than `MAX_MERGED_BLOCKS` top-level blocks it leaves the loop, even when records `start..to` are still waiting:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/mailings.rs#L936-L937

```rust
/// Most merged documents' worth of body blocks Finish & Merge builds.
const MAX_MERGED_BLOCKS: usize = 200_000;
```

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/mailings.rs#L1012-L1016

```rust
        out.body.extend(body);
        count += 1;
        if out.body.len() > MAX_MERGED_BLOCKS {
            break;
        }
```

The result is the same success shape whether the merge ran to completion or stopped early:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/cmd/mailings.rs#L1035-L1043

```rust
        return Ok(json!({"records": count, "path": path}));
    ...
    Ok(json!({"records": count}))
```

`records` counts the copies that were emitted. A caller can't tell records left out by the cap from records dropped by a true `SKIPIF`, and the UI shows no warning.

## Conditions and impact

The cap is reached when records × top-level blocks per letter goes past 200,000. For example, a 100-paragraph letter reaches it after about 2,000 recipient…

title: [A13-1341c] LaTeX import silently keeps only the first 32 MiB of a .tex file and opens it as if complete
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the read-only source audit of 2026-10-13 (upstream 159b84f), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #1341 (closed by the author without a fix); this report covers one problem.

**Severity:** Medium (silent data loss; a save then makes it permanent) **Status:** Present at `00bc6a4b`. Static review only. PR #1927 proposed a fix but is still open and unmerged.

Related: #1341 (closed), #1927 (open PR)

## Evidence

The importer cuts the input at `MAX_SOURCE` bytes and parses only that prefix:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/formats/src/latex.rs#L24-L25

```rust
/// Largest `.tex` source imported (bytes); longer input is cut off.
pub const MAX_SOURCE: usize = 32 << 20;
```

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/formats/src/latex.rs#L1056-L1061

```rust
/// Import a LaTeX source file.
pub fn import(bytes: &[u8]) -> Document {
    let mut d = model::to_doc(&parse(&crate::txt::decode(bytes.get(..MAX_SOURCE).unwrap_or(bytes))));
    d.ensure_nonempty();
    d
}
```

`import` returns a plain `Document`, so it cannot report the cut, and the dispatcher wraps it in `Ok`:

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/formats/src/lib.rs#L37

```rust
        "tex" | "latex" | "ltx" => Ok(latex::import(bytes)),
```

File open accepts files up to 2 GB ([engine/src/io.rs#L415-L417](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/engine/src/io.rs#L415-L417)), so a .tex between 32 MiB and 2 GB reaches this path. The byte cut can also fall inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character or a command/group, which then decodes or parses differently from the source.

Opening (or converting with `wordcraft-cli convert`) a `.tex`/`.latex`/`.ltx` fi…

Related: open PR #2809 (not merged; adds a mutable-ref guard and documents the trust model), storytold/craft-common-actions#6 (closed: `@main` kept on purpose), storytold/craft-common-actions#7 (open: secrets and permissions inside the shared workflow), storytold/craft-common-actions#19 (open draft: CODEOWNERS and a pinned-ref lint).

title: [A13-1358b] SonarCloud workflow uses `secrets: inherit` on a mutable `@main` shared workflow, handing it every repository secret when it only needs `SONAR_TOKEN`
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Re-filed from the read-only source audit of 2026-10-13 (upstream 159b84f), re-checked against upstream main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/commit/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d). Previously filed as #1358 (closed by the author without a fix). This report covers one problem: the same mutable-shared-workflow trust, at a second location found while re-checking.

**Severity:** Medium (least privilege for CI secrets; no compromise alleged). **Status:** static review of the workflow configuration; no workflow was run. Related: #3771 (A13-1358a) (release workflow), open PR #2809, storytold/craft-common-actions#6.

## Evidence
[.github/workflows/sonarcloud.yml#L3-L20](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/.github/workflows/sonarcloud.yml#L3-L20):

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
...
    # Tracked at @main so org-wide CI improvements propagate without PR churn.
    uses: storytold/craft-common-actions/.github/workflows/sonarcloud.yml@main
    secrets: inherit
```

- `secrets: inherit` passes **every** secret the repository has to the called workflow. That includes the Apple, Windows and Azure signing and notarisation secrets used by `release.yml`, unless they live only in a protected environment.

title: Modify Style can't set a style's line spacing, character spacing or indents
author: Lupus7477
body:
## What happens

Modify Style (right-click a style in the gallery › Modify…, or Manage Styles › Modify…) only offers a style's name, font, size, colour, bold, italic and space before/after. There is no way to give a style:

- line spacing (Single, 1.5 lines, Double, At least, Exactly, Multiple),
- alignment or indents,
- character spacing (expanded or condensed), scale, raised or lowered position, or kerning.

The document model and `styles.modify` already carry all of these (`ParaProps`, `CharProps`). Only the dialog lacks them. #2421 (indents) and #2917 (style definition too basic) report parts of this.

## What Word does

Modify Style has:

- a formatting row: font, size, bold, italic, underline, colour, alignment, line spacing and paragraph spacing,
- a preview with the previous and the following paragraph in grey around sample text,
- a description of what the style sets,
- a Format menu whose Font… and Paragraph… open the full Font dialog (with its Advanced page: scale, spacing, position, kerning) and Paragraph dialog for the style.

Nothing changes until OK.

## Proposal

The same in WordCraft:

- Modify Style gets that formatting row, a character spacing row, a live preview and a description.
- Format › Font… and Paragraph… open the existing dialogs for the style. Their OK hands the changes back to Modify Style, and Modify Style's OK sends everything as one `styles.modify` (one undo step). Cancel drops it all.
- The Font dialog gets an Advanced page (scale, spacing, position, kerning).
- The Paragraph dialog's line spacing box offers every rule with its At value, not only a multiple.

Related: #2917, #2421, #3442, #3445.

title: [Feature Request] Please add official OpenCode skill support for WordCraft
author: AHL8192
body:
Thanks for WordCraft — positions in a word processor are the least obvious thing about automating one, and WordCraft exposes them honestly.

WordCraft is one of those rare apps where the agent surface is a first-class citizen rather than a bolted-on API: 16 MCP tools, `.docx` read/write, track changes, comments, mail merge, macros, and the same command engine behind the ribbon. That is 90% of the work, and it is why this request is small.

## Why a skill, when the MCP server already exists?

An MCP server answers *"what can this app do?"*. A skill answers *"what should an agent do next, in what order, with which ids, and which footguns should it avoid?"*

The gap we kept falling into:

| Without a skill | With a skill |
|---|---|
| Command ids discovered by trial and error | Namespaces and ids named up front |
| Coordinates and units guessed | Conventions stated once, with the failure mode |
| Silent coercions quietly corrupt output | Known coercions listed, with the read-back that catches them |
| Every session re-derives the workflow | Verified recipes to copy |

MCP makes WordCraft *possible* to drive. A skill makes it *reliable* to drive — in the same way your own docs do for a human.

## The ask

- [ ] **Ship the skill in-tree** — e.g. `.opencode/skills/wordcraft/SKILL.md` alongside `references/` and `scripts/`, versioned with the app
- [ ] **One line in the README** next to the MCP section saying how to install it
- [ ] **Regenerate the volatile bits at release** (version, tool count, command ids) — the included scripts do most of this already
- [ ] *Optional:* publish to a skills registry, or add `--print-skill` to the CLI so installation is one command
- [ ] *Optional:* an `examples/` artifact the recipes can point at

## What we're handing over

We wrote a complete OpenCode skill while doing real work with WordCraft 0.9.0 on Linux (verified 2026-10-22). It is not a stub or a README restatement — it is the operating manual we wished existed on day one, built…

title: [Feature Request] Add LaTeX and Mermaid Rendering for Markdown
author: mmhs013
body:
With the increasing use of AI, Markdown files containing LaTeX equations and Mermaid diagrams are becoming more common, especially in scientific and technical documentation.

It would be helpful if WordCraft could automatically render these elements when opening or previewing Markdown files.

**Expected behavior:**
- **LaTeX equations:** Automatically render inline equations (e.g., `$E=mc^2$`) and block equations (e.g., `$$E=mc^2$$`) as properly formatted mathematical expressions.

title: Home › Multilevel List: Define New List Style… dialog, and list styles that stay linked to their lists
author: Nghiathan13
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @Nghiathan13._

**Version:** `main` at `00bc6a4`.

## Problem

Home › Paragraph › Multilevel List has the list library, the heading-linked presets, Define New Multilevel List… and Change to Level (`crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs`, the `split(… "multilevel" …)` call). It has no way to make a **list style**: a named style of type numbering that lists use, so that changing the style changes every list that uses it.

- **No Define New List Style… entry and no dialog.** Word puts it under Define New Multilevel List… in the same drop-down, and lists the document's list styles in a List Styles section of that drop-down.
- **No command creates one.** `styles.create` always makes a paragraph style (`StyleKind::Paragraph`, `crates/engine/src/cmd/para.rs`), although the model has `StyleKind::Numbering` and DOCX reads and writes numbering styles.
- **A list style doesn't stay linked to its lists.** On open, an abstract list with `w:numStyleLink` gets a copy of the style's levels and the link is dropped (`crates/docx/src/read/mod.rs`, "Abstracts that only link to a numbering style…"); on save neither `w:styleLink` nor `w:numStyleLink` is written. So a list style made here, or one from a Word file, no longer drives its lists after a save. This is the `w:styleLink` row of #1034.

## Proposed

- **Command** `list.defineStyle`: a numbering style (name, start, per-level number style, format text, font, bold, italic, underline, colour, indents) backed by a list definition from `list.define` (`apply: false`), linked both ways. Programmatic calls never open the dialog.
- **Model and DOCX**: keep the link on the abstract list (`w:styleLink` on the style's own definition, `w:numStyleLink` on lists that use the style), read and write it, and resolve levels through it, with a save-and-reopen test.

title: Feature Request: Slovak (sk-SK) spelling / proofing support
author: TheGreatOneYouKnow
body:
### Describe the Feature
Please add Slovak (sk-SK) spelling support, using the standard Hunspell dictionary like the other languages.

### What is the specific use case?
I need to write and proofread documents in Slovak. Currently WordCraft has no Slovak spellcheck.

### Why is this important?
Slovak is a major Central European language. A high-quality Hunspell dictionary already exists and is widely used (LibreOffice, Firefox, etc.).

Happy to help test once it’s available. Thank you!

title: [feature refinement] Autoscroll: make the cursor direction-aware (neutral in the dead zone)
author: Galex-Z
body:
**Context**
While using middle-click autoscroll, I noticed the cursor is always `CursorIcon::ResizeVertical`: in `crates/ui-egui/src/autoscroll.rs`, `paint` sets it unconditionally, including inside the dead zone. (I first misread the anchored marker as a bug in #3507. Thanks to @FredApps for clarifying that it's the intentional neutral point. This issue is separate from that.)

**Current behavior**
The cursor looks the same whether you're scrolling up, scrolling down, or inside the dead zone, so it doesn't show which way the page is moving or whether it's moving at all.

**Proposal**
Choose the cursor from the pointer's offset from the anchor:
- inside the dead zone: a neutral icon (or keep `ResizeVertical`)
- above the anchor: `ResizeNorth`
- below the anchor: `ResizeSouth`

I'd put the choice in a small pure function next to `scroll_delta`, so it can be unit-tested the same way, and leave the marker as it is.

**Open questions**
- Is this wanted, or is the single up-down cursor intentional?
- Are there platforms where the north/south icons render badly? I'll test on Windows and note it in the PR.

**Offer**
I'd like to implement this. I'd run `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy` and `cargo test`, and add a test.

title: Tables: a page holds one row more than Word's when the border under the last row doesn't fit
author: dfgodvan
body:
A table row that another row follows is placed on a page only when its height fits above the bottom margin. Word also wants the border under the row on that page, so it moves the row on when only the border is missing. WordCraft then keeps one row more on the page than Word, and every later page break in the table shifts by a row.

**Repro.** A4, margins 72 pt, Times New Roman 12, a fixed one-column table of 60 one-line rows with 3 pt borders (`w:sz="24"` on all edges). The bottom margin is swept in 0.4 pt steps; the count is the rows on page 1 (Word for Mac 16, PDF export):

| bottom margin | Word | WordCraft main |
|---|---|---|
| 77.8 pt | 41 | 41 |
| 78.2 pt | 40 | 41 |
| 78.6 … 81.0 pt | 40 | 41 |
| 81.4 pt | 40 | 40 |

At 78.2 pt the 41st row ends 0.6 pt above the margin, but the 3 pt border under it doesn't fit, and Word moves the row to page 2. WordCraft moves it only once the row itself no longer fits (81.4 pt). With 0.5 pt borders the window is 0.5 pt wide: it only shows on long documents, where it moved a whole table's page breaks by one row (found on a 160-page document of fixed-layout tables).

Bottom of page 1 at 78.2 pt (red line: the bottom margin). Word and the fix end the page with row 40, main keeps row 41:

![Bottom of page 1 at a 78.2 pt bottom margin: Word for Mac and this PR end the page with row 40, main puts row 41 there](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dfgodvan/wordcraft/47381dbc8eb0bd97f8e029a02c19aed583494edc/rows-border/page1.png)

title: Layout: a long footnote referenced on a page's last lines moves the reference line to the next page, leaving a large gap (Word keeps the line and continues the note)
author: jpc7k1
body:
### What happens

When a paragraph near the bottom of a page carries a reference to a long footnote that can't fit entirely on that page, WordCraft moves the line with the reference (and the note) to the next page. The page is left with a large empty area above the footnote separator.

Word keeps the reference line on the page, places as much of the note as fits at the bottom, and continues the rest on the next page under the continuation separator. `docs/layout-parity.md` describes the same goal ("A long note continues onto the next page at a line boundary (its first line stays with the reference)").

### Reproduce

Synthetic document (no real content): Garamond 12, double-spaced, justified body; nine paragraphs; five footnotes, on every other paragraph; the third is long (two paragraphs, about 11 sentences) and is referenced from the last lines of page 2.

- Word for Mac 16.114 (exported PDF): 4 pages. Page 2 ends with the paragraph carrying reference 3; the bottom of page 2 holds the first part of note 3; it continues on page 3.
- WordCraft main (00bc6a4b): 5 pages. The line with reference 3 and the whole note move to page 3; page 2 has a large empty area above the separator.

title: control::orphans counts earlier events per lone table-open marker (quadratic)
author: benandez
body:
Found while fixing the 2026-10-22 audit findings (#3692, doc-model group). Checked against main [`00bc6a4b`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/doc/src/control.rs#L437).

**Severity:** Low (CWE-407, quadratic work on hostile input)

**Evidence.** `control::orphans` works out which of a table's content-control opens each lone table-open marker is by counting every earlier event for each marker:

```rust
let nth = events.iter().take(k).filter(|x| matches!(x, ControlEvent::Open { block, off: None, .. } if *block == e.block())).count();
```

Work is O(lone markers × events per story). A document with many unpaired table-wrapping control markers makes every call (it runs on edits that check for orphaned markers) quadratic.

**Suggested fix.** One pass over `events` keeping a running per-block count of table opens (`HashMap<usize, usize>`), recorded at each lone index. Test: many lone table-open markers resolve in linear time and give the same `nth` as before.

title: TrueType hinting has no work bound inside skrifa (residual of audit finding 62)
author: benandez
body:
Residual of audit finding 62 (#3692, font-ingestion group), checked against main `00bc6a4b`.

**Severity:** Low (CWE-400, CPU exhaustion from a hostile font)

**What the fix on `sec/d` covers.** A font asking for huge twilight zones or stack is drawn unhinted; a glyph needing more than 256 KiB of hinting memory is drawn unhinted; a hinted glyph taking over 50 ms turns hinting off for that face (native only).

**What is left.** Inside those limits skrifa's TrueType interpreter can still do about 1M × zone-size point moves on one glyph, including in `HintingInstance::new` (fpgm/prep) before the 50 ms timer can act. On wasm there is no timer at all. skrifa exposes no instruction or work budget.

**Options.**
1. Ask skrifa (fontations) upstream for an instruction/work limit on `HintingInstance` and glyph hinting; use it when released. No fork.
2. Hint in a worker with a deadline and fall back to unhinted outlines on timeout (native only).

Acceptance: a font whose prep/glyph program loops near the limits is drawn unhinted within a bounded time on native and wasm.

title: Zotero listener owner check only on Linux; macOS/Windows/BSD trust any local process on port 23116
author: benandez
body:
Residual of audit finding 21 (#3692, Zotero group), checked against main `00bc6a4b`.

**Severity:** Low (CWE-306, local only)

**Context.** WordCraft connects to Zotero's Word-integration listener on `127.0.0.1:23116` and then obeys the document callbacks it sends. The protocol is fixed by Zotero and has no authentication. The fix on `sec/k` refuses non-loopback addresses, and on Linux refuses the connection unless `/proc/net/tcp(6)` shows the listener is owned by our uid.

**What is left.** On macOS, Windows and the BSDs only the loopback check applies. Another local user who binds port 23116 while Zotero isn't running can drive the open document (insert/convert fields). Documented in `docs/zotero.md` ("Who can drive the document").

**Options.** Look up the listening socket's owner per OS without `unsafe` in our crates:
- macOS/BSD: `libproc`/`sysctl` via a maintained safe wrapper crate
- Windows: `GetExtendedTcpTable` owning PID → process token user, via `windows`/`windows-sys` behind a safe wrapper

Acceptance: on each OS, a listener owned by a different user is refused before any callback runs, with a test like `peer::tests::a_listener_of_another_user_is_refused`.

title: Support prefix licensing through inner suffixes in Hunspell suffix chains
author: coderabbitai
body:
## Summary

Extend the Hunspell affix engine so an inner suffix in a two-suffix chain can license a prefix. The current engine rejects such forms even without `CIRCUMFIX`. This is a broader engine limitation, not a regression specific to Slovak support in #3835.

Requested by @TheGreatOneYouKnow as a separate follow-up.

## Reproduction

Use this synthetic `.aff` file:

```text
SET UTF-8
CIRCUMFIX X
PFX P Y 1
PFX P 0 pre/X .
SFX A Y 1
SFX A 0 a/XBP .
SFX B Y 1
SFX B 0 b .
SFX C Y 1
SFX C 0 c/B .
```

Use this `.dic` file:

```text
1
root/AC
```

The inner `A` suffix licenses prefix `P` and outer suffix `B`. WordCraft rejects `prerootab`; the requester confirmed that libhunspell 1.7.2 accepts it with these rules. Removing `CIRCUMFIX X` also exposes the prefix-licensing limitation: acceptance must not depend on the inner suffix being a circumfix suffix.

## Required changes

Affected area: `crates/proof/src/affix.rs`, especially `AffixDict::contains_excluding`, `AffixDict::form_has_flag`, and `AffixDict::suffixed`.

- Support prefix licensing through an inner suffix's continuation classes within the existing two-suffix limit.
- Handle circumfix pairing across the suffix chain according to libhunspell behavior.
- Preserve rejection of unpaired circumfix forms, including the existing `najrýchlejšie` regression case.
- Keep the change separate from the Slovak support PR because it changes shared matching behavior for all Hunspell languages.

## Slovak impact

The requester reports that this limitation does not affect sk_SK 2.4.9:

- No suffix rule's continuation classes name another suffix flag.
- The 228 suffix rules with continuation classes use only `F` and `s`.
- Therefore, this dictionary never forms a two-suffix chain.
- The reported comparison of 36,154 generated words against libhunspell 1.7.2 still has no verdict differences.

These are requester-reported results, not independently verified in this issue.

Dictionaries that do chain suffixes, including Polish an…

title: "Use system setting" ignores the desktop's dark mode on Linux Mint (Cinnamon)
author: craptocracy
body:
## What happens

In **Options › General › Interface theme**, choosing **Use system setting** leaves WordCraft light while the desktop is in dark mode. Choosing **Dark** or **Light** directly works.

## Environment

- Linux Mint 22.3, Cinnamon, X11
- The desktop's Settings portal reports dark mode correctly:

```console
$ gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop --object-path /org/freedesktop/portal/desktop --method org.freedesktop.portal.Settings.ReadOne org.freedesktop.appearance color-scheme
(<uint32 1>,)
```

## Cause

https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/00bc6a4b028013b2dfb0e85e8b326aeed3ecff6d/crates/ui-egui/src/desktop_theme.rs#L109-L131

1. `org.freedesktop.interface.color-scheme` is not a portal namespace. The standard key is `org.freedesktop.appearance` / `color-scheme`.
2. That standard key answers a `u32` (0 = no preference, 1 = prefer dark, 2 = prefer light), but `read()` only accepts a string (`String::try_from`), so even the right key would be skipped.
3. A `"default"` string from the first key returns `None` straight away instead of trying the next key.

Mint's portal backend ([xdg-desktop-portal-xapp](https://github.com/linuxmint/xdg-desktop-portal-xapp/blob/master/src/settings.c)) answers this setting only under `org.freedesktop.appearance`, so `read()` never gets a usable answer and "Use system setting" falls back to light. KDE Plasma without the GTK portal backend fails the same way, as measured in #761. GNOME's portal serves `org.gnome.desktop.interface`, which is likely why this hasn't shown up there.

## Suggested fix

Read `org.freedesktop.appearance` / `color-scheme` first and accept its `u32` (1 → dark, 2 → light, 0 → no preference). Keep the GNOME string as a fallback, and move on to the next key when an answer is `"default"`. Other Craft apps already read it this way, for example [CADCraft's `desktop_theme.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/main/apps/cadcraft/src/desktop_theme.rs) and the shared [`craf…

title: Paste: charge run formatting copied when a text box story is adopted
author: benandez
body:
Follow-up from #3874 (CodeRabbit review). `block_cost` in `crates/doc/src/edit.rs` now counts every heap payload `InlineObject::clone` copies when a pasted text box adopts its story. Run-level `CharProps` strings (font names, style ids, …) on ordinary text runs are still charged only their shallow size. A story with many runs carrying long formatting strings, adopted by many boxes, can copy more than the 32 MiB paste budget reports.

**Fix:** count run `CharProps` heap payloads in `block_cost`, the same way #3874 counts object payloads. Add a test where long run formatting × many boxes stays within `MAX_PASTED_BOX_BYTES`.

Part of #3692.

title: Keyboard shortcuts for styles: Customize Keyboard and Format › Shortcut key… in the style dialogs
author: Nghiathan13
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @Nghiathan13._

**Version:** `main` at `3a4770e`.

## Problem

Word lets a style have a keyboard shortcut: Format › Shortcut key… in the style dialogs (Modify Style, Create New Style from Formatting, Define New List Style) opens Customize Keyboard on that style, and pressing the keys applies it.

WordCraft's Customize Keyboard (#368, `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs_keyboard.rs`, `tools.customizeKeyboard`) binds keys to **commands** only. There is no way to bind a key to a style, so:

- Define New List Style (#3805) shows Format › Shortcut key… greyed out.
- Modify Style and New Style have no Format menu entry for it.

## Proposed

- Key bindings that name a style: stored with the user's key settings next to command bindings, applied through `styles.apply` (paragraph and character styles) or `list.applyStyle` (list styles).
- Customize Keyboard lists styles as a category, shows a style's keys, and assigns or removes them like a command's.
- Format › Shortcut key… in the style dialogs opens Customize Keyboard on that style.
- `tools.customizeKeyboard` takes a style as well as a command, so agents can bind one.

## Done when

- A key bound to a style applies it, survives a restart, and shows in Customize Keyboard and in the command search's shortcut text.
- Format › Shortcut key… is enabled in Define New List Style and works from Modify Style.
- Engine and UI tests cover binding, applying, removing and a key already in use.

In Word, Text Effects › Outline › Weight shows each weight as its label next to a line drawn at that thickness, from ¼ pt to 6 pt. WordCraft lists only the numbers, and the Text Outline menu stops at 3 pt.

**Current behaviour**
- Home › Text Effects › Text Outline › Weight lists 0.25–3 pt as plain text, with no 4.5 pt or 6 pt ([`wordart_menus.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/3a4770ef8ce037d2650c93e2d5764536549357c7/crates/ui-egui/src/wordart_menus.rs#L133-L138)).

- One shared Weight submenu for Text Outline and Shape Outline. Each entry shows its label and a line sample drawn in code at that weight, with a 1 px minimum so ¼ pt stays visible. This is the same approach as the Underline line samples (#2738).
- Text Outline gets 4.5 pt and 6 pt, matching Shape Outline and the border dialogs. `format.textEffects` already takes any `width`, so the engine doesn't change.
- The current weight is checked.
- Labels go through `tl!("{n} pt")`.

author: Coopers22
body:
**Version:** WordCraft 0.10.0 (Windows x64 MSI), driven through `wordcraft-cli` MCP. The code paths below are unchanged on `main` at 3a4770e.

### Steps to reproduce

1. New blank document, type `Hello world.`
2. Select `world`, run `review.newComment {"text": "Parent comment"}` (gets id 0).
3. Run `review.reply {"id": 0, "text": "Reply"}` (gets id 1).
4. Save as `.docx` and open it in Microsoft Word 16 (Microsoft 365).

### Actual behaviour

WordCraft shows the reply correctly threaded. Word shows only the parent comment: the reply is gone (`Document.Comments.Count` is 1).

The saved file has both comments in `comments.xml`, and `commentsExtended.xml` threads them correctly (`w15:paraIdParent`), but `document.xml` has anchors for the parent only:

```xml
<w:commentRangeStart w:id="0"/><w:r><w:t>world</w:t></w:r><w:commentRangeEnd w:id="0"/>
<w:r><w:rPr><w:rStyle w:val="CommentReference"/></w:rPr><w:commentReference w:id="0"/></w:r>
```

There is nothing for id 1. Word appears to discard any comment without a `w:commentReference` in a story.

### Expected behaviour

Each reply gets its own `commentRangeStart`, `commentRangeEnd` and `commentReference` in the body, as Word writes them: alongside its parent's, over the same text. A file where Word added a reply to a comment has anchors for both ids next to each other.

### Likely cause

`reply()` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs` (around line 163) inserts the reply into `doc.comments` with `parent: Some(..)` but adds no `InlineObject::CommentStart` / end / reference, and the writer in `crates/docx/src/write/story.rs` (around lines 493-506) emits anchors only from those inline objects. Either `reply()` could add the anchors next to the parent's, or the writer could emit them for any comment with a parent that has none.

### Impact

Anyone who answers a review in WordCraft and sends the file back to a Word user loses every reply. Found while testing review workflows on synthetic documents. The same happened with a 3-c…

title: Typing many paragraphs in one text.insert call is roughly quadratic (10,000 lines ≈ 6 s)
author: benandez
body:
Typing many paragraphs in one call slows down faster than the line count grows. Each Enter seems to do work proportional to the whole document, so the total is roughly quadratic.

**Measured** (debug build on a busy machine, one `text.insert` call with `paragraphs`, one line per paragraph):

| Lines | Time |
|---|---|
| 1,250 | 92 ms |
| 2,500 | 439 ms |
| 5,000 | 1.5 s |
| 10,000 | 5.9 s |

Doubling the lines costs about 3.5–4.5× the time.

**Where it matters:** pasting or typing a long document through the control channel, CLI or MCP, and long pastes in the app if they go through the same Enter path. #3875 caps `text.insert` at 10,000 paragraphs per call for every caller, so this is not a hang any more. It is still a slowdown below the cap.

**Not yet known:** which step of Enter (`insert_paragraphs` → Enter in `crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs`) does document-wide work, e.g. a full re-layout, a list or numbering renumber, an undo snapshot of the whole body, or an AutoFormat scan. That needs a profile.

**Expected:** typing N paragraphs costs about N × the cost of one, independent of how many paragraphs already exist.

Found while answering a review question on #3875.
