title: Layout: an empty paragraph closing a section at the bottom of a full page pushes the footnotes below the bottom margin (Word keeps them in place)
author: cyril265
body:
### What happens

If the empty last paragraph of a section doesn't fit above the page's footnotes and the next section starts on a new page, WordCraft keeps the paragraph on the page and starts the footnote area below it. The separator and the note move down about 9 pt, and the note's line ends below the bottom margin. Word keeps the paragraph on the page too, but its footnotes stay where they would be without it.

### Reproduce

[`footnote-below-margin-at-section-mark.docx`](https://github.com/cyril265/wordcraft/raw/pr-assets/fixtures/footnote-below-margin-at-section-mark.docx): A4, 56.7 pt margins, Arial 11 with 8 pt after: `Intro` with footnote 1, `Fill` with 650 pt before, `AAA`, an empty paragraph closing section 1 (next section: new page), `CCC`; footer `Footer`.

`wordcraft-cli convert footnote-below-margin-at-section-mark.docx out.pdf`

```
main: 2 pages; p1 AAA 735.6, separator 775.6, note 783.6-794.6 (bottom margin 785.2); p2 CCC
Word: 2 pages; p1 AAA 736.0, separator 767.7, note 774.5-785.5;                      p2 CCC
```

The same happens with two list items before the empty paragraph (fill 630 pt: note at 783.2 in main, 774.5 in Word).

### Cause

`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`, `place_para_in_flow`: an empty paragraph closing a section before a new page stays on a full page even when it doesn't fit (`closing_mark`). `PageBuilder::flush_notes` then starts the note area at `body_floor()`, the bottom of that paragraph's line, which is below where the notes should start, so they run past the bottom margin.

### Environment

macOS 26.6.2 (Apple silicon), `wordcraft-cli` built from main 3a4770e; Word for Mac 16.114.1.

title: Layout: an empty paragraph closing a section mid-page draws its shading (Word draws none)
author: cyril265
body:
### What happens

When an empty paragraph with shading ends a section in the middle of a page, WordCraft draws a 13.65 pt band of its shading colour. With a continuous break the empty paragraph takes no room, so the band lies under the next section's first line. Word draws no shading for this paragraph, with a continuous or a new-page break.

### Reproduce

[`shaded-empty-section-mark.docx`](https://github.com/cyril265/wordcraft/raw/pr-assets/fixtures/shaded-empty-section-mark.docx): A4, Arial 11 with 8 pt after: `Intro`, `AAA`, an empty paragraph shaded orange (`FFC000`) closing section 1 (next section continuous), `BBB`.

`wordcraft-cli convert shaded-empty-section-mark.docx out.pdf`

```
main: 1 page; BBB 101.6; orange fill 100.0-113.7 across the text width, under BBB
Word: 1 page; BBB 101.8; no fill
```

With a new-page break instead, main draws the same band on page 1 (100.0-113.7) and Word draws nothing.

### Cause

`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`, `place_para`: an empty paragraph before a continuous section (`quiet_marks`) is laid out by `place_para_in_flow`, which draws its line with the shading (`push_para`). Afterwards `place_para` gives back only its room (`pb.y`, `pb.prev`, `pb.content_bottom`), so the drawn band stays under the next paragraph. Before a new-page break the paragraph takes the ordinary path and is shaded the same way, and nothing leaves out the shading of an empty section-closing paragraph mid-page.

### Environment

macOS 26.6.2 (Apple silicon), `wordcraft-cli` built from main 3a4770e; Word for Mac 16.114.1.

title: Layout: after an empty list paragraph that closes a continuous section, the next paragraph sits 14 pt lower (Word puts it one line below the last item)
author: cyril265
body:
### What happens

Two numbered items with automatic space after are followed by an empty numbered paragraph that closes a section, and the next section is continuous. WordCraft puts the next paragraph 27.65 pt below the last item, Word 13.75 pt (one line). In Word the empty paragraph takes no room, and because it is a list item, the last item loses its 14 pt automatic space after, as it would before any other item. WordCraft also draws the label `3.` for the empty paragraph, where Word draws none.

### Reproduce

[`continuous-section-after-list-mark.docx`](https://github.com/cyril265/wordcraft/raw/pr-assets/fixtures/continuous-section-after-list-mark.docx): A4, Arial 11: `Intro`, numbered items `AAA` and `AAB` with `w:afterAutospacing`, an empty numbered paragraph closing section 1 (next section continuous), `BBB`.

`wordcraft-cli convert continuous-section-after-list-mark.docx out.pdf`

```
main: 1 page; AAB 93.6, label 3. 107.3, BBB 121.3
Word: 1 page; AAB 93.8,                 BBB 107.6
```

With the empty paragraph unnumbered, the space after stays in both (BBB 121.3 in main, 121.6 in Word).

### Cause

`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`, `place_para`: for an empty paragraph before a continuous section (`quiet_marks`) it runs `place_para_in_flow` and then restores `pb.y` and `pb.prev` to their values before it. `place_para_in_flow` had already taken the item's automatic space after off `pb.y`, because the empty paragraph is a list item. The restore puts that space back, and `BBB`, which is not a list item, keeps it.

### Environment

macOS 26.6.2 (Apple silicon), `wordcraft-cli` built from main 3a4770e; Word for Mac 16.114.1.

title: Layout: a line that ends exactly at a floating table's top stays above the table (Word moves it below)
author: cyril265
body:
### What happens

When a floating table's top is exactly at the bottom of a line, Word counts the line as touching the table and moves it below. WordCraft leaves the line above the table. For a square-wrapped shape at the same place, Word leaves the line where it is, the same as WordCraft. One twip higher, both move the line for the table and for the shape. So for tables, Word's test includes the line's bottom edge.

### Reproduce

[`table-top-at-line-bottom.docx`](https://github.com/cyril265/wordcraft/raw/pr-assets/fixtures/table-top-at-line-bottom.docx): Letter, 72 pt margins, Calibri 32 single-spaced (39.0625 pt lines, so `P4` ends at 228.25 pt), a page-relative floating table (full page width, one exact 50 pt row) first in the document at `tblpY` 4565 twips = 228.25 pt, then `P1` to `P6`.

`wordcraft-cli convert table-top-at-line-bottom.docx out.pdf`

```
main: 1 page; P4 195.7 (above the table), table 228.25-278.25, P5 284.7
Word: 1 page; table 228.3-278.4, P4 284.9 (below the table),   P5 323.9
```

The same document with other positions: `tblpY` 4564 moves `P4` in both, and 4566 leaves it in both. A shape at 228.25 leaves `P4` at 195.7 in main and 195.8 in Word. At 228.20 both move it.

### Cause

`crates/layout/src/para.rs`, `row_spans`: an area counts for a row only if `e.top < top + h`. The test is strict and is the same for tables and shapes, and the row-skipping branch in the line loop uses it too. For a floating table, Word's test includes the line's bottom edge.

### Environment

macOS 26.6.2 (Apple silicon), `wordcraft-cli` built from main 3a4770e; Word for Mac 16.114.1.

title: Layout: an object positioned relative to the line is placed from its paragraph's top (Word places it from the line that holds its anchor)
author: cyril265
body:
### What happens

Take a floating object with `wp:positionV relativeFrom="line"` whose anchor is on the second or third line of a paragraph. WordCraft places it as if the anchor were on the first line, from the paragraph's top. Word measures the offset from the top of the line that holds the anchor. This happens in a header, in a table cell and in the body.

### Reproduce

[`object-anchored-to-later-line.docx`](https://github.com/cyril265/wordcraft/raw/pr-assets/fixtures/object-anchored-to-later-line.docx): A4, Arial 11, exact 20 pt lines. The header, a one-cell table and a body paragraph each hold a three-line paragraph (`L1` to `L3`, split by line breaks). Each line anchors two 10 pt squares in front of the text, with vertical offsets of 0 and 6 pt relative to the line.

`wordcraft-cli convert object-anchored-to-later-line.docx out.pdf`

```
top of the 0 pt square  line 1  line 2  line 3
header  main:             36.0    36.0    36.0
        Word:             36.0    56.0    76.0
cell    main:            116.5   116.5   116.5
        Word:            116.5   136.5   156.5
body    main:            197.0   197.0   197.0
        Word:            197.0   217.0   237.0
```

In both, each 6 pt square sits 6 pt below its 0 pt square. With `relativeFrom="paragraph"`, Word puts every square at its line-1 position, the same as main.

### Cause

`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`, `float_rect`: the vertical start is the page or the margin for those anchors, and `y0` for every other anchor. Every caller passes the paragraph's top as `y0`: `layout_box` (headers, footers and cells, before the lines are laid out) and `anchor_floats` (body, `y0 - before`). Nothing in `crates/layout` reads `Anchor::Line`.

### Environment

macOS 26.6.2 (Apple silicon), `wordcraft-cli` built from main 3a4770e; Word for Mac 16.114.1.

author: necromancerelux-ux
body:
## Title
Feature request: embedded spreadsheet in a document (Word's Insert › Table › Excel Spreadsheet)

## Summary
WordCraft's tables are good, but there's no way to place a live, editable spreadsheet inside a document the way Word does with **Insert › Table › Excel Spreadsheet**. I'd like to propose this, either as a full embedded object or as a lighter first step (see below).

title: Watermark font name: a trailing backslash or a control character breaks the VML textpath style
author: benandez
body:
`crates/docx/src/write/watermark.rs:27` cleans the watermark font name by deleting `"`, `'`, `;` and `:`, and caps it at 100 characters. It then writes the name into the VML textpath style as `font-family:"{font}";font-size:1pt` (line 50). That stops a name from injecting style properties. It does not escape the characters that are still special inside a CSS string:

- **Backslash:** a name ending in `\` escapes the closing quote. The rest of the style (`;font-size:1pt`) is read as part of the font name, so the watermark loses its size.
- **Newline and other control characters:** a raw newline makes the CSS string invalid, so a reader may drop the `font-family` or the whole style.
- A name containing a quote is saved under a different name, because the quote is deleted instead of escaped.

Severity: minor. Nothing can be injected, but a hostile or unusual font name produces a malformed watermark.

**Suggested fix:** escape the name as a CSS string instead of deleting characters, the way #3862's `css_font_name` does for HTML export: hex-escape quotes, backslash, `;`, `,` and control characters. Keep the 100-character cap. Add a round-trip test with a trailing backslash and a newline.

Found while reviewing #3862 (#3739 is the same class of bug in HTML export).

title: Thai one-face fallback tests fail where the only Thai fonts are Noto (no Latin)
author: benandez
body:
On a Linux machine whose only Thai fonts are Noto Sans Thai, Noto Serif Thai and Noto Sans Thai Looped (Arch / CachyOS), three tests from #2175 (#1549) fail on clean main:

- `fontdb::tests::a_thai_run_with_latin_falls_back_to_one_face` (`crates/fonts`)
- `tests_complex::a_missing_thai_font_draws_the_whole_run_in_one_thai_face` (`crates/layout`)
- `tests_complex::a_thai_substitute_without_latin_hands_the_run_to_one_face_covering_it` (`crates/layout`)

The test run is `[D] น้ำ ค่ำ ปั้น ฝั่ง ปู่ ๑๒๓๔๕๖๗๘๙๐ ฿1,250.50`. The tests only check that some Thai font is installed (`fallback_for('น', 0)` / `thai_font_installed()`). The Noto Thai fonts have no Latin letters or digits, though, so no installed face covers the whole run. `fallback_for_run` then returns `None`, as its doc comment says it should. The layout keeps the per-character fallback: Thai and ฿ in Noto Sans Thai, `[D]` and the Latin digits in Source Sans 3.

This is a test bug, not a product bug. The fallback is right: no single installed face can draw the run. The tests pass on Windows (Tahoma, Leelawadee UI), macOS (Thonburi) and Linux with the TLWG fonts, which have Thai and Latin in one face.

**Fix:** skip these three tests unless the Thai substitute (`word::resolve("TH Sarabun New", …)`) covers the whole run. That check doesn't go through `fallback_for_run`, so the tests still prove it where such a font exists.

title: A command that changes nothing adds an undo step, marks the document edited and evicts the undo history
author: matstrange
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at `3a4770ef8ce037d2650c93e2d5764536549357c7`. **Severity:** Medium (the undo history loses the user's edits). **Confidence:** high — reproduced at runtime against a worktree at this commit.

This is *not* the defect of #3617 (N-09), which is what a step costs in memory. This one is that a command which changed nothing counts as one.

## Root cause and evidence
`Session::run` pushes the undo step before the command runs and marks the document edited after it succeeds. Nothing compares the document before and after.

- [`crates/engine/src/session.rs:1465-1470`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/3a4770ef8ce037d2650c93e2d5764536549357c7/crates/engine/src/session.rs#L1465-L1470) — `checkpoint(label)` for every mutating command, which also clears the redo stack (`checkpoint`, [`:1019`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/3a4770ef8ce037d2650c93e2d5764536549357c7/crates/engine/src/session.rs#L1019)).
- [`crates/engine/src/session.rs:1509`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/3a4770ef8ce037d2650c93e2d5764536549357c7/crates/engine/src/session.rs#L1509) — `self.touch()` on every `Ok`: the revision is bumped (the layout cache is dropped, so the document is laid out again) and the document is marked edited.

So a command that changes nothing — `text.insert {"text": ""}`, Backspace at the start of the document, Enter in a one-line content control — still adds an undo step, marks the document edited, forces a relayout and throws the redo stack away.

## Conditions and realistic impact
The history is bounded by step count alone: `MAX_UNDO = 500` ([`crates/engine/src/session.rs:641`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/3a4770ef8ce037d2650c93e2d5764536549357c7/crates/engine/src/session.rs#L641)). Five hundred commands that change nothing fill the whole stack, and the oldest steps are pushed out of it for good (`undo_evicted` counts them as gone). The user's own edits are then among th…

title: Ctrl+N replaces the current document instead of opening a new window
author: sch401
body:
## Description

When a document is already open, pressing **Ctrl+N** replaces it with a blank document in the same window.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open an existing document.
2. Press **Ctrl+N**.
3. The existing document is replaced by a blank document.

## Expected behavior

A new blank document opens in a separate window. The original document remains open with its editing state preserved.

## Source investigation and suggested approach

`file.new` is registered with `Mod+N`. Its handler calls `s.set_document(doc)` and clears `s.path`, which explains the replacement behavior.

A possible approach is to handle New at the desktop UI layer: when a document is already open, create a separate window with its own session. The start screen could continue using its existing window.

Ctrl+N, File → New, and template creation should use the same routing. The engine command could retain its current session-level behavior for scripts.

## Suggested validation

Check both saved documents and documents with unsaved edits. Verify that the original document's content, undo history, cursor position, and file path remain intact.

## Related issue

- #3455 — Reports the same behavior through File → New and File → Open.

title: Feature request: Support custom equation fonts
author: sch401
body:
## Request

Please add a way to choose the font used for equations, including installed or user-added math fonts such as STIX Two Math, XITS Math, and Latin Modern Math.

This would help match equations to manuscript templates and publication typography.

## Suggested behavior

- Provide an equation font selector and a document-wide default.
- Apply the selected font to mathematical symbols and structures, including fractions, radicals, integrals, and scalable brackets.
- Preserve the choice when saving and reopening a DOCX file.
- Use the same font in the editor and PDF export.
- Show the effective fallback font when the requested font is unavailable.

## Source investigation and implementation ideas

`layout_equation()` currently calls `resolve_math("Cambria Math")` directly. The existing `resolve_math(family)` function already supports a requested font family, OpenType MATH tables, and fallback fonts.

An initial implementation could:

1. Store a document-level math font in `MathProps`.
2. Expose it through the Equation tab.
3. Pass the selected font to the existing resolver.
4. Extend the DOCX math-settings reader and writer to support `m:mathPr/m:mathFont`.

Fonts with an OpenType MATH table would be a useful starting point. Normal text inside equations could retain its separate text-font setting.

## Suggested validation

Switch between two available math fonts and check fractions, radicals, large operators, and stretchy brackets. Confirm that the font choice survives DOCX reopening and appears consistently in PDF output.

title: Replace/Remove TOC leaves Word's title when a section break separates it from the entries
author: RatkoR
body:
Found in review of #4039 (#3889). Present on `main` as well.

**Document:** a TOC created by Word with its entries in two columns (the #3889 reporter's file). Word's Table of Contents control holds:

```
Table of Contents      ← TOC Heading, one-column section
(blank paragraph)
(continuous section break)
Chapter 1 … 1          ← entries, two-column section
…
```

The engine's TOC starts at the paragraph holding the `TOC` field (here the one ending the section), so the title paragraph above it isn't part of the TOC.

**Steps**
1. Open the document and run References › Update Table (`references.updateToc`).
2. Run Insert Table of Contents with settings (`references.toc` with e.g. `{"levels":2}`), or Remove Table of Contents (`references.removeToc`).

**Result**
- Replace keeps the old "Table of Contents" title and adds a new "Contents" heading inside the two-column section.
- Remove leaves the old title.

**Expected:** like Word, the TOC's title goes with the TOC when it is replaced or removed. With a replaced TOC, the new heading stays above the section break.

**To decide:** how Word places a replaced or removed TOC whose content control spans a section break (whether the break and the blank paragraph are kept). Check this black-box in Word before choosing how the engine's TOC should own a title that is separated from the field paragraph.

title: The CSV recipient-list reader has no field cap: a 38 MB file of commas costs a gigabyte
author: matstrange
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at `3a4770ef` (merged 2026-10-23). **Severity:** Medium (memory exhaustion). **Confidence:** high — measured before and after the fix on this machine, through `wordcraft-cli`.

## Root cause and evidence
[`crates/engine/src/cmd/mailings.rs:503-550`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/3a4770ef8ce037d2650c93e2d5764536549357c7/crates/engine/src/cmd/mailings.rs#L503-L550) is the CSV reader behind Select Recipients. It has no cap on the width of a record: every comma becomes a `String` in a `Vec<String>`.

```rust
} else if c == sep {
    row.push(std::mem::take(&mut cell));
}
```

The only cap in the function is on the number of records, and the field cap that does exist (`MAX_FIELDS`, 1,000) is applied **afterwards**, in `header_split`, to a list that has already been built. `header_split` then pads every record to the header's width, so the list costs its records times its width, not the number of values it holds.

The spreadsheet path reads the same data with the same caps and does it correctly: [`crates/formats/src/sheet.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/3a4770ef8ce037d2650c93e2d5764536549357c7/crates/formats/src/sheet.rs#L42-L52) keeps 1,000 columns, 2 M cells and 64 MiB of cell text.

## Conditions and impact
A CSV whose first line is one long run of commas. Every comma is a `String` (24 bytes) before it is dropped.

| Input | Peak memory | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 40,000,000 commas (38 MB) | **1,029 MB** | the list came back **empty** — every cell was blank, so the record was dropped |
| 1,000 columns over 100,000 records (605 KB) | **4,723 MB** | 100 M cells after the records were padded to the header's width |

The second shape is the auditor's N-06 measured on this machine. The file route allows a 2 GB CSV ([`crates/engine/src/io.rs:547`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/3a4770ef8ce037d2650c93e2d5764536549357c7/crates/engine/src/io.rs#L547), `MAX_READ_FILE`), s…

title: A one-core render stall (fixed), and a 1.1–1.46× speed-up from swapping dependencies
author: Ttimmahlax
body:
Hi WordCraft team 👋

We make software and hardware for home devices, and we use WordCraft every day. While doing that
we swapped some of our house technology in underneath it: a faster allocator, and pure-Rust picture
codecs.

Two things came out of it. First, we found and fixed a page-rendering stall in the renderer
WordCraft builds on. Second, WordCraft got noticeably faster, and a few other bugs turned up along
the way.

## The problem we fixed: page rendering crawls when WordCraft gets one CPU core

With the process limited to one core, rendering two pages of a 532-page document over MCP took up
to **42 s** on `main`. The output was identical; most of that time went to waiting, not working.
With two or more cores it takes about 1 s.

**Cause.** The cause is in **vello_cpu**, not WordCraft. `MultiThreadedDispatcher::flush` waits for
its worker threads by calling `try_recv()` in a loop, with no blocking, yielding or sleeping.

- When the process can use fewer cores than the render pool has threads, the spinning thread
  starves the workers it's waiting for.
- On Windows it can also be boosted above their priority.
- We confirmed this from stacks in a sister app (DeckCraft), where the same spin made PDF export
  hang for hours.
- vello_cpu 0.3.0, the latest release, still spins.

**Fix.** One line: while flushing, block on `recv()` instead of spinning. Same two pages, one core,
3 runs each, alternating builds:

| build | one core | two cores | eight cores |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 2.2 / 25.0 / 42.2 s | 1.0–1.3 s | 1.1–1.2 s |
| **with the fix** | **0.8 / 0.9 / 1.0 s** | 0.9–1.0 s | 0.8–1.0 s |

The output is byte-identical. We ship it by vendoring vello_cpu 0.2.0 with that one change in
`vendor/vello_cpu`, wired through `[patch.crates-io]` and excluded from the workspace. A
`PATCHED.md` explains it and when to drop it. We've reported it upstream as linebender/vello#2021,
and we're glad to open a PR here.

title: Edit Data (chart) should be modeless, like Word's Excel window
author: RatkoR
body:
Follow-up to #3859 (dialogs are modal).

In Word for Mac 16.114.1, Chart Design › Edit Data opens the chart's data in Excel, in a separate window. Word stays usable while it is open: you can keep typing in the document. In WordCraft, Edit Data is our own dialog, and #3859 makes it modal like every other dialog.

To match Word, Edit Data should be modeless. It can't simply be marked modeless, though. OK runs `chart.editData` on the chart that is selected when OK is pressed. If the dialog were modeless and the user selected another chart or clicked in the text first:
- another chart would get the first chart's data, or
- OK would fail because no chart is selected.

Suggested approach: the Size dialog already does this (`ChartDataForm` would follow the selection like `SizeForm::follow` in `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs_layout.rs`):
- the dialog remembers which chart it was opened for;
- it starts over, or closes, when the selection moves to another chart or away from charts;
- OK only ever edits the chart the dialog shows.

Then remove `InsertDialog::ChartData` from the modal list in `Dialog::is_modal` (`crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`), and add a test that selecting another chart while Edit Data is open never applies the stale data to it.

title: mcp --connect: keep serving when the app isn't open yet (like lightcraft-cli)
author: nicolasfalesy
body:
When an MCP client (Claude Code) starts `wordcraft-cli mcp --connect 127.0.0.1:7960` while WordCraft isn't running, the CLI exits at once ("can't reach the WordCraft app… Connection refused"), so the client marks the server failed for its whole session; opening WordCraft afterwards doesn't help until a manual reconnect.

`lightcraft-cli mcp --connect` already handles this: it answers `initialize`/`tools/list`, returns "not reachable… will retry on each call" for tool calls, and connects once the app's port opens. Could `wordcraft-cli` do the same (or offer a `--lazy` flag)? storytold/gridcraft#2280 proposes the suite-level version of this (a runtime `mcp.attach`), which would cover it too.

The two related MCP ideas (an Elicitation when the app is closed, and Tasks for long jobs) now have their own tickets: #4153 and #4154.

**Repro:** close WordCraft, add `wordcraft-cli mcp --connect 127.0.0.1:7960` as an MCP server in Claude Code, start a session: the server shows "failed" for the whole session.

**Environment:** Arch Linux, wordcraft-bin 0.10.0.

title: Feature: Add spellcheck="true" attribute to the editor container
author: libyanmahmood17-ship-it
body:
### Feature Request
Please enable native spellchecking by adding the `spellcheck="true"` attribute to the primary `contenteditable` container in WordCraft.

title: Add Greek (el_GR) to supported Hunspell languages
author: chvourliotis-max
body:
## Summary
Greek is not available as a proofing language. A valid el_GR Hunspell
dictionary placed in the user dictionaries folder is never detected,
because the app only looks for a fixed list of locales.

## Environment
- WordCraft 0.8.0 (AppImage, x86_64)
- Fedora Kinoite (immutable Fedora)

## What I see
Options → Proofing → Dictionaries folder is ~/.local/share/hunspell/.
The help text says only pl_PL, pt_BR, it_IT, hr_HR and tr_TR are read
from there, and the status list shows Polish, Portuguese (Brazil),
Italian, Croatian, Turkish, Russian, Czech and Indonesian.
Greek is missing there and in Options → Language.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Put el_GR.aff and el_GR.dic in ~/.local/share/hunspell/
2. Open Options → Proofing and click Apply
3. No Greek entry appears, and Greek is not offered in Options → Language

## Workaround (partially works)
- Downloaded el_GR from the LibreOffice dictionaries repo.
  It declares "SET ISO8859-7".
- Converted both files to UTF-8 with iconv and changed the line to
  "SET UTF-8".
- Copied them as tr_TR.aff / tr_TR.dic and set the document language
  to Turkish.

Result:
- Spell checking works: "καλημέρα" is accepted, "καλημαρα" and "σπητι"
  are marked as misspelled.
- No suggestions are offered ("(no suggestions)"), even for
  one-letter errors like "σπητι" (should suggest "σπίτι").
- The language shows as Turkish, and grammar messages are in Turkish
  (e.g. "Cümle büyük harfle başlar").

## Request
1. Add el_GR to the supported locales, including in Options → Language.
2. Pick up el_GR.aff/.dic from the user dictionaries folder.
3. Handle legacy encodings such as ISO8859-7 declared in the .aff,
   or at least document that dictionaries must be UTF-8.
4. Make suggestions work for non-Latin dictionaries.

Thank you for the great work on WordCraft!

title: Bug Report: Inconsistent Mouse Cursor Behavior Around the Document Page
author: TekkaDmgz
body:
The mouse cursor does not change consistently between the text cursor (I-beam) and the arrow pointer when moving between the document page and the surrounding area.

In Microsoft Word, the cursor changes naturally depending on the mouse position:

- When the mouse is over the document page, the cursor changes to the I-beam, indicating where text can be edited.
- When the mouse is outside the document page, the cursor changes to the normal arrow pointer.

In Wordcraft, this behavior appears to be inconsistent.

Observed Behavior

Left side of the document: When the mouse is outside the page, the I-beam cursor appears instead of the arrow. When moving onto the left part of the page, the cursor changes to the arrow instead of the I-beam.

Inside the document: Further into the document, the I-beam cursor appears as expected.

Right side of the document: When moving outside the page, the cursor remains an I-beam instead of changing to the arrow. Moving back onto the page does not trigger the expected cursor change either.

Expected Behavior

The cursor should behave consistently across the entire document page:

- Outside the page: display the normal arrow pointer.
- Over the editable document area: display the I-beam text cursor.

This behavior should be consistent on both the left and right sides of the page, as well as when moving between the page and the surrounding workspace.

Why This Matters

The inconsistent cursor behavior can be confusing for users because the cursor does not accurately indicate whether they are outside the document or positioned to edit text. Matching the familiar behavior of Microsoft Word would make Wordcraft feel more intuitive and improve the editing experience.

Thank you for your work on Wordcraft!

**Steps to reproduce:**

title: Drop cap from a paragraph style: Drop Cap menu 'keep' ignores it and None can't turn it off
author: dkhlapov
body:
Found while reviewing PR #4077 (Drop Cap follow-ups for #2601). Both points concern a drop cap that comes from a paragraph style instead of being set on the paragraph itself.

**1. `keep: true` ignores a style's drop cap.** The Insert › Drop Cap menu (Dropped / In margin) sends `insert.dropCap` with `keep: true` so each selected paragraph keeps its own lines, distance and font. "Has a drop cap" is read from the paragraph's own properties only, so a paragraph whose drop cap comes from its style gets the defaults (3 lines, distance 0, no font) instead of the style's values.

**2. `position: "none"` can't turn off a style's drop cap.** None clears the paragraph's own drop-cap properties, but an unset property falls back to the style, so the style's drop cap stays.

**Suggested approach.** Give the paragraph an explicit "off" value (a zero-line drop cap) that resolve, layout and the DOCX writer all understand: resolve treats 0 as no drop cap and does not fall through to the style; the DOCX writer and reader round-trip it. With that, `keep` can read the resolved (effective) values.

Both limits predate #4077 (None has never overridden a style's drop cap), so this is a separate, small change touching `crates/doc/src/resolve.rs`, `crates/layout/src/para.rs`, the DOCX read/write and `insert.dropCap` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs`.

title: English proofing: common contextual grammar and word-selection errors are not flagged
author: stetchman2000-source
body:
Follow-up from the proofing benchmark in #4148, split out as requested for separate tracking.

## Environment

- WordCraft CLI: **0.10.0**
- Platform: Windows
- Test format: `.docx`
- Command:

```powershell
wordcraft-cli run --file .\test_corpus.docx --cmd 'review.issues={}' --print
```

## Problem

Several common English contextual word-selection, agreement and verb-form errors produced no finding from `review.issues`.

## Reproduction examples

The following sentences were not flagged:

```text
Their going to submit the report tomorrow.

The new policy will effect employee morale.

The server lost it's connection during the test.

Please put the boxes over they're by the door.

The principle reason for the delay was a failed build.

The list of defects are attached to the ticket.

Each of the engineers have completed the review.

Yesterday we deploy the patch and restarted the service.

She has went through every regression test twice.

Neither the logs nor the screenshot explain why the application crash.
```

Expected corrections include:

```text
Their → They're
effect → affect
it's → its
they're → there
principle → principal
are → is
have → has
deploy → deployed
went → gone
```

The final example also contains agreement/verb-form problems:

```text
Neither the logs nor the screenshot explain why the application crash.
```

## Comparison

For comparison only, Microsoft Word Editor detected several of these in the same unmodified DOCX, including:

- `effect → affect`
- `it's → its`
- `principle → principal`
- `are → is`
- `deploy → deployed`
- `went → gone`

The intention here isn't to require Microsoft Word parity, but to provide compact regression examples for contextual English proofing.

## Expected behaviour

`review.issues` should identify common contextual errors where the individual token may be correctly spelled but is incorrect in the sentence context.

Parent benchmark: #4148

title: MCP: ask to open WordCraft (Elicitation) when a tool is called while it's closed
author: nicolasfalesy
body:
Split out of #4078, as ticket-craft asked.

When an MCP client calls a WordCraft tool while the app isn't open, the server could send an MCP Elicitation ("WordCraft isn't open. Open it?") instead of failing the call. On yes, it would launch the app, wait for its port, and then run the tool.

This needs the deferred `--connect` startup from #4078 first, so the server is still alive when the app is closed. It also needs a client that supports Elicitation; where the client doesn't, the current error stays.

The same would help DeckCraft, GridCraft and the other suite apps (storytold/deckcraft#1248, storytold/gridcraft#2280).

title: MCP: Tasks for long jobs such as exports and batch renders
author: nicolasfalesy
body:
Split out of #4078, as ticket-craft asked.

Long jobs such as a DOCX/PDF export of a big document, or a batch render, currently hold the MCP tool call open until they finish. MCP Tasks would let the server return a task handle at once and report progress and the result later, so the client can keep working and isn't cut off by a request timeout.

The same would help DeckCraft, GridCraft and the other suite apps (storytold/deckcraft#1248, storytold/gridcraft#2280).

title: Drop cap In margin: indents move to the cap's paragraph and push the letter right (Word behaviour)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Follow-up to #4077 (Drop Cap Options dialog). Not covered by #4144, which is about drop caps that come from a paragraph style.

Black-box observation of Word for Mac 16.114 (A4, 2.54 cm margins, Insert > Drop Cap > In margin, 3 lines, distance 0 cm). Positions are cm from the left page edge, accuracy about ±0.1 cm.

**What Word does when "In margin" meets indents**
- A hanging or first-line indent is removed from the text paragraph and kept only on the drop cap's own frame paragraph, so every text line then starts at the same position. The first line therefore moves (hanging 1.27 cm: first line moves right by 1.27 cm; first-line indent: first line moves left about 0.5 cm, lines 2-3 right about 0.8 cm).
- A left indent stays on the text paragraph and is also copied to the cap's paragraph.
- Centre and right alignment are copied to the cap's paragraph but do not move the letter, and the text keeps its alignment.
- The cap's frame is anchored to the page, so the cap paragraph's indents push the letter right: a 2.54 cm left indent moves it about 2.0 cm; a 1.27 cm hanging or first-line indent moves it about 0.75 cm. With a first-line indent the letter then overlaps the text area and the text wraps around it.
- No indent, centred and right-aligned: the letter sits in the margin with its right edge at the margin line, and wrapping is unchanged.

**What WordCraft should do**: match the above when applying or removing an in-margin cap (indent move, letter position, wrapping), with tests for each case.

Full notes and screenshots: Word check 2026-10-24-4077 (kept locally under plan/word/results).

title: Find & Replace: full regular-expression support for proofreaders
author: benandez
body:
## Summary
A user who works as a proofreader and layout designer reported on Discord that, for them, a word processor without a proper regular-expression engine is unusable. They compare it with the KDE Kile/KTextEditor regex support, which is close to Perl's. Word itself has only "Use wildcards". WordCraft can go further.

This issue tracks regex Find & Replace support. The specific pieces are sub-issues.

## What exists today (main)
- Find & Replace › More › **Regular expressions** (`crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs:2103`), and `"regex": true` on `edit.find` / `edit.replace` / `edit.replaceAll` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs:109`).
- The engine is `regex-automata` `meta::Regex`: groups, named groups, Unicode classes (`\p{Lu}`), inline flags (`(?i)`), repetition (`{2,}`). Searches have a work budget (#2773).
- Word-style **Use wildcards**, where `\1` groups do expand in Replace.

Checked with `wordcraft-cli run … --cmd 'edit.replaceAll={…,"regex":true}'`:
| Pattern | Replace | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ` {2,}` | ` ` | ✅ runs of spaces collapse |
| `(?i)SMITH` | `S` | ✅ |
| `(\w+), (\w+)` | `\2 \1` / `$2 $1` | ❌ inserted literally (sub-issue: Replace groups) |
| `(?<y>\d{4})-` | `${y}/` | ❌ inserted literally |
| `\b(\w+) \1\b` | `\1` | ❌ "bad pattern" (sub-issue: backreferences/lookaround) |
| `(?<=Doe, )J\w+` | `X` | ❌ "bad pattern" |

## Reporter's follow-up
They need "everything regex can", especially lookbehind/lookahead and recursion. They currently use LibreOffice Writer, which has a decent regex engine but can't match across lines (multiline), unlike Perl or KTextEditor.

## Sub-issues
- [ ] #4177 Regex Replace: expand capture groups
- [ ] #4178 Regex Find: backreferences and lookaround (the main gap for the reporter)
- [ ] #4179 Regex across paragraphs (multiline mode)
- [ ] #4180 Recursion / subroutine calls and the rest of PCRE (engine decision)

A maintainer may want to attach these as GitHub sub-issues (the filer has no write access).

title: Regex Replace: expand capture groups ($1, ${name}, \1)
author: benandez
body:
Part of #4176.

## Problem
With **Regular expressions** on, the Replace text is inserted literally. Capture groups are never expanded:
- `(\w+), (\w+)` → `\2 \1` gives `\2 \1`, and `$2 $1` gives `$2 $1`.
- `(?<y>\d{4})-` → `${y}/` gives `${y}/`.

Cause: `find_pattern::parse_replace` returns the whole Replace text as one literal piece when `o.regex` is set (`crates/engine/src/find_pattern.rs:356`). Yet the regex search already fills `caps` and passes a `group` closure to `find_pattern::expand` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs:548-551`), so only the parsing is missing.

## Expected
In regex mode, Replace supports:
- `$1`…`$n`, `${name}`, `$$` for a literal `$`, and `$0` / `${0}` for the whole match (the `regex` crate's syntax).
- `\1`…`\9` as an alias (KTextEditor, sed and Word wildcards users expect it).
- `^&`, `^p`, `^t` and `^c` still work as they do now.

Unknown or out-of-range groups expand to nothing and never panic.

## Acceptance
- Engine tests for each form above, including named, missing and out-of-range groups.
- `hostile_params_never_panic` stays green.
- Find & Replace dialog: Replace All with groups works (ui test).
- `docs/` updated: the Find & Replace behaviour and the parity docs.

title: Regex Find: backreferences and lookaround (Perl-style), with a backtrack limit
author: benandez
body:
Part of #4176.

## Problem
The regex engine (`regex-automata` `meta::Regex`) rejects Perl-style features that proofreaders rely on. Both come back as "bad pattern: error parsing pattern 0":
- **Backreferences in the pattern:** `\b(\w+) \1\b` (find doubled words), `(["'])…\1` (find matching quotes).
- **Lookaround:** `(?<=Doe, )J\w+`, `\d+(?= pt)`, `(?<!\.)\.\.(?!\.)` (find two dots but not an ellipsis).

The reporter compares this with KDE Kile/KTextEditor and says that, for them, a word processor without this is unusable. The reporter considers this the main gap.

## Why it's missing
`regex` / `regex-automata` leave out backreferences and lookaround on purpose, so a search always finishes quickly (linear time). Adding them needs a backtracking engine.

## Suggested approach
- Use a pure-Rust backtracking engine for patterns that need it, for example `fancy-regex`. It delegates to `regex` when a pattern needs no backtracking, so ordinary patterns keep today's engine. Its licence and wasm build need checking (`cargo xtask wasm`).
- Never crash, and never hang: set a backtrack limit (`fancy_regex::RegexBuilder::backtrack_limit`) and keep the cumulative search budget from #2773. A pathological pattern must return an error ("pattern too complex"), not freeze the UI or the MCP server.
- Same Find options and paragraph handling as today. Replace groups come from the sibling sub-issue.
- Tell the user which syntax is supported (dialog tooltip or help, and docs).

**Decide together with #4180:** recursion (which the reporter also asked for) is beyond `fancy-regex`. If #4180 picks an engine with recursion, it covers this issue too, so the engine choice should be made once for both.

## Acceptance
- Tests: doubled words, matched quotes, lookbehind and lookahead, and a catastrophic pattern such as `(a+)+$` on a long input returns the budget error quickly.
- `hostile_params_never_panic` stays green.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes, including wasm and assets/licences for the new depen…

title: Regex Find & Replace across paragraphs (multiline mode)
author: benandez
body:
Part of #4176.

## Problem
In regex mode a match can't cross a paragraph mark. With two paragraphs `…ends here` and `next line…`, none of these find anything:
`here\nnext`, `here\rnext`, `here\s+next`, `here^pnext`, `(?s)here.next`

In plain and wildcard modes, a pattern with `^p` already reads consecutive paragraphs as one text (`spans_paras` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs`, around line 464). Regex mode never does.

`^` and `$` already match at paragraph edges (`(?m)^next`, `here$` and `^third$` work), so per-paragraph anchors are fine.

The reporter uses LibreOffice Writer for now, which has "a decent regex interpreter, but cannot work in multiline mode, unlike Perl or… my notepad". Working across paragraphs is a reason to choose WordCraft over Writer.

## Expected
- In regex mode, a paragraph mark is a matchable character. `\n` matches it; decide whether `^p` and `\r` do too. `\s` and `(?s).` then match across paragraphs, as in Perl/KTextEditor.
- `(?m)`: `^`/`$` at paragraph edges (today's behaviour). Without `(?m)`, decide whether they anchor to the story's start and end as in Perl, and document the choice.
- Replace across paragraphs: deleting or inserting a mark merges or splits paragraphs the same way `^p` replacements do today, keeps the first paragraph's formatting, and is a single undo step.
- Matches stay inside one story and one table cell. Tracked-deleted text is skipped, as now.
- The same budget and caps as today (#2773; at most 100,000 matches).

## Acceptance
- Engine tests: find across 2 and 3 paragraphs, replace a mark with a space (join), replace a space with `\n` (split), and lists, headings and table cells at the edges.
- `hostile_params_never_panic` stays green. Docs and parity docs updated.

title: Regex recursion and subroutine calls ((?R), (?1)) and the full PCRE feature set
author: benandez
body:
Part of #4176.

## Problem
The reporter needs "everything regex can", and named recursion in particular. PCRE-style recursion and subroutine calls are rejected today: `(a(?1)?b)` gives "bad pattern", and `(?R)` silently finds nothing. Typical uses: balanced brackets and quotes (`\((?:[^()]++|(?R))*\)`), nested markup.

## Engine choice (needs a maintainer decision)
- `fancy-regex` (proposed in #4178 for backreferences and lookaround) has **no** recursion.
- `pcre2` (Rust bindings to the C PCRE2 library) has the full feature set: recursion, conditionals, `\K`, possessive quantifiers and atomic groups. But it pulls a C build into `engine`, which probably breaks `wasm32-unknown-unknown` (`cargo xtask wasm`). The licence is BSD-3, which is fine.
- A pure-Rust engine that does recursion: none mature that I know of. The other option is to write our own backtracker over the existing `regex-syntax` parse, extended with recursion.

Whichever is chosen, it must keep the never-crash rules: a backtrack/recursion depth limit, the cumulative budget (#2773), and an error rather than a hang or stack overflow on pathological patterns.

## Acceptance
- Balanced parentheses and nested quotes found correctly. A deeply nested or catastrophic pattern returns a "too complex" error quickly. No stack overflow.
- Native and wasm builds both pass, or wasm falls back to the non-recursive engine with a clear "not supported in the browser" error.
- Docs list the exact syntax supported.

title: .doc import drops tracked changes: deleted and inserted text both show as plain text
author: sarsonj
body:
## Summary

Opening a Word 97–2003 `.doc` file that contains tracked changes shows the deleted and the inserted text side by side as ordinary text. The revisions are lost on import, so the document looks garbled. Word shows the same file correctly (All Markup, No Markup or Original).

## Example

A paragraph where *Alice Smith* was deleted and *Bob Jones* inserted, and a date changed from `1. 7.` to `30. 8.`, imports as:

```
Alice SmithBob Jones
… concluded on 130. 87. 2013 …
```

Here the characters of the old and new date are interleaved. The DOCX written from it has no `<w:ins>` / `<w:del>` at all, so the loss happens in the reader, not in layout or rendering.

## Cause

`crates/docbin` has no revision handling. `fmt::apply_char` (`crates/docbin/src/fmt.rs`) drops the revision-mark sprms in its `_ => {}` arm ([MS-DOC] §2.6.1):

| sprm | meaning |
|---|---|
| `0x0801` sprmCFRMarkIns | run is a tracked insertion |
| `0x4804` sprmCIbstRMark / `0x6805` sprmCDttmRMark | insertion author index / date (DTTM) |
| `0x0800` sprmCFRMarkDel | run is a tracked deletion |
| `0x4863` sprmCIbstRMarkDel / `0x6864` sprmCDttmRMarkDel | deletion author index / date (DTTM) |

The author table `SttbfRMark` (`fcSttbfRMark` / `lcbSttbfRMark` in the FIB) is not read either.

A real-world file checked locally carries 30 insertion runs and 25 deletion runs, each with author and date, and all of them import as plain text.

The document model already supports this: `CharProps.ins` / `del` index into `Document::revisions`, and the paragraph mark has the same fields. The DOCX reader fills them, so display, Accept/Reject and DOCX save would work once the `.doc` reader does too.

## Fix plan

1. Recognise the six sprms above when applying CHPX grpprls and piece Prms.
2. Read `SttbfRMark` (a Unicode Sttb) for author names.
3. Convert DTTM (minute, hour, day, month, year − 1900, weekday bit fields) to an ISO date.
4. Deduplicate `(kind, author, date)` into `doc.revisions` and set `ins` / `del` on…

title: .doc import ignores the text language: Czech documents are proofed as English
author: sarsonj
body:
## Summary

A Word 97–2003 `.doc` file imports with no text language at all. The proofing language falls back to the default (here English (United States)), so a Czech document is spell-checked as English and almost every word is underlined. Word shows the same file as Czech in the status bar, with no spelling marks.

## Cause

`crates/docbin` has no language handling. `fmt::apply_char` (`crates/docbin/src/fmt.rs`) drops the language sprms in its `_ => {}` arm, so `CharProps.lang` / `lang_ea` / `lang_bidi` stay `None` for runs and for styles ([MS-DOC] §2.6.1):

| sprm | meaning | `CharProps` field |
|---|---|---|
| `0x486D` sprmCRgLid0_80, `0x4873` sprmCRgLid0 | Latin text language (LCID) | `lang` |
| `0x486E` sprmCRgLid1_80, `0x4874` sprmCRgLid1 | East Asian language | `lang_ea` |
| `0x485F` sprmCLidBi | complex-script language | `lang_bidi` |

In a real-world Czech file checked locally, the document default comes from a style CHPX with `sprmCRgLid0 = 0x0405` (cs-CZ), and a few runs carry `0x0409` (en-US). Word's own DOCX conversion of the same file has `w:lang w:val="cs-CZ" w:eastAsia="cs-CZ" w:bidi="ar-SA"` in its defaults and `en-US` on a few runs. WordCraft ends up with none of them.

## Fix plan

1. Map the sprms above to `lang` / `lang_ea` / `lang_bidi` in `apply_char`, both for runs and for style CHPXs (stsh).
2. Add an LCID → BCP 47 tag table (e.g. `0x0405` → `cs-CZ`, `0x0409` → `en-US`, `0x0804` → `zh-CN`, `0x0401` → `ar-SA`) from the public [MS-LCID] specification. No such mapping exists in the repo yet. Unknown LCIDs and the "no proofing" values (`0x0400`, `0x0000`) leave the field unset.
3. Regression test with a synthetic `.doc` in `crates/docbin/src/tests.rs`: style default plus a run override, checking the resolved run language.
4. Update `docs/file-format-parity.md` and `docs/localization-parity.md`.

Found while looking at #4187 (tracked changes in `.doc`); same reader, separate fix.

title: Layout: a no-break space (U+00A0) takes the font's own glyph width; Word lays it out as wide as a space
author: janvier-s
body:
## Summary

WordCraft shapes U+00A0 with the font's own glyph. In some fonts that glyph is much wider than the space. In Lucida Bright, which ships with Word, `uni00A0` is 1246/2048 em and `space` is 623/2048 em, so it is twice as wide. Word lays a no-break space out as wide as an ordinary space. In WordCraft, text that uses no-break spaces gets wider and wraps where it doesn't in Word.

This is common in French, where a no-break space goes before `:`, `;`, `?`, `!` and `»`. In the document that prompted this (a liturgical booklet, A5), `P :` / `R :` labels sit in narrow table columns. With the wide glyph, `P :` measures 15.19 pt instead of 11.99 pt, so the colon wraps under the letter. Those taller rows then make a vertically centred cell taller, and the text moves away from the pictures anchored beside it.

Fonts in Word's bundled set and in macOS's Supplemental fonts whose U+00A0 is wider than their space include Lucida Bright (all styles), Lucida Sans, Lucida Fax, Bookman Old Style Italic, Baskerville Old Face, Perpetua Italic/Bold and Arial Narrow Bold. That's 50 of 426 fonts checked.

## Repro

[nbsp_width.docx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33913862/nbsp_width.docx) (script below), in Lucida Bright 10.5 pt:

1. `|` + ten U+00A0 + `|` above `|` + ten spaces + `|`.
2. A fixed-layout table whose first column holds 12.45 pt of text, with `P :` followed by a colon, once with a no-break space and once with an ordinary space.

| | Word | WordCraft (main @ 9d1067f) |
|---|---|---|
| The bars in 1 | line up | the no-break line is about 32 pt wider |
| `P :` with U+00A0 | one line | `:` wraps onto a second line |
| `P :` with a space | one line | one line |

Evidence from the real document: replacing the three U+00A0 in those labels with ordinary spaces makes WordCraft's page match Word's exactly, and Word draws both kinds of label at the same width.

## Where it happens

title: Layout: a bookmark is a line-break opportunity; a word that doesn't fit after a bookmark leaves a blank line
author: janvier-s
body:
## Summary

Bookmarks (`w:bookmarkStart` / `w:bookmarkEnd`) sit in a paragraph's text as U+FFFC. When break opportunities are found with `unicode_linebreak::linebreaks`, U+FFFC has the line-break class CB, and UAX #14 rule LB20 allows a break before and after it. So a bookmark is a place where a line can wrap. In Word a bookmark is not part of the text and never changes where a line breaks.

When a word that follows a bookmark doesn't fit, WordCraft breaks after the bookmark. The first line holds only the invisible bookmark, so it looks blank, and the word starts on the next line. A bookmark inside a word can also split the word there.

In the document that prompted this, two `OLE_LINK` bookmarks come before `P :` in a narrow table cell. Combined with #4192, the cell had three lines: a blank one, `P `, then `:`. Word draws a single line.

## Repro

[bookmark_break.docx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33913878/bookmark_break.docx) (script below): fixed-layout tables whose first column is too narrow for "Oremus" (Lucida Bright 10.5 pt).

| Row | Word | WordCraft (main @ 9d1067f) |
|---|---|---|
| "Oremus", no bookmark | the word breaks inside, no blank line | same |
| two bookmarks, then "Oremus" | same as the row above | a blank first line, then the word |
| "Ore" + bookmark + "mus" | same as the first row | wraps at the bookmark |

## Where it happens

`crates/layout/src/para.rs`, around line 1785: the break opportunities from `unicode_linebreak::linebreaks(&text)` include the ends of U+FFFC characters that are bookmarks (`ClKind::Marker` clusters), and `break_after` is set from them. One possible fix: when collecting break opportunities, ignore the marker objects (bookmarks, comment anchors, and other zero-width objects with no visible content), for example by leaving them out of `text` the way hidden text already is, mapped back through `ends`. Pictures and other visible inline objects keep their LB20 breaks.

title: Dragging a picture: a bold drop caret, the anchor mark and live text reflow
author: RatkoR
body:
When you drag a picture, WordCraft gives too little feedback about where it will land, so you drop it blindly and then move it again. Split out of #4068, which is about Position options and captions.

## What Word does (Word for Mac 16.114.1, observed by hand)
- **In Line with Text:** while dragging, a caret follows the pointer in the text and shows where the picture will land. It is a bold version of the normal caret, so it is easy to see.
- **Square wrapping (floating):** when the picture is selected, an anchor icon sits left of the paragraph it is anchored to. While dragging, the paragraphs reflow around the picture live, so you see where it and the text will end up. No caret is shown.

## What WordCraft does
1. **Inline:** a thin dashed insertion cursor (1.5 px, 2 px dashes; `paint_drop_caret` in `crates/ui-egui/src/objects.rs`), hard to see on the page.
2. **Floating, selected:** no anchor mark anywhere. The drop anchors the picture to the paragraph under its top edge (`move_object` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/objects.rs`), but nothing shows which paragraph that is.
3. **Floating, dragging:** only the picture's image and frame move. The text is laid out again after the drop.

## Plan
1. A solid, bold drop caret for In Line with Text pictures (first PR).
2. An anchor mark (drawn in code) beside the anchor paragraph of a selected floating object, which moves during a drag to the paragraph it would anchor to.
3. Live text reflow while dragging a floating object. Larger: the layout has to run with the object at a temporary place on every drag step, without stuttering in long documents.

Related: #4068, #2799 (live preview while dragging text and tables).

title: DOCX: Arabic text shows at 10 pt in Word because styles set w:sz but no w:szCs (WordCraft's own render hides it)
author: jneaimi
body:
WordCraft 0.10.0 (CLI, macOS universal and Linux x86_64).

**What happens**

A new document's `docDefaults` and built-in styles set the Latin size only (`w:sz`), never the complex-script size (`w:szCs`). For example, the Title style holds `<w:sz w:val="56"/>` and no `<w:szCs>`. A right-to-left run (`<w:rtl/>`, Arabic) is sized by `w:szCs` in Microsoft Word and LibreOffice. With none anywhere in the style chain, Arabic falls back to 10 pt, so a 28 pt Arabic title, its headings and its body text all show at 10 pt there.

WordCraft's own render, PNG and PDF, draws the same runs at the `w:sz` size. The document therefore looks right in WordCraft and wrong in Word. Anything that checks WordCraft's previews cannot see the problem.

**Repro** (`wordcraft-cli run --script repro.json`):

```json
{"commands": [
 {"command": "para.style", "params": {"style": "Title"}}, {"command": "para.rtl", "params": {"value": true}},
 {"command": "text.insert", "params": {"text": "مذكرة: تجديد عقد المكتب"}}, {"command": "text.newParagraph"},
 {"command": "para.style", "params": {"style": "Normal"}}, {"command": "para.rtl", "params": {"value": true}},
 {"command": "text.insert", "params": {"text": "ينتهي عقد المكتب في ٣١ ديسمبر."}}
], "save": ["w-size.docx", "w-size.png"]}
```

- In `w-size.png` the title is about 28 pt.
- Converted with LibreOffice (`soffice --headless --convert-to pdf w-size.docx`), the title and the paragraph are both 10 pt.
- `word/styles.xml` has `<w:sz w:val="56"/>` on Title and no `w:szCs` anywhere.

**Expected**

- The default styles and `docDefaults` set `w:szCs` beside `w:sz`, as Word's own Normal template does.
- The renderer sizes complex-script runs by `w:szCs`, as Word does, so previews match Word.

Workaround: `styles.modify` with `chr: { size, sizeCs }` on every style. We found this making Arabic documents with WordCraft headlessly; 18 of 18 Arabic files were affected.

title: DOCX: built-in table styles set w:b without w:bCs, so Arabic header rows are not bold in Word
author: jneaimi
body:
WordCraft 0.10.0.

**What happens**

The built-in table styles WordCraft writes give the header row bold for Latin text only. For example, in `Grid Table 4 – Blue`, the `<w:tblStylePr w:type="firstRow">` run properties are `<w:b/><w:color w:val="FFFFFF"/>`, with no `<w:bCs/>`. Word and LibreOffice make a right-to-left (Arabic) run bold only through `w:bCs`, so an Arabic table's header row is plain in Word, while WordCraft draws it bold.

**Repro**

```

```

Then type Arabic into the header with `para.rtl` true, and save as DOCX. Open `word/styles.xml` and find `GridTable4AccentBlue`: its firstRow `rPr` has no `bCs`.

**Expected**

`w:bCs` beside `w:b` (and `w:iCs` beside `w:i`) wherever a style sets them, as Word's built-in table styles do.

title: Linux builds lay out Arabic differently from macOS (and Word): Arial's Arabic falls back to Noto Sans Arabic
author: jneaimi
body:
WordCraft 0.10.0, the CLI on Linux x86_64 (Debian, in a container with no Microsoft fonts) and macOS universal.

**What happens**

The same DOCX command script gives different page counts on the two platforms when its text is Arabic in Arial:
- a one-page Arabic memo renders as 2 pages on Linux;
- it renders as 1 page on macOS, which matches LibreOffice and Word.

`pdffonts` on the two PDFs shows why:
- On Linux, Arial's Arabic is drawn with the bundled Noto Sans Arabic, and Calibri with Carlito.
- On macOS it uses the system's Arial.

Noto Sans Arabic sets noticeably wider and taller than Arial's Arabic, so lines wrap earlier and the page count grows.

This may be expected font substitution, but it matters for anyone using WordCraft's page count or previews on a server to judge how a document will look in Word.

**Ask**

- Could the Linux fallback for Arial's Arabic be a metric-closer face?
- Or could `info`, or the render output, say when a substitute was used for a complex-script font, so callers know the page count is approximate?

title: Tables: in an autofit table, a hanging-indent paragraph widens its column by the whole left indent
author: janvier-s
body:
## Summary

In a table whose widths follow its content (`tblLayout` not fixed), a column is widened to its longest word. To measure that, WordCraft adds the paragraph's indents to the word, using `indent_left + indent_right + max(indent_first, 0)`. With a hanging indent (`w:ind w:left="600" w:hanging="600"`), `indent_first` is negative and the first line starts at 0, but the whole left indent is still added. A one-word label in a hanging-indent paragraph then widens its column by the full indent, and the other columns give up the difference.

In Word the column keeps its grid width as long as the text fits where it is actually laid out.

Found on a liturgical booklet (A5), where `R :` / `S :` labels in a 24 pt column have `w:left="282" w:hanging="282"`. WordCraft widens that column to 38.6 pt: 13.67 for the label + 14.1 for the indent + 10.8 for the cell margins. (The 13.67 is itself too wide because of #4192.) The Latin text beside it then wraps more, and the table runs onto the next page.

## Repro

[autofit_hanging.docx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33914048/autofit_hanging.docx) (script below): two autofit tables, grid 600 / 3000 twips, `tcW` matching. The first column holds `R:` (Arial 10 pt, about 10 pt wide). The second table's `R:` has `w:ind w:left="600" w:hanging="600"`.

| | Word | WordCraft (main @ 9d1067f) |
|---|---|---|
| no indent | 30 / 150 pt | 30 / 150 pt |
| hanging indent | 30 / 150 pt | **50.8** / 129.2 pt |

50.8 = 10 (`R:`) + 30 (the whole left indent) + 10.8 (cell margins).

## Where it happens

`crates/layout/src/table.rs`: `para_content` (line 1212), and the same formula at lines 80 and 136. The longest word could be measured where it is laid out: on the first line at `indent_left + indent_first`, on later lines at `indent_left`. That gives `max(first-line words) + max(indent_left + indent_first, 0)` and `max(other words) + indent_left`. A paragraph whose only word is on the first line would then need no extra room for a hangi…

title: Tables: in an autofit table, a spanning cell's longest word is split evenly over its columns, so a narrow spanned column takes width from the others
author: janvier-s
body:
## Summary

In a table whose widths follow its content (`tblLayout` not fixed), `column_content` gives the narrowest width of a cell that spans several grid columns to those columns in equal shares. Their own widths are ignored. A cell spanning a wide and a narrow grid column (2600 + 300 twips here) then puts half its longest word on the narrow column. That column now seems too narrow, and `autofit` takes the difference from every other column, even though the span as a whole has plenty of room.

In Word the columns keep their grid widths: the cell's longest word fits in the span.

Found on a liturgical booklet (A5): a Latin / French table whose French cells span grid columns of 2632 + 331 twips. Every other column shrinks to give the 331-twip column half of the French text's longest word, and the narrow label column ends up narrower than its own text.

## Repro

[autofit_span.docx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33914058/autofit_span.docx) (script below): two autofit tables with the same widths. The first has grid 3000 / 2900 twips. The second has grid 3000 / 2600 / 300 twips, and its second cell spans the last two columns. That cell starts with "Incomprehensibilities" (Arial 10 pt, about 100 pt), which fits in the 145 pt span.

| | Word | WordCraft (main @ 9d1067f) |
|---|---|---|
| second cell in one grid column | 150 / 145 pt | 150 / 145 pt |
| second cell spanning two grid columns | 150 / 145 pt | **131.5** / 163.5 pt |

## Where it happens

`crates/layout/src/table.rs`, `column_content`, lines 1147–1155: `c.0 += (need.0 - have_lo).max(0.0) / n`. `have_lo` is the spanned columns' own content minimums, which are zero when only spanning cells cover them. So the whole need is split evenly, however wide each column is in the grid. One option: share the need beyond the spanned columns' minimums in proportion to their grid widths, so a span that already fits in the grid makes no column look short. (#3406 may be related: a narrow column under a spanning cel…

title: Follow-ups from the #4194 batch
author: aiongg
body:
Follow-ups from the review of the batch merged in #4194. None of them blocked the merge.

## Pictures
- [ ] #4171: TIFFs with JPEG compression (compression 7) are refused. Existing ones no longer show on screen or in PDF, RTF export drops them without a word, and Insert refuses them; scanners write these. A fix: walk the strip or tile offsets with JPEGTables and accept each strip whose SOF fits it and the decode budget.
- [ ] #4171: the size ceiling is about 44–59 MP in some formats.
- [ ] #4171: Windows paste (CF_DIBV5 and PNG only) needs a check by hand.

- [ ] #4133: `format.highlight` with no colour toggles, and `{"color": null}` is an error. Decide between toggle and apply.
- [ ] #4099: a yellow line shows above the colour swatch; use the no-colour highlight icon when a swatch is drawn.

## Read Mode

- [ ] #4172: the page colour resets each time Read Mode opens; the reference app keeps it.
- [ ] #4172: some names reach `tl!` as variables.

- [ ] #4079: WordCraft writes UTC in `w:date`. Writing local time there and UTC in `w16cex:dateUtc` would match what other apps expect.

- [ ] #4113: the "Set left- and first-indent with tabs and backspaces" option is off by default.

title: A floating object dropped on a page that only continues a paragraph jumps back to the page where the paragraph starts
author: RatkoR
body:
## What happens
When you drop a floating picture or shape on a page that only continues a paragraph begun on an earlier page, it is drawn back on the earlier page, where the paragraph starts.

1. Make one long paragraph that runs over at least three pages, so page 2 holds only its middle.
2. Insert a picture or shape near the top of page 1 and set **Wrap Text › Square**.
3. Drag it into the middle of page 2 and drop it.

It jumps back to page 1, at the same position on the page, and its anchor mark goes with it.

## What Word does
Word for Mac (observed by hand, a picture and a rectangle, Square wrapping): the object stays where it was dropped on page 2, anchored to that paragraph, with the anchor mark beside the paragraph's top line on page 2.

## Cause
The drop itself is right. `move_object` finds no paragraph starting on page 2, so it moves the object's character to the start of the line nearest the drop on page 2 and positions the object relative to the page (`hRel`/`vRel` = page). But the layout puts a paragraph's page-relative floating objects on the page where the paragraph starts, not on the page of the object's character. So `layout.object()` reports page 0, and `move_object`'s retries can't fix it.

It reproduces headlessly on main: on a 400-sentence paragraph, `arrange.bounds {"page": 1, "x": 100, "y": 275}` moves the character to offset 4310 (on page 1, which starts at 3289), but `find_object` places the shape on page 0.

Found while checking the anchor mark in #4214 (#4195).

title: A floating object dropped just after a page break inside a paragraph jumps back to the page before
author: RatkoR
body:
## What happens

Drag a floating picture or shape onto a page that a paragraph continues onto after a **manual page break inside that paragraph**, and drop it near the first line after the break. The object is thrown back to the page before the break instead of staying where it was dropped.

This is a follow-up to #4250. That fix draws a float anchored on a later page of a long paragraph on that page, and drops onto such a page anchor the object at the line nearest the drop. It doesn't cover this one line yet.

## Why (from reading the code)

- With no paragraph starting on the target page, `move_object_once` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/objects.rs`) anchors the object with `nearest_line`, at the **start** of the line nearest the drop.
- If that line follows a page or column break, the #1632 cover-page rule applies: an anchor right at the start of a line after a break belongs to the line before it (`anchor_lines` in `crates/layout/src/lib.rs` maps it to `li - 1`). So the object is drawn on the page before the break.
- `move_object` retries a cross-page drop 3 times. Each try re-anchors to the same line start, so all three fail and the object keeps its place on the earlier page.

This was found in code review of the #4250 fix. It hasn't been reproduced in the app yet.

## Repro (expected)

1. A long paragraph with a manual page break (Ctrl+Enter) in the middle of it, so it continues onto the next page.
2. Insert a shape, set Square wrapping.
3. Drag it onto the next page, close to the first line after the break, and drop it.

**Expected:** it stays on the page where it was dropped, with the text wrapping around it.
**Actual:** it jumps back to the page before the break.

## To find out

- What Word does: where its anchor goes for a drop beside the first line after an in-paragraph page break, and on which page it draws an object anchored there.
- Possible fixes: anchor after the break rather than at the line's start, or let a page-relative drop (`on_page`) keep the page it…

title: A screen reader can still click controls behind a modal dialog
author: RatkoR
body:
## What happens

While a modal dialog is open (#3859, #4076), a mouse click or a key press can't reach anything behind it. A screen reader still can: it can activate a button behind the dialog, such as File on the ribbon, and that button's action runs.

## Why

- egui 0.36.2 turns an AccessKit `Click` action request into a normal primary click in `Context::get_response` (`context.rs`, around line 1476). It checks only that the widget is enabled and senses clicks. It doesn't check `Memory::allows_interaction(layer_id)`, which is what keeps widgets behind the modal layer from taking keyboard focus.
- Our modal dialogs (`block_behind` in `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`) block the pointer with a backdrop and take the keyboard. They also mark the window `set_modal()` for AccessKit, but the nodes behind it stay in the tree and can still be clicked.

This was found by CodeRabbit in its review of #4076.

## What won't work

- **Making the dialog the root's only child in the AccessKit tree**, as CodeRabbit suggested. egui sends the full tree every frame, so every other top-level node (ribbon, canvas, status bar…) would be left without a parent. `accesskit_consumer` panics on that ("TreeUpdate includes N nodes which are neither in the current tree nor a child of another node", `tree.rs`), and the app would crash whenever a screen reader is running. It would also hide the dialog's own popups (combo-box lists), which egui hangs off the root. This comes from reading the code; it hasn't been reproduced.
- **Disabling the UI behind the dialog** greys out the whole window, which Word doesn't do.

## Possible fixes

- **In egui:** `get_response` would check `allows_interaction(layer_id)` before turning an AccessKit action into a click, as it already does for focus.
- **In WordCraft:** drop AccessKit action requests aimed at widgets behind the modal layer before the frame runs. egui has no public way to get from an AccessKit `NodeId` back to an `Id` or its layer, so this needs a mapp…

title: Tables: min-height row with a picture is still split across pages in v0.10.0 (regression of #1742?); 4-page .docx becomes 5 pages

title: [Feature Request] Restore last scroll position and cursor location on project reopen
author: psign04
body:
[Feature Request] Restore last scroll position and cursor location on project reopen

Description:
As an author working on a long-form monograph in Wordcraft,
I want the application to automatically restore my exact page/scroll position and cursor location when I reopen a project,
So that I can seamlessly resume writing and editing right where I left off, mimicking the standard reading behavior found in PDF readers and eBook software, without having to manually scroll through tens of thousands of words to find my place.
Expected Behavior:
Auto-Save State: Upon closing the project, switching tabs, or exiting Wordcraft, the current chapter ID, active scroll offset, and cursor position should be saved.
Auto-Restore View: Upon reopening the manuscript, Wordcraft should instantly scroll to that exact saved location and place the cursor accordingly.
Fallback: Default to the top of the first chapter only when opening a newly created or imported project for the first time.
Technical Implementation Suggestions (Tech Hints):
Local State Persistence:
During debounced auto-save events or component unmount, serialize the project's session state (e.g., active section ID, scroll top offset, or editor CaretPosition / Selection range).
Persist this payload to localStorage, a local session-state.json file, or the project’s metadata wrapper.
View Restoration Lifecycle:
On project load/initialization, parse the saved session state.
Apply a delayed .scrollTo() or programmatically focus the editor instance (e.g., using requestAnimationFrame) once the document layout and DOM elements have fully rendered to prevent visual layout shifts.
Graceful Fallback:
If the session state is missing, corrupted, or references a deleted section, gracefully default the view to the top of the project's root document

title: [Bug] Caret stays at the left edge on an empty line of a centred paragraph after Shift+Enter
author: Yudhistira-Official
body:
_Written with an AI assistant at the request of @Yudhistira-Official._

**Version:** seen on WordCraft v0.10.0 (`9130181a`); code checked on `main` at `b70c746f` (2026-10-25).
**Environment:** Linux x86_64, AppImage.

## Problem

After a manual line break (Shift+Enter) in a centred paragraph, the new empty line's caret is drawn at the left edge of the text column. As soon as a character is typed, the line jumps to the centre and the caret is correct.

## Steps to reproduce

1. New document. Type `BAB I`.
2. Press Shift+Enter.
3. Press Ctrl+E to centre the paragraph (or Home › Paragraph › Center).
4. Do not type. Look at the caret.

## Expected

The caret sits at the centre of the text column on the empty line, as in Word.

## Actual

The caret is drawn at the left edge of the text column. Typing one character makes the whole line (and the caret) jump to the centre.

## Likely cause

`crates/layout/src/para.rs`:

- The alignment shift is applied to the line's clusters (`(None, Align::Center) => slack / 2.0`, around line 2558).
- A line with no clusters returns early in `reorder_line` (`let n = c1.saturating_sub(c0); if n == 0 { … return; }`, around line 2747), so the line's `xs` stay at the start edge.
- `DocLayout::caret`/`hit` then read that start x. Typing adds a cluster, so the line shifts.

## Suggested implementation

- In `break_lines` or `reorder_line`, when `n == 0`, compute the caret x from `rp.align`:
  - Left: `line.left`
  - Center: `(line.left + line.right) / 2`
  - Right: `line.right`
  - Mirror for RTL paragraphs.
- Keep justified/distributed empty lines at the start edge.
- Add tests in `crates/layout/src/tests.rs`:
  - `caret_on_an_empty_centred_line`
  - `caret_on_an_empty_right_aligned_line`
  - a line after `ClKind::LineBreak` inside a centred paragraph
  - use `DocLayout::caret(&Pos::body(...))` for the x.
- Optional `ui_shot` test to confirm the caret is visibly centred.

title: [Bug] Ctrl+Y does nothing when there is nothing to redo; Word repeats the last action
author: Yudhistira-Official
body:
_Written with an AI assistant at the request of @Yudhistira-Official._

**Version:** seen on WordCraft v0.10.0 (`9130181a`); code checked on `main` at `b70c746f` (2026-10-25).
**Environment:** Linux x86_64, AppImage.

## Problem

Word's Ctrl+Y is Repeat/Redo: it redoes when the redo stack has something, otherwise it repeats the last action. WordCraft binds Ctrl+Y only to `edit.redo`; Repeat is on F4 only. With an empty redo stack, Ctrl+Y is a silent no-op.

## Steps to reproduce

1. New document. Type `Hello`.
2. Press Ctrl+Y.
3. Or: bold a word, move the caret elsewhere, press Ctrl+Y.

## Expected (Word)

- After typing `Hello`, Ctrl+Y repeats the typing (Word inserts `Hello` again, or repeats the last action).
- After Bold, Ctrl+Y applies Bold again at the new caret.

## Actual

Nothing happens when there is nothing to redo.

## Likely cause

- `edit.redo` is bound to `Mod+Y / Mod+Shift+Z` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs`, lines 53–61).
- `edit.repeat` is bound to `F4` only (`crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs`, lines 434–439).
- `edit.redo` has no `when` guard and `s.redo()` is a no-op on an empty stack, so the key is consumed without doing anything.

## Suggested implementation

- Add `edit.repeatOrRedo` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs`:

```rust
CommandSpec::new("edit.repeatOrRedo", "Repeat or Redo", "Quick Access Toolbar", |s, _| {
    if s.can_redo() {
        s.redo();
        sel_result(s)
    } else {
        s.run("edit.repeat", &Value::Null)
    }
})
.key("Mod+Y")
.pure(),
```

- Keep `edit.redo` for the toolbar button and `Mod+Shift+Z` for pure Redo.
- If `edit.repeat` has nothing to repeat, return its existing error or leave the key as a no-op, as Word does.

author: Yudhistira-Official
body:
_Written with an AI assistant at the request of @Yudhistira-Official._

**Version:** seen on WordCraft v0.10.0 (`9130181a`); code checked on `main` at `b70c746f` (2026-10-25).
**Environment:** Linux x86_64, AppImage.

## Problem

After changing a list item from level 1 (`A.`) to level 2 (`a.`), the numbering changes but the indent does not follow the new level. It looks too far out (or too far in) compared with the ruler/level indicator. Dragging the ruler once makes it jump into place.

## Steps to reproduce

1. New document. Type `A. First` and let AutoFormat make it a list, or apply Home › Numbering › `A. B. C.`.
2. (Optional but likely important) Drag the left-indent marker on the ruler to a custom position.
3. Put the caret in the item and choose Home › Numbering › Change List Level › Level 2, or run `para.listLevel {"level":1}`.
4. Compare the number/text position with the ruler markers.
5. Drag the ruler marker a little.

## Expected (Word)

The item takes level 2's number position and text indent; the label and text stay aligned, and the ruler markers show the new level. A previous direct indent does not survive the level change.

## Actual

The number changes to `a.` but the paragraph keeps its old indent, so it is not aligned with the level indicator. Dragging the ruler “corrects” it because the drag writes new direct indents.

## Likely cause

- `para.listLevel` only changes `n.level` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/para.rs`, lines 149–157). It does not clear or update `indent_left` / `indent_first`.

title: [macOS] ⌘Q exits immediately with unsaved changes without prompting to save
author: piyushgoel2808
body:
### Summary
On macOS, pressing **⌘Q** (or selecting Quit from the application menu) immediately terminates WordCraft and loses any unsaved changes in dirty documents.

In contrast, clicking the window close button (`X`) properly intercepts the close request, checks if any document is dirty, and prompts the user whether to save changes.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Launch WordCraft on macOS.
2. Create or open a document.
3. Make an edit so the document is marked dirty with unsaved changes.
4. Press **⌘Q** on the keyboard.
5. **Observed**: The application terminates immediately; unsaved changes are lost without prompt.
6. **Expected**: WordCraft should prompt the user to save changes before closing (matching the close button behavior).

### Root Cause
On macOS, `winit` handles `⌘Q` / `[NSApp terminate:]` by terminating the event loop and exiting the process directly, bypassing egui's window close request.

### Proposed Solution
Intercept `⌘Q` on macOS so that it routes through `egui::ViewportCommand::Close`, allowing WordCraft's existing unsaved-changes guard to prompt the user before exiting.
