title: Web: host WordCraft in the page's own document (no iframe)
author: helenkwok
body:
The web app's host bridge (`?host=parent`, [`host.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/main/apps/wordcraft-web/src/host.rs)) only works inside an iframe: `Bridge::new()` returns `None` when the page isn't framed. A page that loads the wasm-bindgen module into its own document, with its own `<canvas id="wordcraft_canvas">` inside a component, can run WordCraft fine but has no way to hand it a document or receive its saves.

**Why it matters.** Embedding the editor as a component sized to a box, next to the page's own header and controls, is simpler than an iframe (one document, one style sheet, no cross-frame plumbing) and is how a React or plain-JS host usually wants it. I checked it with a web build of current `main`: the editor renders inside the box and keyboard focus stays separate from the page's own inputs; only the bridge is missing.

**Suggestion.** The same opt-in page host mode now proposed for GridCraft and PdfCraft (storytold/gridcraft#2593, storytold/pdfcraft#4732): `data-host="page"` on the canvas turns it on, WordCraft dispatches `wordcraft:ready`, `wordcraft:save`, `wordcraft:dirty` and `wordcraft:failed` on the canvas with the message fields as `detail`, and the page dispatches `wordcraft:open` on the canvas. The events don't bubble, so nothing else on the page hears them. Unframed `?host=parent` keeps today's behaviour (the normal app with downloads), so no save can be posted to nobody, and the parent bridge's messages are unchanged.

I have a working implementation and will open a PR referencing this issue.

title: [Feature Request] [WordCraft] MCP: opt-in protection against overwriting existing files, and logging refused paths
author: MyAIPlugins
body:
## Environment

- WordCraft built from `main`, headless `wordcraft-cli mcp` with `--automation-read-root` / `--automation-write-root`, driven by an MCP client over stdio (Claude Desktop, macOS).

## Context

The write root keeps an agent's saves inside the folders it was given. Inside them, though, an agent can replace any existing file without being asked: `save_document` with the path of an existing file overwrites it, whatever the file is. When the write root is a folder people work in (a client's working folder rather than a scratch folder), one wrong path from the agent replaces a document someone was editing, and nothing in the protocol made that a deliberate choice.

A refused path is also only visible to the agent: the server returns the error as a tool result and logs nothing, so the person running the server can't see afterwards which paths an agent tried to reach outside its roots.

## Request

1. **Opt-in protection against overwriting.** For example a server flag (`--automation-no-overwrite`, or per root) under which `save_document` (and the commands that write a file at a path, `file.saveAs`, `file.exportPdf`...) refuse to replace an existing file unless the call says so explicitly (`"overwrite": true`), with an error naming the file. Saving in place (`save_document` without `path`) would stay as it is. Off by default, so nothing changes for existing setups.
2. **Log refused paths.** When a path is refused by the roots, write one line to the server's stderr (or its log) with the path as given and the path as resolved, so the person can review what the agent tried.

I can prepare a PR for either if the approach fits. Related: #3582 (several roots per kind, PR #4372).

Found and verified with Claude (Anthropic), model Opus 5.5 at medium effort, with human review by Alan Curtis.

title: Linked text boxes of different widths repeat part of a line
author: benandez
body:
When a story flows through linked text boxes of different widths, the next box can repeat the start of a line the previous box already showed.

**Where (main, `crates/layout/src/textbox.rs`)**
- `fit_flow` cuts the story at `Cut { byte: l.start }`: the start of the first line, in the previous box's layout, that doesn't fit.
- The next box lays the story out at its own width (or reuses a nearby width via `near()`). There, the cut byte usually falls in the middle of a line.
- `cut_y` picks the line holding that byte (`l.stop > cut.byte`), and `from_y` keeps that whole line. So the text from the start of that line up to the cut byte appears twice: at the end of box 1 and at the top of box 2.

**Repro (expected)**
Two linked text boxes, the second noticeably narrower or wider than the first, and enough text to overflow the first. The last words of box 1 reappear at the top of box 2. In Word, box 2 starts exactly where box 1 stopped.

**Not caused by** the layout resource caps (#3867 / #4385). The same `cut_y`/`from_y` path runs without them. CodeRabbit flagged it on #4385, and we left it out of that PR as a separate design change.

**Fix direction:** start box 2's layout at the cut byte (re-lay out the remainder of the story from `cut.byte` at box 2's width), rather than slicing a full-story layout by y. Check this against the layout sharing that `MAX_FLOW_WIDTHS` / `near()` exist for. Needs a regression test with two widths.

Found while reviewing #4385; source-traced, not yet reproduced in the app.

title: FORMAT long is not supported in hunspell dictionary .aff files
author: c--w
body:
`parse_aff()` in `affix.rs` currently does not support two-character flags (`FLAG long` in Hunspell `.aff` files). 

Many morphologically rich and complex languages (such as German, Polish, Italian, and others) require `FLAG long` to handle extensive affixation, compounding rules, and grammatical variations. 

Because the parser lacks this support, obtaining the official dictionary files for these languages still leaves them unsupported. This severely limits the utility for international users, as spell checking is an essential feature for document writing.

title: [Linux/Wayland] Missing Quit action and keyboard shortcut (Ctrl+Q) makes apps impossible to close from UI on tiling window managers
author: wcervini
body:
Descripción (Body)
### Description
Across the ArtCraft suite applications (e.g., GridCraft, WordCraft, PhotoCraft, ArtCraft Launcher, etc.), there is currently no in-app way to quit/close the application window—neither via a menu action (`File -> Quit` / `Salir`) nor via standard keyboard shortcuts (`Ctrl+Q` / `Ctrl+W`).

### Why this is a problem
The applications rely on server-side window decorations (system titlebar close button `X`) provided by the window manager via `winit`. 

However, on Linux tiling window managers and Wayland compositors without titlebars by default (such as **Hyprland**, **Sway**, **i3**, etc.), windows do not have a titlebar with a close (`X`) button. Additionally:
- Pressing `Ctrl+Q` or `Ctrl+W` does nothing.
- In apps like GridCraft or WordCraft, `File -> Close` (`Archivo -> Cerrar`) only closes the active document/backstage view, not the application itself.
- `ArtCraft Launcher` also lacks a quit button or `Ctrl+Q` shortcut.

As a result, users on tiling window managers have no way to close the apps from within the application or via standard app shortcuts, and are forced to use compositor-level kill/close window keybindings.

### Expected Behavior
1. Support the standard **`Ctrl+Q`** shortcut across all ArtCraft suite apps and the ArtCraft Launcher to cleanly exit the application (e.g., sending `egui::ViewportCommand::Close`).
2. Add a **Quit / Exit** (`Salir`) option in the `File` (`Archivo`) menu (or top bar) to close the application window.

### Environment
- **OS:** Linux (x86_64)
- **Package format:** AppImage (via ArtCraft Launcher v0.3.2)
- **Display Server / Compositor:** Wayland (Hyprland 0.56.2)
- **Affected Apps:** All apps in the suite (GridCraft, WordCraft, PhotoCraft, ArtCraft Launcher, etc.)

title: Serbian spelling: the affix engine needs numeric flags and more than 128 flags (FLAG num, ~1,900 affix groups)
author: sociolog
body:
Serbian spelling (Cyrillic `sr_RS` and Latin `sh_RS`) can't be offered yet: the affix engine can't read the Serbian Hunspell dictionaries. I'm opening this to pin down what Serbian needs, so the engine work is decided in one place alongside the open PRs on the same code, instead of in yet another PR. Serbian hyphenation is in a separate PR, #4447.

## What the Serbian dictionaries use
I counted these in LibreOffice's dictionaries ([`sr/`](https://github.com/LibreOffice/dictionaries/tree/67032ee957631908098a72edf48dc81cac27e369/sr) at `67032ee`, the collection #3296 tested), and in the `sr_RS`/`sh_RS` pair we use in InDesign, a corrected 2019 variant of the same dictionary (place names capitalized, their adjectives as words of their own):

| | LibreOffice `sr` (Cyrillic) / `sr-Latn` (Latin) | our `sr_RS` / `sh_RS` |
|---|---|---|
| Flags | **`FLAG num`** | `FLAG num` |
| Affix groups (distinct flags) | **1,903** | 1,811 |
| Affix rules | 33,710 | 32,518 |
| Stems | 251,549 | 251,548 |
| Flags per stem | at most 2 | at most 2 |
| Continuation classes | none | none |
| Compounding, `NEEDAFFIX`, `CIRCUMFIX`… | none | none |
| Other directives | `SET UTF-8`, `WORDCHARS`, `KEY` | `SET UTF-8`, `WORDCHARS` |

So Serbian is simple in structure: one affix per word, with no chains and no compounds. It is large in two dimensions the engine caps:
1. **Numeric flags.** `FLAG num` is rejected (`affix.rs` test `FLAG num` → error; also #3296's "don't load yet" list).
2. **More than 128 distinct flags.** Flags are bits of a `u128` throughout `affix.rs` (`Rule::bit`, `cont`, the per-stem `sets`, `forbidden`, `no_suggest`, `by_flag`), and the compact `to_bytes` format writes each flag as one character. Serbian has about 1,900 flags. Mapping numeric flags to characters wouldn't help: a different flag representation is needed, for example a `u16` flag id per rule and a small sorted set per stem, with the `u128` fast path kept for the ≤128 dictionaries.

The same two gaps block the other …

title: PDF export ignores the selected Numeral display mode
author: earlvanze
body:
## Reproduction

1. Open a document containing ASCII digits, such as `2026`.
2. Choose File > Options > Numerals > Hindi. The canvas displays Arabic-Indic digits.
3. Export or print to PDF.

## Actual

The PDF uses Western/ASCII digits. Reopening a document also shows its stored digits, because Numeral is currently a display-only option.

## Expected

PDF/print output should use the active resolved Numeral display mode, matching the canvas. The UI should make the display-only scope clear; persistence of the selection across launches is separately covered by PR #3179.

## Investigation

`wordcraft_pdf::export` and the extension-based PDF path construct `LayoutOptions` with `..Default::default()`, so their numeral mode is `Arabic` rather than the session view setting. Printing via `export_layout` receives the existing session layout and can preserve it.

Copying text from a Markdown source (GitHub, Obsidian, an AI chat) and pasting it into WordCraft inserts the markers literally: `## Heading`, `**bold**`, `- item`, `| a | b |`. The text has to be reformatted by hand, and the only alternative is Keep Text Only, which is the same thing.

title: Keycap and variation-selector emoji sequences render as a box or split glyph

body:
## Problem

Emoji presentation sequences are not drawn as one emoji: a keycap like `1️⃣` (U+0031 U+FE0F U+20E3) shows the digit in the text font and then a missing-glyph box for the keycap; `👩‍💻` (ZWJ) splits into its components; `⚖️` (U+2696 U+FE0F) loses its colour. Lone emoji draw in colour correctly.

The whole sequence is shaped as one cluster in a colour emoji font, as the page already does for lone emoji: `1️⃣` one coloured keycap, `👩‍💻` one glyph, `⚖️` coloured. Text presentation (`❤︎`, U+FE0E) stays text, and a machine without a colour emoji font falls back to the interface glyph.

The page path for colour emoji exists (see #1754, #1874, #2451); this is the sequence part and the interface (the Navigation pane). A PR follows.

body:

body:
A DOCX document created locally in WordCraft was blocked by macOS with a security warning when I attempted to open it.

I created the document directly in WordCraft by pasting text copied from Microsoft Word, then continued working on and saving it. The document was never downloaded from the internet.

When I attempted to open the file, macOS displayed the following warning:

"Apple cannot verify that the document is free of malware that may harm your Mac or compromise your privacy."

I checked the file's extended attributes using Terminal and found:

`com.apple.quarantine: 0081;00000000;;`

I also checked its metadata, which showed:

`kMDItemCreator = (null)`

`kMDItemWhereFroms = (null)`

I was able to resolve the issue by manually removing the quarantine attribute using `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine`.

To investigate further, I created a separate test document directly in WordCraft and saved it as DOCX. This new document did not have the quarantine attribute, suggesting that the issue does not occur consistently.

I haven't been able to identify what triggered the quarantine attribute on the original document. Could this be related to how WordCraft handles DOCX files during saving or subsequent modifications?

title: Navigation pane: at its minimum width the last tab can be clipped in languages with long labels
author: fluorine
body:
Raised in review of #4480 (Navigation pane uses the shared dialog tabs).

**Problem.** The Navigation pane has a minimum width of 200 pt, so its content is 178 pt wide. The three tabs (Headings, Pages, Results) need more than that in languages with long labels. A review estimate for German is about 184 pt of text at 12.5 pt, before padding. Tab padding already shrinks to 4 pt per side, which is the lowest value. `PaneHost` clips the rest, so the last tab (Results) can be partly hidden.

**Not verified.** The German figure is an estimate from the catalog. Nobody has measured it in the running app.

**Why not a scroll area.** A horizontal scroll area hides the last tab just as clipping does, and it adds a scroll bar to a 26 pt strip.

**Options.**
1. Raise the pane's minimum width so the longest translated strip fits. This changes `PaneHost` in craft-libs.
2. Wrap the tab labels onto a second row when they do not fit.

**Done when.** At the minimum pane width, all three tabs are fully visible in every interface language. A kittest checks this with the longest labels.

Related: #4029, #4480.

title: refactor(cli): parse `wordcraft-cli` arguments with clap, following RFC-0012
author: 1Git2Clone
body:
Move `wordcraft-cli`'s argument parsing to [clap](https://docs.rs/clap) derive and [thiserror](https://docs.rs/thiserror), the way photocraft did, so it follows [RFC-0012: Command-line conventions](https://github.com/storytold/craft-contrib/pull/18). Then every Craft CLI behaves the same: the same exit codes, help, errors, environment variables, completions and man pages.

## Reference

- **The rules:** [RFC-0012](https://github.com/storytold/craft-contrib/pull/18).
- **The plan and decisions:** [photocraft#7071](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/7071). It covers what was decided and why, such as rejecting repeated flags, `--version` with no `version` subcommand, and values that start with `-`.
- **The code:**
  - the port, merged as one PR: [photocraft#9167](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/9167);
  - its review follow-up, typed usage errors: [photocraft#9194](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/9194);
  - the ast-grep rules for the CLI code: [photocraft#9750](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/9750), using craft-common-actions' [`ast-grep.yml`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions/pull/80).
- **Files to read in photocraft:**
  - `apps/photocraft-cli/src/args.rs`
  - `apps/photocraft-cli/src/error.rs`
  - `apps/photocraft-cli/src/lib.rs` (`run`)
  - `crates/automation/src/args.rs` (shared flags and environment variables)
  - `apps/photocraft/src/launch_args.rs` (the desktop app)
  - `apps/photocraft-cli/examples/man-and-completions.rs`
  - `lint/ast-grep/`

## Scope

title: No visible keyboard focus indicator
author: d-0-t
body:
## Summary

Build: WordCraft v0.11.0 on Windows.

Keyboard focus reaches some UI elements, but most of the chrome paints no focus state. The only visible focus cues are on egui built-ins: checkboxes, text fields, and the underline that a focused Label gets, such as "More templates →". The hand-painted controls react to hover, press and checked only.

## Steps

1. Open the app.
2. Press Tab repeatedly.

Actual: The focus walks, but it does not change appearance. There is no ring, outline or fill that says where Enter will go.
Expected: A visible focus indicator on the control with keyboard focus, distinct from hover and from the checked or selected state.

## Why

`widgets::bg` chooses a fill for pressed, checked or hovered, then returns. It never reads `resp.has_focus()`, and `theme::Tokens` has no focus colour. `small`, `big`, `split`, the QAT buttons, the title bar and status bar, the Backstage navigation rows, the template tiles, the recent-file rows and the Styles gallery tiles all paint their own backgrounds.

The Backstage tiles, recent rows and Styles gallery tiles only check `hovered()`. The font and size boxes already show focus because they are egui text fields, so they are not the gap.

egui itself maps `has_focus()` to the `active` visuals in `WidgetVisuals::style`, and a focused Label underlines itself. That is why the built-ins show a cue and the custom controls do not.

## Impact

This is the focus-visible requirement, WCAG 2.4.7. Keyboard-only users cannot tell which command Enter will run. It also makes the Tab problem in #3164 look like nothing happens when focus does move.

## Fix

- Add a focus token to `theme::Tokens`, for example a ring colour and width, for both light and dark palettes.
- In `widgets::bg`, draw the fill first and then a 2 px focus ring when `resp.has_focus()`. Keep the ring visible against the ribbon, hover and checked fills.
- Use the same helper for the QAT, title bar, status bar, Backstage navigation, template tiles, recent…

title: KeyTips skip the font and size boxes, Styles gallery and other Home controls
author: d-0-t
body:
## Summary

Build: WordCraft v0.11.0 on Windows.

Alt/F10 KeyTips skip several visible controls on Home. The badges appear on Paste, Cut, Copy, the character buttons and most paragraph commands, but not on:

- the Font name and Font size boxes
- Increase Font Size and Decrease Font Size
- Change Case
- Clear All Formatting
- Character Border, Enclose Characters and Phonetic Guide
- Left-to-Right and Right-to-Left Text Direction
- the Styles gallery
- the Clipboard, Font, Paragraph and Styles dialog launchers

A control with no badge cannot be reached by its KeyTip. The sequence has a hole, and the user has to Tab or reach for the mouse.

## Steps

1. Open the sample document and press Alt, then H.
2. Compare the badges with the controls drawn on the Home tab.

Actual: the controls above have no badge. The Styles gallery has none at all.
Expected: every visible ribbon command has a KeyTip, including combo boxes, galleries and dialog launchers, as in Word.

## Why

`keytips::controls(tab)` is a hand-written list that is supposed to mirror `ribbon.rs`. `letters_for` assigns one flat letter sequence to that list, and `widgets::keytip_badge` only records a badge when a widget's command id or tooltip matches an entry. A control that is not in the list gets nothing.

The font and size combo boxes call `keytip_badge` with the generic name `combo`, but `controls("Home")` has no such entry. The Styles gallery and the group launchers never call `keytip_badge` at all.

The list is a second copy of the ribbon layout, so it drifts whenever a control is added. The flat scheme also differs from Word's group-based sequences, such as Alt+H, F, S for Font Size and Alt+H, F, F for Font name. It runs out of single letters and falls back to two-letter badges, but those letters have no group meaning.

## Fix

- Register badgeable controls during layout, with their id or name and rect, and derive the letters from what was drawn. That removes the parallel list.
- As a first step, add the mi…

title: KeyTip badges cover compact button icons
author: d-0-t
body:
## Summary

Build: WordCraft v0.11.0 on Windows.

When KeyTips are showing, the badge is painted on top of the button icon. On compact ribbon buttons the badge hides most of the glyph, so an icon-only command cannot be identified while choosing its letter.

## Geometry

`widgets::small` allocates a 24×22 px button and paints a 17×17 icon centred at x=12. `keytips::badge` places a 15×15 badge at the control's top-left corner plus 2 px right and 1 px down.

Relative to the button's top-left:

- badge: x 2 to 17, y 1 to 16
- icon: x 3.5 to 20.5, y 2.5 to 19.5
- overlap: 13.5×13.5 px, about 63% of the icon

Only a 3.5 px strip on the right and bottom of the icon stays visible. A two-letter badge is wider than 15 px and covers even more.

## Steps

1. Press Alt, then the tab letter.
2. Look at the badges over alignment and list buttons.

Actual: the badge sits on the glyph. The icon is hard to recognise, so the letter is hard to map to a command.
Expected: the badge sits beside or above the button, or in a reserved corner, and the icon stays recognisable.

## Why

`keytips::show` paints the badges after the ribbon, so a badge always sits on top. `keytips::badge` anchors every badge at the control's top-left corner. Large buttons have more room for that to be a corner overlap; compact buttons do not.

## Possible Fix

- Pass the icon rect, or a badge anchor, to the badge painter and choose a placement that does not intersect the icon: above the button, in the gap between groups, or in a badge lane reserved during layout.
- If the badge must overlap the button, draw it in the button's padding and offset or shrink the icon only while KeyTips are visible. Do not cover the glyph.
- Keep the badge inside the group and window bounds at the top edge.
- Test: for a compact 24×22 button with a 17×17 icon, assert the badge rect does not intersect the icon rect. Cover single-letter and multi-letter badges.

## Related

#3164 tracks keyboard navigation in KeyTip mode. A separate issu…

title: KeyTips: multi-letter command badges cannot be completed, and the second key reaches the document
author: d-0-t
body:
## Summary

On tabs with more than 26 available badge letters, WordCraft assigns two-letter badges such as `AG`. They cannot be activated. Pressing `A` runs the command that owns the single-letter `A` badge, turns KeyTips off, and the next `G` is handled as normal input, so it can be inserted into the document.

## Environment

- WordCraft 0.11.0
- Windows
- Ribbon visible, sample document

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open WordCraft 0.11.0 and press `Alt`, then `H` to show the Home tab's command badges.
2. Find a single-letter badge whose letter also starts a two-letter badge, for example `A` and `AG`.
3. Press `A`.
4. Press `G`.

## Expected

- After `A`, only badges starting with `A` remain, including `AG`. KeyTips stays on and no command runs.
- `G` completes `AG` and runs that command once.
- No document text changes except what that command does.

## Actual

- `A` runs the command for the single-letter `A` badge immediately.
- KeyTips closes and all badges disappear.
- `G` is no longer consumed by KeyTips. It can be inserted into the document, depending on focus.

## Cause

`Phase::Commands` in `crates/ui-egui/src/keytips.rs` compares the key against each badge with `l == name`. It has no prefix state:

```rust
for (ctl, l) in ctrls.into_iter().zip(ls) {
    if l == name {
        hit = Some(ctl.target);
        break;
    }
}
app.ui.keytips = Phase::Off;
```

It then clears `keytip_prefix`, so a partial prefix cannot survive to the next key.

The allocator, `letters_for`, makes the collision systematic. It assigns single letters first. The two-letter fallback runs only when every letter is either used or reserved. The fallback avoids reserved letters, so the first character of every two-letter badge is already assigned to a single-letter badge. Every multi-letter badge is therefore shadowed by a single-letter badge.

The fallback comment says a tab has at most about 20 controls. Home has 32, so the fallback is normal there, not a corner case.

title: [Feature Request] View-only web mode for displaying DOCX documents
author: jesse-schein
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

There are few good free libraries for viewing DOCX documents directly in a browser. WordCraft's web build already renders DOCX files and offers a Read Mode, making it a promising foundation for a browser-based document viewer. A website that only needs to display a document currently has to present the full editor and ask the user to open the file and enter Read Mode manually.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Provide a view-only mode for the web build, optimized for loading and reading DOCX files in a browser or embedding in another website. A host page should be able to load a document directly into the viewer, start in a reading-oriented view, and disable document modification and editing controls while retaining useful navigation and reading features.

Ideally, offer a smaller viewer-focused WebAssembly build that excludes editing functionality where practical, reducing the download size for sites that only need document viewing. A free, browser-based DOCX viewer built on WordCraft would be an excellent opportunity for the project.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Using the existing full web build and manually switching to Read Mode works as a starting point, but it still exposes the editor and requires manual steps. If maintaining a smaller build isn't desirable, a view-only configuration using the regular WebAssembly bundle would still be valuable. The existing bundle is reasonably small when gzipped given the large feature set it includes.

### Additional context

The goal is a practical viewing experience for websites that need to display DOCX documents, rather than a full editing workflow. The existing Read Mode is a useful starting point; the request is for a host-configurable view-only experience that can load a document directly.

title: Caret can't reach the end of a soft-wrapped line in Chinese text (or a word wider than the line): End stops one character short, Right jumps to the next line
author: inter0925
body:
## Summary

When a paragraph wraps **after text** rather than at a space — Chinese/Japanese text, or a single word wider than the line — there is no way to put the caret after the last character of a visual line (other than the paragraph's last line):

- **End** stops *before* the last character of the line.
- **Right** from there moves the caret to the *start of the next line*; it is never shown after the last character.
- **Shift+End** selects the line without its last character.
- **A click on the right half of the last character** (or just past it) puts the caret before that character.
- After the caret is at that position, **Home** and **Down** act on the *next* line, so Down skips a line.

Lines that wrap at a space are not affected (End stops before the trailing space, as intended).

It happens in body paragraphs and table cells, with left, centred, right and justified alignment. Seen on current `main` (2cf1d6c7ae94723a45bd6e7e8c884fe375148750) and in the v0.11.0 web build.

## Steps to reproduce (UI)

1. New blank document.
2. Paste a long paragraph of Chinese text so that it wraps over a few lines, for example this synthetic sentence repeated a few times:
   `春风拂过山岗，溪水绕着村庄静静流淌。春风拂过山岗，溪水绕着村庄静静流淌。春风拂过山岗，溪水绕着村庄静静流淌。`
3. Click at the start of the first line and press **End**.
4. Press **Right**.
5. Press **Home**.

**Expected:** after End the caret is after the last character of the first line, at the right edge. Right then moves past the first character of the second line; Home (from the end of the first line) goes back to the start of the first line.

**Actual:** End leaves the caret before the last character of the first line. Right moves it to the start of the second line. Home then stays there (the caret is on the second line).

The same happens with a long unbroken Latin word (e.g. `Lanternsdriftingoverquietharbours` repeated) that has to be broken mid-word.

title: Web build: Cmd/Ctrl+V pastes twice
author: inter0925
body:
## Summary

In the web build, once something has been copied in WordCraft, **Cmd/Ctrl+V pastes twice**: first WordCraft's own last copy, then the clipboard.

Seen in the official v0.11.0 web build and on current `main` (2cf1d6c7ae94723a45bd6e7e8c884fe375148750), in Chrome on macOS, served from `http://127.0.0.1` (a secure context).

(Split from the original report at the triage bot's request. The two formatting problems are now #4536 and #4537.)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the web build, then File ▸ New ▸ Blank document. Type `Quiet harbour`.
2. Press Cmd+A, then Cmd+C, then → (Right arrow).
3. Press Cmd+V.

**Expected:** `Quiet harbourQuiet harbour`. **Actual:** `Quiet harbourQuiet harbourQuiet harbour`.

If nothing has been copied in WordCraft yet, step 3 pastes once, but the status bar says "the clipboard is empty".

## Cause

`eframe`'s web key handler pushes the Cmd+V **key press**, and then the browser's `paste` event becomes `Event::Paste`. On the desktop, egui-winit sends only the event. In the web build the press reaches the canvas as the `Mod+V` shortcut and runs `edit.paste` with no text. With no clipboard service on the web, that pastes the engine's own last copy. Then `Event::Paste` pastes the clipboard's text. Cmd+C and Cmd+X also run twice, once as the shortcut and once for the copy or cut event.

## Related

- #4536, #4537: the formatting half of the same web clipboard handling.
- #2909: the image cases.

Fixed by #4525.

title: Feature: tracked rewrite that marks only what changed (word/character diff), for agents
author: inter0925
body:
## Problem

With Track Changes on, replacing text marks the whole old range as deleted and inserts the whole new text. For typing over a selection that is what Word does. Agents (MCP, the CLI, `edit.replace`, `edit.replaceText` in #2577) usually rewrite a whole sentence or paragraph to change a few words, though. The reviewer then sees the entire paragraph struck through and reinserted, and can't accept or reject the individual changes.

Example, Track Changes on, synthetic text:

- Before: `The quiet harbour opens at dawn, and the boats leave at six.`
- Agent replaces the paragraph with: `The quiet harbour opens at sunrise, and the boats leave at seven.`
- Today: one deletion of the whole sentence and one insertion of the whole new sentence.
- Wanted: `dawn` → `sunrise` and `six` → `seven` as two small deletion/insertion pairs. The rest stays untouched, keeping its formatting, comments and any earlier revisions.

The same applies to Chinese and to mixed text (`会议改到周三下午` → `会议改到周四上午`), where the unit should be a character (grapheme), not a word.

## Proposal

An option on the replacement command (for example `"minimal": true` on `edit.replaceText` from #2577, or a separate `text.rewrite`) that:

1. Diffs the old and new text of the target (one paragraph, or a range inside one story) with the existing bounded LCS in `cmd/tools/compare.rs` (`lcs_ops`, with its cell budget), over graphemes for CJK and words elsewhere, or simply graphemes.
2. Applies the changes back to front as ordinary tracked deletions and insertions, so earlier positions don't shift. Unchanged text keeps its runs, formatting, comment anchors and fields.
3. Is one Undo step. With no changes it makes no revision and no Undo step.
4. Falls back to the current whole replacement when the texts are mostly different (a threshold), or when the diff would exceed the budget.
5. Refuses, without changes, ranges it can't diff safely: across existing tracked deletions, objects, or table cells. Or it falls back f…

title: cargo xtask ci fails at clippy on Windows: names in crates/mcp/tests/automation_roots.rs is dead code
author: 4waymedia
body:
`cargo xtask ci` on Windows (main at 2cf1d6c, stable 1.97) fails at the clippy step:

    error: function `names` is never used
      --> crates/mcp/tests/automation_roots.rs:213:4

`names()` (line 213) is only called from
`a_link_outside_the_write_root_into_it_is_not_written` (line 219), which is
`#[cfg(unix)]`. On Windows the helper has no caller, and `-D warnings` makes
the dead-code lint fatal, so the whole gate fails before the tests run. The
Linux and macOS runners don't hit it.

Fix: gate the helper the same way as its only caller (`#[cfg(unix)]` on
`names`), so Windows contributors get a green `cargo xtask ci` again. PR #4539.

title: Track Changes: pasting paragraphs over several paragraphs, then Accept All, joins the pasted paragraphs
author: inter0925
body:
## Summary

With Track Changes on, select text that spans more than one paragraph and paste text of several paragraphs over it. Accept All then removes the paragraph breaks the paste inserted, so all the pasted paragraphs end up in one. Pasting over a selection inside one paragraph keeps them, and so does Reject All.

Seen on current `main` (2cf1d6c7ae94723a45bd6e7e8c884fe375148750).

## Steps (wordcraft-cli)

```sh
wordcraft-cli run \
  --cmd 'document.setText={"text":"one\ntwo"}' \
  --cmd 'review.trackChanges={"value":true}' \
  --cmd 'select.all' --cmd 'edit.pasteText={"text":"A1\nB1"}' \
  --cmd 'review.acceptAll' --cmd 'document.text' --print
```

| Old text | Pasted | After Accept All | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| `one` | `A1\nB1` | `A1\nB1` | `A1\nB1` |
| `one\ntwo` | `A1\nB1` | `A1B1` | `A1\nB1` |
| `one\ntwo` | `A1\nB1\nC1` | `A1B1C1` | `A1\nB1\nC1` |

`docs/typing-parity.md` lists both halves as working on their own: "Paste of several paragraphs (tracking on) … Accept All keeps the pasted ones", and "Delete a range from the end of one paragraph into a later one … Accept All removes exactly those". The combination fails. It looks as if accepting the deleted paragraph marks also takes the inserted marks with them. I haven't looked at the cause yet.

title: Track Changes: `document.setText` replaces the text with no revisions
author: inter0925
body:
## Summary

With Track Changes on, `document.setText` (Replace Document Text, the agents' command) replaces the body directly. It records no tracked deletion or insertion, so the change can't be reviewed, and Reject All can't bring the old text back. #88 was the same problem for `edit.replaceAll`, fixed by routing it through the tracked paste path. `edit.replace` and `edit.replaceAll` are tracked on current `main`. `document.setText` is the remaining command in that class: it is the only agent command that assigns `doc.body` directly.

Seen on current `main` (2cf1d6c7ae94723a45bd6e7e8c884fe375148750).

## Steps (wordcraft-cli)

```sh
wordcraft-cli run --cmd 'document.setText={"text":"The harbour opens at dawn."}' --save base.docx
wordcraft-cli run --file base.docx \
  --cmd 'review.trackChanges={"value":true}' \
  --cmd 'document.setText={"text":"The harbour opens at noon."}' \
  --cmd 'review.changes' --cmd 'review.rejectAll' --cmd 'document.text' \
  --save after.docx --print
```

**Expected:** the old text as a tracked deletion and the new text as a tracked insertion, as `edit.replaceAll` does since #88. `review.changes` lists them, the saved `word/document.xml` has `w:del` and `w:ins`, and Reject All restores `The harbour opens at dawn.`

**Actual:**

```text
review.changes: []
document.text: {"text":"The harbour opens at noon."}
```

`after.docx` has `<w:trackRevisions/>` in `settings.xml`, but `document.xml` has no `w:ins` or `w:del`: just a plain run, `The harbour opens at noon.`

## Cause

`document.setText` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs`) builds a new body with `Document::from_text` and assigns `s.doc.body`, whatever `settings.track_changes` is.

## Related

- #88: the same problem for `edit.replaceAll` (closed, fixed in #92).
- #4527: a separate feature discussion. It is about making a tracked rewrite mark only the words that changed. This report is only about the rewrite not being tracked at all.

title: REF \n, \r and \w (paragraph-number cross-references) are updated to the bookmark's text, not the paragraph number

title: Delete Rows / Delete Table with Track Changes on only strike the cells' text; Accept All leaves empty rows
author: Alyosha-dot-shop
body:
## Summary
Two halves of one gap. The second half is #1998 (round trip of `w:trPr/w:ins` and `w:del`), which #1999 is working on and which builds on the `RowProps.ins`/`del` marks in #1925 (Compare). The first half, the editing commands, isn't covered there as far as I can see, so it gets its own issue here; the patch below covers both, in case any of it is useful next to #1925 and #1999.

1. With Track Changes on, **Delete Rows** and **Delete Table** strike the cells' text but leave the rows unmarked. Word, and WordCraft's own Accept All, then leave empty rows and an empty table instead of removing them. A counterparty who accepts all changes in Word gets a table with blank rows.

title: Web build: Copy and Cut put only plain text on the clipboard, so formatting is lost
author: inter0925
body:
## Summary

In the web build, **Copy and Cut put only plain text on the system clipboard**. Pasting into another program, or into WordCraft in another tab, loses bold, italic, headings and the rest. The desktop app puts HTML beside the text (#1523).

Seen in the official v0.11.0 web build and on current `main` (2cf1d6c7ae94723a45bd6e7e8c884fe375148750), in Chrome on macOS, served from `http://127.0.0.1`.

(Split from #4523 at the triage bot's request.)

## Steps to reproduce

1. In the web build, make a word bold, select it and press Cmd+C.
2. Paste it into a rich-text editor, or check the clipboard (on macOS: `osascript -e 'clipboard info'`).

**Expected:** HTML beside the text. **Actual:** only text formats (`«class utf8»`, `string`), so no formatting arrives.

## Cause

eframe's `copy`/`cut` handlers only push `Event::Copy`/`Event::Cut`. The canvas handles them in its next frame, after the browser event is over. `system_clipboard::put` then falls back to `ctx.copy_text`, which eframe writes asynchronously with `navigator.clipboard.writeText`: text only. `Services::set_clipboard_html` is not set on the web.

## Related

- #1523 (closed): the same loss on Linux desktop.
- #4523, #4537: the rest of the web clipboard handling.

Fixed by #4525.

title: Web build: pasting another program's formatted copy inserts plain text
author: inter0925
body:
## Summary

In the web build, **pasting another program's formatted copy** (a web page, Word, Google Docs) inserts plain text. The desktop app reads the HTML and keeps the formatting (#687).

Seen in the official v0.11.0 web build and on current `main` (2cf1d6c7ae94723a45bd6e7e8c884fe375148750), in Chrome on macOS, served from `http://127.0.0.1`.

(Split from #4523 at the triage bot's request.)

## Steps to reproduce

1. In another browser tab, select a sentence with bold and italic words and copy it.
2. Paste it into the WordCraft web build with Cmd+V.

**Expected:** bold and italic are kept. **Actual:** plain text.

## Cause

eframe's `paste` handler reads only `getData("text")`. `Services::clipboard_html` is not set on the web, so `edit.paste` never gets the HTML.

## Related

- #687 (closed): pasting another program's formatted copy on desktop.
- #4523, #4536: the rest of the web clipboard handling.
- #2909: pictures, which keep going through the web build's picture listener (#45, #1349).

Fixed by #4525.

title: Comment ranges inside footnotes and endnotes are dropped when a .docx is read
author: datanerdie
body:
**What happens**

A comment anchored inside a footnote or endnote (`w:commentRangeStart` / `w:commentRangeEnd` in `footnotes.xml` or `endnotes.xml`) loses its range when the file is read. The comment is kept in `Document::comments`, but the note's paragraph has no `CommentStart` / `CommentEnd`, so the comment is anchored nowhere and is saved back without a range.

**Cause**

`read_opened` (`crates/docx/src/read.rs`) reads `footnotes.xml` and `endnotes.xml` before `comments.xml`. `comment_id()` looks the file's id up in `comment_map`, which is still empty while the notes are read, so `w:commentRangeStart`, `w:commentRangeEnd` and `w:commentReference` inside notes all resolve to `None`.

**Reproduce**

A synthetic package with a body paragraph holding a footnote reference, a footnote whose paragraph has `<w:commentRangeStart w:id="7"/> … <w:commentRangeEnd w:id="7"/>`, and `comments.xml` with comment 7. After `wordcraft_docx::read`, the footnote paragraph's objects are only its own `NoteRef` mark.

**Fix**

Read `comments.xml` before the notes parts. A pull request with a regression test follows.

Found while building a Markdown ↔ .docx bridge on `wordcraft-doc` and `wordcraft-docx` (2cf1d6c).

title: Web host: request complete native snapshots without acknowledging Save
author: Srbino
body:
Same-origin iframe hosts can open native JSON, but the existing save bridge follows Save/Save As semantics, including save metadata and clearing dirty on delivery, and only reports boolean dirty transitions. A host cannot request a full native snapshot without acknowledging Save or detect another edit while dirty is already true.

Add correlated native snapshot requests to the existing opt-in host bridge and an opaque revision change notification. A snapshot should include pending comment/reply text through the existing Save preparation, validate its serialization with the native Document parser, and leave dirty state intact. Preserve the legacy save bridge.

The implementation is limited to the existing web host bridge and a small UI preparation/draft revision seam. It does not add a persistence service or claim durable Saved. Unapplied accessibility property fields remain outside the committed model, as with the existing Save flow.

The app itself is launched through the ArtCraft Launcher, and the corruption outlives both the app and the launcher, which points to the graphics driver being left in a wedged state rather than an app-only UI bug.

title: Web host: acknowledge native imports and expose document identity
author: Srbino
body:
A host can send `wordcraft:open`, but the inbox has no correlated completion response. Observing a later change event or snapshot does not establish that the requested native import finished. A host also needs the session's document identity separately from its opaque revision so it can stop persistence after a document replacement.

Extend the existing opt-in host bridge with optional bounded `requestId` on Open and `wordcraft:opened {requestId, document, revision}` only after the native engine completes the import, or a correlated error. Refuse replacement of unsaved changes, pending comment drafts and unconfirmed saves. Preserve legacy Open without an ID. Expose a separate opaque document string on native change/snapshot responses. Successful correlated import should show the native document, as the ordinary inbox import does; refusal must preserve the current UI and draft.

This builds on the native snapshot API in #4573. Durable save acknowledgements and an opaque-origin MessagePort transport remain separate work.

title: File › Options › Proofing: AutoCorrect Options does nothing when no document is open
author: jvspier
body:
**What happens:** with no document open (start screen), File › Options › Proofing › **AutoCorrect Options** does nothing: no dialog and no message. With a document open, the AutoCorrect dialog opens as expected.

**Why:** with no document open, `widgets::enabled` only allows the commands in `works_without_document` (`crates/ui-egui/src/app/commands.rs:959`). `tools.autocorrect` isn't in that list, so `input_dialog` never opens the dialog and the click is silently dropped.

**Suggested fix:** AutoCorrect is a per-user setting, so if its dialog doesn't depend on the document, add `tools.autocorrect` to `works_without_document`. Otherwise, grey the button out with a tooltip, so it doesn't look broken.

Seen on main `2cf1d6c7` (0.11.0).

(Found and written up with help from Claude Code.)

title: Web host: opt-in durable acknowledgements for native saves
author: Srbino
body:
The existing same-origin parent bridge treats its file transfer as the completion of Save. Hosts storing native versions need an opt-in profile where Ctrl+S requests storage, native snapshot export remains separate, and only the host's durable acknowledgement can show Saved. The default bridge contract should remain unchanged. This follows #4573 and #4583.

A browser probe with a native document larger than 4 MiB demonstrates the missing profile: `save=managed` currently still emits the legacy package save, changes save metadata, and clears dirty before any storage acknowledgement.

The proposed bounded profile should bind acknowledgements to an actually exported native snapshot by request ID, document and opaque revision. A known older manual ACK must complete its waiting ticket without clearing newer edits, allowing another Ctrl+S; unknown ACKs must not consume tickets. Pending comment drafts must survive stale ACKs and prevent Save Changes from closing over them. Failed storage must allow retry. Save As and Export should remain copies without acknowledging native storage.

I am working on a separate follow-up with test-first UI/state regressions and a real browser probe; the import/snapshot drafts stay separate.

title: Web host: private capability port for opaque sandbox embeds
author: Srbino
body:
The existing `host=parent` bridge deliberately requires a same-origin parent. An embedding page using `sandbox="allow-scripts"` with a credentialless iframe instead gives the editor an opaque origin; it needs an opt-in capability transport without relaxing that sandbox or the legacy window checks. This follows #4573, #4584 and #4590.

Use `host=port&parent_origin=<canonical HTTP(S) origin>`, with the bundle digest taken from the immutable `/b/<64 lowercase hex>/index.html` path (optionally under `/_editor` for a same-host asset mount, or `/workbook-editor`). The public window channel should carry only a three-field hello and a three-field connect transferring exactly one private MessagePort. Connect must be bound to the exact parent window, configured origin, protocol and bundle, accepted once. Native document bytes and subsequent existing `wordcraft:*` messages then use only that port. Native binary frames need a 32 MiB bound before copying JS input into WASM; legacy ID-less window Open keeps its behavior.

A real opaque-frame browser probe on the current managed-save draft starts the native renderer but emits no hello, confirming the transport is missing. I am preparing a separate follow-up with test-first control/bounds regressions and an actual sandbox browser probe. This does not add an engine-command protocol or change the default host mode.

title: Private native host: apply correlated read-only access without discarding drafts
author: Srbino
body:
A native-version host using the private capability transport in #4591 needs to start the editor locked, bootstrap its exact native document, and unlock only after the host grants this visit write access. Revocation must preserve the open document and pending native comment text.

This is a narrow follow-up to #4591 and #4590. Related: #2229 / #2272 already propose a legacy same-origin editing lock; this issue does not take over that work or its protocol. The private native custody profile additionally needs correlated access acknowledgements, a trusted import entry point while user Open remains blocked, and Save intent suppression while locked.

Proposed scope:

- Keep the guard on the engine session, outside serialized document protection, with legacy defaults unchanged.
- Start private-port instances locked before interaction. Send private ready with `accessProtocol: 1` and `readOnly: true`.
- Apply `wordcraft:set-access {requestId, readOnly}` before processing native input, then return `wordcraft:access {requestId, readOnly}` through the authenticated port.
- Keep navigation, selection, copy and find available. Refuse document mutations, history restoration, user document replacement and saving while locked, including direct queued Zotero mutations.
- Permit a clean native snapshot after trusted bootstrap. Refuse to flush an existing authored comment draft while locked and retain it for a later valid unlock; never acknowledge storage from the access operation.

I am preparing focused engine/UI/control regressions and an actual opaque-frame browser probe. Implementation and browser qualification are not complete yet.

title: Layout: a right tab past the right indent wraps its page number although Word keeps it on the line
author: dfgodvan
body:
Word's TOC styles give an entry a right indent and a right tab with a dot leader at the margin, past that indent. Word keeps the leader and the page number on the entry's line whenever the number fits between the text and the stop, so the number ends past the indent. WordCraft moves the tab and the number to the next line in most of these cases.

What I measured in Word for Mac 16.93 (Letter, 1in margins, Times New Roman 12pt, right indent 1cm = 28.35pt, right tab with dot leader at 468pt, the number "104"):

| Text ends short of the indent by | Word | WordCraft |
|---|---|---|
| 0.4, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5.8pt | leader and number on the line, number ends at the stop | tab and number on the next line |
| 7, 10pt | same | tab and number on the next line |

With a right indent of 0.2cm (5.67pt) the number (18pt) has to fit before the stop: Word keeps it on the line with 18.7pt and 21.8pt left, and wraps it with 16.7pt left or less. WordCraft wraps all of them.

Why. In the line breaker the first character after a right tab is checked against the right indent: the tab has no room yet, so `absorbs` is false. Later characters are absorbed into the tab's room, but the running shift computes the segment width as `x - tx`, which already includes that room, so the room drops back to zero after every second character and the next one is again checked against the indent. In practice the number has to fit inside the indent.

Word | WordCraft before | WordCraft after:

![comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dfgodvan/wordcraft/5aa4ad62e89131637f5465b3c4101ad821ab3ba2/compare-word-before-after.png)

Test document: [right-tab-beyond-indent.docx](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dfgodvan/wordcraft/5aa4ad62e89131637f5465b3c4101ad821ab3ba2/right-tab-beyond-indent.docx)

title: Co-edit over the Macula mesh: bring macula-craft-collab 0.7 into Wordcraft, Deckcraft and Gridcraft

body:
Purpose (capability): someone who installs Wordcraft, Deckcraft or Gridcraft can co-edit a document with another person over the Macula mesh. Today none of the three released apps can.

## Where it stands
- The three apps here carry no dependency on [macula-craft-collab](https://github.com/macula-io/macula-craft-collab), the crate that carries co-editing over the mesh (transport, identity, grants, realm membership).

## Plan
1. **Design comment on this issue first:** the seam each app exposes (document model ↔ `craft_collab`), whether co-editing is a Cargo feature (off by default, so a plain build stays mesh-free), how a user joins a realm and shares a document from the UI, and what the fork line's wiring can be reused for. Reviewed once before code.
2. Wordcraft first, behind the feature, with tests: two instances converge on the same document over a test station.
3. Deckcraft and Gridcraft follow the same shape.
4. The README and guide for each app say how to turn co-editing on.

Tracking for deckcraft and gridcraft is in this issue (cross-repo work: one issue in the primary repo).

title: Markdown import repeatedly normalizes nested undefined reference labels
author: OPUZZLES
body:
On main `d522bfd8b19168aabcd9a64d588397c519c393f9`, opening a Markdown paragraph with nested brackets and no matching reference definition takes quadratic time. The bracket matcher caches its pairs, but each candidate shortcut reference still copies its entire text and normalizes the whole label before a failed lookup.

A synthetic input is `prefix `, N opening square brackets, `x`, N closing square brackets, then ` suffix`. Converting that Markdown to native JSON with `wordcraft-cli` on Linux gives:

| N | Input bytes | Import/save time |
|---|---:|---:|
| 8,000 | 16,015 | 0.195 s |
| 16,000 | 32,015 | 0.738 s |
| 32,000 | 64,015 | 2.993 s |
| 64,000 | 128,015 | 11.699 s |

The complete literal text survives. This is an availability problem during open, not an observed content-loss defect. Adding an unrelated reference definition still reaches the same failed-label lookup path.

The existing lookahead budget in `crates/formats/src/markdown/inlines.rs::tokenize` charges bracket matching and inline destinations, but not reference-label searches/normalization or the eager `text.to_string()` in failed candidates. Charge reference lookup work to that same budget and borrow candidate text until it is actually used. Budget exhaustion should keep the source as literal text, as the current bracket guard does.

I am preparing a focused fix and regressions for this path. #4330 owns comment/definition boundaries, #4263 owns the empty-anchor suffix scan, and #2403 owns additional inline HTML tags. Their current patches do not change this reference-label work.

title: Navigation pane rebuilds the body heading list on unchanged repaints
author: OPUZZLES
body:
Navigation heading-list portion of #3636, split as requested in that discussion.

On main `c4fafc21`, every repaint of Navigation > Headings calls `nav_headings(&app.session.doc)` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panes/nav.rs`. It walks every body paragraph, resolves paragraph styles and list counters, and rebuilds the heading paths, levels and numbered labels. This happens again when the document has not changed, including caret moves and other repaints.

The heading list can be reused until the document identity or revision changes. Text, style and numbering edits, Undo/Redo, opening another document and switching documents must still refresh the list. Selection, collapse/expand and heading click targets must remain live; wrapped labels must keep their current layout.

This scope covers list reconstruction only. Drawing the heading rows, Styles and Comments panes, balloons, table-style tiles and Restrict Editing remain separate parts of #3636. The adjacent Navigation emoji and tab changes are independent presentation work.

I am qualifying this focused change with headless repaint regressions and before/after UI controls.

title: Preview selected text formatting while hovering the floating mini toolbar
author: fluorine
body:
## What happens

When text is selected, hovering a formatting command such as **Bold** in the floating mini toolbar does not preview its effect on the selected text. Users must click the command to see the result and undo or toggle it if they were only comparing options.

## Proposal

While the pointer hovers a formatting command in the floating mini toolbar, preview that command on the current text selection. For example, hovering **Bold** makes the selected word appear bold; moving to another command updates the preview, and leaving the toolbar or dismissing it restores the original document appearance. Clicking a command applies it normally.

The preview should not mutate the document, create an undo step, or lose the selection. It should respect existing command eligibility and formatting behavior.

## Related work

- #2984 added the formatting mini toolbar to text context menus.
- #4357 requests live preview of selected text while hovering font choices in a font dropdown.
- #3026 previews paste options on hover.

This request is specifically about previewing formatting commands from the floating mini toolbar, such as Bold, on the selected text.
